name: Al-Irshaad ila Saheeh al-I'tiqaad - shaykh al-Fawzan
description_short:
A book about the Aqeedah Saheehah and Right Faith and refuting the Shirk and atheism, written by Shaykh al-Fawzaan. 

This is a wonderful and useful detailed book about some of the issues related to Creed.  The book links these issues to some people’s practices today, explaining their rulings and the errors committed in those practices so that they may repent, while also warning others to be aware of them. In this thesis, the Sheikh explains the correct Islamic creed with its evidence from the two divine revelations (Quran and Sunnah), and explains therein the contradictions reported by the people of heresy, polytheism and atheism.

name: Ar-Risalah of Imam ash-Shafi'i (tahqiq by Ahmad Shakir)
description_short:
Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i's "Al-Risala" is a cornerstone in the science of Usul al-Fiqh (principles of Islamic jurisprudence), and is even considered the first independent work in this field. The book aims to establish a clear methodology for deriving Sharia rulings from their primary sources, the Quran and the Sunnah.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi said about it when he looked at it: "I have not looked at the book Al-Risala of al-Shafi'i except that I found new benefit in it."

Al-Shafi'i wrote the book Al-Risala twice. The first is known as the "Old" Risala, which he wrote in Mecca when he was young, in response to a request from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. As for the currently known version, it is the "New" Risala, which he wrote in Egypt. The book is one of the books that al-Rabi narrated from al-Shafi'i. The esteemed scholar Ahmad Muhammad Shakir verified and explained the book.

"Al-Risala" is considered one of the most famous and important books of al-Shafi'i, as it had a great impact on Islamic jurisprudence and its principles. The book provides reliable legal foundations that were missing before al-Shafi'i, as it derives methods for dealing with Sharia evidence, making it an important reference for all students and those interested in the principles of jurisprudence.

name: Al-Fiqh al-Muyassar - Group of Scholars (prefaced by Saalih Aal ush-Shaykh)
description_short:
Al-Fiqh al-Muyassar fi Daw’ al-Kitab wal-Sunna, authored by a group of scholars under the supervision of King Fahd Complex for the Printing of the Holy Quran, is a concise yet comprehensive guide to Islamic jurisprudence, covering essential rulings on worship and transactions. Designed for accessibility, it presents Fiqh rulings with their evidences from the Quran and authentic Sunnah, avoiding excessive complexity to suit beginners and lay Muslims.

Organized into fourteen chapters, the book addresses key topics like purification, prayer, zakat, marriage, and penal laws, using clear language and a structured format to facilitate understanding of Shari‘a principles without delving into juristic disputes, making it an ideal resource for those seeking practical knowledge of Islamic law.

name: As-Sifaat al-Ilahiyyah by Shaykh Muhammad Aman al-Jami
description_short:
An in-depth creedal study originally prepared as a doctoral dissertation by Sheikh Muhammad Aman ibn Ali al-Jami (d. 1415 AH), Dean of the Faculty of Hadith at the Islamic University of Madinah, establishing the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah on the divine names and attributes through a methodology that harmonizes textual affirmation (ithbat) with absolute divine transcendence (tanzih). The author contrasts the scriptural approach of the Salaf with the dialectical methods of scholastic theology, critically examining the doctrines of the Jahmiyyah, Mu'tazilah, Ash'ariyyah, and the philosophers, demonstrating how ta'wil and ta'til deviate from sound linguistic principles and authentic revelation.

A work that combines academic depth with clarity of presentation. An indispensable reference for the researcher in aqeedah and the advanced student in the field of the divine names and attributes.

name: Al-Ittibaa' (le suivi) by Ibn Abi al-'Izz al-Hanafi
description_short:
A rare book by commentator of the Tahaawiyyah, Ibn Abi al-'Izz al-Hanafi. This is a refutation of a contemporary Hanafi who wrote about the superiority of the Hanafi madhab against other madhahib with that implies as blameworthy Taqlid. In addition to the perspective of the blame of Taqlid and the obligation to follow the evidence, there are interesting legal discussions. This is even more interesting than the refutation of blind following of the Hanafi school is made by a Hanafi scholar himself.

This book was not reissued for 25 years. This is a copy of the second edition.

name: At-Takfir wa Dawabituhu - Ibrahim ar-Ruhayli
description_short:
This book by Dr. Ibrahim al-Ruhayli addresses one of the most sensitive topics in Islamic theology: takfir — the act of declaring someone a disbeliever. The author outlines the foundational principles and conditions that govern this ruling, drawing from the Qur’an, Sunnah, and statements of the early scholars. He carefully distinguishes between major disbelief, minor errors, and the criteria that must be met before issuing such a grave judgment.

With a balanced and academic tone, the work refutes excesses on both extremes—those who rush to takfir, and those who deny its legitimate application altogether. It is a valuable contribution for students of ‘Aqidah, contemporary issues, and legal methodology.

name: Tamaam Minnah (correction of Fiqh As-Sunnah) - al-Albani
description_short:
Shaykh al-Albani praised Fiqh al-Sunnah by Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq, saying: "Indeed, the book Fiqh al-Sunnah by Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq is among the finest I have come across in its field — due to its excellent organization, clear style, and the absence of the complex expressions that plague many other books of Fiqh." — Tamam al-Minna, p.10

Despite this praise, he pointed out serious issues: use of weak or baseless narrations, mislabeling authentic hadiths as weak, and applying analogy in place of sound texts. He reviewed the early volumes, made detailed corrections, and sent his handwritten notes to the author. "I had hoped for that, but now my hope is lost — as the author reprinted his book in the same blameworthy state..." — Tamam al-Minna, p.6

After 35 years without meaningful correction, Shaykh al-Albani compiled and published his observations in Tamam al-Minna.

This is the official Saudi edition, released with publication rights. May Allah reward the Shaykh for his sincerity and patience.

name: Sharh Usool I'tiqaad Ahlus-Sunna wal-Jamaa'ah - Al-Laalakaa'ee
description_short:
Sharh Usul I'tiqad Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah is one of the most significant and comprehensive sourcebooks in Islamic Creed (Aqidah). Compiled by the 5th-century scholar Imam al-Lalaka'i, this encyclopedic work serves as a primary reference for the beliefs of the Salaf (the early generations of Muslims). Its unique value lies in its methodology: the author meticulously documents the creed through authentic chains of narration (Isnad), quoting the Companions, the Successors (Tabi'un), and the great Imams of the Sunnah.

The book covers all foundational aspects of the Sunni faith, including Tawhid, the Names and Attributes of Allah, the nature of the Quran, the definition of Iman (Faith), and the status of the Sahaba. It is an indispensable resource for any serious student of knowledge or researcher looking to understand the pure, transmitted creed of Islam as it was understood and documented by the early masters of Hadith.

name: Ighaathatul-Lahfaan min Masaayad ash-Shaytaan - ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
One of the foundational works on the purification and reform of the heart, arranged by Ibn al-Qayyim in thirteen chapters that progress from diagnosis to treatment. He begins with the division of hearts into healthy, sick, and dead, establishes the reality and causes of heart disease and its signs, demonstrates that the Quran contains all the heart’s remedies, then addresses the purification and life of the heart — before entering the subject for which the book was written: the plots and traps of Shaytan against humanity. Here Ibn al-Qayyim appears in the role of social reformer — surveying the innovations and deviations that had crept into his society through Shaytan’s scheming: from visiting graves and asking the dead, to singing, riba disguised as trade, and unlawful forms of divorce.

What distinguishes this book is that it is not mere exhortation but a scholarly investigation marshalling evidence from the Quran, the Sunnah, and the statements of the Salaf for every issue, in Ibn al-Qayyim’s distinctive style that fuses proof with spiritual impact. A book read for knowledge and for the heart — indispensable for anyone who wants to know Shaytan’s doors in order to shut them.

description_short:
Whoever contemplates this book, Bahjat Qulub al-Abrar waqurrat 'Uyoon al-Akhyar, fi sharh Jawami' al-Akhbar or Explanation of 99 hadeeth by al-'Allamah Abderrahman As-Sa'di, in its briefness and clarity will notice that it contains all the beneficial sciences: the science of Tawheed (Monotheism), the principles of Faith, the science of adopting and observing the Path towards Allah, as well as the religious, the worldly, and the medical ethics. It also contains the science of jurisprudence and Islamic rulings in all branches of Fiqh: Acts of Worship, Transactions, Marriage Acts, and others, explaining their rulings and origins, the sciences of various methods of reform, the useful topics, directions to bring private and general benefits, religious and worldly, and to repel whatever harm there is.

They are all taken and learned from the words of the Prophet, may Allah’s Prayers and Peace be upon him, in the form of an explanation of the most comprehensive selected Hadiths, as you will discover, and it is all due to the Grace and Mercy of Allah Alone.

name: Al-Ba'ith al-Hathith sharh Ikhtisar Uloom al-Hadith
description_short:
Al-Ba'ith al-Hathith is a seminal contemporary commentary by Sheikh Ahmad Shakir on Ibn Kathir’s Ikhtisar Ulum al-Hadith, which is itself an abridgment of the foundational Muqaddimah of Ibn al-Salah. This work is considered one of the most important gateways to the science of Hadith terminology (Mustalah al-Hadith). Sheikh Ahmad Shakir modernized the study of this discipline by providing a clear, structured, and critically acclaimed explanation that simplifies complex concepts for the modern student of knowledge.

Sheikh Ahmad Shakir added valuable annotations that reflect his deep expertise as a master of Hadith in the 20th century, often updating classical examples with more contemporary scholarly insights. It serves as a comprehensive manual that bridges the gap between classical theory and practical application in the verification of Prophetic traditions. The work remains a standard text for academic and traditional curricula worldwide due to its precision and clarity.

name: Tayyiba an-Nashr fi Qira-aati al-'Ashr - Ibn Al-Jazary
description_short:
In the entire discipline of Quranic recitation sciences, Tayyibat al-Nashr stands as the supreme authority and undisputed benchmark for the Ten Major Readings (al-Qira'at al-'Ashr al-Kubra). For over six centuries, it has occupied the apex of Qira'at scholarship, marking the historical transition from disparate transmission chains to a unified, universally accepted canon. By condensing an entire library of multi-volume reference works and approximately 980 validated chains of oral transmission (turuq) into a singular, meticulously constructed poem of 1,015 verses, this work standardized the highest level of recitation studies and became the defining matrix through which major variants are verified and preserved.

For students of the sacred sciences and aspiring reciters (muqri'un), mastering this text is both the crowning achievement of their curriculum and the mandatory prerequisite for earning the supreme recitational license (al-Ijazah al-Kubra). Through an intricate architecture of alphabetic ciphers (rumuz) and concise phrasing, the poem leads the learner systematically from universal phonological principles (al-usul)—such as assimilation, vowel inflection, and pause rules—to a detailed surah-by-surah examination of lexical variances (farsh al-huruf). Committing this text to memory transforms centuries of oral transmission into an instant, mentally retrievable reference, making it the foundational asset for anyone seeking true authority in the Quranic sciences.

name: Matn ash-Shatibiyyah (fi Qiraat as-Sab'a) - Ash-Shatibi
description_short:
No reader receives an ijazah in the seven Qira’at until he has memorized and mastered it. Al-Shatibi’s “Hirz al-Amani” (d. 590 AH) is the poem upon which the teaching and certification of Qira’at has been built for over eight centuries.

Al-Shatibi’s “Hirz al-Amani” (d. 590 AH) is the undisputed mother-poem of the seven Qira’at, versifying Abu ‘Amr al-Dani’s “al-Taysir fi al-Qira’at al-Sab’” in a lamiyyah of such precision and beauty that master poets and expert readers alike submitted to it. It covers the usul (principles) of the seven Qira’at and their farsh (specific variant readings) surah by surah, and remains the first text no reader can qualify in the Qira’at without memorizing and mastering.

Edition with 100% Harakat (tashkil).

name: Sharh Al-Haa-iyyah, poem by ibn Abi Dawud, by shaykh Fawzaan
description_short:
Al-Manzumah al-Ha'iyyah by Imam Ibn Abi Dawud al-Sijistani (d. 316 AH) is one of the earliest classical poetic primers summarizing the creed of the early pious predecessors (Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah). Composed in concise, memorable verses rhyming with the letter Haa', this poem outlines core Islamic tenets: the uncreated nature of the Holy Quran (Kalamullah), the beatific vision of Allah in the Hereafter (Ru'yatullah), Divine Decree (al-Qadar), the virtue of the Companions, and the eschatological events of the Resurrection.

In this authoritative commentary, Shaykh Dr. Salih al-Fawzan explains the poem line-by-line with direct scriptural evidence from the Quran and authentic Sunnah. Clarifying foundational principles and dispelling historical and contemporary doctrinal misunderstandings, this work provides a structured, accessible guide for students of knowledge building a solid foundation in classical Aqidah.

name: Al-Farq bayna al-Firaq - Al-Baghdaadee (429H)
description_short:
Very interesting book of al-Baghdadi imam (429H) that demonstrates the reality of the 72 dissident sects, list and explain them and defines the group saved among them. 

The book is divided into five chapters; each chapter includes several subchapters, except for the first chapter, which is devoted to the Hadith of the nation’s division, where he indicates that the Prophet referred to the ideological sects.

In the second chapter, he tackled the manner of how the nation have split into seventy-three sects, while he dedicated the third chapter to explaining the concepts of the misguided sects.

In the fourth chapter, he mentioned the sects that are allegedly affiliated with Islam but not from it, and then he concluded the book with the fifth chapter, explaining the characteristics of al-Firqat an-Naajiyah (the Saved Sect).

name: Al-Jaami' li Shu'ab al-Imaan by Imam al-Bayhaqi
description_short:
A comprehensive book on the foundations of faith and its branches, the author of which collected the texts related to the topic, which numbered (10,808) texts, and it is undoubtedly a huge number, including the Elevated (Marfu’) and non-elevated ones, and he arranged this book on the categories of chapters and sections.

This book contains a selection of Hadiths of the Prophet on the branches of faith that numbered seventy-seven branches, the most important of which are the following: adjusting matters of difference between people, being noble and generous, showing mercy to the young and reverence to the elder, the obligation to refrain from excessive food and drinks and avoid what is not permissible from them, desisting the taking of unlawful money, staying away from places of entertainment that contravene Shari’ah, prohibiting what is reprehensible in clothing, uniforms and utensils, believing in the Angels for the sake of getting closer to Almighty Allah, believing in the resurrection after death, having the belief in the obligation to love Almighty Allah, as well as the belief in the necessity to fear Him, seeking knowledge and other great branches of faith. 

In a magnificent edition in 14 volumes, with a full authentication!

name: Al-Faqih wal-Mutafaqqih - al-Khatib al-Baghdadi
description_short:
Al-Faqih wa al-Mutafaqqih is a foundational masterpiece by Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi that outlines the methodology of Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh) and the essential characteristics of both the jurist (Faqih) and the student of law (Mutafaqqih). This work is unique in how it bridges the sciences of Hadith and Fiqh, emphasizing that a true jurist must be grounded in authentic narrations while a Hadith specialist must understand the legal implications of those texts. It serves as a comprehensive manual for the intellectual and ethical development of anyone pursuing the path of legal scholarship.

The book delves into the virtues of Fiqh, the history of the various legal schools, and the tools required for independent reasoning (Ijtihad). Al-Khatib also addresses the practical etiquette of issuing legal verdicts (Ifta), the proper conduct of students toward their teachers, and the methods of academic debate. By gathering numerous reports from the Pious Predecessors and the early Imams, this work provides a timeless framework for maintaining the integrity and rigor of Islamic legal tradition.

name: Tathir ul-I'tiqaad 'an Adraan al-Ilhaad - Imam as-San'ani
description_short:
Treaty of Aqeedah, specifically the Tawhid written by the Reviver of Yemen, Imam as-San'ani (author Subul as-Salam, 1182H). The author said:

"I have felt compelled to write this book “Tat’hir al I'​tiqad min Adran al-Ilhad” (Purification of the Creed from the Impurities of Atheism) after I have seen and learnt that some people were associating other gods with Allah in many cities and villages, in the countries of Yemen, the Levant, Egypt, Najd, Tihama and all the lands of Islam. It is about believing in the dead and in the living who claim knowledge of the unseen, whereas they are simply people of immorality. Indeed, they do not attend the prayer at the mosque with the Muslims and they are nowhere to be seen kneeling or prostrating to Allah; they have no knowledge of the Sunnah or the Quran, and have no concern about the Resurrection or the Reckoning.

So I felt I have to express my denunciation in forbidding what is wrong, and not be one of those who conceal what Allah has enjoined upon us to reveal, in order to help purify people’s belief."

Verified and authenticated edition with the annotations at the bottom of pages of Sheikh Isma'il al-'Ansari, Abdel Muhsin al-'Abbad and Abdel Aziz ar-Rajihi!

name: Nuzhatu-Nadhar by Imam ibn Hajar (harakat)
description_short: Nuzhatu-Nadhar is at the origin an Ibn Hajar's explanation of his own treaty of mustalah al-hadith: Nukhbatu Al Fikar.
description:
This book is a foundational classical masterpiece in the science of Hadith terminology (Mustalah al-Hadith), composed by the undisputed master of Hadith sciences, Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (d. 852 AH). The work is the author's own definitive commentary (Sharh) on his ultra-concise text, Nukhbat al-Fikar. It serves as an essential, universally relied-upon manual for students and scholars alike, mapping out the structural definitions, classifications, and critical evaluation rules of prophetic traditions.

The text is meticulously organized around the core divisions of Hadith narration, detailing categories such as Mutawatir (consecutive), Ahad (isolated), Sahih (authentic), Da'if (weak), and Maudu' (fabricated). Ibn Hajar unpacks his own dense, abbreviated phrasing from the Nukhba, offering precise linguistic definitions and legal criteria for evaluating chains of transmission (asaneed) and textual contents (mutoon). This work remains a core curriculum standard across the Islamic world for mastering the principles of Hadith criticism.

name: Sharh Alfiat ibn Malik - Ibn Uthaymin (3 volumes)
description_short:
Sharh Alfiyyat Ibn Malik is a highly acclaimed, pedagogical explanation of the foundational 1,000-line poem on Arabic grammar and morphology authored by Ibn Malik. In this comprehensive commentary, the renowned scholar Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih al-'Uthaymin demystifies one of the most challenging texts in the Arabic language curriculum, making it accessible to contemporary students.

Originally transcribed from his classroom lectures, the explanation bears the Shaykh's signature educational methodology. He systematically unpacks the complex grammatical rules, breaks down the often-cryptic phrasing of the poetic verses, and provides clear, practical examples. By utilizing an intuitive question-and-answer format, this work ensures genuine comprehension, serving as a vital bridge between classical Arabic linguistics and the modern learner.

This magnificent official edition is presented in 3 volumes, featuring high-quality printing that is pleasant to read, with some harakat (tashkil).

name: Al-Asmaa was-Sifaat lil-Imam al-Bayhaqi
description_short:
This book consists of (1023) documented texts that Imam al-Bayhaqi organized into chapters on the names of Allah and His attributes.

The author begins with the chapter "Establishing the Names of Allah through Evidence from the Quran, Sunnah, and Consensus of the Ummah." This heading reflects the book's overall subject and the author's purpose. The book concludes with "Chapter on Allah's Saying 'And he thought that We would not decree upon him.'"

Throughout his presentation of the documented texts, the author includes Quranic verses as evidence, commentary on some texts, and introductory remarks explaining the purpose of citing them. He also provides hadith authentication.

name: An-Nihayah fi Gharib al-Hadith wa al-Athar - Ibn Athir
description_short:
Al-Nihayah fi Gharib al-Hadith wa al-Athar stands as the definitive lexicon for understanding the rare and complex terminology found within Prophetic narrations and the sayings of the early generations. Authored by Imam Majd al-Din Ibn al-Athir (d. 606 AH), it is widely considered the pinnacle of its genre. Its prestigious status is best summarized by Imam al-Suyuti in Tadrib al-Rawi, who noted: "It is the best of the books of Gharib, the most comprehensive, the most famous now, and the most widely circulated." This monumental work synthesizes centuries of linguistic effort into a single, structured reference, preserving the honor and precision of the Prophetic tradition.

The work is organized alphabetically, making it a highly functional tool for researchers navigating the depths of the Hadith sciences. By clarifying the linguistic nuances of "Gharib" (rare or obscure) words, Ibn al-Athir provides the key necessary to unlock the true intent of the Revelation and the wisdom of the Sahaba. This volume is a cornerstone for any library dedicated to the Arabic heritage, offering a disciplined and honorable methodology that ensures the scholar’s understanding remains grounded in the authentic language of the first generations, as recognized by the greatest masters of the science.

name: Al-Qamous Al-Muheet by Al-Fayruzabi: Classical Arabic Dictionary
description_short:
English Description:

This monumental work remains the gold standard of Arabic lexicography, so influential that its title, "Al-Qamus" (The Ocean), became the very word for "dictionary" in the Arabic language. Imam al-Fayruzabadi (d. 817 AH) revolutionised linguistic study by condensing the vastness of earlier multi-volume lexicons into a precise, single-volume format using a unique shorthand system of symbols. The methodology follows the traditional "rhyme" arrangement, where words are looked up by their final radical letter, making it an indispensable tool for students analyzing classical poetry, Quranic vocabulary, and complex legal terminology.

The significance of this dictionary lies in its unparalleled breadth, covering approximately 60,000 entries while maintaining a sober and academic conciseness. It serves as a linguistic fortress that preserved the purity of the Arabic tongue during a period of transition, offering students a direct link to the vocabulary of the Salaf and classical literature. For anyone serious about mastering the "Language of the Dhad," this work provides the authoritative definitions and morphological insights required to unlock the deepest meanings of the Islamic heritage and the Divine revelation.

name: Aqeedah at-Tawheed by shaykh al-Fawzaan
description_short:
Aqidat al-Tawhid is perhaps the most widely recognized contemporary textbook on Islamic monotheism. Authored by Sheikh Salih al-Fawzan, this book was specifically designed as a comprehensive curriculum for students of knowledge. It offers a structured and simplified approach to the core tenets of the Islamic creed, making it an essential reference for both beginners and advanced readers.

The book is divided into several thematic sections covering the three categories of Tawhid (Rububiyyah, Uluhiyyah, and Asma wa Sifat). It also includes critical chapters on the pillars of faith, the definition of worship, and a detailed warning against the types of Shirk (polytheism) and Bid'ah (innovation) that contradict sound belief. Its logical progression and use of scriptural evidence make it a staple in Islamic educational institutions worldwide.

name: Al-Muntaqa fil-Ahkam ash-Shari'a min Kalam khayr al-Bariyyah
description_short:
Al-Muntaqa fi al-Ahkam al-Shar’iyyah is a masterwork of legal Hadith compiled by Majd ad-Din ibn Taymiyyah (d. 1254 CE), the grandfather of the famous Shaykh al-Islam. It is an elite collection of approximately 5,000 prophetic traditions meticulously selected to serve as the primary evidence for Islamic jurisprudence.

The book is organized by Fiqh chapters, ranging from ritual purification and prayer to trade and criminal law, making it a functional bridge between raw Hadith and practical legal application. Rather than offering personal opinions, the author presents the "proof-texts" found in the Musnad of Ahmad and al-Kutub al-Sittah.

Its status as a premier reference was cemented by Al-Shawkani’s world-renowned commentary, Nayl al-Awtar, which uses Al-Muntaqa as its foundation.

name: Jaami' bayaan al-'Ilm wa Fadluhu - Ibn Abdil Barr (463H)
description_short:
It is a comprehensive book by the great Imam al-Hafidh Ibn Abdul Barr, stressing the meaning of knowledge, the merit of seeking it, and the praise of striving for it and taking care of it. It emphasises the corruption of speaking about the religion of Allah without knowledge, and the prohibition of judgement without proof. The author also spoke about the etiquette of acquiring knowledge and what the scholar and the learner must adhere to in order to achieve it, citing many prophetic Ahadiths and narrations on this subject.

This great book is an integrated educational curriculum for the education of the student and the scholar. It has also preserved a large collection of the sayings of the Salaf scholars in the virtues of knowledge, the etiquette of its students and methods of its acquisition.

name: At-Tib an-Nabawi / Prophetic medicine (authenticated) - Ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
This book is about the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in the medicine that he practiced and prescribed to others. The book addresses multiple aspects of Prophetic medicine, including medications, general health, Islamic spiritual healing (ruqyah), intercessory energy, physical health, and the relationship between body and soul. Ibn al-Qayyim was able to connect the medical principles found in the Prophetic tradition with the medical knowledge of his era, and did not limit himself to mentioning treatments for illnesses, but gave great attention to their prevention.

Ibn al-Qayyim followed a strict methodology in his book, accepting only those hadiths proven to be authentic. He also connected various hadiths to form a clear picture of the Prophetic approach to treatment and prevention. The book "Prophetic Medicine" has played a major role in spreading awareness about the importance of Prophetic medicine, becoming an essential reference for researchers and scholars in this field. The book has also inspired many doctors and researchers to conduct scientific studies on the effectiveness of treatments derived from the Prophetic tradition.

name: Tuhfatul-Mawdud bi Ahkaam al-Mawlud - ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
This book by Imam Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah is an essential guide for Muslim parents covering all aspects of child-rearing from birth through adolescence. This comprehensive work addresses Islamic rulings on naming ceremonies, circumcision, breastfeeding, education, and moral development.

Originally written as a gift for his son upon the birth of a grandchild, Ibn al-Qayyim created this masterpiece when he had no material wealth to offer but knowledge itself. Organized into seventeen chapters, the book traces the child's journey from conception to the afterlife, providing practical guidance rooted in Quranic teachings and prophetic traditions.

Ibn al-Qayyim's balanced scholarly approach presents different opinions, compares evidence, and offers reasoned conclusions without sectarian bias. The book combines jurisprudence with spiritual development and practical parenting advice, making it indispensable for Muslim families seeking to raise righteous children according to Islamic principles.

The book combines jurisprudence with spiritual development and practical parenting advice, making it indispensable for Muslim families seeking to raise righteous children according to Islamic principles.

name: Al-Ibanah 'An Usul ad-Diyanah - Abul-Hasan al-Ash'ari
description_short:
Al-Ibanah serves as a high-stakes intellectual anchor in the history of Islamic thought. Authored by Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who passed away in 324 H, it represents the definitive moment a master of logic fully aligned his methodology with the traditional path of the early generations and the school of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. This is a disciplined, authoritative manifesto that treats the attributes of Allah and the nature of the Quran with a profound sense of urgency. It stands as a landmark of theological stability, designed to shield the community's core identity from the shifting winds of speculative debate.

The work navigates the deepest waters of the creed with an honorable precision, ensuring that the reader feels the weight of history in every sentence. By reclaiming the early tradition through a rigorous and transparent lens, Al-Ash'ari provided a blueprint for orthodoxy that remains a pillar of the Islamic world. It is an essential reference for those seeking to witness a pivotal restoration of classical thought and a return to the pristine roots of the faith.

name: Mulakhkhass al-Fiqhi by shaykh al-Fawzan (harakat)
description_short:
Al-Mulakhas al-Fiqhi is a highly acclaimed and accessible summary of Islamic jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school. Distilled from a series of radio lectures delivered by Sheikh Salih al-Fawzan, the work provides a comprehensive overview of all major chapters of Fiqh, including purification, prayer, zakat, fasting, and hajj, as well as transactions and personal status laws. It is widely regarded as one of the best contemporary primers for those seeking a clear and reliable understanding of practical religious rulings without the burden of complex technical jargon.

The methodology of the book focuses on presenting the most correct opinions based on the Qur'an and the Sunnah, providing the necessary evidence for each ruling in a concise manner. By avoiding lengthy scholarly disputes and focusing on practical application, Sheikh al-Fawzan has created a manual that is equally suited for beginning students of knowledge and laypeople. The logical organization and straightforward language ensure that the reader can easily navigate the complexities of Islamic law and apply its principles to their daily life with confidence.

name: al-Kabaair by Imam Al-Dhahabi - Authentic Version
description_short:
Al-Kabaair by Imam adh-Dhahabi is a well-known work devoted to the major sins, yet it is also a book that has long been subject to confusion due to the spread of a falsely attributed version. The authentic text represents adh-Dhahabi’s genuine scholarly approach, based on transmitted evidence and careful selection, and occupies an important place in ethical and hadith-based literature.

Many scholars of verification have explained that the widely circulated version differs markedly from the Imam’s style, containing weak or fabricated hadiths and a tone foreign to his methodology, leading some to attribute it to a later Sufi author. A commonly cited distinction appears in the chapter on shirk: the spurious version ends with a supplication, whereas the authentic version is shorter and contains no du‘a. This authentic recension restores the book to its proper and reliable form.
searchable_keywords: al-Kabaair by Imam Al-Dhahabi - Authentic Version

name: Al-Mudawanah fi Furoo' al-Malikiyah - Sahnun
description_short:
Al-Mudawwanah is the primary foundational legal corpus of the Maliki school of jurisprudence, holding the most authoritative position in the Madhhab alongside Imam Malik's Muwatta. It contains an extensive collection of practical rulings and derived legal cases across all branches of Islamic law, encapsulating the direct teachings, legal principles, and deduced opinions of Imam Malik ibn Anas (d. 179 AH) as well as the views of his leading companions, substantiated throughout by supporting Prophetic traditions and narrations.

The compilation began with the legal queries gathered by Asad ibn al-Furat, which Imam Abd al-Salam ibn Sa'id al-Tanukhi, famously known as Sahnun (d. 240 AH), took to Egypt to systematically verify and refine with Imam Malik's foremost student, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim al-'Utaqi (d. 191 AH). Sahnun meticulously audited, rearranged, and classified this vast question-and-answer repository into structured thematic chapters and transmitted it to subsequent generations, leading the monumental work to be commonly named after him as Mudawwanat Sahnun.

name: Tarikh al-Khulafa, History of all the caliphs - Suyuti
description_short:
Tarikh al-Khulafa’ by Imam al-Suyuti is a classic chronicle that documents the lives, virtues, and major events of the Muslim caliphs from the era of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq to the later Abbasid rulers. Drawing on reliable historical works, hadith sources, and biographical collections, al-Suyuti presents a concise yet rich narrative that highlights the justice, achievements, and challenges of each ruler, giving students a clear overview of political and spiritual leadership in Islamic history.

The book also includes valuable sections on the merits of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, the qualities of legitimate governance, key historical incidents, and summarized biographies of notable figures. Its accessible style and reliance on early sources have made it a widely studied introduction to Islamic history and leadership.

name: Kitab az-Zuhd by Imam Abd Allah ibn al-Mubaarak
description_short:
A foundational work in the literature of asceticism and heart-softeners, among the earliest ever compiled with connected chains of transmission. Its author, Imam Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak al-Marwazi (d. 181 AH), united in his person what was scattered among others — scholarship, worship, jihad, trade, and generosity — and his book reflects a lived experience, not merely a collection of texts. He arranged hundreds of narrations across chapters of faith and action: from the encouragement of obedience to the condemnation of worldly attachment, from weeping and awe to sincerity, reliance on Allah, and contentment — selecting the soundest hadiths in both chain and text, following his famous principle: "In authentic hadith there is enough to keep you busy from the weak ones."

A book not read once but returned to whenever the heart needs revival, and an indispensable reference for anyone engaged in hadith, spiritual conduct, and self-purification.

This edition in two volumes (1,319 pages), edited under the supervision of Sheikh Sayyid ibn Bayumi, includes an extensive scholarly study on the concept of zuhd among the Salaf and a detailed biography of Ibn al-Mubarak, with comprehensive indexes for researchers. With most of its tashkil.

name: At-Tibyaan fi Adaab Hamalat Al-Qur'an - An-Nawawi
description_short:
A reference to the Holy Qur'an memorizers. This is a valuable, comprehensible, compelling, and concise book that covers the obligatory and recommended etiquette for the reader and teacher of the Holy Qur’an, and what Allah Almighty has prepared for those who recite the Qur’an and those who adhere to it in terms of honour, prestige, and great reward.

The book comprised ten chapters, which list the virtues of reciting the Book of Allah Almighty, and mention the etiquette of reading, and the recommended verses and chapters at specific times and conditions.

Imam As-Sakhawi said: "This is a precious book. You can not do without - especially teachers and reciters of the Quran recitation".

name: Tafsir ibn Kathir authenticated
description_short:
This is the complete Tafseer by ibn Katheer, among the most known and appreciated, that every Muslim must possess.

Shaykh al-Uthaymeen has said "This is a very useful book in the field of commentary on the Koran-based traditions. It is the more trusty, even though it rarely addresses aspects of grammar and eloquence of discourse."

As-Suyuti said: "He (i.e. Ibn Kathir) has written a Tafsir that no one has written anything like it."

Ash-Shawkani said: "He has written the well-known Tafsir, and it is in volumes. He collected it and transmitted the doctrines, news and narrations. It is one of the best books in Tafsir ever."

Ahmed Shakir said in 'Umdat at-Tafsir: "Tafsir of al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir is the best, the most accurate and precise interpretation, and only comes second to Tafsir of Abu Ja'far at-Tabari, the imam of al-Mufassirin."

name: ' Umdat ul-Fiqh by Ibn Qudaama al-Maqdissi (harakat)
description_short:
'Umdat al-Fiqh is a foundational primer in Hanbali jurisprudence, designed by the master jurist Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdisi (d. 620 AH) as the first stage in his world-renowned four-step curriculum for legal mastery. This text focuses strictly on the most authoritative and relied-upon position (mu'tamad) within the school, making it an ideal entry point for students seeking a clear and uncomplicated understanding of Hanbali law. It covers all the essential chapters of worship and transactions with a precision that reflects the author’s commitment to clarity and legal honor.

What distinguishes this manual from other introductory primers is that Ibn Qudamah utilizes a curated selection of hadiths and athars for every major ruling, ensuring the student is immediately connected to the scriptural roots of the law. By rooting each legal branch in prophetic evidence, the author fosters a deep respect for the Sunnah while providing a structured framework for practical application. name: Taysir al-'Allaam sharh 'Umdatul-'Ahkaam - Al-Basaam
description_short:
Taysir al-'Allam is widely considered one of the most accessible and pedagogically sound contemporary commentaries on 'Umdat al-Ahkam. The original text, compiled by the great Hadith master Imam Abdul Ghani al-Maqdisi (d. 600 AH), consists of the most authentic Prophetic narrations related to legal rulings, sourced exclusively from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih al-Muslim. Sheikh Abdullah al-Bassam (d. 1423 AH) provides a masterly explanation that bridges the gap between complex jurisprudential debates and the needs of the modern student.

The methodology of this commentary is highly organized: for each Hadith, the author provides a linguistic breakdown of difficult terms, an overview of the general meaning, and a numbered list of the jurisprudential rulings (Fawa'id) derived from the text. Al-Bassam avoids overly technical sectarian disputes, focusing instead on the strongest evidence within the Hanbali school and the broader consensus of the scholars. It is an ideal textbook for anyone seeking to master Fiqh al-Hadith (Jurisprudence of Prophetic Traditions) with clarity and precision.

description_short:
One of the most important classical works addressing the question of faith according to the methodology of Ahl al-Sunnah, composed by al-Qadi Abu Ya'la Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hanbali (d. 458 AH), one of the great Hanbali jurists of the Abbasid era. The book treats faith with rigorous scholarship grounded in Quranic and prophetic texts and the understanding of the Salaf, presenting the Sunni approach to refuting the claims of the Jahmiyyah, Mu'tazilah, and Murji'ah. The author clarifies the meaning of faith among the Companions and the Imams, explaining that it encompasses belief, statement, and action.

This is a revised and expanded edition, meticulously edited by Saud bin Abd al-Aziz al-Khilf and published by Dar al-Asimah with premium typesetting on high-quality chamois paper. The work speaks to the student of knowledge seeking to understand Sunni doctrine on faith and to the scholar researching authentic refutations of the doubts raised by those who diverge from orthodox belief.

name: As-Sunnah by Imam al-Marwazi (al-Maruzi) (294H)
description_short:
As one of the most vital theological sourcebooks from the golden age of Hadith codification, this classical masterpiece preserves the foundational creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah through raw, unbroken chains of transmission. Its author, Al-Imam Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi (d. 294 AH), was a towering contemporary of al-Bukhari and Muslim, celebrated across the Islamic world for his unmatched memory and strict adherence to early textual traditions. The volume serves as an authentic, frontline defense of Orthodox Sunni theology, making it an irreplaceable reference for students of knowledge tracing the early preservation of the Islamic consensus (Ijma).

The book operates entirely on the methodology of the Muhaddithun, presenting the creed through a systematic arrangement of Quranic verses, Prophetic traditions, and historical statements from the Sahaba and Tabi'in rather than abstract philosophy. Al-Marwazi focuses heavily on the highly contested issues of his era, detailing the definition of faith (Iman), the obligation of adhering to the Sunnah, and the total rejection of early deviant sects like the Kharijites and Murji'ites. By documenting these early narrations, the text provides a clear, unfiltered blueprint of how third-century Hijri scholars consolidated orthodox belief.

name: Subul as-Salaam : sharh Buloogh al-Maraam (As-San'ani)
description_short:
Subul as-Salam is Imam al-San‘ani’s renowned commentary on Ibn Hajar’s Bulugh al-Maram, praised for its balance between solid Hadith analysis and accessible fiqh explanation. Al-San‘ani clarifies the meanings of each hadith, outlines the legal rulings derived from them, and compares scholarly positions with concise reasoning, making it one of the clearest pathways into understanding evidences used in Islamic jurisprudence. Its structured style helps students move from hadith text to applied fiqh without being overwhelmed.

The commentary has remained popular in traditional study circles because it provides enough depth to train the student in evidence-based reasoning while remaining readable and purposeful. For learners who want a dependable explanation that shows how rulings are built upon sound hadith, Subul as-Salam is considered one of the most suitable companions to Bulugh al-Maram.

name: Dawaabit Takfeer al-Mu'ayyeen - prefaced by al-Fawzan
description_short:
This book is a contemporary theological study analyzing the regulations for individual excommunication (takfir al-mu'ayyan) according to Ibn Taymiyyah, Muhammad bin Abd al-Wahhab, and the Najdi reform scholars. The work features an introductory foreword by Sheikh Saleh al-Fawzan, who commends the author, Rashid bin Abi al-Ula al-Rashid, for his balanced approach to this sensitive topic. The text serves as an academic guide to understanding the boundaries of orthodox Sunni theology while avoiding both extremism (ghuluw) and laxity (irja').

The text is organized into comparative chapters examining the strict conditions (shurut) and legal impediments (mawani') required before applying a judgment of disbelief to a specific person. Al-Rashid evaluates critical principles such as the establishing of clear proof (iqamat al-hujjah), the excuse of ignorance (al-udhr bil-jahl), misinterpretation (ta'wil), and coercion (ikrah). By directly analyzing classical legal verdicts, the author outlines a precise framework that distinguishes general doctrinal rulings from individual excommunication.

name: Tafsir al-Baghawy (Ma'alim at-Tanzil)
description_short:
Ma'alim al-Tanzil, widely known as Tafsir al-Baghawi, is a landmark classical Quranic commentary authored by the renowned Shafi'i scholar and hadith master Imam Muhyi al-Sunnah al-Baghawi (d. 516 AH). He transmits the exegesis of the Companions, the Tabi'in, and those after them alongside prophetic hadiths and narrations that are predominantly authentic, in a clear style free from obscurity and forced interpretation. When Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah was asked which tafsir is closest to the Quran and Sunnah — al-Zamakhshari, al-Qurtubi, or al-Baghawi — he answered: the safest from innovation and weak hadiths is al-Baghawi.

This tafsir stands out for its moderation in size — a medium-length work, neither excessively long nor inadequately short — and for the purity of its athari methodology, making it a lasting reference for the student who wants a reliable tafsir with a sound approach and accessible presentation. Its author earned the title "Muhyi al-Sunnah" (Reviver of the Sunnah) for his exceptional care with hadith and narration across all his works.

name: Fath al-Majid li Sharh Kitab at-Tawhid - Abderrahman ibn Hasan Aal Sheikh
description_short: This work is one of the most authoritative classical commentaries on Kitab at-Tawhid, written by a leading scholar from the family of Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab. It explains the chapters of the original text with clarity and firmness, grounding each issue in Quranic evidence, Prophetic hadith, and the understanding of the early scholars. The author addresses both the foundations of tawhid and the practical manifestations of shirk, major and minor, as they appear in belief, speech, and action.

name: Iqtidaa as-Sirat al-Mustaqim - Ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
Sheikh Al-Islam ibn Taymiyyah has explained in this book that opposing the infidels (Kuffar) is a great rule of the Shari’ah, which has many branches, and a comprehensive principle of its origins with many branches; but some people were astonished and bemused by it and so ruled it out, due to its contrast with the custom upon which they were brought up.

Sheikh Al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, stated that many people were plagued by this type of ignorance, and that he wrote what he had witnessed at that time. He collected all the evidence and the words of scholars, and examined the narrations from many books regarding this issue.

The excellent work of Shaykh al-Islam ibn Taymiyyah, in one volume with full Tahqiq.

name: Matn Al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah and Matn Tuhfat ul-Atfal (Tajwid)
description_short:
This edition compiles two renowned poetic texts on Tajweed for beginners: "Al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah" and "Tuhfat al-Atfal". These works cover essential Tajweed rules for novice Quran readers and have garnered significant attention from scholars due to their simplicity.

The new edition features:

- Updated layout and font

- Thorough verification process

- Comparison of multiple manuscripts

- Footnotes documenting textual variations

- Features to aid Quran students and memorizers

Prepared by Dr. Yahya Al-Ghawthani, this edition offers a comprehensive and accessible resource for those studying Tajweed, incorporating various manuscripts and commentaries to ensure accuracy and usefulness.

name: at-Tuhfatus-Sanniya bi Sharh al-Muqaddima al-Ajrumiya
description_short:
This is a simple and accessible explanation of al-Ajroomiyyah, and ready to grasp easily through its numerous questions and exercises. The author intended to facilitate the understanding of “Al-Muqaddimah al-Ajrumiyyah” by the young disciples, with an easy explanation, adding a lot of exercises and examples that firmly establish the grammar and rules (of Arabic Grammar) in the minds of the students.

He has, therefore, provided a great service to the language of the Noble Qur’an, combining between the rules and application. This explanation is generally used by beginners.

name: Lisaan al-'Arab by bin Mandhoor (the reference dictionary)
description_short:
Lisan al-Arab is the undisputed monarch of Arabic dictionaries and a monumental encyclopedia of the language. Compiled by Jamal al-Din Ibn Manzur (d. 711 AH), it is a vast synthesis of five major classical lexicons, including Al-Sihah and Tahdhib al-Lugha. It does not merely define words; it preserves the very soul of the Arabic tongue by providing an exhaustive record of vocabulary, grammar, and linguistic history as found in the Quran, Hadith, and pre-Islamic poetry.

The work is a testament to the intellectual honor of the Islamic tradition, meticulously documenting the nuances of the "language of the Revelation." Ibn Manzur organized the entries according to the "final-letter" system, making it a functional masterpiece for poets, scholars, and jurists alike. This dictionary serves as an indestructible bridge to the classical past, ensuring that the precision and nobility of Arabic expression are maintained through rigorous academic verification and deep literary reverence.

name: Al-I'tisaam of Imaam ash-Shaatibee (790H)
description_short:
Al-I‘tisam by Imam al-Shatibi (d. 790H) is one of the most influential classical works written on innovation (bid‘ah) and adherence to the Prophetic Sunnah. The author, a foremost Andalusian scholar of the Maliki school, explains the principles distinguishing authentic Sunnah from newly introduced practices in religion, drawing upon Qur’anic proofs, Hadith evidence, and the methodology of the early generations.

Through detailed analysis, al-Shatibi defines the concept of innovation, its categories, and its dangers to faith and society. The book also examines the causes that lead people to deviate from the Sunnah and the importance of collective unity upon revealed guidance.

name: Usool as-Sunnah by Imam ibn Abi Zamaneen (399H)
description_short:
A valuable work among the most important compositions expounding the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-al-Jama'ah, authored by Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Zaminin al-Andalusi (d. 399 AH), one of the foremost Maliki scholars and hadith masters of al-Andalus. The book gathers a collection of hadiths and reports elucidating the foundational principles of Sunni belief — what the early Muslims held and affirmed regarding numerous matters including belief in divine decree, punishment in the grave, the Basin, the Balance, the Path, the creation of Paradise and Hell, obedience and disobedience, intercession, and the vision of Allah on the Day of Judgment, and other essentials of doctrine.

This work stands as one of the most significant testimonies to the unity of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-al-Jama'ah's creed across centuries and lands, demonstrating that this Andalusian imam followed the same Sunni path as scholars of the Islamic East. Major scholars praised him, including Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, Imam al-Dhahabi, Ibn 'Afiif, and others, considering him among the great authorities in knowledge, hadith, and jurisprudence.

name: Al-Rad 'ala l-Zanadiqa wal-Jahmiya - Imam Ahmad
description_short:
Famous risala of Imam Ahmad rebuttal heretics innovators and Jahmiyya. The importance of this book lies in two matters: in its author, and in its subject matter.

First: The author of the book is Ahmed Ibn Hanbal, who is considered an Imam and one of the most important scholars of Ahlus Sunnah wal Jama’ah.

Second: The subject matter of the book deals with the fundamentals of the religion (Usul Ad-Din), the beliefs of Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah and the refutation of the Jahmiyyah’s specious arguments and doubtful matters.

Third: The author’s argumentation with rational evidence in this book

Fourth: The book presents many Qur’anic Verses that the heretics thought were contradictory

Fifth: The Scholars’ praise and approval of the book

This book was written by Imam Ahmed Ibn Hanbal in prison, as stated by a group of scholars, including: Salih Ibn Ahmed Ibn Hanbal, Abu Ya’la al-Hanbali, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah.

Second: The subject matter of the book deals with the fundamentals of the religion (Usul Ad-Din), the beliefs of Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah and the refutation of the Jahmiyyah’s specious arguments and doubtful matters.

Third: The author’s argumentation with rational evidence in this book

Fourth: The book presents many Qur’anic Verses that the heretics thought were contradictory

Fifth: The Scholars’ praise and approval of the book

This book was written by Imam Ahmed Ibn Hanbal in prison, as stated by a group of scholars, including: Salih Ibn Ahmed Ibn Hanbal, Abu Ya’la al-Hanbali, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah.

name: Ar-Rad 'ala al-Jahmiyyah - Imam 'Uthman ad-Darimi (280H)
description_short:
Kitab al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyyah by the renowned 3rd-century Hadith master and traditionist Imam Abu Sa'id Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi (d. 280 AH) is one of the earliest and most foundational primary sources in Sunni Athari theological polemics. Composed during the height of the classical creedal debates, this seminal treatise was written to systematically refute the negating doctrines (ta'til) and figurative re-interpretations championed by Jahm ibn Safwan, Bishr al-Marisi, and their adherents regarding the Divine Names and Attributes.

Relying upon explicit Quranic verses, prophetic traditions with connected chains (asānīd), and statements of the early Companions and Successors, al-Darimi rigorously establishes core tenets of early orthodoxy. Widely cited and praised by major later authorities—such as Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim, and Imam al-Dhahabi—this foundational work remains an essential historical and theological reference for scholars of early Islamic thought, researchers in sect typology (firaq), and students of classical Aqidah.

name: Khalq Af'aal al-'Ibaad by Imam al-Bukhari
description_short:
Among the Salaf books written to refute the people of innovation is that of Imam al-Bukhari, al-Khalq Af'al Ibad, a refutation to Jahmiya and beliefs.

The book began by mentioning the sayings of the Sunnis on the Jahmiyyah sect and the ruling of the takfir (Apostasy) on those who embrace its ideology.

In the second chapter, the author discussed the issue of the creation of actions and proved that the actions of Man are created, thereby replying against the Jahmiyyah sect in this subject.

The book is one of the basic books that have preserved for us a large collection of sayings of the predecessors among the Companions and the followers regarding the Jahmiyyah sect and those who adopt their statements; it also showed us the best way to respond to the people of heresy.

The book includes many comments by the author on the referential texts, and that he not only narrates the texts, but also had replies against the suspicions cast by the Jahmiyyah.

name: Ash-Shamaa-il al-Muhammadiyyah - at-Tirmidhee (authenticated)
description_short:
Al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyah, by Imam al-Tirmidhi, is a foundational reference detailing the physical and moral characteristics of the Prophet Muhammad. Spanning 56 thematic chapters and over 400 narrations, the work documents the Prophet’s appearance, habits, and daily conduct to provide a definitive model for emulation.

Al-Tirmidhi showcases his immense erudition by combining prophetic traditions with reports from the Companions. He enriches the text with critical analysis, clarifying complex linguistic terms and authenticating chains of narration. This structured blend of biography and legalistic Hadith scholarship has made the Shama'il an indispensable classic for understanding the prophetic persona.

name: Zaad al-Ma'aad of Ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
“Zaad al-Ma’ad fi Hadiy Khair al-‘Ibad” is a precious book, by Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, that is rarely matched. Rather, it is unique in its field. The author, indeed, has made it a collection if all that is related to the Prophet, may Allah’s Prayers and Peace be upon him, be it a saying, a deed, or a report.

The book is about the life of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in every sense of the word. It discusses the biography of the Prophet on its surface, but the author adorned this sublime biography with various subjects: jurisprudence, issues of Halal and Haram, ethics, monotheism and guidance.

The best biography of the Prophet, sallallaahu 'alayhi wa sallam, according to Shaykh al-Uthaymeen.

name: Zaad al-Ma'aad of Ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
“Zaad al-Ma’ad fi Hadiy Khair al-‘Ibad” is a precious book, by Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, that is rarely matched. Rather, it is unique in its field. The author, indeed, has made it a collection if all that is related to the Prophet, may Allah’s Prayers and Peace be upon him, be it a saying, a deed, or a report.

The book is about the life of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in every sense of the word. It discusses the biography of the Prophet on its surface, but the author adorned this sublime biography with various subjects: jurisprudence, issues of Halal and Haram, ethics, monotheism and guidance.

The best biography of the Prophet, sallallaahu 'alayhi wa sallam, according to Shaykh al-Uthaymeen.

name: Sharh Qatru Nadaa wa ballu as-sadaa by ibn Hishaam (761H)
description_short:
This book is a timeless classical masterpiece in Arabic grammar and syntax (Nahw), authored by the illustrious grammarian Al-Imam Jamal al-Din Ibn Hisham al-Ansari (d. 761 AH). The work is the author's own definitive and comprehensive commentary (Sharh) on his highly celebrated introductory primer, Qatr al-Nada. Universally recognized for its pedagogical brilliance, it serves as a crucial mid-level textbook across the Islamic world for students transitioning from basic grammar concepts to advanced linguistic studies.

Ibn Hisham systematically breaks down the structures of the Arabic language, meticulously detailing parts of speech, the rules of inflection (i'rab), indeclinable words (bina'), and the specific grammatical agents (awamil) that govern sentences. The book stands out for its clarity of expression, the logical grouping of syntactic rules, and its extensive usage of textual evidences, drawing heavily from Quranic verses, prophetic traditions, and classical Arabic poetry. With Sheikh Muhyiddin's accompanying printed commentary, students also gain an exhaustive grammatical parsing of every single poetic line of evidence (I'rab al-Shawahid), making it the most complete and accessible version for mastering classical Arabic.
searchable_keywords: Sharh Qatru Nadaa wa ballu as-sadaa by ibn Hishaam (761H)

name: Riyad as-Salihin by Imam an-Nawawi
description_short:
Riyadh al-Salihin is perhaps the most universally accepted and widely read Hadith collection in the Islamic world after the Sahihayn. Compiled by the great Imam al-Nawawi (d. 676 AH), this work remains an indispensable cornerstone of any Islamic library, whether for individual study or family reading. It serves as a masterpiece of spiritual and ethical curation, containing nearly 1,900 narrations meticulously organized into chapters that guide the believer through every facet of life—from the inward sincerity of the heart to the outward excellence of social conduct.

The collection is particularly renowned for its emphasis on "Virtuous Character," highlighting narrations that encourage honor, duty, and the pursuit of excellence (Ihsan). Imam al-Nawawi intentionally selected authentic reports that offer a clear scriptural roadmap for those seeking to embody noble traits and moral integrity, avoiding highly technical or obscure reports to ensure the text remains accessible. It is a vital manual for self-purification (Tazkiyah), providing timeless guidance on how to model one's life after the Prophetic example.

name: Jaami' al-'Uloom wal-Hikam fi sharh 50 hadeeth - ibn Rajab
description_short:
Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam est largement considéré comme le commentaire le plus profond et le plus complet jamais écrit sur les Quarante Hadiths de l'Imam al-Nawawi. Rédigé par le maître du Hadith et de la spiritualité, Al-Hafiz Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali (m. 795 AH), cet ouvrage élargit la collection originale à cinquante Hadiths, choisissant ceux qui représentent la « Parole Synthétique » (Jawami' al-Kalim) du Prophète ﷺ. C'est un chef-d'œuvre qui fait le pont entre les sciences techniques du Hadith et la profonde sagesse pratique du cœur.

Ce commentaire se distingue par sa profondeur ; Ibn Rajab ne se contente pas d'expliquer les sens linguistiques, il explore les implications juridiques, l'essence spirituelle et les cadres éthiques de chaque narration. Il met l'accent sur les traits de sincérité, d'honneur et la recherche de la vertu, constituant ainsi une feuille de route pour ceux qui souhaitent aligner leur caractère sur le modèle prophétique.

name: Fiqh al-Ad'iyati wal-Adhkaar - Abdel Razaaq al-Badr
description_short:
Fiqh al-Ad'iyah wal-Adhkar is a transformative contemporary study that moves beyond the simple memorization of prayers to explore the "Fiqh"—the deep, internal comprehension—of spiritual communication. Sheikh Abdurrazzaq al-Badr provides a structured journey into the psychological and theological foundations of Dhikr, emphasizing that true remembrance is an act of the heart before it is a movement of the tongue. The text focuses on the prerequisites of sincerity, presence, and the pursuit of a virtuous character, turning the daily routine of supplication into a conscious path toward spiritual honor and intellectual clarity.

The work is distinguished by its meticulous grounding in primary sources, explaining the specific contexts and linguistic nuances of the Prophetic tradition. By analyzing the "why" behind each invocation, the author bridges the gap between ritual habit and profound spiritual experience. This volume is an essential reference for students and seekers alike, offering a roadmap for purifying the soul and refining the heart through a systematic and evidence-based approach to worship that remains firmly anchored in the heritage of the Salaf.

name: Ijmaa' al-A'immah al-Arba'ah wa ikhtilaafuhum - ibn Hubayrah (560H)
description_short:
Ijma' al-A'immah al-Arba'ah wa Ikhtilafuhum (frequently published under the title Ikhtilaf al-A'immah al-Ulama') by the Hanbali vizier and scholar Yahya ibn Hubayrah (d. 560 AH) is a classic foundational manual in comparative Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh Muqaran). The text represents the dedicated legal treatise extracted from his monumental Hadith commentary, Al-Ifsah 'an Ma'ani al-Sihah, which he composed under the commentary of the prophetic tradition: "Whomever Allah desires good for, He grants him comprehension in religion."

Structured methodically according to standard legal chapters—from purification and prayer to commercial contracts and judicial rulings—the work first identifies the core legal points of consensus (ijma' or ittifaq) shared among the four Sunni Imams (Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal). Following the agreed-upon positions, Ibn Hubayrah systematically enumerates the points of divergence (ikhtilaf), summarizing each school's stances with balance and clarity. This accessible layout makes it a standard reference for students of comparative law, muftis, and researchers studying early legal methodology.

name: Mukhtasar Sahih Muslim
description_short:
This work is the most celebrated abridgment of Sahih Muslim, expertly compiled by the 7th-century scholar Imam al-Mundhiri. He carefully selected the primary Hadiths from the original collection, removing repetitive chains of narration and similar reports to provide a streamlined experience for the reader. This preservation of the core Prophetic traditions allows both students and laypeople to engage with the authentic narrations of Imam Muslim in a more accessible and concise format.

The methodology of the Mukhtasar focuses on thematic organization, where the author retains the essential chapters to ensure the legal and spiritual context remains intact. By presenting the text of the Hadith without the extensive scholarly apparatus found in the full collection, Imam al-Mundhiri facilitates easier memorization and rapid reference. It serves as an essential bridge for those transitioning from introductory primers to the major canonical works of Sunnah.

This edition is fully voweled (100% harakat).

name: Mukhtasar Sahih al-Bukhari
description_short:
Al-Tajrid al-Sarih is arguably the most famous and widely accepted abridgment of the most authentic book of Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari. Imam al-Zubaydi’s primary objective was to make the Prophetic traditions accessible to a broader audience by "stripping" (Tajrid) the collection of its repetitive narrations and lengthy chains of transmitters (Isnad). By retaining only the core text of the Hadiths and citing the primary Companion who narrated them, he successfully condensed the massive multi-volume original into a single, manageable volume without losing the essence of the Prophetic message.

The book preserves the original thematic structure and chapter headings of Sahih al-Bukhari, allowing readers to navigate through legal rulings, ethics, and spiritual guidance with ease. It is an indispensable resource for students of knowledge and general readers who wish to study the authentic traditions of the Prophet ﷺ without the technical complexities of scholarly cross-referencing. This work has remained a staple in Islamic libraries for centuries due to its clarity and practical utility.

name: ad-Daa wad-Dawaae (al-Jawab al-Kaafi) - ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
This is a book in preaching and guidance, as well as beliefs and Shari’ah Law. Ibn al-Qayyim works deals, within its chapters, with the subject of the purification of the soul and its evaluation, according to the Islamic perspective, where the reader travels between its chapters, passing through advice and reprimand. The book deals with the ills of the evil inciting self, showing its flaws and shortcomings, and showing the power of lusts over it; at the same time warning against the tricks and schemes of Satan in leading the soul into sins and misdeeds, and relying on the life of the world and its adornment.

Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyyah wrote this book in response to a man who asked him the following question: "What the scholars say with regard to a man tried by a tribulation, and learned that if it continued it would corrupt both his world and the Hereafter? He has worked hard to get rid of it by all means, but unfortunately he could not, what can he do to get rid of it? May Allah’s mercy be upon he who could help one who is afflicted with a tribulation and Allah helps the servant as long as he helps his brother. Advise us may Allah reward you." The Imam, may Allah have mercy on him, replied by writing this book.

name: Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah
description_short:
Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah is one of the books of Hadith of the Prophet. It is among the Hadith books of valuable consideration by Ahlu Sunnah wal Jamaa’ah. In addition to Sahih Ibn Hibban and Al-Mustadrak ‘Ala Sahihayn by Al-Hakim An-Naisaburi, it is deemed one of the most important books that were written on Al-Sahih Al-Mujarrad (the Absolute Authentic) after the two authentic books of Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
The original title of the book is: Mukhtasar al-mukhtasar min al-musnad as-Sahih ‘an An-Nabiyy bi-naqli al-‘Adl ‘ani Al-‘Adl Mawsoulan ilayhe min Ghayri Qat’in fi Athnaa’ al-Isnaad wa la jurhin fi Naaqili al-Akhbar (The Summary of the Abridged version from the Authentic Narrations of the Prophet, supported by a continuous linkage of upright narrators without any breaks in the chain or any narrators that have been deemed unreliable). It is made clear to us from the book that its author Ibn Khuzaymah had stipulated that he reported only what he had of authentic Hadiths, with trustworthy narrators and uninterrupted chain of transmission.

Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah occupies a high position among the books of Hadith; the importance of this book appears through the authenticity of its Hadiths, the scholarly position of its author and its high degree in Islamic sciences. Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah is considered the most correct of the seven authentic books after the two authentic books by Al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Al-Suyuti said: “Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah is more authentic on the whole than Ṣaḥiḥ Ibn Hibban because Ibn Khuzaymah investigated his narrations very thoroughly, to the degree that he refused to accept a narration if there exist the slightest doubt about its authenticity.”

name: Sayd al-Khaatir - Imam Ibn al Jawzi (Captured Thoughts)
description_short:
Said al-Khatir by Ibn al-Jawzi represents the intellectual essence of a master scholar who recognized that thoughts are fleeting and must be captured before they vanish. Understanding the ephemeral nature of inspiration, he dedicated over twenty years to recording precious insights that deserved preservation.

This unique work emerged from Ibn al-Jawzi's mature life experience as scholar, teacher, and preacher. He systematically documented daily reflections, creating an intellectual journey that encompasses all aspects of life. The book contains sermons, wisdom, spiritual refinements, counsel, literature, and diverse scholarly insights.

Written in an easy yet sophisticated style, it presents profound thoughts in accessible language without sacrificing eloquence. Like varied pearls strung together by a master craftsman, these reflections form a cohesive work that delights both soul and mind, offering readers timeless wisdom drawn from lived experience.

name: Talbis Ibliss by Imam Ibn al-Jawzi
description_short:
Talbis Iblis is one of the most famous and enduring works of Imam Ibn al-Jawzi (d. 597 AH), serving as a comprehensive spiritual and intellectual mapping of how the Devil (Iblis) misleads various groups of people. Writing with the precision of a scholar and the insight of a psychologist, Ibn al-Jawzi examines how different segments of society—including scholars, worshippers, ascetics, and the general public—can fall into error by thinking they are doing good while actually deviating from the Prophetic path. The book is a masterpiece of self-rectification, designed to expose the subtle traps of vanity, innovation (Bid'ah), and misplaced zeal that can corrupt even the most pious intentions.

The work is divided into thematic chapters where the author meticulously analyzes the "deceptions" specific to each group. He critiques philosophical deviations, the extremes of certain Sufi practices, and the scholarly pride that can lead to a neglect of action. By grounding his arguments in the Quran, the Sunnah, and the biographies of the Salaf, Ibn al-Jawzi provides the reader with a "spiritual shield" to identify and avoid the whispers of Iblis. It remains an essential read for anyone seeking to purify their intention and ensure their practice of Islam remains aligned with the authentic, balanced methodology of the early generations.
searchable_keywords: Talbis Ibliss by Imam Ibn al-Jawzi

description_short:
Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad Ibn Taymiyyah -may ALLAH be pleased with him- was asked about the Word of ALLAH the Almighty: {O men! Worship your Lord}, What is worship and what are its branches? Does worship encompass the whole religion or not? What is the reality of worship? Is worship the highest degree or are there higher degrees above it? Give us the answer.

This epistle is the answer of the Sheikh -may ALLAH be merciful to him-.

This epistle is the answer of the Sheikh -may ALLAH be merciful to him-.

name: Al-Fawaaid by ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
A book of wisdom and exhortation unlike any other, in which Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751 AH) gathered scattered benefits collected over time from his reflections on the Quran, the Sunnah, and the states of the soul and heart. He often takes a verse or part of a verse and interprets it in a way no one before him had, or seizes upon a hadith or even a single word from it and draws out meanings of striking depth and rare wisdom. He moves between iman, repentance, knowing Allah, the reality of this world and the next, character, and the virtues of the surahs — each benefit a world unto itself, requiring nothing before or after it.

This book differs from “Bada’i’ al-Fawa’id” by the same author: the Bada’i’ is dominated by linguistic and grammatical investigations, while al-Fawa’id is devotional and faith-centered at its core — a book that touches the soul and the mind alike, suited for reading at any time. Among the most beautiful and most heart-reaching of everything Ibn al-Qayyim left behind.

name: Miftaah Dar as-Sa'aadah of ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
description_short:
Miftah Dar al-Sa‘adah by Imam Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H) is one of his most profound and reflective works, blending theology, spirituality, and the philosophy of knowledge. In it, the author explores the relationship between knowledge (‘ilm), will (iradah), and true happiness (sa‘adah) — demonstrating that genuine felicity lies in understanding Allah’s guidance and acting upon it with sincerity.

The book delves into the virtues of knowledge, the superiority of revelation over human reasoning, and the ways in which sound understanding leads to moral and spiritual excellence. It is a vast ocean of insight, filled with Qur’anic reflections, hadith analysis, and philosophical reasoning framed within Ibn al-Qayyim’s uniquely eloquent style.

name: Sarih as-Sunnah - Aqidah of Imam ibn Jarir at-Tabari (310H)
description_short:
A concise creedal treatise in which the Imam of the mufassirin and historians, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari (d. 310 AH), declares his creed and the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-al-Jama'ah on the matters disputed in his time. He addresses five major questions: the Quran as the uncreated speech of Allah, the believers' vision of their Lord on the Day of Judgment, the creation of human actions, the standing and ranking of the Companions, and faith as something that increases and decreases. He wrote it in the context of serious accusations leveled against him by some of his contemporaries, intending to clarify his position with unmistakable frankness.

This edition was critically edited by Prof. Dr. Tariq ibn Sa'id al-Qahtani, Professor of Aqeedah at the Islamic University of Madinah, and is the first to be established on six distinct manuscripts, four of which have never been used in any previous edition. It also includes an introductory study by the editor entitled "Juhd al-Mubtadi fi al-Ta'rif bi-I'tiqad wa-Kitab al-Tabari," introducing the Imam's creed and the context in which the treatise was composed.

name: Explanation of Sharh as-Sunnah by al-Barbahari - al-Fawzan
description_short:
This book is a highly celebrated, contemporary commentary (Sharh) on Sharh al-Sunnah, the landmark classical treatise on orthodox Sunni creed composed by the 4th-century scholar Imam al-Barbahari (d. 329 AH). The commentator, Sheikh Saleh al-Fawzan—a prominent member of Saudi Arabia's Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Ifta—delivers a lucid, line-by-line explanation designed to clarify the foundational tenets of the Athari creed for modern readers.

The original text by Imam al-Barbahari is famous for its uncompromising stance on preserving the prophetic tradition and the methodology of the Companions. In Ithaf al-Qari, Sheikh al-Fawzan systematically unpacks the condensed, authoritative assertions of the classical text, providing textual evidences from the Quran and Sunnah. The commentary addresses critical theological matters, including the divine attributes, the nature of faith (Iman), the rights of Muslim rulers, and the absolute prohibition of religious innovations (bida'). It serves as a vital curricular standard for students looking to understand early Sunni polemics against deviant historical factions.

name: Sharh Shudhoor adh-Dhahab li Ibn Hishaam
description_short:
Step up to a higher tier of classical Arabic mastery. Sharh Shudur al-Dhahab ("The Explanation of the Splinters of Gold") is Imam Ibn Hisham’s rigorous, upper-intermediate masterpiece. It is specifically engineered for students who have outgrown introductory grammar manuals and need to conquer advanced syntax. In the traditional curriculum of Arabic philology, this text serves as the crucial academic gateway, providing the baseline strength required to unlock the final heights of Alfiyyat Ibn Malik.

Rather than repeating surface-level definitions, Ibn Hisham dissects the underlying mechanics of the language—unraveling complex inflectional variations (i'rab), obscure declension exceptions, and intricate particle interactions. This edition features the unmatched, brilliant notes of Sheikh Muhammad Muhyiddin Abdul Hamid. His analytical footnotes actively break down the densest reasoning and provide an exhaustive, word-by-word grammatical parsing of the challenging classical poetry lines used as evidence (I'rab al-Shawahid).

name: Da'if al-Jaami' by Shaykh al-Albani
description_short:
Da'if al-Jaami 'Muhaddith of this century, Shaykh al-Albaanee, in one big volume, beautiful edition Allahi Berik. Here is the story of this book:

Imam As-Suyuti collected the brief Hadith narrations, reported on the authority of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and arranged them in alphabetical order, taking into account the beginning of the Hadith.

He named the book "Al-Jami’ As-Saghir" which is an abbreviation of his other book "Al-Jami’ Al-Kabir Jam’ Al-Jawami’" and put symbols for the names of the scholars who extracted and authenticated the Hadiths to prevent lengthening, placing the symbols in a list at the beginning of the book, to be reviewed. The listed Hadiths amounted to 10031 Hadiths.

Then Al-Nabahani went on to add many Hadiths which were not recorded by Imam As-Suyuti.

Sheikh Al-Muhaddith Al-Albani, in his part, conducted a thorough verification of the book, after including the addition made by An-Nabahani, and published the book in two major sections:

Sahih Al-Jami’ Al-Saghir and its Addition (2 vols.)

Da’if Al-Jami’ Al-Saghir and its Addition (1 vol.)
