name: Al-Adab al-Mufrad by al-Bukhary
description_short:
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, authored by the preeminent Imam al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH), is a seminal encyclopedia of Islamic manners and ethics. Often referred to as the Isolated Book of Manners, this independent volume contains 1,322 narrations meticulously organized across 644 chapters. While Imam al-Bukhari is famously strict in his Sahih, he adopted broader criteria here, as the focus is on moral refinement and character building rather than strict legal rulings.

The collection focuses on Prophetic teachings regarding social conduct, faith, and human rights, alongside the sayings of the Companions. It provides a granular look at the nuances of family life—with a profound emphasis on the rights of parents—as well as dealing with neighbors, orphans, and the general public. It touches on the ethics of speech, the importance of keeping ties, and the dignity required in daily interactions.

name: Ash-Shari'ah by imam al-Ajuree (360H)
description_short:
Ash-Shari‘ah by Imam al-Ajurry (d. 360H) is an early and foundational work in Sunni creed, authored in a period when theological deviations were spreading and clarification of orthodox belief was urgently needed. The book gathers texts from the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the statements of the Companions and early scholars to establish the principles of belief according to Ahl al-Sunnah, particularly in matters of faith, obedience, authority, and adherence to the prophetic way.

Imam al-Ajurry presents these themes with a strong emphasis on transmitted evidence, avoiding speculative theology and grounding doctrine in the understanding of the Salaf. Because of its early date and clear methodology, Ash-Shari‘ah has long been relied upon by scholars as a key reference for understanding classical Sunni positions before later theological schools became dominant.

name: Al-Ibaanah 'an Shari'atil Firqatin-Naajiyah - Ibn Battah
description_short:
Also known al-Ibana al-Kubra, this is a collection of ahaadeeth and Athaar on the saved group and its characteristics and those opponents, by Imaam Ibn Battah (387H).

This book is one of the origins of the fundamental books of the Sunnis and is considered as one of the encyclopedias of the traditionalist scholars regarding the Sunnah and the beliefs of the Sunnis.

And Ibn Battah, may Allah have mercy on him, followed the path of the previous scholars in his reliance on producing evidence from the Book (Quran) and the Sunnah and the traditions of this nation’s predecessors. He abstained from delving into the sciences of scholastic innovated thought, which the Sunnis unanimously condemn and warn against it and its followers.

In his defense and clarification of the belief of Ahl al-Sunnah, he supported his argument with evidence from the Book, the Sunnah, and the narrated traditions, then he distinguished himself from others, who were classified in this section, by citing an abundance of texts and scholars’ statements with good tabulation, arrangement, and commentary in brief terms. He made sure his book would not turn like some Sunnah books that are void of commentary and explanation.

name: Ash-Sharh wal-Ibanah (Al-Ibanah as-Sughra) Ibn Battah
description_short:
The book “Ash-Sharḥ wal Ibānah”, by Imam Ibn Battah al-Akbari, is one of the abridged books of the Sunnis in the chapters of the Sunnah, belief, worship and ethics. It is also known as (al-Ibānah as-Sughrā) to distinguish it from his other book (al-Ibānah 'an shari'at al-firqah al-nājiyah wa-mujānabat al-firaq al-madhmumah) also known as (al-Ibānah al-Kubrā).

And the book al-Ibānah al-Kubrā is not an alternative to the book al-Ibānah as-Sughrā, while the latter is not an abridged version of the first, as presumed by some people, but rather an independent book, as evidenced by the presence of Hadiths, traditions and chapters that are not found in al-Ibānah al-Kubrā.

It is a book of great value and benefit. The author, Ibn Battah, may Allah have mercy on him, explained that he had written the book after noticing people’s distancing and non-adherence to the Sunnah, the spread of heresies and the taking of ignorant and misguided people as leaders and imams in the religion. This in fact prompted him to compile a short book to remind people of the Sunnah and the obligation to adhere to it in the manner of the righteous predecessors of this nation, and warn them about heresy and misguided whims.

Edition verified by the Muhaqqiq 'Adil al-Hamdan from several manuscripts. Latest edition revised and augmented, checked from 2 manuscripts.

name: at-Targheeb wat-Tarheeb by al-Mundhiree (authenticated + Harakat)
description_short:
Al-Targhib wal-Tarhib by Hafiz al-Mundhiri is a masterful collection of hadiths that employs the divine methodology of encouragement and warning. This comprehensive hadith compilation contains nearly one thousand authentic narrations systematically organized by subject matter, covering essential Islamic practices including prayer, charity, seeking knowledge, and voluntary acts of worship.

The author expertly balances inspiration with caution, presenting hadiths that motivate believers toward righteous deeds while warning against their neglect or excess. Following the scholarly approach of both jurists and hadith specialists, al-Mundhiri organizes the work into books, chapters, and sections for easy navigation. His precise language, careful selection of narrations, and insightful commentary make this an indispensable resource for Islamic education, da'wah work, and personal spiritual development.

This high-quality edition features precise verification of hadith authenticity and comprehensive annotations, making it accessible to both scholars and general readers.

name: Min Usool Aqeedah Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jamaa'ah - Shaykh al-Fawzan
description_short:
A booklet (12x17cm) to put all hands! Excellent and important, the great scholar Saalih al-Fawzaan enumerates nine bases of the Aqeedah of Ahl as-Sunnah wa al-Jamaa'ah:

1. Faith in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Prophets, the Last Day and Destiny good or bad.

2. Faith is made of Word and An Act, it increases with obedience and decreases with the sins.

3. We don't make miscreant a person among Muslims as he did not commit a cancellations of Islam.

4. The obligation to obey the leaders of the Muslims unless it is a sin

5. The prohibition get out against the leader of the Muslims even if he commits what is less than the Kufr.

6. Purify his heart and his tongue against the Companions of the Prophet, sallallaahu 'alayhiwasallam.

7. Love the people of the House of the Prophet, sallallaahu 'alayhiwasallam, and cooperate with them.

8. Believe in miracles (Karamat) those who are near (Awliya) of Allah.

9. Follow what came from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, sallallaahu 'alayhiwasallam, so apparent and hidden.

description_short:

description_short:
Sharh Hilyat Talib al-Ilm is an authoritative commentary by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Salih al-Uthaymeen (d. 1421 AH) on the celebrated treatise on student ethics authored by Dr. Bakr Abu Zayd (d. 1429 AH). The work systematically outlines the moral conduct, decorum, and study methods required of a student of Islamic knowledge.

Through practical explanations and real-life examples, Shaykh al-Uthaymeen expands upon the matn's core themes—including sincerity in intention, stages of learning, manners with teachers and peers, safeguarding time, and upholding integrity in study. His accessible pedagogical style transforms theoretical etiquette into actionable advice, making this volume a foundational guide for beginning and advanced students alike.

name: Adwaae al-Bayaan (Tafseer of Muhammad Ameen ash-Shanqeetee)
description_short:
The Great Scholar of Tafseer Muhammad al-Amin ash-Shanqiti (Professor of Sheikh al-Uthaymeen) gives us a Tafseer recognized having the particularity to explain among others the Quran by the Quran.

Method:

1 - The author gives an explanation of the verses of every sura of the Koran based on the Koran itself. This implies that it is not all verses which are discussed, because many verses had not been clarified by others, but the sunnah.

2 - The author is based on the seven readings of the Koran.

3 - Through the exegesis of the verses, the author expands some scientific research to benefit to readers the following:

Questions of fiqh: the author quotes about multiple legal issues arising from Qur'anic verses, the opinions of different imams of Islam as Malik, Shafii, Ibn Hanbal, Abu Hanifa and others, and bears his choice on the authentic legal evidence.

Language Issues

Dogmatic questions: questions of belief of the people of the Sunnah and consensus.

Questions legal bases (ussool al-fiqh)

Questions of fiqh: the author quotes about multiple legal issues arising from Qur'anic verses, the opinions of different imams of Islam as Malik, Shafii, Ibn Hanbal, Abu Hanifa and others, and bears his choice on the authentic legal evidence.

Language Issues

Dogmatic questions: questions of belief of the people of the Sunnah and consensus.

name: As-Sarim al-Maslul 'ala Shatim ar-Rasul ﷺ - Ibn Taymiyya
description_short:
This comprehensive treatise by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya (d. 728H) examines the grave offense of insulting the Prophet (peace be upon him) and its legal consequences in Islamic law. Drawing on evidence from the Quran, Sunnah, and scholarly consensus, it meticulously outlines the Shari'a rulings on blasphemy while emphasizing the sanctity of the Prophet's honor in Islamic tradition.

Al-Sarim al-Maslul is celebrated for its rigorous methodology, as Ibn Taymiyya engages with diverse scholarly opinions while firmly grounding his conclusions in textual evidence. This approach has given the work enduring influence across all madhhabs, making it a frequently cited reference in discussions of fiqh and theology. Its clarity and analytical depth have established it as an essential resource for both classical scholarship and contemporary discussions about blasphemy, remaining indispensable for students and scholars of Islamic law alike.

name: Al-Kafi fi Fiqh 'ala madhhab Ahl al-Medina - Ibn Abdel Barr (fiqh Maliki)
description_short:
One of the most beneficial mukhtasarat ever composed in Maliki jurisprudence, compiled by the Hafiz of the Islamic West, Imam Abu ‘Umar Ibn Abd al-Barr al-Qurtubi (d. 463 AH) at the request of fellow scholars. He gathered the foundational issues — the usul and ummahat — upon which the branches of legal rulings are built, confining himself to the most authentic in knowledge and the most reliable in transmission. He drew his material from seven primary sources: al-Muwatta’, al-Mudawwanah, the book of Ibn Abd al-Hakam, al-Mabsut of Isma’il al-Qadi, al-Hawi of Abu al-Faraj, Mukhtasar Abi Mus’ab, and the Muwatta’ of Ibn Wahb.

Abu Muhammad Ibn Hazm — Ibn Abd al-Barr’s contemporary and student — said: “Our companion Abu ‘Umar has books with no equal, among them the book called al-Kafi in the fiqh of Malik and his companions.” A work that suffices in place of lengthier compositions on the same subject, suited for the Maliki student seeking a concise, rigorously edited text that gathers the foundations from which to build toward the branches.

name: Al-Furqan bayna Awliya al-Rahman wa Awliya al-Shaytan - Ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
This book is a classical theological treatise dealing with the distinction between the true allies of God and the allies of Satan, written by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728 AH). The author addresses the widespread confusion surrounding spirituality, saintliness (wilayah), and supernatural occurrences in the Islamic world. His main purpose is to establish a clear scriptural criterion to separate orthodox prophetic guidance from deviant spiritual practices and innovations.

The text is organized around the criteria set by the Quran and Sunnah for evaluating spiritual claims and supernatural states. Ibn Taymiyyah analyzes the differences between the true miracles (karamat) granted to righteous believers and the satanic states (ahwal shaytaniyyah) associated with sorcerers or innovators. He uses textual evidences to demonstrate that true proximity to Allah is achieved solely through strict obedience to the Prophet, rather than through abstract experiences, isolated asceticism, or claims of mystical unveiling (kashf).

name: Sunan ad-Daraqutni with notes of Al-Adhim Abadi
description_short:
Sunan al-Daraqutni is a cornerstone of Hadith literature, specifically engineered to navigate the complexities of 'Ilal (hidden flaws) and variant narrations. Compiled by the 4th-century master Imam al-Daraqutni (d. 385 AH), this collection serves as an advanced evidentiary guide for Islamic jurisprudence. Unlike the standard collections that prioritize surface-level authenticity, this work meticulously exposes defects in narrations to protect the integrity of the Sunnah from erroneous conclusions.

The work is organized according to the chapters of Fiqh, providing a functional map of the Prophetic precedents behind religious law. It is an indispensable resource for the advanced researcher, shifting the focus from static rules to the dynamic, honorable process of legal verification and academic honesty. By documenting the exact nature of discrepancies in narrations, it ensures that the student’s understanding remains anchored in a disciplined and meticulous commitment to the truth.

name: Al-Masa'il al-Fiqhiyyah al-lati Hukiya fiha Ruju' al-Sahaba
description_short:
This exceptional academic study investigates a precise and often overlooked aspect of early Islamic legal history: the instances where the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ changed their scholarly opinions. By focusing on verified retractions, the work sheds light on the intellectual humility and rigorous pursuit of truth that characterized the first generation of Islam. Each case is examined through a meticulous analysis of primary sources, exploring the evidence that prompted a Companion to move from one legal position to another, whether due to a newly discovered Hadith or a refined understanding of a specific ruling.

The methodology employed ensures that every reported retraction is subjected to critical scrutiny to verify its historical authenticity before discussing its legal implications. This focus is particularly valuable for the student of knowledge (Talib al-Ilm) seeking to understand the fluidity and development of early jurisprudence (Fiqh). By documenting these shifts in thought, the work provides a deeper understanding of the flexibility within the legal process and the supreme authority of the Sunnah in guiding the final conclusions of the Sahaba, making it a rare and profound addition to any specialized research library.

name: Authentic Athars of the Sahaabah in Fiqh
description_short:
This monumental three-volume compilation serves as a definitive filter for the legal rulings and fatwas attributed to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. By meticulously scanning classical primary sources such as the Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd al-Razzaq, the work extracts thousands of reports and subjects them to rigorous Hadith criticism. Only narrations meeting the standards of Sahih (authentic) or Hasan (good) are included, providing a purified foundational record of how the first generation of Islam interpreted and applied Divine Law.

The collection is systematically organized according to traditional chapters of jurisprudence, making it an indispensable resource for comparative Fiqh and the study of early legal precedents. It allows researchers to clearly distinguish between established consensus and the diverse opinions of the Sahaba, which is critical for understanding the evolution of the various schools of thought. The sober and analytical approach ensures that students of knowledge can rely on these verified accounts to ground their studies in the authentic practice of the Salaf.

name: Sawa'iq al-Mursalah 'ala al-Jahmiyyah wa al-Mu'attilah - Ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
As-Sawa‘iq al-Mursalah is one of Ibn al-Qayyim’s major polemical works, written to refute the theological positions of the Jahmiyyah and other groups that denied or distorted the divine attributes. The book lays out a detailed defence of the scriptural approach of Ahl al-Sunnah, arguing from Qur’an, Sunnah, rational evidence, and the statements of early scholars. Ibn al-Qayyim’s method is rigorous and layered, combining theological reasoning with linguistic analysis, making the work a central reference in discussions on creed and divine attributes.

Across its extensive chapters, the author dismantles the foundations of ta‘til (negation) and false reinterpretation, clarifies the principles of affirming Allah’s names and attributes without likening Him to creation, and responds to the arguments used by speculative theologians. The book is known among students of ‘aqidah for its depth and for the force of Ibn al-Qayyim’s reasoning, serving as an advanced study for those exploring classical Sunni theology.

name: Raf' ul-malaam 'an il-aïmmat il-a'laam - Ibn Taymiya
description_short:
Al-Lajna ad-Da-ima said: "About the reasons for the divergence of scholars, many of them come from the fact that none of them had the whole knowledge. Thus, it is possible that one knows things that the other does not know, and can understand the texts differently from each other when clear evidence does not exist.

Sheikh ul-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, has extensively studied the issue in his book Raf'-ul-Malam. See it, and you will find what you are looking for if Allah wills."

name: 'Uddatu s-Sabirin wa dhakhiratu Shakirin - Ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
Uddat al-Sabirin wa Dhakhirat al-Shakirin is one of the most profound spiritual works by the renowned scholar Imam Ibn al-Qayyim. This classic treatise explores the two essential pillars of the believer's journey: Patience (Sabr) and Gratitude (Shukr). Through a blend of theological depth and psychological insight, the author explains how these virtues serve as the ultimate equipment and treasure for navigating the trials and blessings of worldly life while seeking the pleasure of the Creator.

The text provides a comprehensive analysis of the human soul, detailing the ongoing struggle between intellect and base desires. Ibn al-Qayyim categorizes the various levels of patience—such as patience in obedience, patience in avoiding sin, and patience during calamities—while simultaneously illustrating the transformative power of a grateful heart. Richly supported by verses from the Qur'an, Prophetic traditions, and the wisdom of the Pious Predecessors, this work remains a vital manual for anyone seeking to cultivate emotional resilience and spiritual excellence.

name: Kitab Al-Iman - Al-Hafidh Ibn Abi Shaybah (235H)
description_short:
This classical work by Imam Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah addresses the fundamental concept of faith (iman) in Islamic theology. As one of the great hadith scholars and compilers of the 3rd century Hijri, Ibn Abi Shaybah brings his vast knowledge of prophetic traditions to bear on this crucial theological topic. The work explores the nature of faith, its components, and its relationship to righteous deeds, drawing extensively from Quranic verses and authentic hadith.

Ibn Abi Shaybah's treatment of faith reflects the early Sunni position on this contested theological issue, particularly relevant during the debates between different schools of thought regarding whether actions are part of faith or separate from it. The work serves as an important source for understanding how the early generations of Muslim scholars approached questions of belief, practice, and the criteria for determining a person's spiritual status within the Muslim community.

name: Kitab as-Sunnah of Abdullah, son of imam Ahmad
description_short:
Kitab al-Sunnah is a foundational and preeminent work in the field of Islamic creed ('Aqidah), compiled by the scholar Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who passed away in 290 H. This monumental collection serves as a primary source for the traditionalist perspective, meticulously documenting the beliefs of the early generations regarding the nature of faith, the attributes of Allah, and the refutation of early theological deviations. As the son and primary student of Imam Ahmad, Abdullah provides an unparalleled look into the core tenets of orthodox thought during a pivotal era of Islamic history.
The work is highly regarded for its disciplined reliance on narrations and chains of transmission, rather than abstract speculative philosophy. It covers a vast range of essential topics, including the Quran, the Vision of Allah in the hereafter, and the status of the Companions, all while maintaining a rigorous academic integrity. This reference is an honorable resource for any serious student or researcher looking to understand the historical roots of Islamic theology and the preservation of the Prophetic tradition in its most pristine, original form.

name: Kitab as-Sunnah by Ibn Abi 'Asim (287H)
description_short:
One of the most celebrated works of the Salaf in expounding the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-al-Jama'ah and establishing it through hadiths and narrations with connected chains, compiled by al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Abi 'Asim al-Shaybani (d. 287 AH). Arranged in chapters covering the foundations of belief: the condemnation of heresies and innovations, obedience to the authorities, adherence to the Sunnah, affirmation of the divine attributes — speech, face, hand, ascent, descent, and vision — faith and its increase and decrease, divine decree, the Basin, intercession, and the virtues and ranking of the Companions.

Among the earliest books to gather the chapters of creed in a single work with connected chains of transmission, it has remained an authoritative reference among Ahl al-Sunnah across the centuries. Distinguished by the abundance of its hadiths, the multiplicity of its routes, and the comprehensiveness of its chapters. An essential work for every student engaged in the creed of the Salaf.

name: At-Ta'liqaat ar-Radiyyah 'ala ar-rawdati an-nadiyyah - Albani / Siddik Khan
description_short:
The book “At-Ta’liqat Ar-Ridiyah ‘ala Ar-Rawdah An-Nadiyah” is a commentary by Sheikh Al-Albani on the book “Ar-Rawdah An-Nidiyah” by Siddiq Hassan Khan Al-Qanouji.

“Ar-Rawdah An-Nadiyah”, by Sheikh Siddiq Hassan Khan, is a book on jurisprudence in which its author explained the book “Ad-Durar Al-Bahiyah” and the issues contained therein, then he mentioned his opinion and the opinions of his opponents from among the jurists with the evidence confirming his self-interpretation; he dedicated his subjects to the jurisprudence of worship.

The book “Ad-Durar Al-Bahiyah fil Masa’il al-Fiqhiyah” by Imam Al-Shawkani is a famous jurisprudential script, which is distinguished by its author mentioning the most correct in an issue, without being restricted to a specific doctrine; it is characterized by the ease of its expression, and its distance from overelaboration and assumptions of issues.

Official edition in 3 volumes, prefaced by the Shaykh himself.

name: Kitab at-Tawhid by Imam ibn Khuzaymah
description_short:
One of the greatest works ever composed on affirming the divine attributes according to the methodology of the Salaf, written by Imam Ibn Khuzaymah (d. 311 AH), who was historically known as the "Imam of Imams" due to his independent legal reasoning and mastery of Hadith, it serves as a direct refutation against early rationalist movements like the Jahmiyyah, Mu'tazilah, and Qadariyyah. The text provides a definitive presentation of orthodox Sunni theology by gathering explicit scriptural proofs for individual divine attributes, including Allah's Speech, Face, Hands, Sight, and His Ascent (Istiwa) over the Throne.

The book is distinguished by the abundance of its chains and the diversity of its transmission routes, and by its detailed chapter structure that devotes multiple sections to each attribute, marshalling evidences from different angles. The work is structured like a Hadith compilation, utilizing raw chains of transmission (asaneed) to validate each theological point, making it an indispensable reference for the student in the field of the divine names and attributes, and a living witness to the creed of the people of hadith in the 3rd century of the Hijrah.

name: Kitab at-Tawheed by Imam Ibn Mandah (395H)
description_short:
Kitab at-Tawhid written by a great among the Imams of the Salaf, Imam Ibn Mandah in a beautiful edition with a full Tahqiq.

The author divided this book into four sections. He discussed in the first section Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah (Oneness of Allah’s Lordship) with a lengthy explanation, then Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (Oneness of Worship) in the second section, then Tawhid al-Asmā’ (Oneness of Allah’s Names) in the third, and then Tawhid as-Sifāt (Oneness of Allah’s Attributes) in the fourth. So he made the Oneness of Allah’s Names and Attributes into two separate sections.

In writing his book, the author followed the path of the early Traditionalists among the predecessors. Indeed, their method in writing to corroborate any belief, or to respond to the suspicions that came on a certain issue, is characterized by mentioning the texts from the Qur’an, the authentic of the Purified Sunnah and the traditions of the Companions and the Followers with their chains of authorities under headings indicating the meaning intended by the mention of that text. They would also mention statements that contradict the path followed by the predecessors, and then cite texts in which they would explain the argument against the antagonist one and respond to him.

name: Badaa'i at-Tafsir - Tafseer Ibnul-Qayyim (3 volumes)
description_short:
Bada'i al-Tafsir: Al-Jami' li-Tafsir Ibn al-Qayyim is a comprehensive Quranic exegesis compiled by gathering the profound tafsir insights, linguistic nuances, and theological reflections of Imam Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (d. 751 AH). Since Ibn al-Qayyim did not write a standalone, sequential commentary covering the entire Quran from cover to cover, scholar Yusri al-Sayyid Muhammad methodically extracted his interpretations from across thirty-two of the Imam’s major published works and organized them sequentially according to the traditional order of the Quranic Surahs.

The resulting compilation offers readers a unique, deeply spiritual, and analytically rigorous commentary that blends classical Quranic exegesis with profound legal, rhetorical, and heart-softening reflections. Reviewed and refined by scholar Salih Ahmad al-Shami, this compilation serves as an indispensable reference for students of Quranic studies and scholars seeking to access Ibn al-Qayyim's unmatched mastery of Arabic linguistics, theology, and spiritual purification in a single, well-structured reference.

name: Tafseer Shaykh al-Islaam ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
This work gathers the Shaykh's scattered exegetical statements from his printed and manuscript works into seven volumes. Know that Ibn Taymiyyah never compiled an independent tafsīr, believing much of the Quran is self-evident or explained by the Salaf, focusing on clarifying difficulties. The book collects his intended tafsīr and incidental mentions in his juridical discussions and refutations.

Al-Birzālī said of him: "When he discussed tafsīr, people were astonished by his vast memorization and excellent presentation." His exegesis returns to the Quran, Sunnah, and Salaf statements, verifying their views and weighing opinions with evidence while refuting corrupt interpretations. The work is verified and annotated to connect texts to their contexts, with a scholarly introduction on the Shaykh's methodology, sources, and distinctive features.

name: Rawdatul-'Uqalaa wa Nuzhatul-Fudalaa - Ibn Hibban
description_short:
Rawdat al-'Uqala' (The Garden of the Wise) is a timeless masterpiece of Islamic ethics and social wisdom authored by Imam Ibn Hibban, the author of the celebrated Sahih Ibn Hibban. In this work, the great Hadith master shifts his focus toward the refinement of character, providing a comprehensive manual on the virtues that define a person of intellect and nobility. It is regarded as one of the most beautiful and practical books on Adab (etiquette) and Tazkiyah (purification of the soul) in the Islamic tradition.

The methodology of the book is unique, as Ibn Hibban organizes chapters around specific traits such as intellect, silence, truthfulness, friendship, and patience. For each virtue, he provides a blend of Prophetic traditions, anecdotes from the Pious Predecessors, and poignant lines of Arabic poetry. This creates a rich tapestry of guidance that is as literary as it is spiritual. It is an essential volume for anyone looking to navigate the complexities of social life and personal conduct through the lens of traditional Islamic wisdom.

name: Kitab as-Sunnah by Imam al-Kirmani (280H)
description_short: Kitab al-Sunna min Masa’il Harb ibn Isma‘il al-Hanzali al-Kirmani by Imam Harb ibn Isma‘il al-Kirmani (d. 280H), a prominent third-century student of Imam Ahmad, is a comprehensive work compiling the creedal positions of Ahl al-Sunna, drawn from narrations by Imams Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and other Sunni scholars. The book, named by later scholars due to the author’s lack of a formal title, covers beliefs, worship, transactions, ethics, Hadith critique, and Quranic exegesis, emphasizing the Sunni stance against innovators like the Mu‘tazila and Jahmiyya. It supports each doctrine with authentic Hadiths and sayings of the Companions and their successors, making it a key text for students of ‘Aqidah seeking to understand early Sunni theology. Critically edited by Abu ‘Abdullah ‘Adil ibn ‘Abdullah Al Hamdan, it remains a vital resource for its unique narrations and rigorous methodology.

name: Al-Kaafiyyatu ash-Shaafiyyah (an-Nooniyyah) - Ibnul-Qayyim - 100% harakat
description_short:
Al-Kafiyah al-Shafiyah, widely known as the Nuniyyah due to its rhyming scheme, is a monumental didactic poem composed of nearly 6,000 verses. In this masterpiece, Imam Ibn al-Qayyim provides a comprehensive defense of the Athari creed, systematically outlining the beliefs of the Pious Predecessors regarding the Divine Attributes and the nature of Faith. It is regarded as one of the most significant poetic works in the history of Islamic theology, combining linguistic eloquence with rigorous scriptural evidence.

The poem serves as a detailed refutation of various philosophical and theological schools that deviated from the prophetic tradition. Ibn al-Qayyim addresses complex issues of Kalam (speculative theology) with clarity and poetic precision, making the defenses of the Sunnah memorable and accessible to students of knowledge. For centuries, this work has been a primary source for those seeking to understand the nuances of the creed of the Salaf and the historical debates that shaped Islamic theological discourse.

name: Al-Qawaa'id wal-Usool al-Jaami'ah - As-Sa'di
description_short:
Al-Qawa'id wa al-Usul al-Jami'ah is a masterful and concise work by Sheikh Abdurrahman as-Sa'di that outlines the fundamental legal maxims (Qawa'id Fiqhiyyah) and universal principles of Islamic law. The book is designed to provide students with a comprehensive framework, allowing them to connect vast numbers of secondary legal rulings (Furu') to a few central, unifying principles (Usul). This approach simplifies the study of Fiqh, transforming it from a collection of isolated cases into a coherent and logical system.

The work details approximately 60 major maxims covering various chapters of jurisprudence, from acts of worship to financial transactions. Sheikh as-Sa'di’s hallmark clarity and pedagogical skill are evident throughout, as he explains each rule with evidence from the Qur'an and Sunnah followed by practical examples. It is widely considered an essential primer for anyone looking to master the foundations of Hanbali Fiqh and the broader objectives of the Sharia.

name: Ad-dalil 'ala Manhaj as-Salikin
description_short:
Al-Dalil ala Manhaj al-Salikin is a precise and scholarly explanation of the famous jurisprudential primer Manhaj al-Salikin, originally authored by Sheikh Abdurrahman as-Sa'di, the author of the world-renowned Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman (Tafsir al-Sa'di). In this work, Sheikh Dr. Khalid al-Mushayqih provides the primary scriptural evidences (Adillah) for the legal rulings presented in the original text, effectively bridging the gap between the summarized manual and the foundational sources of the Sharia.

The methodology focuses on clarity and academic depth, making it an excellent resource for students of the Hanbali school. Sheikh al-Mushayqih, a prominent student of Sheikh Ibn al-Uthaymin, employs a pedagogical approach that mirrors the clarity found in the works of his predecessors. By documenting the proofs from the Qur'an and the Sunnah for every Fiqh issue, he ensures that the reader develops a robust understanding of the legislative reasoning behind daily practices in worship and transactions.

name: Min Akhbar as-Salaf as-Salih - Zakariyyah ibn Ghulam Qadir
description_short:
Drawing from the pure wellspring of the early generations of Islam, Min Akhbar as-Salaf as-Salih is an uplifting compilation of historical narratives. The author methodically gathers more than 2,000 authentic reports (athar) detailing the lives, worship, and profound character of the Righteous Predecessors. Unlike generic storybooks, this work is anchored in rigorous verification of chains of transmission, ensuring that every narrative presented is historically reliable and protecting the reader from widespread but fabricated anecdotes.

Shaykh Zakariyyah ibn Ghulam Qadir structures the book thematically, making it an excellent resource for personal reflection or regular study circles. Readers will find dedicated sections on the sincerity of the early scholars, their devotion to night prayers, their fear of Allah, and their steadfastness upon the Sunnah. This edition features clear typography, making it a highly beneficial and trustworthy resource for students of knowledge seeking to strengthen their faith and methodology through the true history of the Salaf.

name: Al-Rad 'ala al-Mubtadi'a - Ibn al- Banna al-Hanbali (471H)
description_short:
Imam Ibn al-Banna' al-Hanbali's (d. 471H) Al-Radd 'ala al-Mubtadi'ah (The Refutation of the Innovators) is a significant classical treatise that systematically addresses theological doctrines considered innovations deviating from the creed of the early Muslims. The work tackles key theological disputes of his era, including Divine Attributes, Divine Decree, and the nature of Faith.

Ibn al-Banna' identifies specific groups like the Mu'tazila and Jahmiyyah, countering their arguments with evidence from the Quran, Sunnah, and the understanding of early Muslim generations to defend the Athari theological perspective. This classical polemical text has been made accessible through Sheikh 'Adil ibn 'Abdillah Al Hamdan's scholarly edition, providing contemporary readers with a reliable version of this important defense of traditional Islamic creed.

name: Kitab al-Qabas fi Sharh Muwatta Malik ibn Anas - Ibnul-'Arabi al-Maliki
description_short:
The book “Al-Qabas fi Sharh Muwatta’ Malik bin Anas”, by sheikh and judge Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn al-ʿArabī al-Maʿāfirī al-Ishbīlī” is one of the most important explanations of the book “Muwatta’ Imam Malik bin Anas”. It earned the recognition of scholars, both ancient and present, with its explanation of all the included Hadiths, and the interpretation of the ones qualified as Gharib (Hadith conveyed only by one narrator), which facilitated their understanding.

The importance of this book is due to the following:

- The importance of the Andalusian influence, which is one of the main sources of literature classified by the prominent Maliki scholars.

- It contains many of the rulings drawn up by the author.

- It contains in-depth explanation, enlightenment and details of the issues.

- The book was distinguished for its good arrangement and ingenuity of its classification.

- The abundance of benefits in Hadith, language, fundamentals and jurisprudence.

- Highlighting issues and labelling them

- The value of the author, the writer of famous books, who is considered one of the most brilliant scholars of the Maliki school of thought.

name: Ibn Taymiyyah's Position on Ash'aris - A. al-Mahmoud - 2 volumes
description_short:
This work by Dr. Abd al-Rahman al-Mahmoud is considered one of the most significant contemporary academic studies regarding the relationship between Ibn Taymiyyah and the Ash'ari school. The book is characterized by its exhaustive research and objective analysis, tracing Ibn Taymiyyah's positions through his various treatises and letters. It provides a deep dive into his critiques of Ash'ari theology concerning the Divine Attributes, Divine Decree (Qadar), and Faith (Iman), making it an indispensable reference for understanding the development of Islamic theological schools.

The methodology is based on a comparative and analytical framework, where the author presents Ash'ari views from their primary sources before detailing Ibn Taymiyyah’s responses and points of divergence. Written with scholarly sobriety and meticulous documentation, this extensive work—originally a doctoral thesis—serves as a foundational text for students of knowledge specializing in Kalam (speculative theology) and comparative creed. It is highly valued for its ability to synthesize complex philosophical arguments into a coherent academic narrative.

name: Shifaae al-'Aleel fi masaail al-Qadaa wal-Qadar - Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya
description_short:
Shifa al-Alil is an authoritative and exhaustive theological treatise by the illustrious scholar Imam Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751 AH), dedicated entirely to the complex subjects of Divine Decree (Qada), Predestination (Qadar), and Divine Wisdom (Hikmah). In this monumental work, the author meticulously deconstructs the various philosophical and sectarian views that have historically caused confusion among the Ummah. He provides a robust defense of the orthodox Sunni position, emphasizing that Allah’s actions are always rooted in perfect wisdom and ultimate purpose, effectively healing the "ailment" of doubt and confusion that many face regarding these intricate matters of faith.

The book is characterized by its deep integration of Quranic evidence, Prophetic traditions, and rational arguments. Ibn al-Qayyim goes beyond simple definitions, diving into the causative relationship between human actions and Divine will, and explaining the concept of Ta’lil (Assigning Reason) to Allah’s laws and creations. This work is indispensable for students of Creed (Aqidah) and philosophy, offering a spiritual and intellectual remedy that strengthens a believer's submission to Allah's decree while providing the logical tools to refute deviant ideologies.

name: al-Akhlaq wa al-Siyar (or Madawat al-Nufus) by al-Imam Ibn Hazm
description_short:
Al-Akhlaq wa al-Siyar — also known simply as Madawat al-Nufus — by Imam Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi (d. 456H) is a timeless masterpiece of Islamic ethics and self-discipline. The author offers an honest and profound reflection on human character, emotions, and the art of moral and spiritual healing, addressing the roots of virtue and vice in the human soul.

Drawing from revelation, reason, and personal experience, Ibn Hazm examines the inner conflicts of desire and intellect, the causes of sorrow and joy, and the pursuit of lasting happiness. His tone is at once sharp and compassionate, philosophical and deeply spiritual, making this one of the most insightful guides to self-reform in the Islamic tradition.

name: Kitaab al-Masaahif - Al Imam Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud
description_short:
The subject of this book is: The Book of Allah Almighty, in terms of its compilation in all its stages, the differences in the Qur’anic copies of the regions, what has been reported on the Qur’anic books of some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, the recitations that have been transmitted from some of the followers. It also discusses what has been said about the Quranic script and its punctuation, writing it and receiving payment for it, and a set of rulings related to the Holy Qur’an, such as touching the Qur’an when one is impure, selling it, mortgaging it, travelling with it to the land of the Kuffar (Disbelievers), leading worshipers in prayer while reciting from the Qur’an, and so on.

The author's approach: he divided his book into many chapters, and under each chapter he included some Hadiths and reports related to it, which he narrated on the authority of his teachers with their chains of transmissions.

Excellent edition verified from 2 manuscripts, with numerous annotations on the Hadiths, their referencing and authenticity.

name: As-Sirah an-Nabawy li Ibn Hisham
description_short:
al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham is the earliest and most famous classical biography of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that has reached us in a complete, structured form. It is based on the earlier work of Ibn Ishaq, but Ibn Hisham edited, arranged, and refined the narrative by removing weak reports and poetry he deemed inappropriate, producing a more reliable and organized version.

The work presents the life of the Prophet ﷺ from before his birth through the Makkan and Madinan periods, covering events such as the Hijrah, battles, treaties, and the Farewell Pilgrimage. It also contains detailed genealogies, descriptions of Arab tribes, and early Islamic society. For over a millennium, it has served as the most influential and widely taught reference in prophetic biography (sirah).

name: Nayl al-Awtar by Imam ash-Shawkani
description_short:
One of the most important works in the jurisprudence of hadith rulings, composed by Imam al-Shawkani (d. 1250 AH) as a commentary on "Muntaqa al-Akhbar" by Majd al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 652 AH), which gathers nearly five thousand hadiths of legal rulings. Al-Shawkani explains each hadith from the angles of chain, text, and language — analyzing transmission routes, narrator reliability, and hidden defects ('ilal), cross-referencing the critical judgments of al-Bayhaqi, al-Daraqutni, and Ibn Hajar's Talkhis al-Habir.

He then systematically records the positions of the four Sunni schools, the Zahiri school, early independent mujtahidun such as al-Awza'i and Sufyan al-Thawri, and the Hadawiyyah-Zaydi tradition, applying usul al-fiqh to weigh competing arguments and adopting an evidence-based approach to determine the strongest legal position (tarjih), free from school affiliation.

This dual competence in hadith criticism and comparative jurisprudence is what has made Nayl al-Awtar a lasting reference for anyone seeking to understand the hadiths of rulings through ijtihad rather than taqlid. It is commonly placed alongside Fath al-Bari in the library of the student of hadith and fiqh.

name: Fath al-Qadeer (Imam Shawkaanee's Tafseer)
description_short:
This work is a cornerstone of Quranic exegesis, where Imam al-Shawkani masterfully combines two methodologies: Tafsir bi-l-Ma’thur (transmitted reports) and Tafsir bi-l-Diraya (rational and linguistic analysis). The methodology is characterized by independent legal reasoning (Ijtihad). The author presents the verses followed by relevant Hadiths and narrations from the Salaf, while rigorously discussing linguistic nuances and legal rulings, providing a comprehensive resource for the serious student.

The text is highly regarded for its emphasis on evidence and its departure from blind imitation (Taqlid), which is evident in Shawkani’s scholarly critiques of earlier commentators. It remains a fundamental pillar for studying the verses of legal rulings (Ayat al-Ahkam) and the contexts of revelation.

name: I'lam al-Muwaqi'in 'an Rabb il-'Alamin - Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
description_short:
This classic ibn al-Qayyim discusses of Fiqh, of Usool, of Maqasid al-Shari'ah and of Tarikh at-Tachri', of Siyasiya Shari'a...

It is a book that combines jurisprudence and its principles, the objectives of Shari’ah, the history of legislation and Islamic governance. In it, he urged to follow the Prophet’s traditions and produced clearly the sources of legislation. He explained Omar’s letter to Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, which is considered a source in providing proof and rulings in Islamic jurisprudence.

Then the author dealt with a detailed study of some jurisprudential and fundamentalist subjects, such as usury, blocking the means (to what is prohibited) and tricks (to bypass Shari’ah), analogy, interpretation, the conditions of a mufti, and the etiquettes of fatwa and the saying of Talaq (divorce) three times by the husband.

The book concluded with lengthy chapters on the fatwas of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and arranged them according to the chapters of jurisprudence. The author discusses the issues at length and in detail, with argumentation, explanation and justification.  He uses the style of guidance with good choice and preference, the strength of the character, and the extracting of Hadiths with their reference to their Sunnah books sources.

name: al-Fusul fi Sirat ar-Rasul - ibn Kathir
description_short:
Imam Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH), the renowned historian and exegete, authored this work as a brilliant distillation of the Prophetic biography, specifically tailored for students of knowledge seeking a reliable and concise overview. The methodology prioritizes authentic narrations, as the author leverages his mastery of Hadith to filter the vast historical record into a coherent, chronological narrative. It covers the Prophet’s life from birth to death, including his physical descriptions (shama'il) and specific characteristics (khasa'is), making it an indispensable foundation for anyone beginning a serious study of Islamic history.

The significance of Al-Fusul lies in its balance between brevity and scholarly depth; it provides the essential milestones of the Sira without the exhaustive detail found in his larger work, Al-Bidayah wa-l-Nihayah. The text is structured to facilitate easy memorization and review, offering a sober and academic tone that honors the Prophetic legacy through rigorous verification. For the modern student, it remains a primary source that reconnects the heart to the Prophetic example while maintaining the highest standards of traditional historical criticism.

description_short:
Imam Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH), the renowned historian and exegete, authored this work as a brilliant distillation of the Prophetic biography, specifically tailored for students of knowledge seeking a reliable and concise overview. The methodology prioritizes authentic narrations, as the author leverages his mastery of Hadith to filter the vast historical record into a coherent, chronological narrative. It covers the Prophet’s life from birth to death, including his physical descriptions (shama'il) and specific characteristics (khasa'is), making it an indispensable foundation for anyone beginning a serious study of Islamic history.

The significance of Al-Fusul lies in its balance between brevity and scholarly depth; it provides the essential milestones of the Sira without the exhaustive detail found in his larger work, Al-Bidayah wa-l-Nihayah. The text is structured to facilitate easy memorization and review, offering a sober and academic tone that honors the Prophetic legacy through rigorous verification. For the modern student, it remains a primary source that reconnects the heart to the Prophetic example while maintaining the highest standards of traditional historical criticism.

The work organizes a vast range of Qur’anic disciplines into clear chapters, covering topics such as revelation, compilation, qira’at, linguistic features, rhetoric, abrogation, reasons for revelation, classification of verses, and the methods of tafsir. name: The life of the Salaf, between word and deed (+1300 pages)
description_short:
Hayat al-Salaf Bayna al-Qawl wal-Amal ("The Life of the Salaf Between Speech and Action") by Ahmad bin Nasir al-Tayyar is a profound, wide-ranging compilation of biographical accounts and classical narratives detailing the lives of the early righteous generations. The book directly addresses a critical and recurring spiritual malady: the modern disconnect between acquiring theoretical religious knowledge and actually manifesting it in practical, daily action.

Al-Tayyar methodically structures the work into comprehensive thematic chapters, exploring core Islamic virtues such as absolute sincerity (Ikhlas), deep-seated fear of Allah, genuine humility, rigorous night prayers (Qiyam al-Layl), and detachment from worldly distractions (Zuhd). Rather than relying on abstract concepts, the author provides hundreds of inspiring, documented historical examples showing exactly how the Companions and early Imams structurally mirrored their creed in their deeds. It serves as an essential manual for Tazkiyah (purification of the soul) and a practical roadmap for readers seeking self-rectification.

name: Tafsir al-Qurtubi - Al-Jami' li Ahkam al-Quran
description_short:
This is one of the finest Tafsirs focusing on legal verses while covering the entire Qur'an. This unique tafsir systematically addresses reasons for revelation, variant recitations, linguistic analysis, hadith authentication, rare vocabulary, and jurisprudential opinions from early and later scholars.

Al-Qurtubi's methodology includes extensive citation of Arabic poetry and critical engagement with predecessors like Ibn Jarir, Ibn Atiyyah, and Ibn al-Arabi. He avoided most storytelling traditions and Israelite narratives while refuting philosophers, Mu'tazila, and extreme Sufis.

Despite being Maliki, al-Qurtubi objectively discusses all legal schools, following evidence over sectarian loyalty. His fair approach led him to defend positions criticized by fellow Malikis. The work distinguishes itself by combining comprehensive Qur'anic commentary with detailed legal analysis, making it indispensable for scholars and students.

name: Adh-Dhari'ah: Explanation of ash-Shari'ah by Al-Ajurri by Shaykh Rabee'
description_short:
This work is a focused explanatory study on Kitab Ash-Shari‘ah by Imam Al-Ajurry, one of the foundational early texts of Sunni creed. Shaykh Rabi‘ ibn Hadi Al-Madkhali does not rewrite or abridge the original work, but rather clarifies its objectives, themes, and methodological intent, helping the reader understand why Imam Al-Ajurry structured the book as he did and what doctrinal principles it aims to establish.

The book is especially useful for students of ‘aqidah who wish to approach Ash-Shari‘ah with proper context and balance. It highlights the Salafi foundations of the text, addresses common misunderstandings, and situates the work within the broader tradition of early Sunni responses to theological deviations, while remaining anchored to textual evidence and scholarly transmission.

name: Al-Ma'ani al-Imaniya fi Sharh al-Asma al-Husna ar-Rabbaniya
description_short:
Here is a rare book. Composed of three volumes, 100% harakat, it deals with a complete and very thorough the most noble topic of all: The names of Allah ta'ala. The methodology and depth explanations of sublime names of Allah is unique and we often sought as a complete book on the subject.

Indeed for each name he established his linguistic reality, cites verses and hadiths that mention it. Then he explains the meaning of the name and the fruit it brings in the faith of the believer and also its implications. His words are almost exclusively quotes from great imams of the Sunnah.

The author has received numerous ijaza and studied with many great Salafi chouyoukhs. For this particular topic, the names and attributes of Allah, we know that good about it and the high quality of this book, for the rest we rely on Allah and do not do praise nor critical. We propose this book as it is a desired and important topic, but rarely so deeply processed, and all harakats at that. But it stops there because we do not know enough about the sheikh on the remaining issues of Aqeedah and Minhaj.

name: Zaad al-Maseer fi 'ilm at-Tafseer - Ibn al-Jawzi
description_short:
Among the most beneficial and carefully edited tafsirs in collecting the opinions of the exegetes, authored by Imam Ibn al-Jawzi (d. 597 AH) as a middle ground between his larger “al-Mughni” and his abridgment “Tadhkirat al-Arib.” It gathers the sayings of the Salaf and the leading scholars in a concise, precise style that is neither tediously long nor insufficiently short. It brings together the branches of tafsir in each verse: the opinions of the commentators numbered and attributed, the occasions of revelation, the abrogating and abrogated, the variant readings and their justifications, the clarification of unusual words with poetic evidence, and the fiqh rulings connected to the verse — all in Ibn al-Jawzi’s characteristically effortless yet rigorous prose where not a word is wasted.

A tafsir that spares the intermediate student from consulting many other books, and one that Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah himself relied upon to survey the various positions in tafsir. Among the finest works Ibn al-Jawzi produced across his more than three hundred titles.

name: Badaa-i' al-Fawaa-id - Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
description_short:
A uniquely woven book unlike any other in Ibn al-Qayyim's body of work, and unlike any other book entirely. Following the tradition of scholars who recorded whatever insights, rarities, and gems crossed their path — regardless of subject — he gathered between its covers linguistic and grammatical investigations, exegetical flashes, discussions of fiqh and usul, creedal questions, spiritual reflections, and poetic evidence, moving from one topic to the next without ever tiring the reader because each insight is a world unto itself.

The book is dominated by linguistic and grammatical investigations, but its real value lies in opening a window onto how Ibn al-Qayyim thinks — how he reads a verse, how he extracts meaning from a hadith, how he discusses and debates with his teacher Ibn Taymiyyah. One of Ibn al-Qayyim's wonders that no student of knowledge can do without.

name: Mutammimah al-Ajrumiyyah - al-Hattab al-Ru'ayni - 100% harakat
description_short:
Mutammimat al-Ajrumiyyah fi 'Ilm al-Arabiyyah by the Maliki jurist and grammarian Shams al-Din al-Hattab (d. 954 AH) is a classic intermediate primer designed to expand upon Ibn Ajurrum's foundational Al-Muqaddimah al-Ajrumiyyah. The author methodically supplements the original text by filling in essential grammatical chapters and fine nuances that were either condensed or omitted. It details the conditions of nominal and verbal sentences, case inflections (i'rab), irregular noun patterns, and operative particles with balanced precision.

By bridging the divide between elementary grammar and expansive works such as Qatr al-Nada or Alfiyyah Ibn Malik, al-Hattab delivers a structured pedagogical manual free from tedious dialectical debates. Its clarity of expression, systematic definitions, and reliance on standard classical citations have cemented its status as an indispensable curriculum text across traditional seminaries and university language faculties.

name: Al-Iqna' fi Halla Alfadh Abi Shuja' - Al-Khatib Ash-Shirbini (Shafii)
description_short:
Al-Iqna' is a preeminent commentary on the classical Matn of Abu Shuja' in Shafi'i jurisprudence. Written by the renowned Egyptian scholar Al-Khatib al-Shirbini (died 977 AH), this work is famous for its clarity and its sharp focus on the linguistic and legal roots of the school. It serves as an essential pedagogical bridge, guiding students from the brief summaries of the original text into a deeper understanding of evidence and reasoning without the daunting length of massive encyclopedias.

The work is highly regarded for its systematic breakdown of technical terminology and its consistent use of scriptural evidence (dalil) to substantiate legal rulings. Al-Shirbini maintains a disciplined, accessible style that avoids excessive scholarly disputes, making it the preferred textbook for intermediate students in the Shafi'i tradition. Its enduring presence as a cornerstone of the Al-Azhar curriculum for centuries is a testament to its reliability and its effectiveness in anchoring complex legal concepts through clear, verified academic methodology.
searchable_keywords: Al-Iqna' fi Halla Alfadh Abi Shuja' - Al-Khatib Ash-Shirbini (Shafii)

name: Nur ul Idah fil-Fiqh al-Hanafi - Ash-Shurunbulali (harakat)
description_short:
Nūr al-Idāḥ wa Najāt al-Arwāḥ is one of the most widely studied beginner-level texts in Hanafi Fiqh, especially in the fields of purification and worship. Written by the renowned Egyptian scholar Hasan al-Shurunbulali (d. 1069H), the book presents the practical rulings of Taharah (purification), Salah (prayer), Zakah, Sawm (fasting), and Hajj in a clear and structured format.

The author avoids theoretical debate and focuses on practical, applicable rulings based on the relied-upon positions in the Hanafi school. It became a standard primer in traditional madrasah systems and is often studied with its famous commentary Maraqi al-Falah.

name: Mukhtasar al-Quduri fil-Fiqh al-Hanafi
description_short:
Mukhtasar al-Quduri is one of the most authoritative and widely studied foundational texts in Hanafi Fiqh. Authored by Imam Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Quduri (d. 428H), this compact manual systematically presents legal rulings across all major chapters of Islamic law: purification, prayer, zakah, fasting, Hajj, transactions, family law, judiciary, criminal law, and more.

The text is known for its precision, balance, and conciseness, and it became a cornerstone of the Hanafi legal tradition. For centuries, it has served as a central reference for students, scholars, and jurists, and many major commentaries have been written upon it, such as al-Jawhar al-Naqi and al-Lubab.

name: Al-I'tibaar fin-Naasikh wal-Mansookh fil-Hadeeth - Al-Hafidh al-Hazimi (584H)
description_short:
Here is a book about a sharp and important subject of Hadith : repealing and repealed. This book is among the most famous writings in this area, from the hand of a great scholar , Hafidh , pious and Muhaddith , Abu Bakr al- Hazimi ( 584H ).
The author begins his presentation on the Nasikh wal-Mansukh with a long introduction explaining this important science. Then the book is written in chapters of Fiqh, and for each subject which are repealed, he cites the issue, then lists the hadiths and their pathways that have been repealed and those who have abrogated, sometimes he discussed the issue and ikhtilaf ulema above, he comments too.
 
Although the book is already great as it may, it is presented in an edition boasting a sharp upstream research on the subject and the particular book, in which the researcher identifies and classifies ahaadith identified by the author. It also performs important annotations on the hadiths cited their reference and authenticity. Finally there is a summary of research by verses, hadiths and by personalities.

It is therefore, in 8 volumes, one of its most important explanations by the great scholar Fakhr ad-Din ar-Raazi al-Jassaas (305-380H), author of the famous Tafseer "Ahkam al-Quran" .

This great work comes to us in a checked and referenced edition, which is the result of four doctoral theses presented at the University of Umm al-Qurra of Makkah.

name: A-Sarim al-Munki fi r-Rad ala as-Subki - ibn Abdel Hadi
description_short:
Story of the book: Everything revolves around visiting graves, visiting mosques and visiting the Prophet sallallaahu alayhi wa sallam. Between what is legislated and what is forbidden and innovated.

Originally Shaykh al-Islam ibn Taymiyyah wrote a rebuttal to one of his contemporaries: Al-Ikhnaa-ee. After the death of Ibn Taymiyyah, rahimahullaah, another of his critics at the time, Imam as-Subki, so wrote a rebuttal to the refutation of ibn Taymiyyah known as the "Shifa-u s-fi Saqam Ziyarati Khayri l-Anam ". However, this book is filled with weak and invented hadeeth and the author distorted the real opinion of Shaykh al-Islam on various topics.

Imam al-Hafidh Ibn Abdel Hadi, famous student of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, thus refuted him so perfectly that it is said that his book is the most comprehensive in its field (visit tombs, mosques and the Prophet sallallaahu alayhi wa sallam). He refutes the hadeeth used by as-Subki one by one and the implications he claims, as he relates the real opinion of his Sheikh to answer charges of as-Subki.

An outstanding book in a secure editing and verified by 3 Muhaqqiqat from four manuscripts.

name: Topics of Aqeedah in which some scholars Hanbali diverged
description_short:
Here is a Magisterium thesis entitled: Issues of Aqeedah in which diverged some of Jurists Hanbali with the Imam of Madhhab (ie Imam Ahmad).

In fact, the majority of Fuqaha Hanabila was on the Aqeedah Saheehah, and this book classifies errors by subject according to the books of Fiqh and chapters related thereto and cites the divergent positions and that of the madhhab and the one of Imam Ahmad and of course give the evidence. Examples of topics: The Names and Attributes of Allah, invocations in groups, praying in churches, Tawassul, construction on the graves, reading the Qur'an for the dead, sticking and Tawaf among tombs, visit the grave of the Prophet sallallaahu alayhi wa sallam, swear by his name, visit the graves for women ...

This book is useful for all because most topics are errors in which many scholars have fallen among other mathaahib, and it is therefore important to know.

name: Kitaab ar-Rooh by ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
description_short:
This is a book in which Imam Ibn al-Qayyim raises the issue of the soul that was not mentioned in other books of the predecessors. It contains information about the soul and the spirit, the difference between them, the relationship of the soul to the body, and its fate after death. He based his analysis upon the Qur’an and the Sunnah and supported his arguments with proofs from the two revelations, and from reason and logic.

The famous book on the Soul written by Ibn al-Qayyim in a safe and verified edition.

name: Wujoob al-Hijrah fi Sabeeli Llah - The obligation of Hijrah
description_short:
A booklet on the Hijra and its obligation, written by a professor specialized in the Quran and Tafseer, which makes thorough an exegesis of the famous verse in Surah al-Nisaa on Hijrah:

(Indeed, those whom the angels take [in death] while wronging themselves - [the angels] will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell - and evil it is as a destination.) An-Nisa.! 97.

The author explains the context of the revelation, explains all terms of the verse and goes all the benefits and rules that may have drawn from this noble verse (43 Fawaid and Ahkaam).

No student of the Quran in the Muslim world has not memorized it or heard it recited. The Jazariyyah by Imam Muhammad ibn al-Jazari (d. 833 AH) is the undisputed mother-text of the science of tajweed. In 109 lines it covers the core rules of tajweed: the articulation points and characteristics of letters, the rules of nun sakinah and tanwin, the lengthenings (mudud), the rules of stopping and starting, and the etiquettes of recitation. A precise, comprehensive poem that has been the first text given to the student of Quranic recitation in memorization circles and teaching assemblies for centuries.
This edition, verified by Sheikh Ayman Rushdi Suwayd, one of the foremost contemporary authorities in tajweed, is a premium large-format edition (12×17 cm) with elegant layout, high-quality printing, and 100% Harakat (tashkil). name: Irwa al-Ghalil by shaykh al-Albani
description_short:
Irwa' al-Ghalil is a monumental masterpiece of modern Hadith scholarship and a cornerstone in the science of Takhrij (Hadith verification). In this multi-volume work, Sheikh Muhammad Nasiruddin al-Albani meticulously verifies and grades the thousands of narrations found in Manar al-Sabil, a famous primer of Hanbali jurisprudence. The Sheikh does not merely state the authenticity of a Hadith; he provides a deep, investigative analysis of the chains of narration (Asanid), citing the judgments of classical scholars of Jarh wa Ta'dil and offering his own expert conclusions. This work is credited with reviving the rigor of Hadith methodology in the contemporary era, bridging the gap between Fiqh manuals and the primary sources of the Sunnah.

For the serious student of knowledge and the researcher, this book is an indispensable laboratory of Hadith science. It demonstrates how to trace narrations across hundreds of classical sources and how to apply the technical rules of the discipline to determine a Hadith's grade. Beyond its technical utility, the book serves as a vital companion to the study of Hanbali law, ensuring that the practitioner’s legal rulings are built upon the solid foundation of authentic Prophetic traditions. It is widely considered one of the Sheikh’s greatest intellectual legacies and a primary reference for anyone specializing in the verification of the Sunnah.

name: Fataawa al-Baghawee (516H)
description_short:
This volume is a prestigious collection of the legal verdicts (Fatawa) of Imam al-Baghawi, the renowned Shafi'i jurist, Hadith master (Hafidh), and polymath. Known as "Reviver of the Sunnah," al-Baghawi is the celebrated author of two of Islam's most foundational works: Sharh as-Sunnah in Hadith and Ma'alim at-Tanzil (widely known as Tafsir al-Baghawi). This collection provides a rare and direct window into the jurisprudential methodology of an Imam who stood as a pillar of the Salaf’s tradition, bridging the sciences of revelation with the practical application of the law.

The work contains a total of 888 fatwas meticulously classified by thematic legal topics, covering a wide array of worship (Ibadat) and social transactions (Mu'amalat). It serves as a scholarly treasure for students of the Shafi'i school and researchers of early Islamic jurisprudence, offering clear, authoritative answers rooted in the Prophetic tradition. Having access to these verdicts allows the reader to appreciate the profound depth and balance of al-Baghawi’s scholarship, making it an essential addition to any library dedicated to the classical sciences.

name: Disavowal of 4 Imams from Innovations of the Mutakallimin
description_short:
This scholarly work investigates the theological stances of the four great Imams—Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal—clarifying their adherence to the way of the Salaf (pious predecessors). Dr. Abd al-Aziz al-Humaydi meticulously demonstrates that the founders of the major schools of jurisprudence remained entirely free from the innovative philosophical and speculative methods (Kalam) that later emerged. By citing their authentic statements and documented beliefs, the author proves that the Imams prioritized textual revelation over the abstract rationalism of the Mutakallimun.

The book serves as a rigorous academic defense against the historical claims that the four Imams shared the complex theological frameworks of later scholastic sects. Dr. al-Humaydi establishes clear criteria for distinguishing the simple, scriptural creed of the early Imams from the innovative terminologies and debates introduced by later theologians. It is an essential resource for students of Aqidah (Creed) and Islamic history, providing the necessary evidence to reconnect the foundational legal schools with their original, orthodox theological roots.

name: Qa'idah Mukhtasar fi Qital al-Kuffar - Ibn Taymiya (harakat)
description_short:
This book is a classical legal treatise addressing the conditions of fighting and making peace with non-Muslims, written by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728 AH). The work clarifies a critical principle in Islamic jurisprudence: that the legal justification for fighting non-Muslims is active aggression (hirab) against Muslims, not their mere disbelief (kufr). It provides an essential reference for understanding traditional Islamic rules of engagement, clearly distinguishing between combatants and peaceful non-combatants.
The text is organized around scriptural evidences from the Quran and Sunnah, alongside the historical practices of the Prophet Muhammad and the early Companions. Ibn Taymiyyah analyzes the various treaties and truces established in early Islamic history to demonstrate that peace is the foundational state when aggression is absent. He systematically refutes the notion that Islam sanctions the killing of peaceful individuals due to their faith, detailing the legal protections guaranteed to non-Muslim citizens (Dhimmi) and those under peace covenants (Mu'ahid).
The text has been established, verified, and deeply annotated by Dr. Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah al-Zeer Al Hamad, who also provided a comprehensive and beneficial introductory study. This volume features a clean layout, clear typography, and full tashkil (100% Harakat).

name: Stories of Prophets by shaykh As-Sadi
description_short:
Qisas al-Anbiya' by Sheikh Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir al-Sa'di (d. 1376 AH) presents the lives and monotheistic missions of the Quranic prophets from Adam to Muhammad (peace be upon them) with remarkable clarity, conciseness, and sound textual grounding. Completely free from unverified Isra'iliyyat and dense historical digressions, it stands as one of the shortest, simplest, and most accessible introductory books to begin with on the subject of Quranic prophetic stories.

Rather than offering a mere chronological chronicle, the author methodically highlights the core theological tenets, moral virtues, and educational guidance derived from each prophet's mission. This concise and practical study is drawn directly from the author's thematic exegesis, Taysir al-Latif al-Mannan fi Khulasat Tafsir al-Qur'an.
category_paths: Home>History & Biography>Stories of the Prophets (Qisas al-Anbiya)

name: I'raab Al-Alfiat (ibn Maalik) - 2 volumes
description_short:
I'rab al-Alfiyyah (historically known as Tamrin al-Tullab fi I'rab Alfiyyah Ibn Malik) by the celebrated 9th-century AH grammarian Khalid al-Azhari is a classical masterpiece in practical Arabic syntax.

Rather than focusing purely on theoretical rules, this work serves as an exhaustive, verse-by-verse grammatical parsing guide for Ibn Malik's famous 1,000-verse poem (Alfiyyah). It deconstructs the structural components of each line, outlining the operational roles of the nouns, verbs, particles, and hidden pronouns. This text remains an indispensable training manual for advanced students looking to bridge the gap between understanding grammatical theory and masterfully applying parsing (I'rab) to complex classical literature.

description_short:

A specialized work on distinguishing the balanced manhaj of Ahl al-Sunnah from the extremism of the Haddadiyyah who departed from the way of the Salaf in the name of Salafiyyah. Suited for the student who wants to understand this fitnah in detail and with evidence.

name: Ar-Risalah at-Tabukiyyah - Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
description_short:
al-Risalah al-Tabukiyyah is a profound spiritual and intellectual treatise by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, written during his journey to the region of Tabuk. In this work, the author reflects deeply on the verse:

{فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ} (So race toward all that is good), and builds around it a complete roadmap for the believer's journey toward Allah.

The book explores two fundamental themes: seeking Allah’s pleasure (talab al-marḍāt) and fleeing from His punishment (firar min al-muqaddar), emphasizing that true servitude requires movement with both love and fear. It also touches on the states of the heart, sincerity, patience, striving, and the dangers of spiritual stagnation. Though short in size, the work is extremely rich in meaning and deeply rooted in the Qur’an and Sunnah.

The book explores two fundamental themes: seeking Allah’s pleasure (talab al-marḍāt) and fleeing from His punishment (firar min al-muqaddar), emphasizing that true servitude requires movement with both love and fear. It also touches on the states of the heart, sincerity, patience, striving, and the dangers of spiritual stagnation. Though short in size, the work is extremely rich in meaning and deeply rooted in the Qur’an and Sunnah.

name: Tayseer al-Lateef al-Manaan (Tafsir summarized of Sheikh as-Sa'di)
description_short:
Taysir al-Latif al-Mannan is a unique and masterful work by Sheikh Abdurrahman as-Sa'di, the author of the world-renowned Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman (Tafsir al-Sa'di). In this volume, he provides a thematic summary of the Qur'an, distilling the essence of his lifelong expertise in exegesis into a highly accessible format. Unlike traditional verse-by-verse commentaries, this book organizes the message of the divine revelation into its major objectives, such as the principles of Tawhid, the stories of the Prophets, legal rulings, and ethical manners.

The methodology focuses on extracting the core lessons and universal benefits of the Qur'an in a streamlined narrative style. Sheikh as-Sa'di avoids technical complexities, highlighting instead the coherence and wisdom of the Qur'anic guidance. Written toward the end of his life, it serves as the final synthesis of his scholarship, offering an indispensable birds-eye view of the scripture's message for both students and general readers looking to understand how the various themes of the Qur'an interconnect to guide the believer's daily life.

name: Fadaail a-Quran - Ibn Kathir
description_short:
Fada'il al-Qur'an (Virtues of the Quran) is a significant work by the illustrious Imam, Hafidh, and exegete Ibn Kathir (d. 774H). This book compiles the virtues, merits, and special characteristics of various Surahs and verses of the Quran, gathering traditions and narrations to encourage Muslims to engage more deeply with the Divine scripture, motivating them toward memorization, understanding its meanings, and acting upon its teachings.

The work presents Hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ, sayings of the Companions and Salaf, and scholarly insights on the specific rewards and spiritual benefits of reciting and reflecting upon particular parts of the Quran. Such compilations hold a special place in Islamic tradition, fostering love and reverence for the Quran.

name: Nasiha for my son - Ibn al-Jawzi (100% harakat)
description_short:
A letter full of advice written by Imam ibn al-Jawzi for his son entilted : Laftatu al-Kabad ila Nasihati al-Walad. I'll let you read the summary of an anonymous reader found on the internet:

"A father talking to his son. That is the express summary of this book! An anguished father for the future of his son and his relationship with his religion.

He decided to write him this letter, full of good advice, exhortation, showing him the direction to follow: the importance of seeking knowledge, learning the Quran and its merits and virtues of asceticism, discretion and live retired from the worries of this world. We also learn to regret the past acts, multiplied good works.

A tender book, where each player to feel this son whose father says his concern about his fate and lavishing many helpful advice."

name: Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari li Ibn Battal (449H)
description_short:
One of the earliest and most important commentaries on Sahih al-Bukhari, composed by Imam Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Khalaf ibn Battal al-Qurtubi then al-Balansi (d. 449 AH), a leading Maliki jurist of al-Andalus. The commentary is distinguished by its primarily jurisprudential character: it focuses on the legal rulings derived from al-Bukhari's hadiths, presents the disagreements among the Companions, the Tabi'in, and the founders of the legal schools with each side's evidence, and pays particular attention to al-Bukhari's tarajim — his chapter headings — explaining their meaning, al-Bukhari's intent behind them, and their connection to the hadiths placed under them.

This sharh is one of the most important sources used by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani in his "Fath al-Bari," from which he quoted extensively, drew upon, and engaged in discussion. An essential reference for anyone seeking to understand the jurisprudential dimension of Sahih al-Bukhari and the paths of reasoning the Imams followed in dealing with hadiths of legal rulings.

This premium, high-quality Saudi edition features a comprehensive research summary. In addition to standard indexes (verses, Hadiths, and Athar), it includes a highly practical index by Fiqh topics, making thematic research exceptionally easy.

name: Al-Kafi fi Fiqh al-Imam Ahmad - Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdissi
description_short:
Al-Kafi by Imam Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdisi (d. 620H) is one of the foundational works of the Hanbali school of jurisprudence, written by one of its most authoritative jurists. It serves as a comprehensive manual that presents the established rulings of the madhhab with clarity, conciseness, and careful organization, free from excessive debate or detailed evidence, making it ideal for memorization and systematic study.

The book covers the full range of Fiqh topics — worship, transactions, personal status, judiciary, and criminal law — summarizing the relied-upon (mu‘tamad) positions in the Hanbali madhhab. It stands between Ibn Qudamah’s abridged ‘Umdat al-Fiqh and his encyclopedic al-Mughni, representing the balanced and accessible middle level of his legal scholarship.

name: Minhaj as-Sunnah an-Nabawiyah - Ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
The most expansive and comprehensive work Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728 AH) ever produced on establishing the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah in the questions of the Caliphate, the Imamah, the ranking of the Companions, divine decree, and the attributes of Allah. Written in refutation of “Minhaj al-Karamah fi Ithbat al-Imamah” by the Shi’i scholar Ibn al-Mutahhar al-Hilli and the Twelver Imami doctrine, it went far beyond a simple response into an encyclopedic work of over two hundred chapters: verifying the hadiths and historical reports related to the era of the Companions and the fitnah, engaging the methods of the mutakallimun and philosophers on the divine attributes and the origination of the world, and grounding the position of Ahl al-Sunnah in evidence on every question — with a breadth of knowledge and depth of investigation scarcely found elsewhere.

Among the greatest works Ibn Taymiyyah ever produced, and the need for it today is no less than the day it was written — it only grows with the spread of Shi’ism and the dissemination of its doubts. A book no library of a student of knowledge can be without, and no one who takes up the defense of the creed and methodology of Ahl al-Sunnah can dispense with.
