name: Ar-Riqqah wal-Bukaae - Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdissi
description_short:
Ar-Riqqatu wal-Bukaae (sensibility and tears) is a book of Imam Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi on high-facts of the Salaf, their noble characters, the stories of the best beings that serve as examples, reminders, that put us in front of our failures and weaknesses.

Ibn Qudama ranked his book by time, by first citing some passages of all life and the person of the Messenger of Allah sallallaahu alayhi wa sallam, including his death, then the rightly guided caliphs the sahabas, then tabi'ins, and finally those who followed them.

A whole series of biographies that serve as examples to all of us.

Verified and authenticated edition.

name: Al-Hidayah ila Bulugh an-Nihayah - Makki Al-Qissi (437H)
description_short:
The author is named Mekki ibn Abi Talib al-Qissi (355-437H) is a great scholar native of Qayrawan, Tunisia. He will travel to Egypt, Arabia and Andalusia where he will study with the greatest scholars of his time, Mention may be made in in his hometown as one of its Shaykh none other than ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani, the famous "Little Malik" author of ar-Risalah Treaty.

What makes this unique is Tafseer is first author, who had accumulated a lot of science in the Quran and Tafseer which he summarized and selected the best to deliver this great Tafsir.

And Al-Qissi is as his Shaykh al-Qayrawani, Salafi in Aqeedah, Maliki in madhhab. His words are clear in the names and attributes.

And so overall his Tafsir is excellent and relevant.

Add to that a thorough Tahqiq which is the result of several theses doctarat from the University of Fez, you have in your hands an absolutely beautiful and important book that we recommend all heart...

name: Fatwas on contemporary issues (preface Fawzan & Mufti)
description_short:
Fataawa ash-Shar'iyyah fi Qadaaya al-'Asriyyah is a carefully compiled collection of fatawa from some of the most prominent scholars of Saudi Arabia, including Shaykh Ibn Baz, Shaykh al-Uthaymeen, Shaykh Salih al-Fawzan, Shaykh ‘Abd al-‘Aziz Aal ash-Shaykh, Shaykh al-Luhaydan, and others.

The book focuses on major contemporary issues that have affected the Muslim world in recent decades. It addresses sensitive and often misunderstood topics such as takfir, rebellion against Muslim rulers, political unrest, jihad, and specific events and figures, including discussions related to Osama bin Laden and acts of bombing. The fatawa aim to clarify the positions of recognized scholars on these matters, based on established principles of the religion.

The work is introduced by several senior scholars, including Shaykh Salih al-Fawzan, the Grand Mufti Shaykh ‘Abd al-‘Aziz Aal ash-Shaykh, Shaykh ‘Abd al-Muhsin al-‘Ubaykan, and Shaykh Muhammad ibn Hasan Aal ash-Shaykh, which reflects the importance and endorsement of the subject matter.

name: Manhaj al-Albani fi Takhreej
description_short:
The methodology of Sheikh al-Albani in Takhrij, ie referencing ahaadeeth and different chains of transmission, but also the judgment given them: Sahih, Hasan, Da'if.

The author of this research (thesis magisterium obtained excellent mention) takes a median position in outlining the methodology of Sheikh, his place and his choices in the science of Hadith and Fiqh, and he also cites his contemporaries who were in divergence with him (either on some TasHiH or some TaD 'if, or on the use of hadith Da'if).

Research is honest, neither passionate nor spiteful, but tries to demonstrate the place of Sheikh in the field of hadith, his methodology in comparison to his predecessors among muhaddithins, Hadith he rendered authentic or weak on which his contemporaries, Salafi or not, have disagreed, and why.

name: Al-Fitan wal-Malaahim - Ibn Katheer (An-Nihaayah)
description_short:
Al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim by the renowned historian, exegete, and Hadith master Imam Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH) is one of the most authoritative classical references on Islamic eschatology. The work is dedicated to documenting the prophecies and events of the end of times, providing a comprehensive narrative of the minor and major signs of the Hour, the emerging trials (fitan), apocalyptic conflicts (malahim), the appearance of the Mahdi and the Dajjal, the descent of Isa (Jesus), and the eventual destruction of the world followed by the Day of Judgment, the Resurrection, and the eternal abodes of Paradise and Hellfire.

The text originally forms the final section of Imam Ibn Kathir’s monumental universal history encyclopedia, Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, where the author transitioned from chronicling the history of creation and past nations to chronicling the future history of humanity based on divine revelation. In compiling this work, Ibn Kathir applied his rigorous Hadith scholarship by systematically gathering textual proofs from the Quran, prophetic traditions, and early narrations, critically examining their chains of transmission and harmonizing apparent discrepancies to present a lucid and sound chronology of future events.
category_paths: Home>History & Biography>The Unseen & End of Times (Al-Ghaybiyat)

name: At-Turuq al-Hukmiyah - Ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
al-Turuq al-Hukmiyyah fi al-Siyasah al-Shar‘iyyah is one of the most important classical works on Islamic legal governance and public policy. In this groundbreaking book, Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah explores how a Muslim ruler or judge (qadi) can apply the principles of Shari‘ah in achieving justice, preserving rights, and managing society — even when no explicit textual evidence exists for a particular case.

The book addresses judicial procedures, investigation, evidence, discretionary punishments (ta‘zir), appointing judges, and the qualifications of rulers. Ibn al-Qayyim emphasizes that the ultimate goal of Islamic governance is justice, and that strict literalism must be balanced with maqasid (objectives) and wisdom (hikmah). His treatment of criminal law, social regulation, and administrative judgment makes this work a foundational reference in Islamic legal-political thought.

This text remains highly relevant for scholars, judges, and students of Islamic law and governance, especially in discussions of policy, judicial discretion, and the dynamic application of Shari‘ah principles in real-world contexts.

We also offer on our site the summary of this work by Shaykh al-Uthaymeen

name: Mukhtasar Khalil - Harakat (Fiqh Maliki)
description_short:
Mukhtasar Khalil is the undisputed crown jewel of Maliki jurisprudence and the primary reference for legal rulings within the school. Compiled by the 14th-century Egyptian scholar Khalil ibn Ishaq al-Jundi (d. 776 AH), this text is celebrated for its incredible density, condensing the vast sea of Maliki legal thought into a precise and comprehensive manual. It serves as the definitive authority for identifying the Mu'tamad (relied-upon) positions of the school, covering everything from the intricate details of worship to the complexities of inheritance and commercial law.

The work is a masterpiece of linguistic economy and academic discipline. Khalil meticulously filtered through the opinions of earlier masters to provide the most accurate and preferred legal views, creating a text that has guided jurists, judges, and students across the Maghreb, West Africa, and beyond for centuries.

100% harakat.

name: Aqidatu at-Tawhid al-Kubra - al-Makki ibn 'Azuz at-Tunisi
description_short:
Very interesting! The author of these two Treaties of Aqeedah is a Tunisian Maliki scholar almost contemporary of Imam Muhammad ibn Abdelwahhab (he was born 70 years after the death of Imam).

Having learned and taught religion in Algeria (his father had immigrated due to the French colonization), but also in Tunisia, he traveled and head out in search of the truth about what is already called at the time the Wahhabi of Arabia. His quest for truth and sincerity will therefore lead to the Cham and Arabia and so he finds himself with the reality of the Salafiyyah and the truth of his way, he will follow thereafter.

This book brings together two treaties: Aqidah at-Tawhid al-Kubra and Aqeedah at-Tawheed as Sughra. 2 are presented with all harakats and verified from manuscripts. As for the Aqeedah al-Kubrait has plenty of annotations by the Muhaqqiq.

Therefore we recommend that Treaty of Salafiyyah Aqeedah written by a great scholar Maliki who made the effort to seek the truth and go beyond hearsay and prejudice.

name: Rad ad-Darimi 'ala Bishr al-Marisi al-Jahmi - Naqd 'Uthman ad-Darimi
description_short:
A monumental work among the most important compositions refuting the Jahmiyyah, compiled by Imam al-Hafiz Abu Sa'id 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darmi (d. 280 AH), the learned scholar of Khorasan renowned for his fierce defense of the Sunnah and refutation of people of innovation. The book contains a systematic refutation and exposition of the errors and fabrications of Bishr al-Marisi the Jahmite and his sophistries regarding tawhid and the divine attributes, alongside the affirmation of truth grounded in the Quran, the prophetic Sunnah, and the statements of the Companions and scholars. The author proceeds in a methodical and precise manner in refuting the doubts and false claims, supported throughout by Quranic evidence and the prophetic tradition.

This work is counted among the vital preserved testimonies to the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-al-Jama'ah and the defense of monotheism against Jahmite distortion and denial of the divine attributes. Great scholars praised al-Darmi, including Yahya ibn Mu'in and Abu Zur'a al-Razi, who spoke of his excellences and brilliance in composition. Al-Dhahabi said of him: 'Uthman al-Darmi was strong in the sight of the people of innovation — meaning fierce and formidable in combating bid'ah.

An excellent edition — the most reliable, as it has been verified against four manuscripts, with 100% harakat (fully vocalized).

name: Fath Dhil-Jalali wal-Ikram bi Sharh Bulugh al-Maram - Al-Uthaymin
description_short:
Fath Dhi al-Jalal wa al-Ikram is the monumental and highly celebrated explanation of Bulugh al-Maram min Adillat al-Ahkam, the famous collection of legal hadiths compiled by Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani. Authored by the great jurist Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih al-'Uthaymin, this extensive work stands as one of the most beneficial contemporary resources for studying the jurisprudence of the Sunnah.

The Shaykh applies his signature pedagogical methodology to each narration: he meticulously unpacks the linguistic meanings of the vocabulary, assesses the chain of transmission, and then extracts the legal, theological, and moral benefits in clear, numbered points. Rather than strictly adhering to the Hanbali school, the author consistently favors rulings supported by the strongest evidences (rajih). This makes the book an indispensable, evidence-based encyclopedia of fiqh that no serious student of knowledge can dispense with studying.

The official edition has been revised and expanded, and is now compiled in 9 very large volumes, with most of the text featuring harakat (tashkil).

name: Al Adhkar by imam an-Nawawi
description_short:
This seminal work is arguably the most famous collection of supplications and etiquette in the Islamic world, compiled by the legendary Imam al-Nawawi. It serves as a comprehensive encyclopedia of the Adhkar (remembrances) that a Muslim needs from the moment they wake up until they return to sleep. The methodology is remarkably systematic; Imam al-Nawawi categorizes the narrations based on specific life events, legal rulings, and spiritual states, drawing primarily from the "Six Books" of Hadith with a focus on authenticity and practical application.

The significance of Al-Adhkar lies in its dual nature as both a spiritual guide and a legal reference. Beyond providing the texts of the supplications, the author often includes scholarly commentary on the virtues of specific words and the correct manner of performance. For the Student of Knowledge (Talib al-Ilm), this book is an essential companion for building a life centered on the remembrance of Allah. Its sober, academic, yet deeply moving tone has made it a staple in Muslim households for centuries, acting as a definitive bridge between the Prophetic tradition and the daily life of the believer.

It serves as a comprehensive encyclopedia of the Adhkar (remembrances) that a Muslim needs from the moment they wake up until they return to sleep. The methodology is remarkably systematic; Imam al-Nawawi categorizes the narrations based on specific life events, legal rulings, and spiritual states, drawing primarily from the "Six Books" of Hadith with a focus on authenticity and practical application.

The significance of Al-Adhkar lies in its dual nature as both a spiritual guide and a legal reference. Beyond providing the texts of the supplications, the author often includes scholarly commentary on the virtues of specific words and the correct manner of performance. For the Student of Knowledge (Talib al-Ilm), this book is an essential companion for building a life centered on the remembrance of Allah. Its sober, academic, yet deeply moving tone has made it a staple in Muslim households for centuries, acting as a definitive bridge between the Prophetic tradition and the daily life of the believer.

description_short:
One of the most important book of Fiqh al-Furoo 'by Imam ibn Muflih al-Hanbali (763H), comparing the opinions of the 4 schools and other great imams, citing differences, consensus and majority opinion.

The book is excellent was praise from scholars of all times, such as ibn Kathir or Ibn Hajar who were almost contemporaries of ibn Muflih.

The best edition of Al-Fourou ', with Tahqiq of Dr. Abdullah at-Turki, in 12 volumes. The text of Al-Fourou 'is verified from 4 manuscripts. Next is al-Mardawi's annotation "TasHiH al-Furoo '" (885H). Also comes the comments "Hachiyyah" of Taqi ad-Din Abu Bakr ibn Qudama (861H). And finally the annotations of the Muhaqqiq on some people cited, place, or complicated term.

Harakat in part.

name: al-Muhalla by Imam ibn Hazm
description_short:
Al-Muhalla is one of the largest and most impressive books of Fiqh in existence. Adil Salahi from Muslim Heritage describes it thus:

This book is a wealth of scholarship, in which Ibn Hazm discusses each question separately. On each question, he cites the views of earlier scholars of high achievement, not restricting himself to the views of the four schools of Fiqh, but also citing the rulings of scholars like al-Hassan al-Basri (d. 110), al-Laith ibn Saad (d. 175), Ata' (d. 114), Sufyan al-Thawri (d. 161), al-Awza'ie (d. 157), etc. He also quotes the evidence they cite in support of their views. He then discusses why he considers their views incorrect, and produces the evidence in support of his own view. This makes for a highly scholarly discussion. Many scholars describe Al-Muhalla as the encyclopaedia of Islamic Fiqh. Indeed, it has preserved many of the views of early scholars whose work was either not documented or lost. The only problem with Al-Muhalla is that Ibn Hazm is often scathing in his criticism of his opponents. Yet there is no doubt that he is an honest defender of what he considers to be the truth. Any scholar who wants to exercise ijtihad, in order to arrive at rulings for questions encountered in present day life cannot overlook Al-Muhalla. 
However, this book is a must-Islamic Fiqh, for a public knowledgeable or advanced.

Imam Ibn Abd al-Salam said: "I did not see, in all the books of knowledge in Islam, anything like Ibn Hazm's al-Muhalla nor like Ibn Qudama' al-Mughni."

It is truly one of the most valuable Fiqh encyclopedias available, especially for advanced students of Fiqh.

name: 'Uyoon al-Athar  (complete Sira Nabawiya 100% harakat)
description_short:
Uyun al-Athar is a monumental work of Prophetic biography compiled by the 8th-century scholar Ibn Sayyid al-Nas. It is distinguished by its holistic approach, seamlessly integrating the Siyar (biography), Maghazi (military expeditions), and Shama'il (physical and moral characteristics) of the Prophet ﷺ. The author, a master of Hadith, utilized a vast array of primary sources, many of which are now lost, making this work a vital preservation of the early Seerah tradition.

The methodology of the book is characterized by scholarly rigor and a balanced narrative style. Unlike other works that focus solely on history, Ibn Sayyid al-Nas applies the standards of Hadith criticism to the reports he includes, often providing chains of transmission and discussing the reliability of narrators. This ensures that the reader is presented with a biography that is not only spiritually moving but also academically grounded in the authentic tradition of the Pious Predecessors.

This edition is fully voweled (100% harakat).

name: Sharh Mukhtasar al-Quduri - Al-Sindi al-Qasimi (Fiqh Hanafi)
description_short:
A simplified commentary on “Mukhtasar al-Quduri,” known as “al-Kitab,” by Imam Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Quduri al-Baghdadi (d. 428 AH) — the foundational pillar of the Hanafi school and among the first texts a student of Hanafi fiqh studies. The Mukhtasar contains approximately twelve thousand fiqh issues arranged across the standard chapters of fiqh, its expressions characteristically condensed and compressed, requiring explanation. Sheikh Mawlana Ghulam Mustafa al-Sindi al-Qasimi produced this commentary to unpack those expressions and make them accessible to the student in a clear, direct style.

Mukhtasar al-Quduri is a core text in the curriculum of Shari’ah colleges and study circles, particularly across the Indian subcontinent — no beginner can dispense with studying it, and no advanced student with consulting it. This edition from Dar Ibn Kathir has most of its tashkil.

name: Al Muharrar fi Fiqh al Imam Ash-Shafi'i - Imam ar-Rafi'i (623H)
description_short:
Dive into a Shafi‘i masterpiece that shaped Islamic law for generations.

Imam Abu Al-Qasim Al-Rafi'i (623H), a leading Shafi‘i scholar, wrote Al-Muharrar fi Fiqh Al-Imam Al-Shafi‘i as a clear, concise guide to the Shafi‘i school, building on works like Al-Ghazali’s Al-Wajiz. Its crisp prose and organized rulings, backed by Quran, Hadith, and scholarly consensus, highlight the strongest opinions while noting school variations. This text became a foundation for Al-Nawawi’s Minhaj Al-Talibin, a key source for Shafi‘i legal rulings.

In Shafi‘i circles, Al-Muharrar is prized for sharpening the school’s legal methods, blending clarity with depth. Al-Rafii’s knack for simplifying complex debates, as Ibn Al-Mulqin noted, “it lives up to its name,” makes it perfect for scholars and students alike. It remains a go-to for grasping Shafi‘i Fiqh, offering timeless insights into law and practice.

Dive into a Shafi‘i masterpiece that shaped Islamic law for generations.

Imam Abu Al-Qasim Al-Rafi'i (623H), a leading Shafi‘i scholar, wrote Al-Muharrar fi Fiqh Al-Imam Al-Shafi‘i as a clear, concise guide to the Shafi‘i school, building on works like Al-Ghazali’s Al-Wajiz. Its crisp prose and organized rulings, backed by Quran, Hadith, and scholarly consensus, highlight the strongest opinions while noting school variations. This text became a foundation for Al-Nawawi’s Minhaj Al-Talibin, a key source for Shafi‘i legal rulings.

In Shafi‘i circles, Al-Muharrar is prized for sharpening the school’s legal methods, blending clarity with depth. Al-Rafii’s knack for simplifying complex debates, as Ibn Al-Mulqin noted, “it lives up to its name,” makes it perfect for scholars and students alike. It remains a go-to for grasping Shafi‘i Fiqh, offering timeless insights into law and practice.

name: Fiqh as-Sahaabiyaat
description_short:
Book very interesting, the Fiqh of Sahabiyat (female-companions of Prophet sallallaahu alayhi wa sallam).

The author (it is a Risalah Magisterium) reports the opinions of different Sahabiyat, in order of Chapter Fiqh. For each question, she gives us the opinion of the Sahabiya and the opinion of the the Ulama and Madhahib on the subject, then debate opinions of each one and finally proposes the predominant opinion on the matter.

A well-ordered and referenced research.

name: The Qira'at reported in the Sunnah
description_short:
Two books in one around the same topic: Differences readings of the Qur'an according to hadiths narrated from the Messenger of Allah, sallallaahu alayhi wa sallam.

The first book is writing for a teacher of al-Azhar (specialized in Hadith and Head of Masahif review committee) that identifies and make the Takhrij of hadith related Qira'at, surah by surah.

Hafs Ad-Duri (246H), one reading narrator, writes the second on the same principle. Authenticated by the author of the previous search.

description_short:
Excellent work by the Grand Imam of Hadith, Imam ibn Mulaqqin (804H) teacher of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani on the specifics of the Messenger of Allah, sallallaahu alayhi wa sallam.

There are five main chapters:

  1. The specifics regarding religious obligations
  2. The specifics regarding prohibitions
  3. The specifics regarding permissions
  4. The specifics regarding benefits and miracles
  5. Among Fawaid to remember regarding the specifics of the Prophet

Edition authenticated, verified and annotated, which underlies the work of a Risalah Magisterium from University of Medina.

name: Sharh Duroos Muhimmah (ibn Baz) – Abdurrazaq al-Badr

name: Jalaa al-Afham fi Fadl Salat wa Salam ala Muhammad - Ibn al-Qayyim
description_short:
Jala' al-Afham is a comprehensive and unique masterpiece by Imam Ibn al-Qayyim dedicated to the virtues, rulings, and benefits of sending prayers and salutations upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Widely considered the most authoritative work on the subject, it meticulously gathers authentic traditions and scholarly insights, providing a profound spiritual and academic exploration of this central act of devotion in Islam.

The book is logically organized into five distinct sections, covering the primary Hadiths on the topic, the specific times and places where salutations are recommended, and the numerous spiritual and worldly benefits attained by the believer. Ibn al-Qayyim also delves into the linguistic and theological meanings of "As-Salat," offering a deep dive into the nature of the Prophetic status. It is an essential volume for anyone seeking to strengthen their connection to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ through verified traditional sources.

name: Mayyarah al-Kubra: al-Durr al-Thamin wa-l-Mawrid al-Mu’in
description_short:
Ibn ‘Ashir’s “al-Murshid al-Mu’in” (d. 1040 AH) is the most widely taught matn in Maliki fiqh across the Maghreb, gathering the essentials of Ash’ari creed, Maliki jurisprudence, and Junaydi spiritual discipline. His student Imam Muhammad ibn Ahmad Mayyarah al-Fasi (d. 1072 AH) produced this extensive commentary known as “Mayyarah al-Kubra,” explaining the poem verse by verse, drawing on the major Maliki authorities such as al-Baji and Ibn al-‘Arabi, combining precise jurisprudential analysis with a spiritual and educational dimension — connecting the rulings to their higher purposes and to tazkiyah, as Ibn ‘Ashir intended for his poem.

Among the greatest and most comprehensive commentaries on Matn Ibn ‘Ashir, indispensable for the student of Maghribi Maliki fiqh. An elegant two-volume edition edited by Dr. Rabih Zarwati, published by Dar Ibn Hazm, with hadith referencing and biographical notes on the scholars cited. The author also produced an abridgment of this commentary known as “Mayyarah al-Sughra” for those who prefer the summary, also available.

New beautiful edition from Dar Ibn Hazm in two volumes, edited by Dr. Rabih Zarwati, verified and annotated with hadith referencing and biographies of the scholars cited.

name: Mukhtar as-Sihah by ar-Razi (arabic dictionnary)
description_short:
Mukhtar al-Sihah is one of the most celebrated and enduring dictionaries in the history of the Arabic language. Compiled by the scholar Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Razi (d. 666 AH), it is a masterful abridgment of the monumental Al-Sihah by Ismail ibn Hammad al-Jawhari (d. 393 AH). Al-Razi meticulously selected the most frequently used words in literature, Islamic jurisprudence, and daily speech, intentionally omitting rare or archaic terms to create a more functional and accessible reference. This work has served for centuries as an essential tool for anyone seeking to preserve the honor and precision of their Arabic expression.

The dictionary is organized according to the "old" alphabetical system, where words are categorized by their root's final letter (the chapter) and then their first letter (the section). Al-Razi did not merely condense the original text; he refined it by adding various linguistic benefits and clarifying morphological structures that are vital for students of heritage texts. This volume remains a staple for the serious researcher and the bibliophile, offering a bridge to the classical linguistic tradition through a concise and disciplined format that prioritizes clarity and academic integrity.

name: Ar-Risala al-Wafiya li Madhhab Ahli Sunnah - ad-Dani (440H)
description_short:
Al-Risalah al-Wafiyah is a foundational and authoritative treatise on the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, authored by the celebrated Andalusian master of Quranic recitations, Imam Abu 'Amr al-Dani. In this work, the author departs from his primary expertise in Tajwid to provide a comprehensive and rigorous exposition of the traditional Athari creed. The text serves as a definitive record of the theological positions held by the early generations of scholars, particularly focusing on the Divine Attributes, the nature of the Qur'an, and the principles of faith.

The methodology of the book is characterized by its reliance on textual evidence and the consensus of the Pious Predecessors. Imam al-Dani meticulously outlines the core beliefs that distinguish the Sunni path from various philosophical and heterodox movements of his time. This work is highly regarded by historians and theologians alike for its clarity and its role in preserving the heritage of the Maliki-Sunni intellectual tradition in the Islamic West (the Maghreb and Al-Andalus).

name: Al-Fiqh al-Akbar by Imam Abu Hanifa
description_short:
Al-Fiqh al-Akbar is one of the most famous texts attributed to Imam Abu Hanifah in the field of creed. It addresses fundamental issues of faith, Divine attributes, and other important matters of Aqidah discussed by the early generations.

Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khamis begins this study with an introduction to the life of Imam Abu Hanifah, his writings, his creed, and his stance toward Ilm al-Kalam. The first part of the book presents Al-Fiqh al-Akbar according to the narration of Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah, while the second part contains the narration of Abu Muti al-Balkhi, also known as Al-Fiqh al-Absat. This structure allows readers to compare the two transmitted versions and better understand their contents and historical context.

name: Mukhtasar al-Fiqh al-Islamy - Muhammad at-Tuwayjri
description_short:
This book is an easy-to-understand summary of all Islamic Fiqh with proofs, in a very large volume of +1100 pages.

It includes the laws of Islam, taking into account the benefit of the Muslim house in particular.

It was collected and arranged from several books on monotheism, faith, morals, etiquettes, supplications and rulings, making it useful for the worshipper, the preacher, the teacher, the merchant, the mufti, the judge and the supplicant to Almighty Allah.

It was developed in such a way to tackle the issues that concerns every Muslim, and then mention the most correct ruling from the sayings of scholars - if evidence of preponderance appears - by referencing it from the Holy Quran or the authentic Sunnah or both.

Furthermore, it is a general definition of the religion of Islam, belief and rulings, morals and etiquettes, and a call to Almighty Allah with insight. It is a renewed work of which multiple editions have been issued, adding many of what is new to Muslims in terms of rulings, controversial issues, etc.

The author has worked hard to divide it into jurisprudential chapters appropriate for the current era. He stated the rulings without any violation, and used the evidence without elaboration to aid the layperson in obtaining the ruling directly and the scholar in reaching the summary of the jurisprudential rulings without elaboration.

description_short:

name: Al Jaami' fil-Khasaais (an-Nabi, al-Anbiya...) - 100% harakat - Musa al-'Azimi
description_short:
Al-Jami' fi al-Khasa'is is an expansive and meticulously researched encyclopedia dedicated to the unique characteristics and exclusive privileges (Khasa'is) granted to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. This work is authored by the distinguished contemporary historian Musa bin Rashid al-'Azmi—the renowned author of the celebrated biography Al-Lu'lu' al-Maknun fi Sirat al-Nabi al-Ma'mun. In this volume, Al-'Azmi synthesizes the classical scholarship of the early centuries AH, drawing from the heritage of masters such as Imam al-Suyuti and Ibn al-Mulaqqin, into a modern, highly organized format that reflects a deep commitment to the honor and dignity of the final Messenger.

The book is structured to cover the Prophet's ﷺ unique attributes in this life and the hereafter, his exclusive legal rulings, and the miracles that distinguish him from all other creation. By using a rigorous evidence-based approach, Al-'Azmi provides a clear and inspiring roadmap for understanding the Prophetic model of virtue. This volume is an essential reference for any student of the Seerah or researcher looking to explore the foundational elements of Prophetic excellence through the lens of one of the most respected biographers of our time.

Superb Saudi edition, 100% vowelized (harakat).

name: Sirah al-'Atiq Abi Bakr as-Siddiq - 100% harakat - Musa al-'Azimi
description_short:
This comprehensive biography explores the life and legacy of the first Rightly Guided Caliph, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (d. 13 AH). Authored by the acclaimed historian Musa bin Rashid al-'Azmi—celebrated for his foundational work Al-Lu'lu' al-Maknun—this volume offers a meticulous, evidence-based account of the man known as "Al-'Atiq." The narrative spans from his early life in the pre-Islamic era to his pivotal role as the closest companion of the Prophet ﷺ and his subsequent leadership of the Ummah during the most critical period of the 1st century AH.

Al-'Azmi’s methodology focuses on the traits of virtue, honor, and unwavering duty that defined Abu Bakr’s character. The book details his sacrifices during the Hijrah, his steadfastness during the Prophet's ﷺ passing, and his strategic genius in preserving the integrity of the state during the Riddah wars. By filtering through historical reports with scholarly rigor, the author presents a portrait of a leader whose life serves as a blueprint for moral and political integrity in Islamic history.

Superb Saudi edition, 100% vowelized (harakat).

name: Maqasid al-Shariah al-Islamiyyah wa 'alaqatuha bi adillat al-shariah (Thesis)
description_short:
This work is widely regarded as one of the most comprehensive and academically rigorous contemporary references on the Higher Objectives of Islamic Law (Maqasid al-Shari'ah). Dr. Muhammad Sa'd al-Yubi provides a systematic framework that bridges classical legal theory with modern application, making it a staple text in university curricula and specialized Sharia research. It stands out for its clarity in defining the boundaries of Maqasid and its relationship with the science of Usul al-Fiqh.

The text provides an in-depth analysis of the various categories of objectives—the necessities (Daruriyyat), needs (Hajiyyat), and luxuries (Tahsiniyyat)—while exploring the history of this science from its early development to its modern formulation. By synthesizing the contributions of classical masters like Al-Shatibi with contemporary insights, the author offers a robust methodology for understanding the wisdom behind Divine legislation. It is an essential volume for any student or scholar seeking to understand the underlying purposes and public interests protected by Islamic law.

name: Mandhumah 'Aqilat Atrab al-Qasaid (fi ilm Rasm al-Masahif) - al-Shatibi
description_short:
The second ra’iyyah poem by Imam al-Shatibi (d. 590 AH), the sister of his celebrated “Hirz al-Amani” in the Qira’at. In approximately 298 lines he versified Abu ‘Amr al-Dani’s “al-Muqni’” on the science of mushaf orthography, encoding the rules of Uthmanic rasm: what is omitted, what is retained, and what is written contrary to standard spelling conventions in the Uthmanic masahif.

Al-Dhahabi said: “The caravans traveled with his two poems, Hirz al-Amani and ‘Aqilat Atrab al-Qasa’id, and countless people memorized them, and master poets, great rhetoricians, and expert readers all submitted to them.” An indispensable poem for anyone seeking qualification in the science of mushaf orthography.

This edition, verified, authenticated, and annotated by Dr. Ayman Rushdi Suwayd, includes the connected sanad of the poem and explanations of select terms and constructions arranged alphabetically. With most of its tashkil.

name: Ikhtiyarat al-Imam ash-Shawkani al-Fiqhiyah
description_short:
Whoever wants to know the Fiqh of Imam Shawkaani have to take this book. It is indeed a work dedicated to the great Imam of Yemen, one of the Imams that marked the Ummah of their passage. Indeed Imam ash-Shawkaani was Zaydi in madhhab by education, he was a scholar without madhhab. Many today claim to don't follow any madhhab but this is rarely true, however, for the imam Shawkaani it was a reality, a duty he had imposed to himself.

Imam saw a lowering in the Taqlid, a form of Jahl, unlike the mandatory of following the evidence is the real science in his eyes. So Ash-Shawkaani left us a Fiqh is the result of a pure Ijtihad.

That's what this research shows us: the first half of the book is devoted to the imam ash-Shawkaani imam himself, his biography, his works, his positions, and foundations. Then the second part sets out its legal opinions and positions on issues of fiqh to divergence in the adoration.

Beautiful Saudi edition. This research is a Doctoral thesis that comes from Morocco (Fes).

name: Adab at-Talab wa Muntaha al-Arab - Ash-Shawkani
description_short:
Adab al-Talab is a quintessential manual for students of knowledge, authored by the renowned Yemeni polymath Al-Imam al-Shawkani (d. 1250 AH). This work serves as a comprehensive guide to the psychological, ethical, and methodological framework required for a successful journey in the Islamic sciences. Al-Shawkani outlines the path of the scholar with surgical clarity, emphasizing the importance of sincerity, the dangers of intellectual arrogance, and the necessity of rising above blind sectarianism (Taqlid).

The book is celebrated for its balanced approach, blending practical advice on study habits with deep spiritual insights into the responsibilities of the learned. Al-Shawkani utilizes a range of hadiths and athars to root his instructions in the Prophetic tradition, ensuring that the student’s pursuit remains an act of worship rather than a mere academic exercise. It is a work of high linguistic precision that remains exceptionally accessible, making it a timeless resource for anyone committed to the pursuit of truth and virtuous character.

name: Tarikh ibn Khaldun (Kitab al-'Ibar - The Muqaddima)
description_short:
Kitab al-'Ibar or Tarikh ibn Khaldun is the complete works of the great theologian and philosopher Ibn Khaldun (808H). His work is preceded by an introduction - The Muqaddima - which is in itself a work apart and very important, which is still studied worldwide today, whether in Muslim countries than non-Muslim countries.

This is a book in which the author has compiled the knowledge of his predecessors, such as: Ibn Isaac, Al-Waqidi, Ibn Saad, at-Tabari and others. Ibn Khaldun wrote this book, refined it and made it easy for people to understand. He mentioned the history of humanity since creation to his era and included some of the sciences and wisdom. The book contains various benefits and diverse knowledge. The author did not rely on mere transfer, but included the rules of habit, policy rules, the nature of civilization and conditions in the human socialising.

The book is divided into four sections. The first section includes an Introduction to the virtue of history and then talked at length about the nature of civilization. The second section deals with the uprisings of the Kharijites and other factions. Then he started the third section with the rule of Asfar Ibn Shiruya over Gorgan and Ray regions. The fourth section began with the news of Abi Ishaq’s escape and Rabah’s pledge of allegiance to him and the subsequent events.

description_short:

name: Aqidah topics in which some Shafii Scholars diverged
description_short:
Here is a Magister thesis entitled: Issues of Aqidah in which diverged some Shafii jurists with the first Imams of the Imam Shafii Madhhab.

The writer of this research exposes each chapter errors or innovations that we find in some Shafii scholars. In Aqeedah is found mainly Taweel of Divine attributes, the Tabarruk and other issues close to Ash'ariyya way.
Whenever exposed: (1) the subject matter, its definition among the people of the Sunna and the Ash'ari; (2) the opinion of Ar-Ramli; (3) discussion and rebuttal of evidences of Mukhalifin; (4) comparing the words of the late scholars Madhhab and those of the first scholars of the Madhhab and finally (5) the position of Ahl as-Sunnah about the subject in question through the word of some imams.
Then comes the same work for each chapter of Fiqh which are developed related errors in belief and innovations.

This book is useful for everyone because most topics are errors in which many scholars have fallen, especially the Imams of the Ummah who were close to the Asharis as Ibn Hajar, an-Nawawi, al-Bayhaqi (all three Shafi'is) etc ... and therefore it is important to know that.

name: Al-Qadim wal-Jadid fi Fiqh ash-Shafi'i (2 volumes)
description_short:
A very interesting research in the Fiqh of Imam Ash-Shafi'i, on two types of the opinion that we find the old and the new (before and after his departure for Egypt).

Here is the book's structure:
1- The books of Ash-Shafi'i Imam and those who reported his advice.
2- Usul Fiqh of Shafii
2.1 The foundations that have remained unchanged in the Qadim and Jadid
2.2 The foundations that have changed (with examples)
3- Sources of Fiqh Shafii
3.1 His Shuyukh
3.2 The books he studied
3.3 His opinions diverging from some of his sources (Malik and Shaybani)
4- Al-Qadeem wa al-Jadeed
4.1 The subjects of old and new Fiqh (by chapters)
4.2 An-Nach-ah - al-Madhaan - al-Fatrah
4.3 The specifics of Qadeem and Jadeed

name: Al-Ashbaah wan-Nadhaair - As-Suyuti (Fiqh & Usul Shafi'i)
description_short:
Al-Ashbah wa al-Nazair is a definitive masterpiece in the science of legal maxims (Qawa'id Fiqhiyyah) within the Shafi'i school of thought. Authored by the prolific polymath Imam Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (d. 911 AH), this work serves as a grand architectural map of Islamic law, organizing vast legal branches into coherent, universal principles. It meticulously details the five "Grand Maxims" that govern the majority of jurisprudence, such as the principle that "Certainty is not removed by doubt," providing a structured and disciplined approach to understanding the inner logic of the Shari'ah.

The work is celebrated for its ability to bridge the gap between abstract legal theory and practical application (Furu'). By grouping similar legal cases together, al-Suyuti enables the student to develop a sharp legal intuition and a profound mastery of the school’s methodology. This text is not merely a legal manual; it is an honorable intellectual exercise that preserves the integrity of the Shafi'i tradition, making it an indispensable resource for jurists and researchers seeking to navigate the complexities of law with precision and academic rigor.

name: Muntakhab al-Ahkam of Imam Ibn Abi Zamaneen (399H) - Fiqh Maliki
description_short:
Muntakhab al-Ahkam, or Anthology of juridical Jugdments, by Imam Ibn Abi Zamanine al-Andalussi is one of the most important books having dealt with the science of Fiqh of legal sentences, deductions, and applications.

The book is divided into 10 parts dealing respectively with disputes, justice, pre-emption right, possession, marriage, divorce, sales, hidden defects, letting and renting, and other issues. name: At-Tashil fil-Fiqh 'ala Madhhab al-Imam Ahmad
description_short:
"Al-Tashil fi al-Fiqh ala Madhhab al-Imam Ahmad" by al-Ba'li (d. 778 AH) is a concise primer of Hanbali Fiqh covering worship, transactions, and personal status matters. The book is distinguished by its clear style and simple presentation, making it suitable for beginning students of the school. It gains particular importance for its accuracy in transmitting Imam Ahmad's original positions, especially given the later developments in the school that sometimes deviated from its foundations. Ibn al-Imad praised the book for its rare benefits that distinguish it from other primers, and its simplified approach helps in mastering Hanbali jurisprudence, making it an essential reference for understanding the fundamentals of the school.

The Dar Atlas al-Khadra edition, edited by Yasir al-Thumairi (1441H/2020), relied on two manuscripts to ensure textual accuracy and includes most of the Harakat to facilitate reading.

name: Mizan al-I'tidal fi Naqd ar-Rijal - Dhahabi ('Ilm Jarh wa Ta'dil)
description_short:
Here is a book of criticism of the reporters written by Imam adh-Dhahabi, one of the most important works in the science of Jarh wa Ta'deel.

In his book he identifies - in alphabetical order - liars narrators, unknowns, those to be abandoned, and he also wanted to distinguish them from scholars in hadith whose degree is low due to memory or certain breaches. He also took care to avoid some misleading expressions that may exist in some Muhaddith and which are not entirely clear on the weakness of the narrator.

Magnificent edition in 5 volumes, all verified and authenticated by various Muhaqqiq with many relevant and important annotations to give sources and other references which also mention the narrators.

name: Musnad al-Imam ash-Shafi'i (2 volumes)
description_short:
The Musnad ach-Shafi'i is a collection of hadith used in the Madhhab Shafii as argument. It is classified by chapter of Fiqh.

So this work is actually a collective work of the first imams of the Madhhab containing the hadiths reported and which appear in al-Umm and al-Mabsut, both of Imam Shafii.
So it does not figure as one of the works of the Imam as ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani explains. Nevertheless, it remains a known and used collection.

Very beautiful verified and authenticated edition, with the degree of authenticity of the hadiths in annotations, and the harakats partly on the hadiths, and with several search indexes.

name: The view Crescent of Ramadan (4 Rasaail)
description_short:
Collection gathering 4 Risala on the theme of the sight of Hilal (crescent) to determine the coming of the month of Ramadan.

The 4 epistles are as follows:

Al-'Ilm al-Manshoor fi Ithbaat ash-Shuhoor, by Imam Taqi ad-Din as-Subki (771H), a great legal authority of his time, Judge of the Judges of Damascus, Shafii of Madhhab.

Tanbih al-Ghaafil wa al-Wasnaan 'ala Ahkaam Hilaal Ramadaan, by Shaykh Muhammad Amin ibn 'Abidin (1252H), called Khatim al-Muhaqqiqin, was a respected Hanafi scholar and jurist in Damascus where he was Mufti.

Al-Falk ad-Dawaar fi Rouyah al-Hilaal bil-Nahaar, by Shaykh Abd al-Hay al-Lucknawi (Mawlana Abdul Hayy) , he was Muhaddith, Faqih and Usuli in India (1304H).

Al-Qawl al-Manshur fi Hilal Khayr ash-Shuhur, by Mawlana Abdul Hayy al-Luckanwi also.

All these Risalas have been written because of controversies that have occurred in the epochs of the different authors, and which they wished to clarify by recalling the rules and statutes surrounding the vision and determination of the new month according to the evidence of the Qur'an and the Sunnah and the words of the People of Science.

Verified and referenced edition.

The Musnad are collections which are classified by narrators, and therefore by Sahabas, Imam at-Tayalisi begins for example by the 10 companions promised to Paradise. It seems that the collection is not directly the work of the Imam, but what his pupil Yunus ibn Habib assembled from what the Sheikh transmitted to him.

Imam Abu Dawud at-Tayalissi (133-204H) is a Muhaddith and Hafidh of the first three centuries, he reports among other from Sufyan ath-Thawri and Shu'bah and transmitted the hadith to Imam Ahmad and Ali Ibn al-Madini.

Beautiful edition, with the majority of harakats, research summaries, and the referencing of the hadiths in the other collections.

name: Raf' Al-Yadayn fi as-Salat - Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
description_short:
Dans ce traité concis mais rigoureux, Raf‘ al-Yadayn fi al-Salah, l’imam Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah démontre, à partir des hadiths authentiques, la légitimité du geste de lever les mains à certains moments de la prière, notamment avant et après l’inclinaison (ruku‘). Il y répond aux objections soulevées par ceux qui ont contesté cette pratique.

L’ouvrage reflète son attachement à la Sunna prophétique, en combinant analyse de chaînes de transmission et argumentation respectueuse. C’est aussi un exemple de méthodologie savante dans le débat intra-juridique.

This edition of Rafʿ al-Yadayn fī al-Ṣalāh is part of the scholarly series by Dar ‘Atā’āt al-‘Ilm dedicated to the verified works of Ibn al-Qayyim. It was edited and supervised by Dr. ʿAlī al-ʿImrān, based on a single manuscript. Like usual in this series, the edition includes editorial footnotes, biographical notes, and chapter structuring for clarity and readability.

name: At-Tawil inda al-Mufassirin min as-Salaf (Ashari Thesis)
description_short:
Caution! This is an Ashari thesis, we propose it as research for advanced students in this subject.

The thesis follows the following plan: the meaning of Tawil, Tawil accepted and Tawil rejected, Tawil in the words of the Prophet, companions and Salafs, while illustrating each time with examples taken from 6 great Tafsir: Tafsir at -Tabari, Tafsir ibn 'Atiyah, Tafsir al-Qurtubi, al-Bahr al-Muhit, Tafsir al-Baghawi and Tafsir Ibn Kathir.

The author defends the Tawil's permission by putting forward evidence and examples and in this way wants to prove the validity of the Tawil according to the Asharis.

We wanted to propose this book for 2 reasons:

- Part of the thesis includes the Tawil which is accepted among the Atharis / Salafi, with quotations and examples, gathered in a same work.

- The other part of the thesis will demonstrate to the student Salafi the falsity of the author's argument, which mixes the truth with the false taking examples completely extrapolated and in reality not applicable to the Sifat of Allah. What to know the false arguments of the Asharis (which are weak).

For warned reader only!

name: Al-Assas fi al-Mantiq (for advanced students)
description_short:
Ilm al-Mantiq is the science of rhetoric or logic, and more precisely Aristotelian logic. This science is a derivative of Kalam but much more pushed and tends towards philosophy. If the latter is blameworthy in the vast majority of cases, the use and knowledge of Mantiq (logic) can serve interests in demonstrating logical arguments or to refute philosophical thoughts either innovated by the Mu'tazili of the Ummah, either the theories of non-Muslim philosophers.

This science is tinged with eloquence and Kalam and can only be studied by a person with a certain level and firmness in Aqida. Some scholars have allowed the study to be used for argumentation and refutation.

We have chosen a book for beginners so that anyone who wants to understand this science can see its outlines. This book is an ultra-simplified explanation, with a contemporary and pedagogical methodology of a mantiq matn very often commented, The Isagogé, al-Isaghouji.

For warned reader only!

Note: This explanation of what Mantiq is is based on our general knowledge and may be imprecise or partially wrong.

name: 12 Risala on inimitability of the Qur'an - I'jaz al-Quran
description_short:
A collection of 12 epistles from the 4th to the 14th centuries on the dogma of the inimitability of the Qur'an (I'jaz al-Quran), that is to say, its miraculous and unique character, which can not come from anyone other than 'Allah azza wa jall. The collection brings together scholars from all sides, the Mu'tazili, the Ash'ari and the Atharis (Salafis) because all are unanimous on this point of Aqida.

Here is the list of scholars:

  1. Al-Qadi Abd al-Jabbar al-Mu'tazili (415H)
  2. Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi (456H)
  3. Abd al-Qadir al-Jarjani (471H)
  4. Al-Qadi 'Iyad al-Maliki (544H)
  5. Abu Abdullah al-Qurtubi (671H)
  6. Badr ad-Din az-Zarkachi (794H)
  7. Jalal ad-Din as-Suyuti (911H)
  8. Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim ad-Dahlawi (1176H)
  9. Muhammad ad-Dumiati al-Khadri (1287H)
  10. Muhammad Siddiq Hasan Khan (1307H)
  11. Muhammad Rashid Rida (1354H)
  12. Muhammad at-Tahir ibn 'Achur (1393H)


Very nice verified edition.

description_short:
This book of Ibn Al-'Arabi deals with the position of the Companions after the death of the Messenger of Allah sallallaahu 'alaihi wa sallam. It is therefore a book dealing with the virtues (Manaqib) and history (Tarikh), but also a book of defense of the noble companions because it is the Aqida of the people of the Sunnah that to love them and defend them, and only the people of innovation and Kufr can afford to criticize and insult the Sahaba, because criticizing the Sahaba is of course criticize the Prophet who guides and educated them, and the refuge with Allah.

Good edition annotated by Sheikh Muhib ad-Din al-Khatib, an Egyptian scholar known for his criticism of the Shiites, his defense of companions (notes related to historical references, certain expressions and sources of athars and hadiths).

name: 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah 'inda al-Malikiyyah
description_short:
A book on a very important theme: the actions of the people of Medina. Indeed the acts of the people of Medina are a very used proof in the Maliki madhhab.

However the scholars Maliki, even the students of Imam Malik have diverged on the understanding and use of this evidence.

An excellent book very simple to read which is the basic doctoral thesis of Sheikh Idriss Dardour that he defended at the University of Zitouna in Tunisia.

name: At-Taj wa al-Iklil li Mukhtasar Khalil - Al-Mawwaq al-Maliki
description_short:
Al-Taj wa al-Iklil is a preeminent explanation of the Mukhtasar Khalil in Maliki jurisprudence by the Granadan Mufti, Imam al-Mawaq (897H), who was the distinguished pupil of Imam Abul-Qassim ibn Siraj (848H). In this excellent Sharh, the author focuses on returning to the foundational words of the Imams of the school, providing a rich lineage of transmission and legal thought. It is a masterful work where the author brings back the original statements of the Maliki masters, occasionally reporting the opinions of other Madhahib for comparison before establishing the preponderant opinion among the views within the school.

This work serves as an essential treasury that reconnects the concise phrases of Khalil to the broader classical tradition, making it a vital tool for those seeking the most weighted views and the underlying logic of legal rulings. The author's approach reflects a disciplined academic rigor, meticulously documenting opinions to ensure the legal lineage remains intact and honorable. It remains a foundational resource for anyone navigating the complexities of the Maliki tradition with precision and intellectual integrity.

This magnificent edition in 5 volumes has been meticulously verified and referenced. It features a comprehensive summary of research tools, including indices by Quranic verse, Hadith, and specific subjects of Fiqh for effortless navigation.

name: Sharh Mushkil al-Athar by Imam at-Tahawi (Tahqiq Arnaoot, 16 vol.)
description_short:
This book of the great Imam Abu Ja'far at-Tahawi is a collection of hadith related to legal judgments and divergent issues, classified by chapter of Fiqh. He has related the prophetic Hadiths, which are subject to divergences as to their authenticity or their application, and he also brings back the words of the companions and Ulema of the time.

The Imam at-Tahawi analyzes and explains the evidence and their contradictory arguments, discusses the weaknesses or defects of the transmission chains.

It is the most voluminous work that has come down to us from the 3rd century. It is a true encyclopaedia that has been and still is widely studied because of the great number of science it contains, such as the science of hadith and the criticism of the chain of narration, the apparent contradictions in the hadiths and the proofs, the legal judgments, the divergences of the Fuqaha etc.

Excellent edition in 16 volumes, verified, authenticated and annotated by the Muhaqqiq and Muhaddith Shu'ayb al-Arnaoot, with the 16th volume entirely devoted to the research summaries by theme, and harakat partly in the matn of the hadith.

name: 5 Risala on the Hadith Da'if and its status
description_short:
A collection of 5 contemporary rare epistles (from the last century) on the Hadith Da'if in Islam. Indeed, there are 3 opinions concerning the use of weak hadiths:

  • The total ban, regardless of the subject, is the opinion of Cheikh al-Albani and Cheikh Ahmad Shakir.
  • The permission (under conditions) for legal advice, good works and virtues - is the opinion of Imam Ahmad, Abu Hanifah, Abu Dawud and it is also reported by Imam Malik.
  • The permission (under conditions) for good works and virtues - this is the opinion of the majority of scholars of all tendencies and schools.

  1. Abdulhay al-Luknawi (1304H) - Muhaddith Hanafi
  2. Zafar Ahmad al-Uthmani (1394H) - Savant Hanafi
  3. Muhammad Zahid al-Kawthari (1371H) - the last Mufti (Hanafi) of the Ottoman Empire
  4. Tahir al-Jazairi (1338H) - Mufti of the Malikites of Damascus
  5. Shabir Ahmad Usmani, (1369H) - Savant Hanafi


Very beautiful edition verified, annotated, with the biographies of each author.

This collection is useful for the confirmed student seeking to know the status of Hadith Da'if among the great Asharis scholars who are references to most Asharis brothers in the world.

name: Tafsir Ibn Faras (597H) - Ahkam al-Quran (3 vol.)
description_short:
The Tafsir of Ibn Faras al-Andalusi is a Tafsir Fiqhi, that is, his role is to explain the verses on legal issues. It takes all the Qur'an but only stops on verses dealing with jurisprudential subjects (Fiqh) or verses abrogating and repealed.

This Tafsir, which is one of the most important bequeathed to us by the Malikite school, explains the verses according to the opinion of the scholars of science, he cites the points of convergence and divergence on the subjects of Fiqh, and the Sheikh does not make the Ta'assub his Madhhab, he sometimes gives his opinion which may be different from his school if the evidence lead him to a different opinion.

Beautiful edition verified by 3 researchers, published for the first time, in 3 volumes, with Takhrij of hadiths.

name: Iqamah ad-Dalil 'ala Da'f Adillah Takfir at-Ta'wil - As-San'ani
description_short:
Epistle of Imam as-San'ani (1182H) on the issue of Takfir people who practice Ta'wil without proof on the verses and hadiths. The Ta'wil is to give an interpretation to some words to distract them from their apparent meaning and thus distort the meaning. Several groups practice it on the Attributes of Allah in particular, like the Mu'tazila and the Ash'ariya.

There is a group of scholars who have made them unbelievers for this, but al-Emir as-San'ani here demonstrate the weakness of this opinion, explains why and recalls the rules to be used for this type of Takfir and that this can not be applied in the issue of Ta'wil.

Very good edition with introductory research on the author and subject, the text is checked and annotated, the hadiths are authenticated. Finally the Muhaqqiq finishes the work with several quotes from al-San'ani and al-Shawkani on the Bid'a and the Takfir.

name: Tahqiq al-Murad fi Sharh Matn az-Zad - Abdullah ibn 'Aqil (harakat)
description_short:
Tahqiq al-Murad is a concise and focused commentary on the famous Zad al-Mustaqni in Hanbali jurisprudence, authored by the eminent "Sheikh of the Hanbalis," Abdullah ibn Aqil. This work represents the distilled annotations from the Sheikh’s classes, reflecting his deep expertise as one of the primary students of Sheikh Abdurrahman as-Sa'di. Prefaced by Sheikh Salih al-Fawzan, it serves as a reliable link between the classical Hanbali tradition and the insights of contemporary masters of the school.

The methodology involves a systematic explanation of the text's terminology while outlining the official positions of the Madhhab. Beyond traditional commentary, the book includes the specific legal preferences (Ikhtiyarat) of both Sheikh Ibn Aqil and his teacher, Sheikh as-Sa'di, alongside relevant legal maxims and foundational rules. It is designed to guide the student through the complexities of Fiqh with academic precision, focusing on the practical application of the rulings.

This edition features the majority of the text with harakat.

name: Tarjihaat Shayikh al-Uthaymeen fi Kitaab at-Tahaara
description_short:
Legal research gathering the choices (Ikhtiyarat) of Imam Al-Othaymin in the Chapter of purification, comparing them with his original madhhab, ie the Hanbali madhhab.

The author of this research, which is a dissertation of the magisterium, gives the opinions of the Madhhab Hanbali for each question of the Tahara chapter, then the opinion chosen by Sheikh al-Uthaymin, then discusses the arguments of each one and finally gives his opinion on the matter.

Saudi edition, with a thorough biography of the Sheikh, a research summary, annotations citing references to the words and hadiths.

name: Al-Kifaayah fi Ma'rifah Usul 'Ilm ar-Riwaayah - al-Khatib al-Baghdadi
description_short:
While Mustalah's books and Usul's books in the Hadith were originally separated, the great Imam Muhaddith, al-Hafidh al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, wrote a unique book bringing together the two sciences.

Al-Khatib al-Baghdaadi wrote dozens of books on the sciences of the hadith, be it musnad, books of mustalah, Adab of Muhaddith or Talib, or on narrators.

Al-Kifaayah is one of his unavoidable and very important works in the science and foundations of the Hadith.

name: Al-Jami' li Akhlaq ar-Rawi - al-Khatib al-Baghdadi
description_short:
This monumental work by Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi is a comprehensive guide to the ethics and etiquette required for both the narrator of Hadith and the student seeking it. It covers a vast array of topics, from the initial intention of seeking knowledge to the technical and spiritual preparation required for teaching. As a central pillar of Hadith pedagogy, it outlines the moral character and professional conduct expected within the scholarly circles of the Sunnah.

The work is structured as an encyclopedic collection of narrations, anecdotes, and advice from the Pious Predecessors. It details the manners of the teacher in the classroom, the proper way to handle manuscripts, and the respectful conduct of students toward their mentors. This text is essential for anyone wishing to understand the traditional atmosphere of Islamic learning and the rigorous ethical standards that have historically governed the transmission of Prophetic traditions.

name: Al-Fasl lil Wasl al-Mudraj fi an-Naql - al-Khatib al-Baghdadi
description_short:
This is the first book written on a specific area of the science of the hadith, but nevertheless very important, the Mudraj, by the great Imam Muhaddith, al-Hafidh al-Khatib al-Baghdadi. The hadiths mudarraj are those in which a narrator has introduced a remark or speech in addition. It is a high degree of the science of the hadith reserved for the most experienced Muhaddith, as are certain kinds of 'illa, irregularity.

Al-Khatib al-Baghdaadi wrote dozens of books on the sciences of the hadith, be it musnad, books of mustalah, Adab of Muhaddith or Talib, or on narrators.

Al-Fasl lil-Wasl is a must in his field, and he is presented here with a high quality Tahqiq which is the result of a PhD thesis. There is a long introduction to the author, the book and the topic, precious annotations and a very comprehensive research summary (verses, hadiths & athars, names, subjects ...)

Excellent Saudi edition in 2 volumes, verified and annotated...

description_short:
Superb work of more than 900 pages which deals with a serious subject: The abandonment of the Sunnah.

The author first identifies what this implies and what it implies, its forms and manifestations - the bid'a in particular.

Every point of this excellent research is developed with much detail and argument.

name: Athar al-Arabiyyah fi Istinbat al-Ahkam al-Fiqhiyyah
description_short:
A very interesting and very important PhD thesis: Effects of Arabic in the establishment of the legal rules of the Prophetic Sunnah.

Indeed, if everyone generally understands that Arabic is the key to understanding religion, because it is the language of both revelations (the Qur'an and the Sunnah), it is important to see that in practice the application of the rules of Arabic has direct consequences on the understanding of legal texts.

This research was built on three main axes: to demonstrate the link between the Arabic language and the legal sciences (shariah), the effects of linguistic argumentation in the establishment of legal rules, and the effects of grammatical argumentation in the establishment of legal rules.

Each time the author recalls the existing categories, he argues, he exposes with concrete examples what he is advancing and do not forget to give the references of each word as well as those of the hadiths (with authentications according to al-Albani).

Very nice Saudi edition.

name: Collection of hadiths of the causes of revelation - Al-Isti'aab fi Bayan al-Asbab
description_short:
This encyclopedic three-volume work is the fruit of a scholarly collaboration between two prominent students of Sheikh al-Albani: Salim al-Hilali, a specialist in Hadith and Tahqiq, and Muhammad Musa al-Nasr, an expert in Quranic sciences. Together, they have produced the definitive modern authority on Asbab al-Nuzul (reasons for revelation), meticulously filtering authentic narrations from the weak reports found in classical literature. For every Hadith cited, the authors provide a clear degree of authenticity followed by detailed annotations that dissect the chains of transmission and primary sources with academic rigor.

The methodology ensures that the "Student of Knowledge" (Talib al-Ilm) navigates the historical context of the Quran with absolute certainty, as each entry is rooted in verified Prophetic traditions. While the primary focus remains on authenticated Hadiths, the work also incorporates various Athars (statements of the Sahaba) with their respective referencing to provide a complete picture of early scholarship. By removing historical distortions and unreliable accounts, this collection serves as an essential bridge for those seeking a Tafsir that is both traditionally grounded and scientifically verified.

name: Kitab al-Iman by Imam ibn Mandah (395H) - 2 volumes
description_short:
Kitab al-Iman is a comprehensive and authoritative collection of narrations concerning the nature of faith, compiled by the scholar Ibn Mandah, who passed away in 395 H. This work serves as a vital encyclopedia of the traditionalist creed, meticulously documenting the statements of the Prophet, his companions, and the early generations. It addresses central theological questions such as the definition of faith, its increase and decrease, and the relationship between belief and action, providing a structured map of orthodox belief through the lens of early Hadith scholarship.

The author was renowned for his vast travels in search of knowledge and his immense memory, qualities that are reflected in the breadth of sources cited within this text. By grounding abstract theological concepts in documented narrations, the work preserves the integrity of the early Islamic worldview. It is an honorable resource for any student seeking to understand the foundational proofs of the creed and the disciplined methodology of the early masters in defending the Prophetic tradition.

This excellent Egyptian edition in 2 volumes features the rigorous Tahqiq of Sheikh Ali ibn Nasir al-Faqihi. It includes beneficial annotations and comprehensive research summaries that facilitate navigation through the extensive collection of reports and thematic discussions.

name: Manaar as-Sabeel fi Sharh Ad-Daleel - Ibn Duyaan (Fiqh Hanbali)
description_short:
A beneficial commentary on the matn "Dalil al-Talib li-Nayl al-Matalib" by Sheikh Mar'i ibn Yusuf al-Karmi (d. 1033 AH), one of the most important Hanbali fiqh primers which confined itself to the relied-upon position of the school. Sheikh Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Duwayyan (d. 1353 AH) commented on it concisely, citing the evidence and reasoning for each ruling, with reference to other opinions when needed — especially when stronger in evidence. He draws extensively from Ibn Qudamah, Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, his student Ibn al-Qayyim, the author of al-Furu', and the author of al-Insaf.

A book suited for the beginner through its clarity and for the intermediate student through the richness of its benefits, forming with the matn of "Dalil al-Talib" a complete pair — the matn for memorization and the sharh for understanding and application.

Sheikh al-Albani dedicated his renowned "Irwa' al-Ghalil" to verifying the hadiths of this book, making al-Dalil, al-Manar, and al-Irwa' an inseparable trio for the student of Hanbali fiqh.

Indeed these Fatawas were given during open assizes that the Shaykh gave in his own house in Unayzah, every Thursday, and where any person could come and ask his questions. name: 6 Essential books of Hadith (Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, Ibn Majah)
description_short:

name: Al-Hawashi al-Azhariyyah fi Hal Alfadh al-Jazariyyah - Khalid al-Azhari (905H)
description_short:
A commentary on the Jazariyyah poem in tajweed by the grammarian Imam Khalid ibn Abdullah al-Azhari (d. 905 AH), the author of “al-Muqaddimah al-Azhariyyah” and “al-Tasrih bi-Madmun al-Tawdih” and one of the most renowned grammarians of the 9th Hijri century.

What sets this sharh apart is that between its author and the poet of the Jazariyyah stands only one man in the chain of transmission: al-Azhari received it from his teacher Abd al-Da’im al-Azhari, who took it directly from Ibn al-Jazari himself. He unpacks the poem’s expressions with the precision of a grammarian who knows the positions of words and the secrets of syntax, giving this commentary a linguistic dimension not found in purely tajweed-based explanations.

An elegant Syrian edition from Dar al-Ghawthani lil-Dirasat al-Quraniyyah, edited by Muhammad Barakat, reviewed and prefaced by the great Sheikh and reader Muhyi al-Din al-Kurdi.

description_short:
This book by the great Imam specialist, Abu 'Amr ad-Daanee comes to explain and treat the subject of harakat/tashkeel in the composition of the Koranic copies. The last part of the book contains examples and diagrams of writing.

The copies of the Qur'an that we are reading now are very different from the first collections of the Sahaba and Tabi'in era. Indeed the Arabic language at the time was written neither with points nor with harakats or tashkil. We quickly added points at the top or bottom of some letters to differentiate them, especially for learning and reading non-Arabs. Then came the addition of harakats (chadda, damma, fatha ...) for the same purpose.

And this is part of the sciences of the Quran, his writing, his calligraphy, his preservation were the subject of work and have a history.

Edition magnificent, verified, authenticated, annotated, with harakats in majority.

name: Lisan al-Mizan - Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani (Jarh wa Ta'dil)
description_short:
Lisan al-Mizan is a monumental biographical dictionary specializing in the narrators of Hadith who were criticized, considered weak, or categorized as unknown. Building upon the foundational work of Imam al-Dhahabi’s Mizan al-I'tidal, Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani meticulously refined and expanded the biographies, focusing primarily on those narrators excluded from the canonical "Six Books." It serves as a definitive guide for scholars to navigate the complex landscape of narrator reliability and the preservation of Prophetic truth.

The work is a masterclass in the science of Jarh wa Ta'dil (criticism and praise), showcasing the intellectual integrity and rigorous verification methods of the classical tradition. By identifying fabricators and those with poor memories, Ibn Hajar protects the sanctity of the Sunnah while highlighting the honorable efforts of earlier critics. This text is an essential tool for any researcher seeking to master the historical and technical dimensions of Hadith authentication.

This 2017 edition in 11 volumes features the verification of specialist Abd al-Fattah Abu Ghuddah, with vocalization on difficult names. The final volume provides an extremely comprehensive and useful research summary.

name: Usul ash-Shashi (Usool Fiqh Hanafi)
description_short:
Usul al-Shashi by the classical jurist Nizam al-Din al-Shashi (7th century AH) is one of the most celebrated introductory textbooks in Hanafi legal theory (Usul al-Fiqh). Designed with pedagogical clarity, this concise and authoritative manual introduces students to the four foundational sources of Islamic legislation: the Quran, the Sunnah, scholarly consensus (Ijma'), and analogical reasoning (Qiyas). It methodically breaks down linguistic indicators, semantic meanings, and legal rulings, grounding theoretical principles directly in derived practical jurisprudence (furu').

Containing the relied-upon (Mu'tamad) positions of the Hanafi school, the text enjoys widespread consensus among Hanafi scholars regarding its essential value and utility for developing students of knowledge. For centuries, it has served as a core curricular pillar in traditional Islamic seminaries across India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, Turkey, Jordan, and across Asia, making it an indispensable starting point for mastering classical Hanafi jurisprudence.

name: Hifdh al-'Umr & Tanbih al-Na'im - Ibn al-Jawzi
description_short:
This single volume brings together two classic masterpieces by Imam Ibn al-Jawzi that tackle the twin spiritual diseases of laziness and procrastination. The first treatise, Hifdh al-Umr, is an incredible manual on time management and spiritual urgency. It breaks down the human lifespan into seasonal stages, showing how each phase of life—from youth to old age—carries specific responsibilities and unique devotional opportunities that will never return once gone. It delivers a profound lesson on self-discipline and resource management, written long before modern self-help books existed.

The companion treatise in this volume, Tanbih al-Na'im al-Ghumr, acts as a powerful wake-up call to shake the reader out of spiritual slumber and heedlessness. Together, these two works provide actionable advice on overcoming inertia, avoiding toxic worldly distractions, and structuring one's day around the acquisition of knowledge. Packed with sharp reminders and moving historical anecdotes of how the righteous predecessors used every single breath for the sake of the afterlife, this double-feature book is an absolute must-read for anyone looking to reclaim their days and live a purposeful life.

Beautiful edition of high quality, verified and authenticated, with a beautiful layout.

name: Bustaan al-Waa'idheen wa Riyaad as-Saami'een - Ibn al-Jawzi
description_short:
Imam Ibn al-Jawzi was the undisputed master orator of Baghdad, and this classic text gives you a front-row seat to the very gathering sessions (majalis) that moved thousands to tears and repentance. The book reads like a series of beautifully structured spiritual transcripts, where each chapter tackles a specific theme—from the reality of death and accountability in the afterlife to the immense virtues of Quranic recitation and sacred months. It is an incredible collection of classical exhortation that focuses on softening the heart, restoring spiritual focus, and snapping the reader out of worldly distraction.

What makes this work so compelling is the sheer eloquence of Ibn al-Jawzi's prose. He masterfully weaves Quranic verses and Prophetic traditions together with moving historical anecdotes of the Sahaba and early ascetics, delivering them with a rhythmic, powerful Arabic rhetoric that hits the soul directly. Whether you are a student looking for rich material to build impactful khutbahs, or simply a reader seeking a deep, authentic spiritual reset from a giant of Islamic heritage, this book remains an essential and deeply rewarding companion.

name: Regarding the murders committed in Mecca - Al-Bouhouti
description_short:
The context of the Risala is as follows: in 1041, a notable of Mecca decides to take control of it by rising against the ruler in place at the time, causing during this rebellion the death of 200 Meccans. The Ottoman Caliph will be called to the rescue but the matting of the rebellion will cause deaths again, especially on the side of the attackers.

Imam Mansur ibn Yunus al-Buhuti, Imam of the Hanabila of his time and reference of his Madhhab, therefore decided to write a Risala following these events to clarify what the Shari'ah allows and does not allow to deal with the unjust rebels, the warring enemies, the rebels and the apostates, and this in general in some cases and especially on the blessed land of the Haram of Makkah.

Rare book (published in 1988), very good edition verified, authenticated and annotated, Harakat partly.

name: Tafsir ibn 'Arafa al-Maliki - 5 volumes
description_short:
The Tafsir of Imam ibn 'Arafah, the great Imam Maliki of his time, in the most complete edition.

Indeed, the Imam did not leave a Tafsir properly speaking like other Imams, but he did, of course, teach his students about the Tafseer of the Qur'an. The greatest transmitter of Tafsir of ibn 'Arafa is his pupil ibn Umar al-Wachtati al-Ubi.

This Tafsir as presented here is the result of several university researches that have succeeded each other to complete the work previously done. Thus the first two volumes are essentially the Tafsir of the Imam, and the last three are composed of the words of the Imam, according to several sources of different students, and also other Mufassir Maliki like ibn 'Atiyah for example, in order to complete the Tafsir until Surat an-Nass.

This allows the reader to enjoy a complete Tafsir, according to the madhhab of the original author (Maliki - Ashari), on almost the entire Quran.

The Muhaqqiq did a precise job from the available manuscripts and provided important and complementary annotations.

It is a reference work towards which the scholars return.

name: Adab al-Kaatib of Imam Ibn Qutaybah
description_short:
Adab al-Katib is a work written by the famous literary, linguist and Arabic grammarian: Ibn Qutaybah ad-Dinawari (276H).

In this book, he mentions a whole set of theoretical and practical rules concerning Arabic literature that are incumbent on all those who want to undertake to become a writer or to specialize in the Arabic language and its subtleties.

This could be called today: the essential culture for the writer.

The author of this book wanted to make this book a companion for each author or writer in Arabic wishing to correct his language and his writing.

Ibn Khuldun in his Muqaddimah praises this book by saying: "I have heard from my scholars that the foundations and foundations of this science (Arabic language and literature) are based on four great works: "Adab al- Katib"of Ibn Qutaybah, "al-Kâmil" of al-Moubarrid, "al-Bayan Wat-Tabyin" of al-Jahiz, and "an-Nawadir" of Abu 'Ali al-Qali al-Baghdadi, the rest of the works of this science succeeds these four bases and draws from them."

Superb edition (2016), verified, annotated and authenticated, with harakat in part.

name: Mandhumah 'Aqilat Atrab al-Qasaid - al-Shatibi + CD Audio
description_short:
The second ra’iyyah poem by Imam al-Shatibi (d. 590 AH), the sister of his celebrated “Hirz al-Amani” in the Qira’at. In approximately 298 lines he versified Abu ‘Amr al-Dani’s “al-Muqni’” on the science of mushaf orthography, encoding the rules of Uthmanic rasm: what is omitted, what is retained, and what is written contrary to standard spelling conventions in the Uthmanic masahif.

Al-Dhahabi said: “The caravans traveled with his two poems, Hirz al-Amani and ‘Aqilat Atrab al-Qasa’id, and countless people memorized them, and master poets, great rhetoricians, and expert readers all submitted to them.” An indispensable poem for anyone seeking qualification in the science of mushaf orthography.

This edition, verified, authenticated, and annotated by Dr. Ayman Rushdi Suwayd, includes the connected sanad of the poem and explanations of select terms arranged alphabetically. A large-format edition (17×24 cm) with 100% Harakat (tashkil), accompanied by an audio CD of the poem recited by Sheikh Ayman Suwayd.

name: Al-Muqaddimat ul-Jazariyyah fi Tajweed - Al-Jazari (Large size)
description_short:
No student of the Quran in the Muslim world has not memorized it or heard it recited. The Jazariyyah by Imam Muhammad ibn al-Jazari (d. 833 AH) is the undisputed mother-text of the science of tajweed. In 109 lines it covers the core rules of tajweed: the articulation points and characteristics of letters, the rules of nun sakinah and tanwin, the lengthenings (mudud), the rules of stopping and starting, and the etiquettes of recitation. A precise, comprehensive poem that has been the first text given to the student of Quranic recitation in memorization circles and teaching assemblies for centuries.

This edition, verified by Sheikh Ayman Rushdi Suwayd, one of the foremost contemporary authorities in tajweed, is a premium large-format edition (17×24 cm) with elegant layout, high-quality printing, and 100% Harakat (tashkil). An edition worthy of this great matn, suited for memorization, teaching, and review.

name: Al-Imam al-Ajuryy and his opinions in the Fiqh
description_short:
The life, work and Fiqh of the great Imam of the Salafs, Al-Imam, al-Muhaddith, al-Qudwah, Sheikh al-Haram, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hussain al-Ajurree.

He was truthful, very pious, one of the fervent defenders of the Sunna and the authentic Aqeeda, Shafi'i of Madhhab (contrary to what the researcher says, he is quoted well as Shafi'i in Tabaqat Shafi'iyyah known). However, like any great specialist Imam whose level reached Ijtihad, he had divergent opinions of his original madhhab.

The first third of the book is devoted to his biography, then the rest of the book deals with his Usool and his opinions in different Fiqh questions. And for each question the author compares his opinion with the other existing opinions and gives the prevailing opinion according to him.
