name: Tafsir Al-Bahr al-Mohit of Imam ibn Hayyan (22 vol.)
description_short:
A major Tafsir although less known, written by a Maliki Imam of Andalusia, Abu Hayyan (654-745H).

His Tafsir excels in grammatical explanations and details about Balaghah. Indeed he was a great specialist in the Arabic language, moreover he was inspired by two other Tafsir focused on this theme, the Tafsir of Zamakhshari and Ibn 'Atiyyah.

It explains the words, their I'rab, their meaning, the linguistic and literary range of the sentence, the Balaghah forms used, it also deals with the variations of the different readings and their rules in Arabic language. Finally it also explains the causes of revelation as well as the legal rules of the verses.

Superb edition in 22 volumes, verified and annotated, and the last volume contains search indexes.

name: Al-Milal wa an-Nahal by Ash-Shahrastani (548H) - Sects & Religions
description_short:
In this work "al-Milal wan-Nihal", Abu al-Fath al-Shahrastani (548H) speaks, as the title indicates, of the different religious dogmas and sects that humanity has known.

The author begins his book by talking about sects affiliated with Islam. He quotes the known sects, then for each sect the author enumerates the various (sub-sects) that are in fact drifts and branches of the main sect, mentioning their founder and explaining in detail their doctrines, their dogmatic deviations, their errors and their innovated beliefs, here are some examples:

The Mu'tazilah and their sub-sects ; The Khawarij and their sub-sects ; The Mourjia and their sub-sects ;
The Shi'ites and their sub-sects ...

Then he does exactly the same job but this time with the people of the Book and their sects:

Then again for the other polytheistic religions: Zoroastrians (majous), pagans worshipers of idols and statues, worshipers of celestial bodies, beliefs of the Arabs during the pre-Islamic period, the various polytheistic doctrines present in India, ...

He also mentions a long chapter on philosophy and philosophers (from Greek philosophy to Arabic philosophy) mentioning the founders of different currents and also explaining in detail their misguided doctrines and erroneous beliefs.

name: Regarding Hadeeth "My wife does not prevent the hand of a man who touches her"
description_short:
Here are two Risalahs, one from Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani and the other from Ibn Abdelhadi, about a controversial hadith where a person who came to the Prophet salallahu 'aleyhi wa sallam and said: "My wife does not prevent the hand of a man who touches her." So he said salallahu 'aleyhi wa sallam: "divorce her." [...] (Abu Dawood 2044-2049).

There are big differences on the meaning of the hadith but also on its authenticity because one group of scholars accepts it and another refuses it. The Muhaqqiq of these two Risalahs makes the point in the introduction on this subject which is very useful for the reader.

Edition verified, authenticated and annotated.

name: Mawsu'ah at-Tafsir al-Mathur - 25 volumes
description_short:
Probably the most important and most impressive Tafsir developed in our time. This Tafseer brings together ALL the Hadeeth of the Prophet, the Athaar of the Sahaabas, Taabi'eens and Taabi' Taabi'een that exist.

This monumental work is the fruit of 10 years of research, in hundreds of books of Tafseer, Hadeeth, Fiqh, Aqeeda etc ... in order to gather all the hadiths and athars existing and provide their reference.

The lastest edition in 25 volumes is absolutely beautiful, with a great quality of printing and layout, and the referencing of all the athars and hadith, and the authentication of all hadiths.

And as if that was not enough, we also find annotations taken from the great Imams of Tafsir to clarify and deepen the explanation.

The first volume is a Madkhal to fully understand the work and its methodology, and the last is a search summary by hadith (alphabetical order) and by athars (by name of Sahaba or Tabi ').

name: Hidayah al-Murtab (poem on Ayaat Mutashabbih) - As-Sakhawi
description_short:
This is the first work of scientific poetry written on the theme of Mutachabbih verses, the verses that are similar or close. It is an ancient science (the first work was written in the 2nd century of the Hegira) and important for students and memorizers of the Holy Quran.

This poem is the work of Imam 'Alam ad-Din Abul-Hassan' Ali ibn Muhammad as-Sakhawi (558-643H). He is the pupil of Imam ash-Shatibi, the author of the famous Matn in Qur'anic readings and the rules of Tajwid.

This edition contains the Matn 100% harakat and many useful supplementary and explanatory annotations, as well as an introductory research on the subject of Ayat Mutashabbih.

name: 3 Rasail fi 'Ilm Mustalah al-Hadith - Abu Dawud, ibn Tahir, al-Hazimi
description_short:
The common point of these 3 epistles is the knowledge of the conditions of the 6 Imams of the Hadith in the acceptance of chains of narrations (Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nassai, Ibn Majah).

Knowing the conditions of these great imams is an essential prerequisite for the study of their book or the science of the Hadeeth. The 3 Risalas are as follows:

  1. Risalah al-Imam Abi Dawood al-Sijistani ila Ahl Makkah fi Wasf Sunanihi - Imam Abu Dawud (author of the Sunan, 275H)
  2. Shuroot al-A-immah as-Sittah - Al-Hafidh Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Maqdissi (507H)
  3. Shuroot al-A-immah as-Khamsah - Al-Hafidh Muhammad ibn Mussa al-Hazimi (507H)


These 3 works are verified and commented by the Muhaddith Abdul Fattah Abu Ghuddah who has written introductions to each book and additional annotations to facilitate the reader's understanding. Harakat in part.

name: Jaami' ibn Faaris - Jaami' fi al-Qira'at al-'Ashr wa Qira'at al-A'mash
description_short:
This work is one of the most comprehensive that exists, it was written by Imam Abul-Hasan ibn Faaris (452H) and Imam ibn al-Jazary reports that originally this Jaami 'gathers 35 different Tariqat in the Qur'anic readings and it is one of the most authentic work in the field. Ibn al-Jazary drew from this book for his own works.

This treasure of Qiraat science is published for the first time from the only manuscript available, which contains 18 different Riwayahs.

At the beginning of his book, Ibn Faris exposes the different rules of reading and the specificities of each Riwayah, examples to support. Then, according to the order of the surahs, he mentions every word and verse that has differences of reading or writing according to the different Riwayahs.

description_short:
The Athars of Imam ibn al-Qayyim are a collection of books and epistles of Imam ibn Qayyim al-Djawziya with careful verification from several manuscripts. This edition is considered by many specialists as the best on the works of Ibn al-Qayyim. Several serious Muhaqqiq worked on it under the supervision of Sheikh Bakr Abu Zayd.

This Majmou 'includes the following books:

(01) Badaa'i al-Fawaa-id: 5 volumes (1775 pages) + 1 volume for detailed research indexes (important for this book). Checked from 14 manuscripts.

(02) Al-Waabil as-Sayyib wa Raafi' al-Kalim at-Tayyib: 1 volume (603 pages). Checked from 4 manuscripts.

(03) Jalaa al-Afhaam fi Fadl al-Salaat wa al-Salaam wa Khayr al-Anaam: 1 volume (795 pages). Checked from 6 manuscripts.

Majmoo 'ar-Rasaail which includes the following epistles:
(04) Ar-Risaalah at Tabookiyyah: 138 pages, 10 manuscripts.
(05) Risaalah ila Ahad Ikhwaanih: 104 pages, 4 manuscripts.
(06) Ighaathah al-Lahfaan fi Hukm Talaaq al-Ghadbaan: 123 pages, 1 manuscript.
(07) Qutyaa fi Seeghah al-Hamd: 84 pages, 2 manuscripts.

All books have annotations referencing and authenticating hadiths and detailed research indexes.

name: Al-Hamawiyyah al-Kubra - Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
Some of the inhabitants of the city of Hama’ from the Levant sent a question in the year 698 AH to Ibn Taymiyyah, asking him about the scholars’ opinions on the Attributes with which Allah has described Himself in the following Verses: (The Most Beneficent (Allah) Istawa (rose over) the (Mighty) Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty) (Surat Taha: 5), and (Then He Istawa (rose over) towards the heaven when it was smoke) (Surat Fussilat: 11); and the Prophetic Hadiths: “Verily, the hearts of all human beings are between two of the Fingers of the Most Merciful” and “Almighty Allah will put his Foot in Hell Fire”.

Ibn Taymiyyah answered these questions in great detail and clarification (this answer was known as “The Great Hamawiyyah Creed,” in a 50-page treatise, and it is included in “A Collection of Great Messages”. Historians have mentioned that in this treatise Ibn Taymiyyah spoke about the doctrine of the Companions, the followers, the diligent Imams, and the earlier theologians, such as Abu al-Hasan al-Ash’ari, and al-Qadi Abu Bakr al-Baqlani and al-Juwayni; and that his sayings and compositions were inferred, and from some of their books that they saw belief in Allah’s Attributes as one of the obligations of religion, without questioning Allah’s Attributes, likening Allah’s Attributes to those of His Creation, distortion of the meaning, or denial of Allah’s Attributes.

name: Musnad Abi Ya'la (307H)
description_short:
The Musnad of Abu Ya’la is a major collection of Prophetic traditions, organized according to the Companion who narrated each report. Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili, a contemporary of the authors of the "Six Books," was renowned for his longevity and the "elevation" of his chains of transmission ('Uluww al-Isnad). This work is historically recognized in two versions: the Musnad al-Kabir (The Large) and the Musnad al-Saghir (The Small), with the latter being the version preserved and studied in this edition.

The methodology provides a vast landscape for studying chains of narrations, including numerous reports not found in the Sahihayn. Major scholars such as Ibn Hajar and al-Haythami held this work in high regard, frequently utilizing it to extract unique narrations (Zawa'id).

This comprehensive compendium contains 7,555 Hadiths, complete with their respective chains of narrators (Isnad). Following the systematic arrangement seen in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, the author has indexed the entries by the names of the Companions, gathering all narrations attributed to a specific Companion under their individual biography for ease of reference and comparative study.

name: As-Sunan al-Kubra of Hafidh al-Bayhaqi
description_short:
al-Sunan al-Kubra by al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi is one of the most important Hadith compilations in Islamic history, particularly in the domain of legal (Fiqh-based) Hadith arrangement. It gathers thousands of narrations, often with complete isnads, organized by chapters of Islamic law—covering rulings in purification, prayer, zakah, fasting, transactions, judiciary, punishments, oaths, and more.

What sets this work apart is al-Bayhaqi’s method: he combines authentic Hadiths with narrations from the Companions and Tabi‘in, followed by his own critical analysis and scholarly insights. His careful reasoning reflects deep knowledge of Hadith sciences (‘ilm al-rijal, ‘ilal, grading), as well as a jurist’s attention to legal application. The work bridges Hadith and Fiqh in a way that has long served scholars of both disciplines.

Imam al-Dhahabi said: "Al-Sunan al-Kubra by itself is proof of al-Bayhaqi’s vast memorization, deep insight into narrators and hidden defects, and firm Shafi‘i jurisprudence. None of our scholars equals him in this field."

name: Tafsir Ibn al-'Arabi - Ahkam al-Quran
description_short:
Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi al-Maliki (d. 543 AH) was a towering Andalusian judge and polymath whose mastery of Hadith and Fiqh allowed him to bridge the scholarly traditions of the Islamic West and East. This seminal work is a cornerstone of legal exegesis, organized by Surah and focusing exclusively on verses containing legal rulings. He employs a rigorous methodology that extracts jurisprudence directly from the text, discussing evidences from the Quran and Sunnah while engaging with various schools of thought. His approach utilizes the principles of jurisprudence (Usul) and Arabic linguistics, making it an essential guide for students mastering the art of legal deduction.  

The text holds a prestigious position as one of the finest Maliki contributions to the genre of "Ayat al-Ahkam" and served as a primary source for Imam al-Qurtubi in his later exegesis. Throughout the volumes, the author’s expertise is evident in his logical refutations and commitment to authentic narrations while discarding baseless legends. It provides the student with a robust legal framework to understand the Sharia’s objectives through the Quranic revelation.

name: Al-Majmu' Sharh al-Muhaddhab - Imam an-Nawawi (22 volumes)
description_short:
One of the most important encyclopedia of Fiqh that was written, under the pen of the great Shafii Imam, an-Nawawi (author of Riyadh as-Salihin), comparable to the Mughni of Ibn Qudama al-Maqdissi, because it exposes the differences in the 4 schools.

This immense collection is the explanation of a great work by Fiqh Shafii, the Muhadhab of Imam ash-Shirazi (476H). Imam an-Nawawi (676H), who died at the age of only 45, was unable to finish the Charh (up to the Riba chapter). His work was then continued by Imam as-Subki (756H) in the same style but without being able to finish it either.

The work that complements this essential Sharh is the work of Sheikh Muhammad Ayman ash-Shabrawi (specializing in the Hadith, he studied at Sheikh Muqbil and Sheikh al-Albani), who is the Muhaqqiq of this edition of the Majmu ', and who finished the explanation of the original Matn, thus allowing the reader to have an entirely completed work.

His work is faithful to the methodology of Imam an-Nawawi, taking care to explain the Matn in the light of the great Imams Shafii, citing all the evidence for each subject and their authenticity, and quoting the opinions of others. Madhhab and their arguments.

name: Hashiya Ibn Abidin ala ad-Durr al-Mukhtar - Fiqh Hanafi
description_short:
Radd al-Muhtar 'ala al-Durr al-Mukhtar, universally celebrated as Hashiyat Ibn Abidin, is the paramount and definitive encyclopedic reference for legal rulings and fatwas in late Hanafi jurisprudence. Authored by the eminent 13th-century AH Syrian jurist Imam Muhammad Amin Ibn Abidin (d. 1252 AH), known as the seal of the verifying scholars (Khatimat al-Muhaqqiqin), this monumental super-commentary serves as an exhaustive marginal gloss on Imam al-Haskafi’s Al-Durr al-Mukhtar (which itself comments on Tanwir al-Absar).

Recognized across the Muslim world as the ultimate relied-upon (Mu'tamad) authority for judges, jurists, and muftis, Ibn Abidin synthesizes centuries of Hanafi legal heritage with meticulous analytical rigor. He methodically resolves complex discrepancies between earlier classical authorities, investigates custom ('urf), and provides nuanced legal reasoning across every branch of Islamic law, from ritual worship to intricate commercial transactions and family law. It remains an indispensable cornerstone for students of Hanafi fiqh, judges, and comparative legal researchers.

name: Tabaqat al-Kubra of Ibn Sa'd - 5 volumes (100% harakat)
description_short:
Imam Ibn Sa'd (d. 230 AH), the dedicated student of al-Waqidi, compiled this monumental encyclopedia as the first comprehensive record of the Prophetic era and the generations that followed. The methodology is pioneering, organizing the biographies of the Sahaba, Tabi'un, and later scholars into "Classes" (Tabaqat) based on their seniority, merits, and geographical locations. By documenting thousands of individuals, including a dedicated section for women, Ibn Sa'd provided the essential framework for "Ilm al-Rijal" (biographical evaluation), allowing students to verify narrator reliability through historical context.

The significance of this work lies in its proximity to the source of revelation, offering a vivid and sober portrayal of the early Islamic community’s intellectual fabric. It begins with a detailed biography of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, serving as one of the earliest and most authentic sources of Sira. For the student of knowledge, Al-Tabaqat is more than a history book; it is a vital academic tool that reconstructs the golden ages of Islam with a focus on virtue and scholarly transmission, making it a cornerstone of any serious research library.

Edition verified from the complete manuscript of the work, with referencing of Hadeeth, 100% harakat.

name: Memoirs of Ali at-Tantawi - Dhakariyat 'Ali at-Tantawi (9 volumes)
description_short:
Sheikh 'Ali al-Tantawi is a Syrian scholar of Egyptian origin. Born in 1909 and died in 1999, he had a very rich life, indeed he was a student, journalist, judge, teacher, preacher or writer. He lived in Syria and Saudi Arabia and traveled extensively for different diplomatic missions, especially for the Palestinian cause.

His memoirs consist of many articles written over time, in which he tells his biography, from his childhood to old age, tells us anecdotes of all kinds, gives us lessons ... He also gives a lot of details on the historical events he witnessed during his life, as well as the cultures, cities and continents he knew or visited. He also spoke about the Islamic religious or political problems of the Ummah of the 20th century, indeed he was a witness and important player in the Palestinian crisis and lived during his lifetime the regained independence of all the colonized Muslim countries.

His memoirs read like a biography, a novel, a book of history ... This is a great opportunity to read literary texts and enriching for students in Arabic, this kind of literature is paramount to improve his level especially in Balaghah. It thus benefiting from the pen of a great writer and can practice the richness of Arabic in a book that are not purely scientific.

name: Al-Iqna' li Talib al-Intifa' of Imam al-Hajjawi (Fiqh Hanbali) - Harakat
description_short:
Al-Iqna‘ li-Talib al-Intifa‘ by al-‘Allāmah Musa ibn Ahmad al-Hajjawi (d. 968H) is one of the cornerstone texts of Hanbali jurisprudence, widely studied for centuries as an intermediate manual in Fiqh. It represents a mature and well-organized presentation of the legal rulings of the Hanbali madhhab, systematically arranged across the major chapters of worship and transactions.

The book is valued for its balance between conciseness and precision, offering a clear articulation of the relied-upon (mu‘tamid) positions within the madhhab while occasionally noting variant opinions from authoritative Hanbali jurists. Together with Zad al-Mustaqni‘, it forms the primary foundation of later Hanbali legal study and commentary.

description_short: This work provides an authoritative and specialized commentary by Sheikh Abd al-Karim al-Khudayr on the celebrated Introduction to Sahih Muslim. While Imam Muslim—the author of the world-renowned Sahih Muslim—is best known for his collection of authentic traditions, his "Introduction" is a foundational manifesto of Hadith science. In this commentary, Al-Khudayr explores the methodology of Hadith criticism, the classification of narrators, and the rigorous criteria used to distinguish authentic reports from weak or fabricated ones.

name: Hashiyyah 'ala Ikhtisar 'Uloom al-Hadith (ibn Kathir) - Abdulkarim al-Khudayr
description_short:
This volume contains the extensive and highly specialized annotations (Hashiyah) by Sheikh Abd al-Karim al-Khudayr on the classic work Ikhtisar 'Ulum al-Hadith. The original text was authored by the great Imam Ibn Kathir—the author of the world-renowned Tafsir Ibn Kathir—who summarized the definitive foundation of Hadith sciences by Ibn al-Salah. Sheikh al-Khudayr’s annotations provide a deep academic dive into the technical terminology, historical development, and methodologies used by the early masters of Hadith.

The methodology of this Hashiyah is rooted in traditional scholarly rigor. Sheikh al-Khudayr meticulously clarifies intricate points regarding the authenticity of narrations, the nuances of Hadith nomenclature (Mustalah), and the subtle differences between the schools of the early and later specialists. It is an indispensable resource for advanced students of knowledge and researchers seeking to master the "Science of Men" (Rijal) and the critical evaluation of Prophetic traditions, all while benefiting from the combined legacy of Ibn Kathir’s summary and Al-Khudayr’s contemporary insights.

name: Sharh al-Waraqat (Usul al-Fiqh) - Abdulkarim al-Khudayr
description_short:
Tahbir al-Safahat is an academic and highly detailed commentary by Sheikh Abd al-Karim al-Khudayr on the seminal text Al-Waraqat by Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni. Al-Waraqat has served for centuries as the primary entry point for students into the science of Usul al-Fiqh (Principles of Islamic Jurisprudence), and in this volume, Sheikh al-Khudayr provides a contemporary breakdown that honors the depth of the classical tradition.

The methodology of the commentary focuses on defining the technical terms of legal theory, such as commands and prohibitions, general and specific rulings, abrogation (Naskh), and the conditions for independent reasoning (Ijtihad). Sheikh al-Khudayr’s explanation is known for its pedagogical precision, as he bridges the gap between the concise, often complex language of Imam al-Juwayni and the needs of modern students. It is an essential work for anyone looking to build a strong foundation in how Islamic law is derived from its primary sources.
feature_id_17: In Part

name: Sharh al-Arba'in an-Nawawi - Abdulkarim al-Khudayr
description_short:
Al-Riyadh al-Zakiyyah is a brilliant contemporary commentary by Sheikh Abd al-Karim al-Khudayr on the most famous Hadith collection in the Islamic world, The Forty Nawawi by Imam al-Nawawi. This work is distinguished by its meticulous academic depth, providing a comprehensive analysis of the 42 fundamental Prophetic narrations that encompass the core pillars of Islamic creed, law, and ethics.

Sheikh al-Khudayr’s methodology involves a thorough linguistic examination of the Hadith texts, followed by a detailed exploration of their jurisprudential (Fiqh) implications and spiritual lessons. He draws extensively from the classical commentaries of the past, such as those by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali, while presenting the material in a clear, structured format suitable for modern students.

name: At-Ta'liqat as-Saniyyah 'ala al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah- Abdulkarim al-Khudayr
description_short:
Al-Ta'liqat al-Sunniyyah is a precise and academically rigorous commentary by Sheikh Abd al-Karim al-Khudayr on the seminal creedal text, Al-Aqidah al-Wasitiyyah by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. This commentary is highly regarded for its adherence to the methodology of the Pious Predecessors (Salaf) and its focus on clarifying the essential tenets of Islamic monotheism, the Divine Attributes, and the fundamentals of faith.

Sheikh al-Khudayr’s methodology is characterized by meticulousness and a deep connection to classical scholarly terminology. He unpacks the concise phrases of Ibn Taymiyyah with linguistic precision and scriptural evidence from the Qur'an and Sunnah. This work is an excellent resource for intermediate students of knowledge who seek a commentary that balances traditional depth with clear, contemporary explanation, ensuring a robust understanding of the Sunni creed in its most authentic form.

description_short:
Sabil al-Rashad is a powerful contemporary commentary by Sheikh Salih al-Fawzan on the classical work Tathir al-I'tiqad by Imam al-San'ani, the author of the famous Subul al-Salam. This treatise is a foundational text in the purification of the Islamic creed, specifically addressing the concept of Monotheism (Tawhid) and the necessity of directing all acts of worship solely to Allah, free from the taints of innovation and associationism.

Sheikh al-Fawzan's explanation is renowned for its accessibility and logical flow. He meticulously breaks down Al-San'ani's arguments regarding the reality of polytheism in later generations and the confusion surrounding intercession and seeking aid. This volume is an essential guide for anyone seeking to understand the Athari approach to creedal purity and the practical implications of a sound belief system in the face of modern and historical deviations.

name: Fath al-Wali al-Hamid fi Sharh ad-Durr an-Nadid (Shawkani) - Al-Fawzan
description_short:
Fath al-Wali al-Hamid is a masterly contemporary commentary by Sheikh Salih al-Fawzan on the classical text Al-Durr al-Nadid by the renowned Imam al-Shawkani. This work is a dedicated treatise on Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (the Oneness of Worship), specifically focusing on purifying one's devotion to Allah from all forms of associationism (Shirk). Sheikh al-Fawzan brings his characteristic clarity and precision to Al-Shawkani’s original arguments, making this essential study of monotheism accessible to both students and the general public.

The book addresses critical issues regarding intercession (Shafa'ah), the reality of seeking aid from the deceased, and the boundaries of legal and illegal mediation in worship. Sheikh al-Fawzan carefully breaks down Al-Shawkani's proofs, which are heavily rooted in the Qur'an and Sunnah, providing contemporary context and further scholarly insights.

name: Al-Bayan fi 'Addi Ayyi al-Qur'an - Abi Amr ad-Dani (444H)
description_short:
This work of the great Imam specialist, Abu 'Amr ad-Dani comes to explain and treat the subject of the number of verses in the Qur'an.

The copies of the Qur'an that we are reading now are almost all identical, but the numbering of the Mushaf was the subject of divergence for the people ok knowledge, because of the different readings, the inclusion or not of the Basmalah as the first verse of every surah etc.

Imam ad-Dani is one of the greatest references in this field that are the sciences of the Koran. The number of verses, its writing, its calligraphy, its preservation were the subject of work and have a history that we must also know.

Beautiful edition, verified, authenticated, annotated.

name: Mishkat al-Masabih by Imam at-Tibrizi (741H)
description_short:
Mishkat al-Masabih is a celebrated Hadith collection authored by al-Khatib al-Tabrizi. It serves as an enhanced, expanded version of Masabih al-Sunnah by al-Baghawi. While al-Baghawi’s original work was lauded for its comprehensive categorization of prophetic traditions, covering everything from creed and ethics to law, it lacked source citations for the narrators.

Al-Tabrizi refined this by meticulously authenticating the narrations and identifying the Companions who reported them. He innovatively organized each chapter into three sections: the first features traditions from Sahihayn (Bukhari and Muslim); the second includes reports from the other major Sunan and Musnad collections; and the third contains supplemental, thematic narrations. By adding over 1,000 Hadiths, al-Tabrizi transformed the work into a standard reference, earning it numerous commentaries and widespread acclaim.

name: Tafsir of the Quran for the youngest
description_short:
Crafted by specialists in Islamic history and education, this brilliant and indispensable work is specifically designed to make the Divine Word accessible to children and young people. The methodology is both pedagogical and synthetic, perfectly adapted for a young audience approaching the Quran for the first time. It bridges the gap between classical scholarly tradition and modern learning needs by focusing on a simple, clear explanation of the great lessons to be taken from the revelation while demystifying difficult vocabulary through concise definitions.

By avoiding complex linguistic disputes, the text ensures that students (Tulab al-'Ilm) can focus on the core guidance and moral foundations of each Surah. The structure promotes ease of understanding, making it an ideal resource for both classroom instruction and family study circles. Its significance lies in its ability to instill a direct, meaningful connection with the Quran from an early age, serving as a vital stepping stone toward more advanced studies in exegesis.

name: Nur al-Yaqin fi Sirah Sayyid al-Mursalin - Al-Khudhari
description_short:
This book is a timeless classical masterpiece of modern Prophetic biography (Seerah), universally celebrated for its exceptional clarity, beautiful literary prose, and pedagogical value. Authored by the prominent Egyptian scholar, judge, and historian Sheikh Muhammad al-Khudari Bek (d. 1345 AH / 1927 CE), the text serves as an accessible, highly reliable chronicle of the life of Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), successfully bridging the depth of massive classical volumes with the readability required by modern students.

Al-Khudari's primary objective was to present a pure, authenticated historical account free from weak or overly embellished narrations. To achieve this, he systematically synthesized material from the most authoritative primary sources of Islamic history—such as Sirat Ibn Hisham, Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd, and Tarikh al-Tabari—while constantly aligning the historical events with relevant verses from the Holy Quran and authentic Hadiths. For decades, Nur al-Yaqin has been adopted as a standard foundational curriculum text in schools, institutes, and prestigious universities like Al-Azhar, making it an indispensable volume for anyone seeking a structured, chronological understanding of the prophetic era.

Al-Khudari's primary objective was to present a pure, authenticated historical account free from weak or overly embellished narrations. To achieve this, he systematically synthesized material from the most authoritative primary sources of Islamic history—such as Sirat Ibn Hisham, Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd, and Tarikh al-Tabari—while constantly aligning the historical events with relevant verses from the Holy Quran and authentic Hadiths. For decades, Nur al-Yaqin has been adopted as a standard foundational curriculum text in schools, institutes, and prestigious universities like Al-Azhar, making it an indispensable volume for anyone seeking a structured, chronological understanding of the prophetic era.

name: The biography of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab- 100% harakat - Musa al-'Azimi
description_short:
Following his acclaimed work on the first Caliph, Musa bin Rashid al-'Azmi—the renowned author of Al-Lu'lu' al-Maknun fi Sirat al-Nabi al-Ma'mun—presents this definitive biography of the second Rightly Guided Caliph, Umar ibn al-Khattab (d. 23 AH). This volume provides a scholarly and narrative-rich exploration of the man known as "Al-Faruq," documenting his life from the pre-Islamic era through his transformative conversion and his pivotal leadership during the expansion of the Islamic state in the 1st century AH.

The author utilizes a rigorous, evidence-based methodology to highlight Umar's legendary justice, his administrative genius, and his unwavering commitment to the honor of the Ummah. From the establishment of the Hijri calendar to the sophisticated governance of a rapidly growing empire, Al-'Azmi portrays Umar as a paragon of duty and moral strength. By sifting through historical reports with academic precision, the book offers a clear and inspiring portrait of a leader whose legacy of integrity remains a foundational pillar of Islamic civilization.

Super Saudi edition, 100% harakat.

name: The biography of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan - 100% harakat - Musa al-'Azimi
description_short:
In this third installment of his series on the Rightly Guided Caliphs, Musa bin Rashid al-'Azmi—the acclaimed author of Al-Lu'lu' al-Maknun fi Sirat al-Nabi al-Ma'mun—chronicles the life of the third Caliph, Uthman ibn Affan (d. 35 AH). Known as "Dhun Nurayn" (The Possessor of Two Lights), Uthman's life is presented here through a lens of profound modesty, immense generosity, and unwavering dedication to the Prophetic legacy during the formative 1st century AH.

The biography meticulously details Uthman's early acceptance of Islam, his two-fold migration, and his pivotal role in funding the Muslim community during its greatest hardships. Al-'Azmi employs a disciplined historical methodology to explore the major milestones of his twelve-year caliphate, including the definitive compilation of the Quran (Al-Mushaf al-Uthmani) and the vast naval expansions of the Islamic state. Crucially, the author addresses the complex trials (Fitna) at the end of Uthman's reign with scholarly objectivity, portraying a leader who prioritized the blood of the Muslims over his own life, embodying the highest virtues of honor and sacrifice.

Great Saudi edition, 100% harakat.

name: Sharh Tajrid at-Tawhid al-Mufid of Al-Maqrizi - shaykh al-Fawzan
description_short:
Ifadat al-Mustafid is a masterly contemporary commentary by Sheikh Salih al-Fawzan on the classical treatise Tajrid al-Tawhid al-Mufid by the famous historian and scholar, Imam al-Maqrizi (d. 845 AH). This work is a profound exploration of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (the Oneness of Worship), specifically designed to strip away the layers of innovation and traditionalism that can obscure the pure monotheism taught by the Prophets.

Sheikh al-Fawzan’s commentary brings characteristic clarity to Al-Maqrizi’s rigorous defense of the Athari creed. The book meticulously defines the essence of sincere devotion, warns against the various forms of major and minor Shirk, and addresses the reality of seeking aid from other than Allah. By bridging the scholarly depth of a 9th-century AH master with contemporary pedagogical needs, this volume serves as a vital guide for any student seeking to understand the pillars of faith and the practical requirements of a sound creed.

name: Tafsir al-Quran al-'Adhim - Ibn Abi Hatim ar-Razi (327H)
description_short:
Here is one of the most famous Tafsir of the Salafs, on the common methodology of the first generations which was the Tafsir according to the Hadiths and Athars.

Hafidh ibn Abi Hatim ar-Razi (327H) reported in his Tafsir only 4 levels of Athars: the Hadiths of the Prophet, then the Tafsir of the Sahabahs, then Tabi'in, then Tabi Tabi'in and finally those who followed these.

His Tafsir is complete, verse by verse, when it's not word by word, until Surat al-Hud, then by selected Surah after that.

name: Treaty on the meditation of the Quran - Dr. A. Ma'sarawi & Dr A. Salih
description_short:
A very good book that details the Tadabbur al-Quran, the meditation and introspection that the reading of the Word of Allah is supposed to require by two Shuyukh of Al-Azhar, specialists in the Koran and its sciences.

They first define the Tadabbur, then how the Qur'an and the Sunnah invite us to that, then the various works and actions that help to meditate the Qur'an (Ikhlas, Isti'adha, Tajwid, attentive listening, the best moments , the reflection, the Qiyam Layl ...), and the things that prevent on the contrary (Kibr, carelessness, heart disease, sins ...). Finally the authors expose the fruits of Qur'anic meditation (Khushu ', al-Istinbat, al-'Amal bima fihi).

A good Risalah short but very beneficial to remind us to order.

name: Kitab al-'Adhamah by Abi Shaykh al-Asbahani (369H)
description_short:
Among the works of the Salafs who expose the Aqida and the Sunnah, here is that of the Hafidh Abi Ash-Sheikh as-Asbahani (274-369H).

His work deals with the Greatness of Allah, His Power, Dominance, and Governance, thus bringing together what relates to His Lordship and Attributes, and therefore what that implies regarding His Oneness in worship that the He owes it, that nothing can be equal or similar to Him.

Thus this work gathers Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah, Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah and Tawhid al-Asma wa al-Sifat, and also concerning the Faith to the invisible.

Excellent thorough Tahqiq with important annotations on narrative chains and narrators.

This Saudi edition is available only in this version where the last two volumes were published later and the first 3 reissued, so there is a slight difference in edition between the two.

name: Ar-Rad 'ala Ahl al-Bid'a - Ibn Qasim al-Qurtubi (353H)
description_short:
This Risala is rare, the manuscript from which it comes is unique and goes back to a student of Ibn Qasim al-Qurtubi. He makes a true statement of Aqida according to Ahl as-Sunnah, taking no detour and going into details.

It is an unknown work of the Aqida Athariyyah of the first centuries. Its author, Maslamah ibn Qasim al-Qurtubi took the science of many scholars of his time. His biography is controversial because it was falsely associated with a book of Sihr that he could not have written, just as he was called Mushabbih. But Ibn Hajar rectified all this in Lisan al-Mizan by saying that it was his opponents who called him so.

Saudi edition verified and annotated.

name: Al-Khulasah al-Fiqhiyyah 'ala Madhhab al-Hanabilah (100% harakat)
description_short:
This contemporary textbook serves as a brilliant, highly structured synthesis of the Hanbali school of jurisprudence. The author cleverly merges the core text and legal rulings of two of the most trusted and heavily relied-upon manuals in the late Hanbali tradition: Zad al-Mustaqni by al-Hajjawi and Dalil al-Talib by Mar'i al-Karmi. By breaking down the intricate scenarios of these two classical texts and sorting them systematically, the work delivers a comprehensive overview of standard Hanbali positions, aligning every ruling with the official corrections and standard preferences of Imam al-Mardawi in his monumental Al-Insaf.

The manual stands out for its layout and exceptional pedagogical utility. It is fully vocalized with tashkil from cover to cover, ensuring that difficult Arabic terminology, technical phrases, and proper legal vocabulary are pronounced without error. Furthermore, every ruling is reinforced by the underlying legal evidence from the Quran and Sunnah, supplemented by relevant references to the authentications of Sheikh al-Albani where applicable. Whether you are a beginning student trying to navigate the foundational standard rulings of the school, or an advanced researcher looking for a sharp, streamlined comparative breakdown of Zad and Dalil, this work provides an efficient reference.

Excellent explanation perfectly suitable to begin in the Madhhab Hanbali and / or to start the study of the book Zad al-Mustaqni'.

You will find (in order):

- An introduction to the Madhhab and its major works, Zad al-Mustaqni 's place among them, definitions of the legal terms and terminology of the school, and several important points to know.

- The Matn of Zad al-Mustaqni' on the part covering 'Ibadat (Tahara, Salat, Janaiz, Zakat, Hajj and Siyam), with simple annotations to explain the work. The Sheikh quotes the official opinion of the school but also the opinion of Ibn Taymiya. In the margins he quotes the opinions of other schools and references to return.

- At the end are several dozens of biography of the great Imams of Islam, from the first centuries until the 10th century, any school confused, in order to give a real general culture to the students on these men that we must know so much they brought to Islam.

The Sharh is the work of a Kuwaiti Sheikh, prefaced by Sheikh Ahmad ibn Abdallah ibn Humayd, who teaches Fiqh in Mekkah.

name: Iqra wa Arqa: Advices on Books and Reading - Dr. Ali al-'Imran
description_short:
Iqra’ wa Arqa (Read… and Rise) by Dr Ali al-‘Imran is an inspiring work that calls readers to rediscover the transformative power of reading, reflection, and knowledge through the perspective of faith. The author—well known for his scholarly editing of the works of Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim—shares profound insights on how reading nurtures intellect, strengthens belief, and refines the soul.

In addition to his reflections, Dr al-‘Imran includes a structured reading program for students, guiding them toward a gradual and purposeful engagement with essential Islamic and intellectual works. This makes the book both inspirational and practical for those seeking to build a lifelong relationship with beneficial knowledge.

Beautifully written and deeply motivational, Iqra’ wa Arqa appeals to students, educators, and anyone yearning to reconnect with the enriching discipline of meaningful reading.

name: Kitab al-Fasih - Imam Tha'lab (291H)
description_short:
With the conquests of territories, the Muslim empire has absorbed more and more non-Arabs, and in doing so the foreign words and misspellings of orthographies or phonetics have multiplied. Scholars have immediately written books to correct these errors and recall the correct word in literary Arabic, Fusha.

This work presented here, in the best edition, is the book that has survived and refers, and which was subject to many explanations.

Saudi edition, 100% harakat, color print, with explanatory introduction and research index.

name: Al-Musawwadah fi Usul al-Fiqh - Aal Taymiyyah
description_short:
Al-Musawwadah is a work written by 3 generations of the Ibn Taymiyyah family: Abu al-Barakat Majd ad-Din Abdul-Salam ibn Taymiyyah (652H), his son Shihab ad-Din Abdulhalim ibn Abdessalam ibn Taymiyyah (682H) and his famous grandson, Ahmad ibn Abdelhalim ibn Taymiyyah (728H).

This work of Usool Fiqh is particular, because the science of Usul Fiqh is usually divided into two great schools, Hanafi School and Shafii School (which have been followed for all or part by the majority of scholars). Here the authors, Hanbali recognized, have compared and analyzed the rules and foundations of his schools, quoted their arguments, quoted the opinions Hanbali and finally exposed the divergence and the most solid opinions.

Excellent Saudi edition in 2 volumes, fruit of the PhD thesis of Muhaqqiq, verified from 5 manuscripts, with many annotations on the text, the people cited, the hadiths and the context.

name: Jam' al-Juyuch wa ad-Dasakir ala ibn 'Asakir (ibn Abdelhadi) + 2 books
description_short:
3 books in 1 (read until the end):

The first is a rebuttal against Abul-Hassan al-Ash'ari, by one of his contemporaries, Abu 'Ali al-Ahwazi, entitled: Mathalib ibn Abi Bishr

The second book is a work by Yusuf Ibn Abdelhadi al-Hanbali (909H) who supports the first work and develops the statement concerning the errors of Imam al-Ash'ari: Kashf al-Ghata 'an Mahdi al-Khata.

To understand the third work, it must first be noted that the famous Hafidh ibn 'Asakir wrote a well-known refutation to the first Risalah "Tabiyyin Kadhib al-Muftari fima Nussiba ila al-Ash'ari". The third work is a refutation to this Risalah, still by Ibn Abdelhadi: "Jam 'al-Juyush wa ad-Dasakir' ala ibn 'Asakir".

May Allah reward the publisher for publishing these three works together in a very beautiful edition with introductions, Tahqiq and footnotes.

name: Complete study of Umdat ul-Fiqh 6 Vol. (Tables, Questions, MCT, CD)
description_short:
Beautiful contemporary work intended for the in-depth study of the Matn of Hanbali Fiqh Umdah al-Fiqh, Imam ibn Qudama al-Maqdissi.

Divided into 6 volumes in soft cover, printed in color on glossy paper, with a QR Codes containing all the structure of the work in the form of diagrams in a PowerPoint document.

The study looks like this:
  • The Chapter of Al-Umdah with the harakat.

  • Then the development of the chapter in titles, subtitles and numbered point, enumeration of conditions, sunnasetc ...

  • Then are listed the Fawaid, the points of reflection, on what subject of Usul Fiqh the subject is related, questions are asked to invite to develop the subject, to link it to contemporary questions and the student is invited to ask about the ins and outs of the Masail by using his reflection and inviting him to do some research.

  • Also at the end of the chapter is a series of multiple choice questions and also series of questions in the form of tables inviting to check the corresponding right Hukm.

In short, an excellent way to learn in a methodical and detailed way the Matn of Umdatul-Fiqh.

name: Al-Kalam 'ala Mas-alah as-Sama' - Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
description_short:
Published in full for the first time, here is the answer to a question asked to Ibn al-Qayyim regarding as-Sama ', the listening. If it can mean listening to the Qur'an or other permitted things, its meaning has slipped over time on Sufi songs with or without instruments, and other types of innovated or prohibited acts. Ibn al-Qayyim develops the subject with evidences and relying on the Fatawas of scholars of the four schools.

The Muhaqqiq has collected the manuscripts allowing to have the complete text, it also gathered before the work of Ibn al-Qayyim the Fatawas of great contemporary scholars to the author (8th century) such as: Taqi ad-Din as-Subki, Abil-Walid al-Maliki, Burhan ad-Din ibn Abdelhaqq al-Hanafi, Ibn Kathir ...

name: Simplified Study of Fiqh of Imam Ahmad (Diagrams, tables, Exercises)
description_short:
Here is a box containing 4 booklets designed to learn Fiqh in a complete but very educational way.

Each subject of Fiqh is exposed in the form of a diagram with arrows and colors in order to structure the comprehension, the ins and outs of the questions, the conditions, the branches, etc. Then comes questions in the form of answers to be formulated, from MCQ or series of questions in a table inviting to check the correct Hukm to confirm his learning.

The first book deals with Fiqh al-Akbar, ie Aqidah. It also covers an introduction to the Fiqh by explaining the history, the great Imams, the schools and their respective histories, the causes of differences.

The second covers the part of the Fiqh of I'badat.

The third deals with Fiqh Mu'amalat, rhe Family and legal penalties.

The last book contains the legal rules and Usul al-Fiqh.

In this new edition, the audio courses (mp3) and supports are available by QR codecovering.

An excellent work supervised by Sheikh Amir Bahjat, extremely pedagogical and well constructed that will teach you and allow you to revise in a simplified and methodological way.
searchable_keywords: Simplified Study of Fiqh of Imam Ahmad (Diagrams, tables, Exercises)

name: Ahkam al-Qur'an by Imam al-Bayhaqi / Ash-Shafi'i
description_short:
Although this book is from the pen of Imam al-Bayhaqi, it is actually the words of Imam ash-Shafi'i on the fundamental rules of science of the Koran and on the legal rules drawn from the word of Allah azzawa Jall.

This book was not written by Imam Al-Shafi’i - may Allah have mercy on him - but rather a collection and arrangement of the texts of Al-Shafi’i, which indicates the extent of his knowledge of the precise meanings of the Qur’an.

The purpose is to gather between Usul and Ahkaam of the Quraan; it is similar to the book Ahkam al-Qur’an by al-Jassas, and the book Ahkam al-Qur’an by Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi.

The book was compiled by one of the greatest Imams of his school, the Hafidh Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi (458H).

The purpose is to gather between Usul and Ahkaam of the Quraan; it is similar to the book Ahkam al-Qur’an by al-Jassas, and the book Ahkam al-Qur’an by Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi.

The book was compiled by one of the greatest Imams of his school, the Hafidh Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi (458H).

name: Kitab as-Siyar of Shaykh al-Islam al-Fazari (186H) - Maghazi & Siyar
description_short:
The Book of As-Siyar is one of the oldest books dealing with the subject of military campaigns, biographies andJihad, and related provisions and legislations. The author Abu Ishaaq al-Fazaaree, may Allah have mercy on him, followed a very good method, as he cited every issue with a Hadith Marfu’ (Traceable Hadith). If he does not find a Hadith Marfu’, then it will be by the sayings of a Companion of the Prophet. Then he would substantiate the issue, after that, with the sayings of those who came after the Companions, until he ends up with his scholars from among the Followers of the Tabi'in. Hence, the book is a source in the knowledge of the jurisprudence of the military campaigns, biographies andJihad.

Many of those who came after the author benefited from the book and quoted from it, such as Imam Ibn Jarir at-Tabari in his book “Tahdib al-Athaar” and Ibn Qutaybah in his book “Gharib al-Hadith”.

Excellent edition in 2 volumes, great quality of publishing, authenticated from manuscripts, and with references of the Hadiths or Athar. There is a detailled biography of Imam al-Fazary in introduction.

name: Wahy al-Qalam by Mustafa Saadeq Al-Rafe'ie
description_short:
“Wahy al-Qalam” book is a literary work written by Mostafa Saadeq Al-Rafe'ie, and is one of the most beautiful books written by the author. The book is composed of three parts, which are a collection of critical and constructive articles inspired by the contemporary social life and Islamic stories and history.

This kind of book is very important to perfect our level of Arabiclanguage, because the great writers use the figures of style and the most advanced techniques of the Arabic language, something that one can not reach in the reading of the technical books of Fiqh or Aqida.

In an article by Professor Wael Hafez Khalaf, published in Majallat al-Mujtama' al-Kuwaitiyyah, on the anniversary of the death of Al-Rafe'ie, entitled: (Al-Rafe'ie is the source of literature and the authority in Arabic language).
Shaykh Mohammed Rashid Rida described him as: “The most wonderful writer, the prolific poet and author, a man of great taste and accurate understanding, the diver on the jewels of meanings.”
Al-Muhaddith Ahmed Shakir described him as: “The Imam of writers in this era and the authority in Arabic language”.

name: Hujjat Allah al-Balighah - Shah Waliullah ad-Dehlawi
description_short:
This book is considered by researchers as one of the most important books written by Imam Waliullah Dehlawi. He wrote it in Arabic. It is one of the most useful books after the books of Imam Al-Shatibi if one wants to understand the purposes of Shari’ah law and it secrets.

Hujjat Allah Al-Balighah deals with the secrets of Islamic law, in all its parts and dimensions. The whole Islamic religion is presented in a coordinated and arranged fashion and in an inspiring and innovative way, which no scholar or Imam in Islamic history could produce. But this Imam, who was born in the land of India, was able to write it.

This book explains how Islam was found suitable for all races, cultures and people of the world and how successfully it solves social, moral, economic and political problems of human beings. Sheikh Muḥammad Manz̤oor Nomānī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “In my entire life, I have not benefited from the book of any human beings, as Allah has benefited me by this book. In this book, I have known Islam as a complete way of life, linked to each other. Many of the things of this sacred religion, which I believed in before by the faith of tradition, I started to believe in it, after studying this book - praise be to Allah - by insight and proof.”

Beautiful Syrian edition held in two volumes, authenticated and corrected, with annotations on the hadith and to clarify the meaning of the text when necessary.

name: Tafsir An-Nasafi (Madarik at-Tanzil wa Haqa-iq at-Ta-wil)
description_short:
It is a brief and useful interpretation, shortened by An-Nasafi from the interpretation of Al-Baydhawi and from Az-Zarkashi’s Al-Kashshaf. The author said, with regard to this Tafsir: “A book adopting a middle course in the interpretations, combining different ways of syntax and the Seven Modes of Recitation (of the Qur’an), containing particulars of rhetoric and semiotics [...] not long and boring, nor is it short and insufficient.”

An-Nasafi does not go into grammatical matters except gently, and he adheres to the Seven Modes of Recitation that are Mutawatirah, attributing each recitation to its reader. He also makes mention of the Major Sunni Madhaahib (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi’i and Hanbali) when interpreting the Verses of the rulings, often champions his Hanafi Madhab and responds to those who oppose him. He is Maturidi in the Sifat. He refuses the Hadith Mawdu' and and denounces the reference to the Isra’iliyyaat.

This Tafsir is an excellent way to benefit from the Balaghah explanation of az-Zarkashi without the Invented Hadith or the long I'rab.

The book is medium in size, easy to deal with, has been in circulation for centuries, famous among the people, was accepted by scholars and was taught to students in Al-Azhar and other schools of Shari’ah for several years.
searchable_keywords: Tafsir An-Nasafi (Madarik at-Tanzil wa Haqa-iq at-Ta-wil)

It is a brief and useful interpretation, shortened by An-Nasafi from the interpretation of Al-Baydhawi and from Az-Zarkashi’s Al-Kashshaf. The author said, with regard to this Tafsir: “A book adopting a middle course in the interpretations, combining different ways of syntax and the Seven Modes of Recitation (of the Qur’an), containing particulars of rhetoric and semiotics [...] not long and boring, nor is it short and insufficient.”

An-Nasafi does not go into grammatical matters except gently, and he adheres to the Seven Modes of Recitation that are Mutawatirah, attributing each recitation to its reader. He also makes mention of the Major Sunni Madhaahib (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi’i and Hanbali) when interpreting the Verses of the rulings, often champions his Hanafi Madhab and responds to those who oppose him. He is Maturidi in the Sifat. He refuses the Hadith Mawdu' and and denounces the reference to the Isra’iliyyaat.

This Tafsir is an excellent way to benefit from the Balaghah explanation of az-Zarkashi without the Invented Hadith or the long I'rab.

The book is medium in size, easy to deal with, has been in circulation for centuries, famous among the people, was accepted by scholars and was taught to students in Al-Azhar and other schools of Shari’ah for several years.
searchable_keywords: Tafsir An-Nasafi (Madarik at-Tanzil wa Haqa-iq at-Ta-wil)

name: Al-Mustadrak 'ala as-Sahihayn - Al-Hakim (405H)
description_short:
Al-Mustadrak ala aṣ-Ṣaḥeeḥayn or Mustadrak Al-Hakim is a five volume Hadith collection written by Hakim al-Naysaburi, in which the Hafidh collected additional authentic Hadiths that existed already in Sahih Al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim that he considered authentic, according to the conditions of either Sahih al-Bukhari or Sahih Muslim or both. He added some of the Hadiths that his independent opinion has led him to consider them authentic, with each type being distinguished from the other. But scholars have stated: He is lenient in the conditions of authenticity, and there are weak Hadiths.

Ibn Hajar said: “Al-Hakim was lenient in his authenticity of Hadiths, because he wrote the first draft of his book and when he started revising it, he died suddenly, or for other reasons.”

This famous collection is presented in an excellent edition in 9 volumes, meticulously verified from 6 manuscripts, just as each Hadith is referenced and authenticated according to the judgments of the other Imams of the Hadith more reliable, to know the exact degree of authenticity. Prefaced by Sheikh Shu'ayb al-Arnaout.

name: Maqamat al-Hariri with explanations, luxurious edition
description_short:
Al-Maqaamah (plural form: Al-Maqaamaat) is a novel in rhymed prose that is quoted in a specific place and includes many of the pearls of the Arabic language, unique masterpiece of literature, wisdom, proverbs and rare poems, which indicate the capacity of knowledge and the high status of the public storyteller, in rhymed prose. This book contains fifty literary Maqaamaat by one of the most famous people of this art: Abu Mohammed Al-Qasim Ibn Ali Ibn Mohammed Ibn Othman Al-Hariri, of Basra, Iraq. Al-Hariri was a scholar of Arabic language and literature and is primarily known for the refined style and wit of his collection of tales, Al-Maqaamaat.

This edition has been adorned with a detailed explanation of the Maqaamaat, combining all kinds of benefits and knowledge.

Dar Al-Minhaj Publications has adopted the Boulaq Edition (الطبعة البولاقية), putting its artistic and printing touches on it, in a very large size (20x28cm) for the sake of restoring rare antique books.

The book has been meticulously restored letter by letter, so the eye can enjoy looking at it and is easy to read. The Scientific Committee of Dar Al-Minhaj has also reviewed the Maqaamaat, in order to correct it and clear some obvious errors.

name: Bustaan al-'Aarifeen by Imaam an-Nawawi
description_short:
Bustan Al-‘Arifin is a book pertaining to asceticism, softening of hearts, piety and purification of the heart and soul by the Sayings of Allah and His Messenger, may Allah’s peace and blessing be upon him, the statements of his Companions, as well as many quotes from the great Awliya’ (those devoted to Allah) and people of knowledge.

Because this world is a mortal existence and not eternal, an abode of transit and not of joy, and an abode of impermanence and not of immortality, the Noble Qur’an has warned us against relying on it and be deceived by it, as well as the Prophet’s Hadiths and wise sayings of the Salaf Salih. That is why the most intelligent people in this world are the worshippers and the most reasonable in it are the ascetics. Imam An-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy upon him, said: “Human being must really follow the path of the wise, and adopt the doctrine of the insightful.”

The book’s author - an expert critic - mentions a collection of valuable matters that soften the heart and facts of knowledge, in a composed manner that distances his readers from boredom. Bustan Al-‘Arifinis based on the Verses of the Qur’an, the Prophet’s Hadiths, and the sayings of the first generations (Salaf Salih) and eminent later people.

Excellent Saudi edition, verified from manuscripts, great layout, most of Harakats, referencing of the Hadeeth.

name: Tanbih al-Ghafilin of Imam Abu Layth as-Samarqandi (373H)
description_short:
The book is an important reference for preachers, Du’at and teachers, for two reasons: the first is due to the course through which the author aims to give advice and moral guidance; the second reason is due to the method of As-Samarqandi in jurisprudence, which feels like he is addressing the public in a manner of invitation and intimidation (At-Targhib wat-Tarhib), and by relying on Ahadiths and traditions, whose style are predominated by invitation and intimidation, in order to move the emotions. He adopted the method of the righteous ancestors (the Salaf Salih) in asceticism, piety and preparation for the Day of Judgement.

Ad-Dhahabi said in his book “Siyar A’laam An-Nubala’”: “Abu al-Layth al-Imam al-Faqih al-Muhaddith, Abu al-Layth Nasr Ibn Mohammed Ibn Ibrahim As-Samarqandi al-Hanafi, the author of “Tanbih al-Ghafilin” ... His opponents spread rumours about him that he used Fabricated Ahadith.”

So indeed this book is known to gathering a lot of weak Hadith, even false ones. So we propose this book in a very beautiful edition, verified and authenticated, with annotation regarding the sources of the hadith and what the scholars says about the narrotors and its authenticity.

name: Al-Madkhal ila ‘Ilm As-Sunan - Imam al-Bayhaqi
description_short:
Imam al-Bayhaqi was one of the scholars who dealt with so many Islamic sciences and his writings areaperfect example of that. He has written many books about the Sunnah, about the Hadiths of Rulings, in ethics and moral values, in the Islamic Faith and in virtues. His book “As-Sunan Al-Kubra’” is more like a comparative jurisprudence, especially with the Hanafi’s scholars. The author wanted to gift us with a book that would be an introduction to those who wanted to read his book “As-Sunan Al-Kubra’”.

He divided his book into three basic parts: the terms used in Prophetic Tradition (Istilah al-Hadithiyyah); then the terms used in Usool al-Fiqh, and then the ethics of the teacher and student (Adab al-'Alim wa al-Muta'alim). For every chapter he quotes Hadiths and Athars.

So whoever wants to delve into the seas of “As-Sunan Al-Kubra’”, he must start with this book “Al-Madkhal ila ‘Ilm As-Sunan” to identify the methods and terminology of the scholars’ narrations of Hadith, according to Sha’fi’i Principles of Islamic Jurisprudence. It is truly a gem combining the method of Hadith scholars and Islamic Jurists.

Gorgeous Saudi edition in 2 volumes, with the referencing of every Athar and Hadith, and their authenticity according to some Muhaddith.

name: An-Nadiyah al-Islamiyah fi Siyar A'lamuha al-Mu'asirin (6 volumes)
description_short:
This book brings together the biographies of contemporary scholars (from the end of the 19th century to the beginning of the 21st century). The author wanted to gather the biographies of important scholars of our era, in order to make a modern biographical work, bringing together scholars of any horizon, any country, any specialty.

The author was an expert in Arabic literature (he presided in particular the faculty of Arabic language of Al-Azhar). He died in 2011, one year after the date of the publication of the 6th volume. It must be seen that Dr. Muhammad Rajab al-Bayyumi has compiled the biographies according to his religious and contemporary environment. As an Azhari scholar specialized in literature, one should not expect to find the great Salafi shuyukhs who died recently or at the end of the 20th century, even if we find great personalities such as Ahmad Shakir, Ibn Badis, Al-Ibrahimi or Muhammad ibn Ibrahim. You will discover the life of contemporary scholars who have marked their time or their places of life, or the sciences in which they were specialized.

Edition in 6 volumes, the volumes were published as the author advanced his work, the first volume in 1995 and the last in 2010. In the last volume there is a summary covering the 6 volumes.

name: Epistles of al-Allamah Makki bin Abi Talib al-Qissi
description_short:
A collection of precious treatises from the legacy of Imam Maki ibn Abi Talib al-Qaysi in the linguistic and grammatical Quranic sciences, gathered by Dr. Ahmad Hasan Farhat. The collection contains four treatises: on the particles "kalla, bala, and na'am" and the pause rules for each in the Quran, with their linguistic origins, reasoning, and grammatical positions; an abridgment of the above for practical use; a treatise on the elongation of the vowel in "ata, amana, and Adam" in response to those who objected to it; and a treatise on the doubled ya in the Quran and in Arab speech.

These treatises address questions rarely given dedicated treatment in the classical tradition, combining grammatical precision with the science of recitation in a methodology the editor identifies as distinctively original to Maki. They were edited by Dr. Ahmad Hasan Farhat, who spent decades locating and editing Maki's manuscripts from libraries around the world — a project rooted in his doctoral thesis on Maki's tafsir and qira'at, which had previously produced his critical edition of the "Al-Idah li-Nasikh al-Quran wa-Mansukhuhu."

name: Imam Ahmad's Musnad classified by chapters and simplified
description_short:
This book was prepared according to the Last Wish of Imam Adh-Dhahabi (died 748 AH), who said about Musnad Imam Ahmad:

“May Allah make available to this Great Volume someone who will arrange it, revise it, delete what is repeated, correct what is distorted, clarify the situation of the transmitters of its Hadiths, warn to the Mursal Hadith and weaken the Munkar Hadiths.
He then should arrange the names of the Prophet’s Companions in alphabetical order; put on each Hadith a symbol of Al-Kutub As-Sittah, i.e. books containing collections of Hadith compiled by six Sunni Muslim scholars. They are sometimes referred to as As-Sihah al-Sittah. They are: Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abu Dawud, Sunan at-Tirmidhi, Sunan an-Nasa’i and Sunan Ibn Majah.
And if I had not been able to do so for the weakness of my sight, lack of intention, and near death I would have done so.” (Siyar A’laam An-Nubala’: 13/525)

The Shaykh Salih ash-Shami, the Muhaqqiq said: “I have read the above statement after the preparation of this book and before the final correction. If I had seen it before I started working on the book, I would not have added anything to what Imam al-Dhahabi had wished for.” Indeed, he has also classified and arranged the Musnad according to the classic Fiqh chapters found in the Sounans.

Beautiful edition, 100% harakat, a great way to address this famous collection of Hadith.

name: Majma' az-Zawaid of Imam al-Haythami
description_short:
Majma’ Al-Zawa-id is a prominent example of the al-Zawa’id methodology of Hadith collection. It contains Hadith extracted from Musnad Ahmad, Musnad Abu Ya’la, the Musnad al-Bazzar, and three of At-Tabarani’s collections: Al-Mu’jam al-Kabir, Al-Mu’jam Al-Awsat and Al-Mu’jam As-Saghir. 

In the introduction, the Hafidh al-Haythami said:

"My teacher and mentor, prominent scholar of East and West, Sheikh Zayn al-Din Abu al-Fadl Abdul Rahim Ibn al-Iraqi, may Allah be pleased with him and grant him Paradise, said: “Collect these classified books and delete their Isnaad, so that the Ahadith of each category may be assembled in one category.” So I spent my time in collecting them..."

It is a huge book of Sunan collection that contains many of the Ahadith, of which the collector has paid great attention; until it became more than 18,700 Hadith.  Al-Haythami provides commentary on the authenticity of each Hadith and evaluates some of the narrators. Not only that, but he gave his rulings upon the Hadith he graded and sometimes talked about defect in the Hadith. Majma’ al-Zawa’id is arranged in the manner of a Sunan collection, by topical chapter titles relating to jurisprudence.

This book is “Sharh As-Soudour bi Sharh hal Al-Mawta wal-Qoubour,” and it is written by Jalal al-Din As-Souyouti. The author spoke about the Barzakh (the Stage between this world and the Hereafter), in which he mentioned death, its virtues, the manner of death, the attribute of the angel of death and his assistants, what happens to the dead when they die, the soul after its separation from the body, and its ascension to Allah, its meeting with other souls, and then its place. And he also spoke about the condition of the grave, its punishment and tightness, what benefit people in the grave; explaining all this from the time of the death throes until one is dead, adding to that the conditions of the Resurrection, the attributes of Paradise and Hellfire and the Signs of the Time.

The book is based on the Book of Allah, the Hadiths of Prophet Muhammad, may Allah’s Peace and Blessing be upon him, and the words of the great Imams of Hadith.

name: Al-Mumti' al-Kabir fi at-Tasrif - Ibn 'Usfur Al-Ishbili (669H)
description_short:
Dozens of books have been devoted to the topic of morphology, dealing with its subject and its materials by various means and methods. Until the Seventh century AH, there were abundant books on the subject, full of dry texts and footnotes and lengthy and elusive explanations. This led people to describe this science as harder than syntax and difficult for the students and teachers alike. This book transcends the history of its time and is an introduction for clarity, eloquence and simplicity.

However, when Ibn ‘Uṣfūr took up this scientific field he was able to breathe in it his Andalusian breath, paint it with the colours of simplicity, smoothness and purity. He collected all the morphological material which is needed by every student, researcher or author, and presented it in an easy educational method, establishing a friendly dialogue between himself and his readers, involving them in the formulation of results and information, and exploring their questions and problems, related to the subject, its elements, principles and rules.

Therefore, scholars were so impressed by this valuable book that Abu Hayyan an-Nahwi used to take it with him in all his travels, and collected the various copies.

Very serious edition, authenticated from 3 manuscripts.

description_short:

This book was written for the service of the Arabic language, and in order to bring morphology very easily to every student of this science of great importance.

name: At-Tafsir al-Mawdu'i li Suwar al-Quran al-'Adhim - Boxed Set
description_short:
“At-Tafsir Al-Mawdu’i li-Suwar al-Qur’an al-Azim” is written by Abd Al-Hamid Mahmud Tahmaaz and it is in Eight Volume boxed set. It contains an explanation (Tafsir) of all the Surahs of the Qur’an in a distinct scientific approach. It is one of the finest books of contemporary Tafsirs. It is a Tafsir that benefits the general intellectuals, Du’at and students. It contains useful knowledge, links the Verses to the contemporary needs of Muslims, correct misconceptions and also guidelines for strong faith and behaviour, in an easy style and avoidance of difficult specialized terms.

The author gathered the 'Ilm of dozens of Exegesis (ancient and modern) to extract the meaning and the objective of the verses and the stories of the Quran. He mention the sources in footnotes.

This book is part of a separate new type of Science of Qur’an Interpretation (Ulum al-Qur’an); however, it has ancient evidence and previous objectives. It appeared recently, and is meant to interpret the Holy Qur’an through its many topics tackled by the Verses. In a brief and abbreviated definition, it is a discipline that deals with issues according to the Qur’anic objectives, through one or more Surahs. To clarify this type of Tafsir, it is like talking about a particular issue by mentioning the Verses that have dealt with this topic or issue.

A excellent overall Tafsir, in a gorgeous boxed set, high quality.

name: Majmu' Rasail al-'Allamah Mar'i al-Karmi al-Hanbali
description_short:
Collection of the works of Mar’i Ibn Youssef al-Karmi (1033H), the insightful famous scholar, the author of many books and one of the most distinguished Hanbali’s scholars.

He was a Faqih, Usuli, Mufassir, Muhaddith, Nahwi, with a broad understanding of jurisprudence, has full knowledge of Al-Ulum An-Naqliyyah and Al-Ulum Al-Aqliyyah and he has the upper hand in all the sciences. He acquired knowledge from scholar al-Mardawi (1026 AH) and Yahya Ibn Musa’ al-Hajjawi. His scholars then gave him the license to teach and narrate Islamic religious knowledge. He was the top teacher in Al-Azhar Mosque he dedicated his entire time to learning, teaching and giving Fatwa, and writing and authentication. His books have become popular and a success. None of his numerous enemies could challenge his books or belittle them.

Ibn Humaid said: “He was a scholar, the most knowledgeable person, a researcher, an interpreter of the Qur’an, a narrator of Hadith, an Islamic jurist, al-Usuli, a grammarian and one of the most prominent Hanbalis in Egypt.”

Ibn Badran said: “One of the most prominent scholars of this doctrine in Egypt (i.e. the Hanbali Madhab).”

Abu Zayd said: “The scholar and an Islamic jurist.”

Excellent, high quality and very serious edition (Turkish publisher), gathering more than 50 books in different subject.

name: Qala-id al-'Iqyan fi Ikhtisar Aqidat Ibn Ḥamdan - Ibn Balban al-Ba'li
description_short:
An amazing, wonderful and very valuable abridged book. The author wrote this book to establish the real Aqeedah of the Hanbali scholars. Imam Ibn Balbān ad-Dimashqi al-Hanbali summarised this book from “Nihayat al-Mubtadi'in fi Usul ad-din” by Imam Ibn Ḥamdān al-Ḥarrānī al-Ḥanbalī (died 695 AH).

In this book, he summarized the Hanbali Sunni doctrine, refine it with evidence and proof and remove any kind of distortion. He wrote his book specifically according to the doctrine of the honourable Imam Ahmed Ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him.

This book had become widely known to the extent that it became the foundation and an authority of the Hanbali doctrines. This book could be a textbook for teaching students, because of its simplicity, ease of expression, clarity of its topics and the sincerity of its author. The author revealed in this book the falsity attributed to the Hanbali School: Tashbih (i.e. affirming similarity to Allah), Tajsim (Anthropomorphism) and Jiha (direction). The book is divided into five sections, a conclusion and a supplement as an advice to the Muslims.

The Muhaqqiq also wrote an explanation to the book (it is published after the main text) ; he supported it with statements from the Hanbalis’ books.

Very nice Saudi edition, 100% harakat on the Matn, verified, authenticated and annotated, with a superb layout.

name: Jami' al-Usul fi Ahadeth ar-Rasul - Ibn Athir (Tahqiq al-Arnaout)
description_short:
Ibn al-Atheer (606H) compiled in his book the following six books of Hadith: al-Muwatta, Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abu Dawud, Sunan al-Tirmidhi and Sunan al-Nassai.

The Hadiths are organized into themes, chapters and subchapters. To facilitate the search, al-Hafidh ibn Athir listed the chapters in alphabetical order rather than in the order of the case law chapters (as this differs according to collections or legal schools).

Other exceptional things, the author, a great specialist of the Hadith, takes the trouble to explain the important words of the Hadiths.

The chains of the Hadiths have been suppressed, except for the name of the Sahabi which records the Hadith of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).

This exceptional collection of thousands of hadiths, gathered in 13 volumes, is verified and annotated by Sheikh Abd al-Qadir al-Arnaout and his students, and he gives in annotations the references of each Hadith and its degree of authenticity according to the great Muhaddith.

name: Sharh az-Zarqani ‘ala Muwatta al-Imam Malik
description_short:
One of the most celebrated commentaries on Imam Mālik’s al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, this work by the renowned Maliki scholar Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Bāqī al-Zurqānī (d. 1122 AH) has become a cornerstone in Mālikī jurisprudence. Known formally as Anwār Kawākib Nahj al-Sālik, it is widely referred to as Sharḥ al-Zurqānī.

Al-Zurqānī explains every word of the Muwaṭṭaʾ with clarity and precision. He focuses on rare vocabulary, grammar, and detailed juristic analysis. The commentary is structured by merging the original text with explanatory notes, following the order of Imam Mālik’s compilation. It highlights various legal opinions, details the differing views among scholars, and defends the Mālikī school with supporting evidence. In discussing hadiths, the author traces their sources — especially from the six major collections — and gives special attention to narrations found in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

name: Tarikh Adab al-Arab by Mustafa Saadeq Al-Rafe'ie
description_short:
In the first part of the book Al-Rafe’ie has studied the Arabic Language, its origins, the phases of its refinement, its spread in the tribes, its phonetics, the different dialects of the speakers and the secrets of the language system. He singled out the second section of this part talking about narration and narrators.

The second part is devoted to the Holy Qur’an and prophetic rhetoric.

The third part contains a presentation of the history of Arab poetry, its schools, the fine arts created from it, the Andalusian literature, the writing and its history among the Arabs, the anecdotes of Arabic books, rhetorical devices and figures of speech.

Al-Muhaddith Ahmed Shakir described Mustafa ar-Rafi'i as: “The Imam of writers in this era and the authority in the Arabic language”.

name: Al-Ikhtiyar li Ta'lil al-Mukhtar - Imam al-Mawsili (683H)
description_short:
This is a book of Hanafi jurisprudence. Even more, it's a major one, it's an authority among the Ahnaf for centuries.

The author has compiled earlier in his youth an abridged book in Hanafi jurisprudence which he titled “al-Mukhtar lil Fatwa”. This book is studied and many works in the Hanafi Madhhab were made from it. Some scholars who studied his book asked him to provide an exposition indicating the causes of his legal issues and their meanings and mention additional branches (for more explanation). They also asked him to report any disagreement among the followers of the Hanafi School and explain its cause.

So he put forward this exposition, which he called “al Ikhtiyaar li Ta’leel al-Mukhtaar. It began with the book of purity and ended with the book of inheritance.

description_short:
This biography compendium of the Hanbali scholar Salih bin Abdul Aziz Al-Uthaymin (1410H) is the most complete book for Madhhab Hanbali.

Indeed, Sheikh Bakr Abu Zayd, who worked on the Tahqiq of the book, explains in the introduction that the author was very thorough in his work of researching and collecting the biographies of Hanbali scholars, beginning from Imam Ahmad to his time (the 14th century), bringing together more than 3,000 biographies.

Shaykh Bakr explains that if he combined everything that existed then as a work devoted to Hanbali scholars, it would turn around 1600 biographies only.

In spite of all the Shaykh Salih refrained from quoting all the biographies, and that is why the Muhaqqiq discovered during these researches some other hundreds of biography not present in the book, which he then gathered in a subsidiary work entitled "Fa-itu at-Tashil".

name: Jaami' al-Ummahaat (Mukhtasar ibn al-Haajib al-Far'i)
description_short:
Jami' al-Ummahat aw Mukhtasar ibn al-Hajib al-Far'i is a book on Maliki jurisprudence in which the author (Ibn Al Hajib) compiled a collection of jurisprudence issues and its branches summarized from the statements of the Maliki scholars and their famous books. He said: “When I was writing my book, I used to collect the famous books on jurisprudence, then write their content in a brief wording, and then compile it in a book until it was completed.” Some scholars who have studied the book mentioned that Ibn Al-Hajib had summarized his book from sixty books, and that it includes sixty-six thousand jurisprudence issues.

The praise for the book has been widespread in and outside the Maliki School of jurisprudence, and suffices here the testimony of Kamal al-Din al-Zamalkawi Ash-Shafi'i, who said: «The Shafi'i School does not possess something similar to the Malikis’ abridged book of Ibn Al Hajib”, and this testimony suffices enough as stated by Ibn Farhun.

Imam Ibn Daqeeq al-Eid said: "This book came with the wonder of wonders! The author hoped for a masterpiece work and his prayer was answered. He contented with the hardest of purposes; he brightly displayed and expressed his thoughts in his words in the most excellent manner.”

Excellent edition, verified from 5 manuscripts, with useful annotations.

name: Wajh an-Nahar (annotations to the Mushaf) - Abd al-Aziz ibn Harbi
description_short:
Wajh an-Nahar li Kashif 'an Ma'ani Kalam al-Wahid al-Qahhar is like a dictionary of difficult or technical words of the Quran. But let the Sheikh Abd al-Aziz ibn Harbi explains himself:

"In this book I did not intend to explain the Verses of the Qur’an, or to present its rulings as our predecessors had done, or to explain its unusual words as those who had written in the “Vocabulary of the Qur’an” had done before. But I pursued another course: In this book, I have combined the interpretation of the vocabulary of the Qur’an, and its unusual sentences whose syntax, meaning, pronouns and formulas are difficult to compose, and added to it some valuable benefits, clever remark and inferences that I have read in the books of Tafsir and other books of jurisprudence, fundamentals of Islamic jurisprudence, of what I have heard from Muslim scholars and what Allah has revealed to me."

Very beautiful edition.
