name: Athar al-Imam Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah - 24 to 27
description_short:
The Athars of Imam ibn al-Qayyim are a collection of books and epistles of Imam ibn Qayyim al-Djawziya with careful verification from several manuscripts. This edition is considered by many specialists as the best on the works of Ibn al-Qayyim. Several serious Muhaqqiq worked on it under the supervision of Sheikh Bakr Abu Zayd.

This Majmou' includes the following books:

(24) Miftah Dar As-Sa'adah: 3 volumes (1889 pages). Verified from 7 manuscripts.

(25) Ighathah al-Lahfan fi Masaid ash-Shaytan: 2 volumes (1396 pages). Verified from 7 manuscripts.

(26) Kitab ar-Ruh: 2 volumes (884 pages). Verified from 8 manuscripts.

(27) Al-Kalam 'Ala Masalah as-Sama': 1 volume (381 pages). Verified from 1 manuscript.

All books have annotations referencing and authenticating hadiths and detailed search indexes.

name: Ash-Shajarah an-Nabawiyyah (Family Tree of the Prophet)
description_short:
The unique work of the scholar Hanbali Yusuf Ibn Abdelhadi (909H) known as Ibn Mubarrid, who retraced as much as he could the Genealogical Tree of Messenger of Allah, going back to Adam, 'alayhim as-salat wa as-salam.

He also added many other chapters around the extended family of the Prophet (Uncles, Aunts, cousins, brothers and sisters of milk etc ...

At the end of the book are color photocopies of manuscripts superbly calligraphy and genealogical agencies, so much more beautiful than modern printing, you will definitely like it!

Very nice edition, verified from 3 manuscripts and previous editions, with some Harakat (especially on the proper names).

name: Tafsir al-Jalalayn in Annotations of the Holy Quran (3 formats)
description_short:
A beautiful edition of one of the most widespread Tafsir in the world, often studied first and foremost in the science of Tafsir.

These brief annotations were first of all the work of Jalal-ad-Din al-Muhalli (864H) and were completed by Imam Jalal ad-Din as-Suyuti (911H).

This edition has no "corrective" annotations, it is the original text, but the editor has added in footnotes the book "Al-Mukhtar As-Sahih min Asbab an-Nuzul" for adding some Fawa'id on the causes of the revelation of the verses.

The edition is of high quality, and it is available in 3 formats (cover colors are random).

description_short:
The Names of Allah Almighty are many, and they are very important for the Faith of the Muslim. This book is a significant attempt to collect other Beautiful Names, which are not the Ninety-nine Beautiful Names, but they do not oppose them, because Allah’s Names are countless.

In this Book, more than forty Beautiful Names of Allah, the Almighty, were counted, along with a description of each Name, an explanation of its meaning, its purposes and all the Verses indicating it.

A masterly work of the great scholar ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah in a beautiful Syrian edition verified and with referencing of the cited evidence.

name: Bughiah al-Muqtasid Sharh Bidayah al-Mujtahid (16 volumes)
description_short:
Here is the full explanation of the famous work of Fiqh compared by Ibn Rushd al-Hafid (595H), by Shaykh Muhammad al-Wa-ili. He is a contemporary scientist who died recently (1431H), Rahimahullah, who was the pupil of Shaykh Muhammad Amin al-Shanqiti and Sheikh al-Albani, he had among others as a pupil of Sheikh Soulayman ar-Ruhayli.

The commentator explains the words of Ibn Rushd, he details the various opinions cited by Ibn Rushd, citing the arguments and evidence. This beautiful edition is verified and annotated by Shaykha Kamilah al-Kuwari, giving the sources of the Hadiths and their degree of authenticity and the sources of the words quoted.

Very nice edition in 16 volumes, with some Harakats.

name: Juhud al-Malikiyyah fi Taqrir Tawhid al-’Ibadah
description_short:
This book is a comprehensive contemporary academic study focused on documenting the historical contributions of the Maliki school to the monotheism of worship (Tawhid al-Ibadah). Written by Dr. Abdullah bin Fahd al-Arfaj, it serves as a detailed mapping of classical Maliki literature to verify that the school's jurists consistently championed devotional monotheism. The text provides a clear presentation of orthodox theology by gathering explicit statements from premier Maliki authorities across different eras, refuting the misconception that later jurists within the school overlooked issues of creed and devotional practice.

The book is structured into detailed chapters that examine specific devotional acts and how Maliki scholars regulated them. Al-Arfaj categorizes these practices around standard doctrinal and jurisprudential themes, detailing the strict Maliki stance on supplication, vows, slaughtering, seeking aid (istighathah), and the prohibition of extreme veneration of graves. By using direct textual extraction from primary Maliki manuals and fatwa collections, the author provides a reliable reference for students investigating the integration of law and creed within the school.

name: Siwar Ummi - Ali ben Jabir al-Fifi
description_short:
Let's see what the author himself said about his book:

"In this book I have talked about the mother and her beating heart, the father and his overflowing tenderness, the teacher and his kindness towards his disciples, the brothers who share the soul, the beats, the dreams and the thoughts, and the friend whose existence embodies life. I have also spoken about the noble word and the word inhabited by evil; about gallantry and about the kindness with which peoples’ hearts are filled. I have also mentioned something about the diseases of the soul and the hearts’ medications.

In this book, I did not come up with peculiar things, nor did I seek wonders, or search for strange and rare stuff. Rather, I have tried to look at and contemplate the same scenes that everyone sees, but I have used another lens, which is a purely subjective lens, bearing my own colours and my modest experience. I have come up with the usual and well-known, and then I reproduced it and formulated it by either setting an example or adding further clarification."

** This book is a bestseller in the Arabian Peninsula **

name: Ar-Rajul An-Nabil - Ali ben Jabir al-Fifi
description_short:
“Ar-Rajul An-Nabeel” is considered among the modern books that have dealt with the biography of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in an easy linguistic style, while avoiding the usual form of presenting information that might affect tediously those who are not accustomed to reading.

The idea of writing the book “Ar-Rajul An-Nabeel” had been with Ali Ibn Jaber Al-Fifi for a long time, as he himself said in the introduction of the book: “I had thought for a long period of time of writing about the Prophet’s biography, talking about the days of his prophethood, and having the honour to write something about his pure merits and qualities...”

He also said: "I have called this book “Ar-Rajul An-Nabeel” because he, peace and blessings be upon him, was the noblest man known to mankind, and because nobility is evident in every aspect of his life, in his contentment and anger, in his grief and joy, before and after his prophethood; he is truly the noble man."

** Written by the bestseller author of "Li Annaka Allah" **

name: Al-Fasl fi Al-Milal wa al-Nihal - Imam Ibn Hazm
description_short:
This book is a study of the beliefs of non-Islamic religions, such as worshippers of the sun and planets, Christianity, idolaters, and many others, and also the opinions of Islamic groups and their doctrines such as the Mu’tazilah, al-Jahmiyyah, al-Qadariyyah, Shiites and other Islamic sects. It is an in-depth study of these beliefs and groups, and this edition has useful comments that serve the topic.

Unlike other similar books, this book is distinguished by a complete boldness in criticism, prudence in thought, discussion of thoughts of different Islamic and Non-Islamic groups and their criticism based on what was adopted by each group, then referring thereafter to the decisive and correct interpretation of the Qur’an and the Sunnah.

It took Ibn Hazm, may Allah have mercy upon him, up to twenty years to write this book, and he kept refining it and adding to it until his death.

Excellent edition in 3 volumes, reviewed, authenticated and annotated by two Saudi researchers from the Imam Muhammad bin Saud Islamic University  (major research work based on 14 manuscripts).

name: Tafsir ibn Juzay - Tashil al-Ulum at-Tanzil
description_short:
The book is about the interpretation of the Noble Qur’an and all other related sciences. The author has taken a beneficial course by making it a concise summary, discussing four purposes that include four benefits:

The first benefit: Collecting a great amount of sciences in a small book for the convenience of students, and bringing it closer to those interested. This book contains what was included in the long collections of science, but only after summarizing, scrutinizing and revising their chapters, and deleting their redundant and useless materials. The author has included in it every essential discipline of the science of the Qur’an, without excess or negligence; then he was determined to shorten the phrase, summarizing as much as possible and avoiding lengthening and repetition.

The second benefit: He has mentioned wonderful wits and great benefits that are rarely found in a book, which he has adopted from his scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, or from what he has collected from rares stories.

The third benefit: clarifying the problems, either by solving intricate issues or by using expressive language, raising the possibilities and clarifying the summaries.

name: Diwan al-Khansa - The complete works
description_short:
Al-Khansa was the most famous 7th century Arabic poet and the best known female poet in Arabic literature. She spent the greatest part of her lifetime during the pre-Islamic days, and when Islam prevailed, she embraced it and went to see the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, as a member of the delegate of her tribe, Banu Sulaym. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to ask her to recite her poetry to his admiration. Her full name is Tumadir bint ʿAmru Ibn al-Ḥarith Ibn al-Sharid al-Sulamiyyah, from the tribe of Banu Sulaym, from Qays Aylan, from Mudhar, from Najd.

Most and finest of her poems were about her brothers Sakhr and Mu’awiyyah, killed in the pre-Islamic era. She mourned their death in poetry and gained fame for her elegiac compositions. Her Diwan (poetry collection) contains what had been memorized of her poetry.
Al-Khansa’ had four sons, all of whom converted to Islam and were all killed in the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah in 16 AH. When she received the news, she did not grieve, but said, “Praise be to Allah who honoured me with their martyrdom. And I have hope from my Lord that He will reunite me with them in the abode of His Mercy.”

name: Diwan Abu Nawas, selection of poems by Abu Nuwas
description_short:
His full name was Al-Hassan Ibn Hani Ibn Abdul-Awal Ibn Sabah Al-Hakami, nicknamed Abu Nawas (146 AH-198 AH); he was the poet of Iraq in his era. He is the first to approach poetry in its urban style, taking it out of the Bedouin dialect.

Al-Jahidh said: “I have not seen a man who was more eloquent and possessed more command of the language than Abu Nawas.”

Abu Ubaidah said: “The status of Abu Nawas [..] was similar to that of Imru'-ul-Qays with the early generation. He was praised in a poem whereby the poet said: This is the one who mastered the language terminology and chose the best of it.”

Kulthum Al-Atabi said: “Had Abu Nawas lived in the pre-Islamic era, no one would have been preferred over him.”

Imam Ash-Shafi’i said: “had it not been for the impudence of Abu Nawas, I would have taken knowledge from him.”

name: Ad-Durar al-Bahiyah fi Masa-il al-Fiqhiyyah - Ash-Shawkani
description_short:
Ad-Durar Al-Bahiyyah is Matn (original script) of Fiqh (jurisprudence) written by Imam ash-Shawkaani which has the distinction of giving directly the dominant speech in the different issues of Fiqh, without following any particular Madhhab (Islamic school of thought). The book is easy to read and is distinguished by its dissociation from the assumption of problems.

The author has provided a useful explanation and named it “Ad-Darari Al-Mudhi’a”, in which he has cited the evidence upon which he built his compilation.

Very good Saudi edition, verified from the manuscript of Imam Shawkani himself. With additional annotations, mostly from the author's other works, to clarify certain issues. With most of the Harakat on the Matn.

name: Fiqh as-Sunnah ‘ala Madhhab al-Maliki (2 volumes)
description_short:
An excellent work that will please our Maliki brothers who wish to know the argumentative evidence associated with the legal rules taught in the books of the Maliki school.

In fact, beginners' manuals are often devoid of proof, but this work, written in a modern and structured composition, cites the proofs of the Quran and the Sunnah which are at the origin of the rules set forth in the school of Imam Malik ibn Anas.

name: Bidayat al-Mubtadi fi al-Fiqh al-Hanafi - Abi Bakr al-Marghinani
description_short:
Written by Imam Abi Bakr al-Marghinani (593H), Bidaayah al-Mubtadi is an excellent and well known Matn in the Hanafi Fiqh. Although it can be compared to the famous Mukhtasar of Al-Quduri, it has several differences:

Bidayah al-Mubtadi corrects some of the errors that exist in al-Quduri, he also adds several rules that have been omitted in Quduri, so the text is longer.

Also, Bidayat al-Mubtadi is better organized and clearer to understand, easier for the reader.

Finally, it has a well-known explanation called al-Hidayah, which is written by the author of the Matn himself.

Beautiful Egyptian edition, verified and authenticated by an Azhari Fiqh teacher, with 100% harakat on the text.

name: Dawabit al-Jarh wa at-Ta'dil - Dr AbdelAziz Al-Abdellatif
description_short:
This book “Dawaabit fi Al-Jarh wa Ta'deel” was written by the Hadith scholar Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Abd Al-Latif, an Associate Professor at the College of Hadith at the Islamic University of Madinah.

It is a textbook for study at the College of Hadith at the Islamic University of Madinah. It was selected to be taught to students of the College of Hadith; and this indicates the scientific value contained in the book, which you should not miss. The book is easy in its wording and arranged in high accuracy.

It is one of the best books on the regulations of discrediting and accrediting the narrators of Hadith, and Dr. Abdulaziz, may Allah have mercy on him, taught the book to his students at the College of Hadith at the Islamic University of Madinah for several years. He used to benefit from the students' questions when he explained some of their expressions, adding to them or restricting them, and then he would include those additions in his book and remove some phrases.

Very beautiful Saudi edition, the latest one, with an appendix of about a hundred pages that focuses on the case of the narrator of Hadith Isra'il ibn Yunus as-Sabi'i.

name: Taysir Mutashabihat al-Quran wa 'Ulumih - 'Ali Fahmi an-Nuzhi
description_short:
Excellent work on the subject of the Mutashabihat, the verses or parts of verses that are similar or look alike. This book is very complete and well structured, it was designed by a Quran teacher who is specialized in learning and has a lot of experience. The book is prefaced by 3 recognized specialists in Egypt in the sciences of the Quran and reading.

Here is the structure of the book:

1-    Chapter One: Mutashaabihaat of Surat Al-Baqarah only, then Mutashaabihaat of each Surah (from Surat Al-Imran to Surat An-Nas)
2-    Chapter Two: Collecting the Mutashaabihaat of each Surat separately from Surat Al-Imran to Surat Al-Kahf.
3-    Chapter Three: (proof from the Qur’anic words) in which he talks about the verbal Mutashaabihaat, such as the difference between death and killing, torment and pain, body and flesh, the Prophet and the Messenger, praise and thanksgiving, reverence and submission, miserliness and scarcity, the way and the path, ... and so on.
4-    Chapter Four: (Reflections on the Qur’anic discourse) such as referring to two by one, referring to one by the plural form, discourse of endearment, honour, majesty, praise, vilification, gender, anger, substance, insult, sarcasm, alienation, incitement, incompetence ... etc.
5-    Chapter Five: Various Quranic information
6-    Chapter Six: It is divided into several studies

name: Masa’il al-Imam Ahmad (Riwayah Ismail Ibn Sa’id ash-Shalanji)
description_short:
Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: "And Masa’il Ismail Ibn Sa’id are the most significant issues narrated from Imam Ahmed"

He also said: "Ismail asked Imam Ahmad about some issues long after Ibn al-Hakam, because Ibn al-Hakam accompanied Ahmad in the past, and he died about twenty years before Imam Ahmad’s death. As for Ismail, he was an adherent of the School of Ahluar-Ra’y (interpretation based on rational discretion), then he adopted the School of the people of Hadith (the Traditionists-jurisprudents), and asked Imam Ahmad those issues late in his life, along with Sulayman Ibn Dawud Al-Hashimi and other Hadith scholars ..."

Abu Bakr al-Khallal said: "He has narrated many issues and I do not think that any companion of Abu Abdillah (i.e. Imam Ahmed) has narrated better or as many issues as him. I found no one who narrated them from him, except Ibrahim Ibn Ya’qoub Al-Juzjani, he has narrated them on the authority of Ismail Ibn Sa’id".

The beautiful Saudi edition gathered everything that remains from those questions asked by Isma'il Ibn Sa’id ash-Shalanji from Imam Ahmad. With some of the Harakat.

name: Qa'idah Fahm as-Salaf as-Salih: Mafhumuha, Hujaytuha, Atharuha
description_short:
Very thorough research on the famous methodological rule imposing the understanding of the Quran and the Sunnah according to the understanding of the Pious Predecessors.

First the author brings back all the proofs of the Qur'an which enjoin to return to the Salafs in case of divergence of understanding, the proofs of the Prophetic Sunnah, and finally the Ijma' of the people of science and quoting proofs for each of the 4 schools, as well as the scholars of Hadith, Kalam and Sufis. He then cites the arguments by sound logic demonstrating the importance of returning to the Fahm of the Salaf as-Salih.

Then the author explains the repercussions of this rule of following the Salafs in three main areas: Tafsir, 'Aqidah and finally Sunnah and Bid'ah.

Superb research work, methodological, combining theoretical evidence and their practical application.

Saudi edition in 2 large volumes (more than 700 pages per volume), of high quality.

description_short:
One of the Aqidah treaties of the first generations, from the pen of the Amir al-Mu'minin of Tafsir, Ibn Jarir at-Tabari. Here are some of the important topics covered in this book:

- Issues of ignorance in religious matters, when it is acceptable and when it is forbidden, and the judgment of execution for disbelief.

- The subject of the divine attributes and the fact that their knowledge must come from scriptural sources and not from reasoning.

- The Qur'an and the Good Belief about it.

- Various Aqidah questions concerning the Lordship of Allah and His Oneness, and that these questions should be known out of necessity.

- The punishments or delights of the grave.

- The question of the vision of Allah by the Believers in the Hereafter among the Sunnah People.

Very beautiful Saudi edition, published with the annotations of Sheikh ibn Baz, verified from a manuscript. With the majority of the Harakats.

name: Kitab al-’Arsh by Imam adh-Dhahabi
description_short:
Kitab al‑‘Arsh (The Book of the Throne) by Imam adh‑Dhahabi is a work dealing with the attributes of Allah related to the ‘Arsh (Throne), including His ‘uluww (elevation), istiwa’ (establishment), and related divine attributes. 

The text cites verses of the Qur’an, hadiths, and reports from the salaf to support its positions, defending orthodox creed against deviations (such as those of the Jahmiyyah) and addressing theological disputes over how the Throne is to be affirmed without likening God to His creation.

The tahqiq by Dr. Muhammad ibn Khalifah al-Tamimi reflects a high level of academic rigor and precision. It includes a detailed verification of the attribution to Imam adh-Dhahabi, careful scrutiny of the text's narrations, and in-depth commentary on Hadith chains and their authenticity according to the scholars. The muhaqqiq also clarifies theological, methodological, and linguistic points, making this a reliable and well-annotated scholarly edition.

name: Musnad al-Imam al-Humaydi (219H) - Dar at-Taaseel
description_short:
Among the important Masaaneed, there is “Musnad Al-Humaydi”, the Sheikh of Imam Al-Bukhari. He began his Musnad with the collection of Hadiths reported by the Ten Companions who were promised Paradise, then Al-Muhajirun (the Immigrants) and then Al-Ansar (the Supporters) men and women.

The collection contained some 1300 Hadiths. He concluded his Musnad with a statement explaining his creed (Usul as-Sunnah).

Superb edition from the very serious Saudi publisher, Dar at-Taaseel. Merkez researchers have checked the work from 4 manuscripts while correcting errors in existing old editions.
Finally there are annotations on difficult words, with detailed research summaries (by verses, by Hadiths and Athar, by narrators), 100% Harakat.

name: Musnad Ishaq Ibn Rahwayh (238H) - Dar at-Taaseel
description_short:
This book is part of Ishaq Ibn Rahwayh’s Musnad. The first two volumes include A’ishah’s Musnad, Abu Hurairah’s Musnad, and Umm Salamah's Musnad may Allah be pleased with them. It is generally what we have left from the Musnad Ishad ibn Rahwayh, and this edition is based both on manuscripts and the Sanad of 'Abdallah ibn 'Aqil. Then the volumes 3 and 4 gathered some remained parts found in manuscripts that are related to this Musnad, and the overall amount of Hadith in the 4 volumes is 4516.

The book is one of the foundations of the Authentic Six Books (Al-Kutub As-Sittah) - except Ibn Majah and other Hadith books, because the author is one of the noblest of their scholars.

The author has listed Hadiths under biographies bearing the name of the narrator, he has avoided unfounded and fabricated narrations, and the book included the Sahih, Hasan and Da’eef Hadiths.

Superb edition from the very serious Saudi publisher, Dar at-Taaseel. Merkez researchers have checked the work from manuscript while correcting errors in existing old editions.
Finally there are annotations on difficult words, with detailed research summaries (by verses, by Hadiths and Athar, by narrators), 100% Harakat.

name: Musnad al-Imam ad-Darimi - Dar at-Taaseel (with Isnad and Tashkil)
description_short:
Beautiful edition, sure and verified, with chain of transmission going up to Imam ad-Darimi. This is very important because the science of Hadith is a science of transmission, and this edition comes from this methodology.

The Dar at Taaseel edition is recognized worldwide for its seriousness, and because the one who chairs the Merkez, Sheikh Abderrahman ibn 'Aqil, is the son of Sheikh Abdullah ibn Aqil, and the Shaykh was one of the Musnid of our century, he had many Ijaza on many books.

Here is the Sunan of Imam ad-Darimi, also named Musnad. This Musnad includes many Hadiths in various chapters of jurisprudence. In his compilation, Al-Darimi adopted the method of listing subject matters and chapters, beginning with a great introduction discussing knowledge and its merits, then the Book of Purification, and concluding with the Book of the Virtues of the Qur’an.

Luxurious 100% harakat edition, with referencing according to at-Tuhfah, and notes for difficult words. Search indexes of the Hadiths in alphabetical order and by chapter.

name: Al-Muwatta of Imam Malik - Riwayah az-Zuhri (with Isnad and Tashkil)
description_short:
Beautiful edition, sure and verified, with chain of transmission going up to Imam Dar al-Hijrah, Malik ibn Anas. This is very important because the science of Hadith is a science of transmission, and this edition comes from this methodology.

This is the Muwatta according to the version reported by Imam az-Zuhri. This is very important because the most widespread version is that of al-Laythi, who transmitted one of the earliest versions of the Mowatta, as he did not followed Imam Malik until his death. This is not the case of az-Zuhri who, for his part, received the last revised version by Imam Malik of the Muwatta, and what could be called the final and thus more complete version of that of al-Laythi.

Available in 2 very good edition: Dar at Taaseel and Risalah al-'Alamiyyah (Tahqiq Bashar Mar'uf).

name: The biography of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (Abu Turab) - 100% harakat - Musa al-'Azimi
description_short:
In the final installment of his monumental series on the Rightly Guided Caliphs, Musa bin Rashid al-'Azmi—the renowned author of Al-Lu'lu' al-Maknun fi Sirat al-Nabi al-Ma'mun—delivers a masterful biography of the fourth Caliph, Ali bin Abi Talib (d. 40 AH). This volume explores the life of "Abu Turab," from his childhood as the first youth to embrace Islam to his role as the legendary lion of the battlefield and the gate of the city of knowledge.

Al-'Azmi employs a disciplined, evidence-based methodology to document Ali’s unwavering bravery, profound wisdom, and deep-rooted commitment to justice. The narrative details his heroic stand during the Hijrah, his pivotal victories at Badr and Khaybar, and his complex leadership during the internal trials of the 1st century AH. By sifting through historical reports with academic rigor, the author highlights the traits of honor and duty that defined Ali's character, presenting a portrait of a leader who remained a steadfast guardian of the Prophetic legacy through the most turbulent periods of early Islamic history.

name: Mufradat Alfadh al-Quran - Al-Asfahani
description_short:
Mufradat Alfadh al-Qur'an by the celebrated linguist and scholar Al-Raghib al-Isfahani (d. 502 AH) is one of the most authoritative classical lexicons dedicated to the semantic analysis and vocabulary of the Holy Quran. Holding an unparalleled position among works of Gharib al-Qur'an, the book investigates the core lexical meanings of Quranic words, tracing their etymological roots, metaphorical extensions, and subtle theological implications. It bridges linguistic precision with deep scriptural reflection, serving as an indispensable foundation for exegetes, theologians, and students of Arabic linguistics.

The author structured the work alphabetically according to the three-letter Arabic roots, making it an accessible and systematic reference for scholars. Under each root, Al-Isfahani meticulously begins with the primary literal meaning of the word before exploring its secondary derivations, idiomatic usages, and spiritual dimensions, substantiating his definitions with supporting verses from the Quran, authentic Prophetic traditions, classical Arabic poetry, and rational wisdom.

name: Dictionary of Hadith Terminology
description_short:
Navigating the vast and intricate vocabulary of Hadith sciences can be a daunting task for students, and this contemporary dictionary is built to solve exactly that. It serves as an exhaustive, alphabetically ordered reference encyclopedia that defines the technical terminology used by Hadith scholars (Muhaddithun) across the centuries. From foundational terms like Sahih, Dha'if, and Mursal to highly specialized expressions found in the fields of Ilm al-Rijal (biographical evaluation) and Ilal (hidden defects), this dictionary clarifies the vocabulary needed to decipher classical chains of transmission and text evaluations.

What makes this dictionary incredibly useful is its dual approach to defining terms. Dr. Syed Abdul Majid Al-Ghawri provides a concise linguistic definition for each entry before breaking down its technical application in the science of Hadith, supporting his explanations with clear examples and statements from classical authorities like Ibn Hajar, Al-Nawawi, and Al-Suyuti. Organized beautifully in a clear layout, it eliminates the need to cross-reference multiple classical text introductions (Muqaddimat), making it an invaluable desktop companion for any student or researcher actively engaging with the books of the Sunnah.

description_short:
It is the most famous work of Imam al-Ghazali, and one of the most famous and widespread Islamic books. It deals with Faith, works and piety, and how to attain a level of excellence (Ihsan) in its fields. It is therefore a book of purification and education of the soul, commonly called Tasawwuf.

The book is divided into four parts, each containing ten books. It explains the doctrines and practices of Islam and shows how these can become the basis for a life of deep devotion.

  • People and social customs.
  • The soul, the vices that people must master and overcome, the virtues that they must strive for.

name: Nikat al-Quran - Abi Muhammad al-Muqri (395H)
description_short:
The book (Nikat Al-Qur’an) is one of the books that took interest in analysing the Book of Allah, collecting all related sciences in concise words and a brief style. The author has attached importance to the method of recitations (Qiraa’at), explaining the diversity of the Qur’an reciters regarding different words. He then mentioned their reason and argument in terms of language and meaning. He mentioned the opinions of the interpreters, and the recitations of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. He also defined the Suras revealed in Makkah and the ones revealed in Madinah, and the number of Verses. All this justifies the title of the book (Nikat al-Qur’an) as it does not specialize in the method of recitations or guidance, but rather takes from every science a story and benefits.

Given the time of writing the book (before 395 AH), which was the time of recording and narration, it is considered an essential source for the sciences that he had embarked upon the advancement of the book’s time makes it a source of many uncommon methods of recitations of the seven imams (reciters) and of the number of Verses and opinions of the interpreters. In addition to the author’s knowledge of the methods of recitations, his purpose in writing the book is to clarify the conformity or harmony of the Qur’anic recitation with Arabic, being the third pillar of the approved recitation, which makes the book suitable for those who specialize in the methods of recitation and its disciplines.

Very beautiful Saudi edition in 2 volumes, verified from the manuscripts and annotated by 4 researchers.

name: Bidayatu al-Hidayah - Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (505H)
description_short:
Bidayatu al-Hidayah is a book by Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali; it is considered a preface to the book Ihya’ ‘Ulum ad-Din. Al-Ghazali divided it into two parts: 

It’s a book on Tassawuf, meaning here: the forms of obedience, the etiquette of sleeping, waking up, entering the toilet, performing ablution, washing, performing tayammum, entering and leaving the mosque, the period after sunrise till noon, and the etiquette of preparing for the prescribed prayer, which are the foundation of the religion, and one of the pillars of Islam. He mentioned matters related to the Imamate, such as following the Imam in prayer, the Sunnah acts of Friday and Fasting. He also talked about avoiding sins, in which he explains sins of the heart, and that they are more dangerous than sins of body parts, and the etiquettes of companionship with the Creator - glory be to Him - and with mankind.

Nice edition, 100% Harakat.

name: Tahafut al-Falasifah (The Incoherence of the Philosophers) - al-Ghazali
description_short:
Imam al-Ghazali is one of the greatest figures of Islam, one of those who marked their time, who continued to mark the generations that followed, and who marked their Juridical and Doctrinal school.

After having studied in depth many sciences, both religious and philosophical, al-Ghazali came with this book to denounce the invalidity of Philosophy in the face of Faith, although he himself is an Asharite and a practitioner of 'Ilm al-Kalam, he wanted to clarify through this book the falsity of making logic an absolute point as unfortunately some scholars like Avicenna. He thus establishes that Faith must always dominate philosophy and logic in divine and metaphysical questions.

name: Understanding Modern Atheism and its Mechanisms
description_short:
Among the unforeseen repercussions of the September 11 events is its impact on mobilizing atheist groups to advocate and preach their atheistic vision. This study is concerned with exposing some aspects related to this new atheistic pattern, because students of theological history will realize that atheism enjoys a moment of strength and weakness, and that it passes in the form of waves ravaging the human society from time to time. 

Each of these waves shares common and different characteristics and features with other atheistic waves. Therefore, it was important for the specialists in Creed to know the most important developments in the atheistic discourse, provide a doctrinal discourse capable of resisting this new atheistic tide, and to protect people from falling into its traps, which is what this study seeks to introduce and explain.

name: Maqalat at-Tafwid bayna as-Salaf wa al-Mutakallimin
description_short:
One of the issues that occupied much of the writings and studies of many of those engaged in Ilm al-Kalaam was the issue of (At-Tafwid) and proving its attribution to the Salaf Scholars. For the scholars of Kalaam, At-Tafwid means that the meanings of Divine Attributes cannot be perceived by human beings, as they have no knowledge about them. To prove that, these have collected many of the Salaf’s sayings which they believed to be proof of what they intend to confirm.

This book, “Maqalat at-Tafwid bayna as-Salaf wa al-Mutakallimin” is an accurate tracking of this issue, a monitoring of its history and causes, and a refutation of its origins and principles. The book includes a reply to one of the most important books that has dealt with the issue of At-Tafwid, entitled “Al-Qawl at-Tamam bi Ithbat at-Tafwid. Madhhaban li as-Salaf al-Kiram”.

name: At-Tafsir al-Kabir li Fakhr ad-Din ar-Razi (604H) - Mafatih al-Ghayb
description_short:
It is regarded as the largest Tafsir (interpretation) based on rational discretion and reason, in which the author mentions the causes of the revelation of the surahs and the occasions that took place between them. He proceeds with a detailed interpretation of the universal sciences, and does not forget to mention the fundamental, grammatical and rhetorical issues, as well as the rational deductions.

In his Tafsir, Al-Razi explains the meanings of the Noble Qur’an and its Signs. It contains extensive research in various sciences, such as 'Ilm al-Kalam, and the sayings of philosophers and people of wisdom. Al-Razi mentions the doctrines of jurists and their evidence in the Verses of legislation; he successfully supports the doctrine of Asha'irah and refutes that of the Mu'tazilah, the sayings of erring sects, and disproves the opinions of the philosophers.

However, since Al-Razi did not complete it, Shihab Ad-Din Al-Khubi Ad-Dimashqi (639 AH) took the initiative to complete a portion of it, then came Najm Al-Din Al-Qamuli (727 AH) after him, and finished the last part, in a manner that cannot distinguish the original from the complement.

Beautiful Egyptian edition in 16 volumes, with authentication of the Hadiths.

name: Al-Quran, Tafsir wa Tadabbur wa ‘Amal - Very large size (A4)
description_short:
A Tafsir both simple and complete, ideal for reading and daily meditation. The goal of the Merkez behind this tremendous work is to put meditation, introspection and practice back into the heart of the Muslim's life in his reading of the Quran.

For this purpose this "Tafsir" follows two paths:
The first is a continuous tafsir of the Qur'an in a summarized way, based on the work of ibn Kathir.
The second is the highlighting of four aspects for each page of the Mushaf: the definition of complex words, the works that are highlighted in the verses, the advice and guidance to which Allah enjoins us, and the meditation and reflection on several of the passages or verses of the page.

Presented in a magnificent edition in a very large format (A4), this work will satisfy everyone: the beginner or the average person who will learn many things in a simple and concise style, but also the student who will review his knowledge and discover Fawaid.

name: At-Tarikh al-Kabir by Imam al-Bukhary
description_short:
Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari wrote this huge compilation containing nearly 40,000 biographies of Hadith's narrators when he was only 18 years old. It shows his genius and precociousness, Rahimahu Llah.
The narrators range from the Companions to the contemporaries of Imam al-Bukhari.

This great work enjoys here an excellent Tahqiq with this beautiful Saudi edition of 11 large volumes. Indeed, the Muhaqqiqs were based on more than 10 manuscripts and existing editions in order to bring the best possible version.

In addition to at-Tarikh al-Kabir, there is another book called al-Kunna on the narrators and their Kuniyas, again by Imam al-Bukhari.
Finally, there is a research index to facilitate the use of this very important work in the science of narrators.

name: Sharh Mandhumah al-Mimiyyah by Hafidh Hakami - Abderrazzaq al-Badr
description_short:
This work is a profound and gentle explanation by Sheikh Abdul Razzaq al-Badr of the famous Mimiyyah poem regarding academic advice and etiquettes. Originally composed by the brilliant scholar Sheikh Hafiz al-Hakami (d. 1377 AH), this poem is a masterpiece of didactic poetry that outlines the path for every seeker of knowledge. It provides a clear framework for those who wish to combine academic achievement with moral excellence.

The commentary focuses on the virtues of knowledge, the necessity of sincerity (Ikhlas), and the honorable character traits that a student must embody. Sheikh al-Badr’s explanation is particularly valued for its emphasis on duty, honor, and the rejection of negative behaviors that hinder spiritual and intellectual growth.

name: Nihayah al-Muhtaj bi Sharh al-Minhaj - Ar-Ramli (Fiqh Shafii)
description_short:
This book is a monumental masterpiece of late Shafi'i jurisprudence, standing as one of the ultimate twin pillars of authority for legal verdicts (fatwa) within the school. Written by the eminent Egyptian jurist Imam Shams al-Din al-Ramli (d. 1004 AH)—historically celebrated as "Al-Shafi'i al-Saghir" (The Little Shafi'i)—the text is an exhaustive, definitive commentary (Sharh) on Imam al-Nawawi’s foundational legal manual, Minhaj al-Talibin.

Alongside Ibn Hajar al-Haytami’s Tuhfat al-Muhtaj, this work represents the final crystallization of Shafi'i legal thought, with al-Ramli’s rulings being particularly relied upon by the scholars of Egypt and the Levant. The text comprehensively analyzes ritual worship (ibadat), complex financial transactions (muamalat), family law, and judiciary codes. It is highly valued for its clarity, systematic organization, and its inclusion of the collective feedback of contemporary scholars who reviewed and approved the text during the author's lifetime.

name: Ahaadith Mu'allah Dhaahiruha as-Sihha - Sheikh Muqbil al-Wadi'i
description_short:
Sheikh Muqbil bin Hadi al-Wadi'i said on this work: “In the study of “Sahih al-Musnad Mimma Laysa fi as-Sahihayn” I used to pass through Ahadith that appear to be correct (Sahih and authentic), but I find them in another book to be Mu’illah (derived from the word ‘illa, that is, weakness in its chain of authority). A researcher would perhaps read them and think that I should check their chain of authority for their authenticity. So I set aside a notebook for these Hadiths, collecting about four hundred, and then compiling them in a single book, to make them more useful, as was the case with “Sahih al-Musnad Mimma Laysa fi as-Sahihayn”. I ask Allah to benefit from it, and to make my work sincerely for His Sake.
Most of these benefits come from the books of the scholars, as you will find out, Allah willing. I have only made the collection, and All Praise is due to Allah Who has guided me to it.”

Very beautiful edition, with most of the Harakat.

name: The genius of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
Abqariyyat Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah ("The Genius of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah") by Ahmad bin Nasir al-Tayyar is a brilliant intellectual study that analyzes the multi-dimensional brilliance of Ibn Taymiyyah through a meticulous, direct examination of his monumental Majmu' al-Fatawa. Moving away from standard, chronological life timelines, the author systematically combed through the entirety of the compendium to extract tangible evidence showcasing Ibn Taymiyyah’s exceptional scholarly intellect, behavioral ethics, and spiritual methodology.

It thoroughly examines Ibn Taymiyyah's profound mastery over the core objectives of Sharia (Maqasid), his methodology in handling complex, unprecedented crises (Nawazil), his exemplary conduct with his adversaries, his unmatched skills in legal weighting (Tarjih), and his vast expertise regarding historical sects and legal schools. Furthermore, the text sheds light on his behavioral and spiritual school (Suluk), detailing his extraordinary ability to untangle deep scholarly dilemmas while maintaining the utmost respect and manufacturing excuses for the errors of other scholars.

name: Al-Jami' fi Kutub al-Iman wa ar-Rad 'ala al-Murjiah (2 volumes)
description_short:
Excellent collection aimed at bringing together the great works of the Salafs which explains the authentic definition of the faith in response to the stray groups in this field which are the Murjiahs and the Khawarij.

The researcher and Muhaqqiq 'Adil al-Hamdan therefore gathered 10 works of the Salafs on al-Iman and also wrote the first volume of this research "Al-Madkhal ila al-Jami' fi Kutub al-Iman wa ar-Rad 'ala al-Murjiah "which gives the context of these Risalahs, in particular by clearly explaining the Aqida of the Murjiah and their particularities.

Here are the 10 Kutub gathered:

  1. Al-Iman, by Abi 'Ubayd al-Qassim ibn Sallam
  2. Al-Iman, by Ibn Abi Shaybah
  3. Al-Iman, by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
  4. Al-Iman, by Ibn Abi 'Umar al-Madani
  5. Al-Iman, by Muhammad ibn Aslam at-Tussi
  6. Charh al-Iman wa al-Islam, by Zubayr ibn Ahmad az-Zubairi
  7. The chapters on al-Iman wa ar-Rad ala al-Murjia from Nukat al-Quran by Al-Qassab
  8. Ar-Rad ala al-Murjia from the book "At-Tanbih wa ar-Rad" by Al-Mulatti
  9. Al-Iman, by Qadi Abi Ya'la
  10. The chapters on al-Iman wa ar-Rad ala al-Murjia from Al-Hujjah fi bayan al-Mahajjah by At-Tamimi


All of these works are checked from manuscripts and the author's biography is given.

name: Al-Majalis al-Madaniyah fi Sharh Musnad al-Imam Ahmad - al-Kittani
description_short:
Here is one of the rare explanations of Imam Ahmad's Musnad, written by Shaykh Muhammad al-Kittani, one of the eminent Shaykhs who taught at the Masjid Nabawi in Medina.

He uses modern methodology in his explanation, using simple terms and explanations. His style is direct and concise, commenting only if he finds it necessary.

His Sharh develops the following points: details the chains of transmissions and narrators, and sometimes the Fiqh of the Hadith and the opinions of Ulemas, Fawaid and relevant annotations. Importantly, it gives the degree of authenticity of each Hadith.

Shaykh died, rahimahullah, without being able to complete the Musnad, the explanation goes as far as Hadith 8618.

The first volume contains a biography of the Shaykh as well as his chains of transmission which go back to several collections of Hadith. There is also a detailed research on the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, its composition, its place, etc ...

Gorgeous Saudi edition, 100% Harakat on the Hadith, and only part of it on the explanation.

name: Al-Idhah li Nasikh al-Qur’an wa Mansukhih - Mekki ibn Abi Talib al-Qissi
description_short:
One of the most important works in the science of Quranic abrogation (nasikh wa-mansukh), composed by Imam Maki ibn Abi Talib al-Qaysi — the leading authority on Quranic recitation in al-Andalus and the preeminent Quranic scholar of his era. Rather than simply listing abrogating and abrogated verses as was customary, he took a rare foundational approach: beginning with a rigorous treatment of abrogation's definition, types, conditions, and the scholarly disagreements surrounding it, before moving to application across Quranic verses. His stated aim was to close the door on the undisciplined proliferation of abrogation claims that had become widespread.

This book is an essential reference for any student engaged in Quranic sciences and the principles of tafsir. It was edited by Dr. Ahmad Hasan Farhat based on four manuscripts, the oldest being a copy from the Qarawiyyin library in Fez dated 510 AH. The edition was part of Farhat's broader doctoral project to gather and edit the complete scholarly legacy of Maki ibn Abi Talib.

name: I'lam al-Isabah bi A'lam as-Sahabah - Imam al-Khalili al-Maqdassi
description_short:
This book by Imam Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Khalili is a summary of the Hafidh of the Maghreb, Ibn Abd al-Barr and his immense work, "al-Isti'ab fi Ma'rifah as-Sahab". This book is one of the first biographies of the Sahabas. The methodology of the work consists of recalling who brought back from this Companion, as well as some prophetic narratives brought back by the latter. He also quotes their age and death and classifies the Sahabas in alphabetical order, as will be repeated after him by several historians or Muhaddith such as ibn al-Athir or ibn Hajar al-Asqalani. Al-Isti'ab is therefore a very important work in his field.

This summary is an improved version of the book “Al-Isti’āb”, by adding some biographies, such as Al-Mustadrak and Al-Mudhayyal, and mentioned only the essential aspects in the biography of each Companion without any breaching. He has added a scientific verification approach, such as checking thoroughly the facts regarding some Companions, and introducing some biographical and Hadith benefits that covered many paragraphs of the book, which made it one of the abridged books on the biographies of the Companions.

The book of Imam al-Khalili is of great significance, as it includes nearly 5000 names of the Companions, more than what is mentioned in its original book, “Al-Isti’āb”, which added more value to the importance of its study and publication.

This book includes nearly 3000 of the Prophet’s Hadiths, which the scholar had thoroughly studied and scrutinized, so that the book can provide a comprehensive scientific service.

Published for the first time in a very large volume of + 1100 pages, with the Harakats on some names.

name: History of Muslim Andalusia, from conquest to downfall
description_short:
The author is the first to include all of Andalusian history in a single volume systematically at the university level, and he said that it was set up that way intentionally for that purpose. In his book, he relied nearly on 200 references, in four different languages.

The author has divided the history of Andalusia into eight eras:

- The era of the conquest: It is the period in which the armies of Tariq bin Ziyad and Musa bin Nusayr entered Andalusia.

- The era of the Governors: It is the period that followed the conquest, and continued until the end of the Umayyad dynasty.

- The era of the Emirate: It is the period that began with the entry of the Umayyad Abdul-Rahman Al-Dakhil to Andalusia, where he declared it independent (administratively) from the Abbasid state.

- The era of the Caliphate: This era began when Abdul-Rahman Al-Nasir declared himself a Caliph, and it can be considered the pinnacle in the Andalusian history.

- The Age of Taifa Kings: After the fall of the Umayyad Caliphate in Andalusia, the Age of Taifa Kings began, and it is the beginning of the state of frailty in Andalusia.

- The era of Almoravids: This period began with the entry of Yusuf bin Tashfin to the Iberian Peninsula, and was characterized by the elimination of the Taifa kings and the establishment of the pillars of strength in Andalusia.

- The era of Almohads: It began after the fall of Almoravids.

- The era of the Kingdom of Granada: This era represented the last period of the glorious history of Andalusia, before the final fall.


Very nice edition in a large volume, with many notes and references.

name: Rebuttal to those who deny Ijtihad and its necessity - As-Suyuti
description_short:
As-Suyuti said in the introduction of his book: “People have been overwhelmed by ignorance, and blinded by the love of stubbornness which made them deaf. So they consider Ijtihad (independent reasoning) as a serious and grave issue, and deemed it repudiated among people. These ignorant people did not know that Ijtihad is one of the legal obligations, which should be fulfilled by a group of people in the Muslim community in every country at all times…”

This book proves that Ijtihad is permanent, continuous, and never interrupted in any age. The author responds to those who deny Ijtihad and ignore that it is an obligation in every age, by citing the sayings of senior Maliki scholars on this topic, and that time does not go without the presence of a Mujtahid. He encourages Ijtihad, enlightens its related benefits, with many chapters dedicated to these topics.

name: Al-Ayn wa al-Athar fi 'Aqa'id Ahl al-Athar - 'Abdel-Baqi al-Ba'li
description_short:
The author said in his introduction: "Praise be to Allah Whose Existence is necessarily deduced in the admiration of His deeds. Allah is Free and Far Above, in His Being and His Attributes, from all analogues and examples. He created all that exists, and not an atom’s weight of it escapes His Knowledge. Glory be to Him Who cannot be perceived by illusion or be determined by imagination. Indeed, He is unlike anything that comes to one’s mind.

I praise Him, Glory be to Him, and thank Him, that He has guided us to His true religion, and removed all the ambiguities of deviation and delusion. I repent to Him and ask His Forgiveness from all errors and mistakes, and I asked Him for salvation on the Day when the mountains move away.

A friend of mine, whom I cannot disagree with, has asked me to compile a book that includes Three Principles.

The first one: is about all that is stipulated of the doctrines of the Hanbalis, according to Imam Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with him.

The second one: deals with the controversial issues disputed between the Hanbalis and the Ash’aris, with mention of the Hanbalis’ proofs for argument.

The third one: deals with the issue of scholastic theology, in which he mentioned what was narrated from Imam Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with him.

So I answered him to all those principles and named the book: Al-‘Ayn wa-al-Athar fī 'Aqā'id ahl al-Athar."

name: Irshad Uli al-Absar wa al-Albab li Nayl al-Fiqh - Sheikh as-Sa'di
description_short:
Irshad Uli al-Basa'ir wa al-Albab is an exceptionally accessible manual of Islamic jurisprudence penned by the great scholar 'Abd ar-Rahman as-Sa'di. Written with the explicit goal of simplifying fiqh for students and laymen alike, the author adopts an intuitive Question-and-Answer format. This structure strips away the complex jargon of classical texts, allowing the reader to directly grasp the core rulings, conditions, and pillars of everyday acts of worship and transactions without confusion.

The book covers the standard chapters of fiqh, traversing from purification and prayer to family law and commerce. True to Shaykh as-Sa'di’s methodology, the text heavily favors rulings supported by the strongest evidences from the Quran and Sunnah, rather than restricting itself to the strict parameters of a single madhhab. It serves as a perfect introductory text for beginners looking to build a sound, evidence-based understanding of practical Islamic rulings without being overwhelmed by peripheral scholastic debates.

This rare work has been reprinted in a new large-format edition (A4), with most of its tashkil and hadith referencing.

description_short:
This is a monumental work in the science of contemporary Hadith: the result of a long work of research and composition by Sheikh Salih al-Shami, who collected the 114,194 Hadiths that make up the collections of Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa-i, ibn Majah, ad-Darimi, Imam Ahmad, Ibn Hibban, ibn Khuzaymah, al-Hakim, Al-Bayhaqi... When the rehearsals were removed, he had 28,430 Hadith left.

From there, he made a selection work by choosing Hadiths that would not be repeated in the different chapters, choosing each time the version of the Hadith containing the most details and information. He also consistently favoured Sahih or Hasan Hadiths, leaving only weak Hadiths if they are supported by authentic Hadiths or if the chapter in question contains only weak Hadiths, specifying the weakness each time.

In the end the Sheikh managed to collect 3,191 Hadith which he classified by chapter, knowing that 55% of them come from the collections of Bukhari and Muslim. 

A formidable work which has its place in all libraries, may Allah reward its author with the Firdaws and the company of the Messenger of Allah sallalahu alayhi wa sallam in the afterlife.

name: 500 Qur’anic Words that may be misunderstood
description_short:
Allah has sent His glorious Book to contemplate on the meaning of its Verses and act upon it, being a light and guidance for all mankind, and this is the fruit of its recitation. What is most sought by contemplation is the knowledge of the meanings of the Verses and the clarification of the ambiguous vocabulary. With the Grace of Allah, many people have been reading the books of Tafsirs in order to understand and contemplate on the meaning of the Verses of the Qur’an, by searching for the interpretation of ambiguous words and vocabulary; however, they overlook words that they think they comprehend their meanings and interpretations, while they are far from the correct meaning. This book attempts to correct this problem by explaining 300 words commonly misunderstood by readers.

** This book is a bestseller in the Arabian Peninsula **

name: Zubdah at-Tafsir - Muhammad al-Ashqar
description_short:
Zubdat al-Tafsir, by Muhammad Sulayman 'Abd Allah al-Ashqar, is an abridged version of Ash-Shawkaani’ “Fat’h Al-Qadir”, may Allah have mercy upon him, where he reduced it to one statement in the interpretation of the Verse. But when the recitations are different, he opts for the interpretation corresponding to the recitation of Hafs, and derives from the study of the conditions of the narrators the outcome of the narrations which he compiled at the end of his research.

Al-Ashqar’s choice of this interpretation is due to its comprehensiveness, because, in addition to the interpretation, it includes a study of the rulings of the Noble Qur’an and jurisprudence of its teachings. In this Tafsir, Imam Ash-Shawkani opposed many heresies and deviant beliefs and adhered to the approach of the righteous ancestors (Salaf Salih).

A copy of the Qur’an is attached to this edition of this Tafsir.

name: ZAD Academy Learning Programme - Level 1
description_short:
Good news for students, here is the Zad Academy Level 1 pack, for learning religious sciences.

Here is a short description of the Zad Academy programme: 

Zad Academy is a virtual educational program that aims to facilitate Islamic knowledge for those who passionately seek it through use of the internet and a special television station, Zad TV.

The main purpose behind establishing the academy is to teach Muslims what they cannot afford to be ignorant of and to propagate authentic Islamic knowledge which is based on the Quran and Sunnah according to the understanding of the pious predecessors. This will be achieved in an easy, modern way, with high standards of professionalism.

The academy will teach seven academic sciences via distance learning, namely:

  1. Creed
  2. Exegesis
  3. Hadeeth
  4. Jurisprudence
  5. Biography of the Prophet, sallallaahu ‘alayhi wa sallam
  6. Arabic Language
  7. Islamic Education

Students will be able to watch the lectures daily on Zad TV. The final exam will not have a set specific time for all students, thereby giving students more options to choose timings that fit their schedules better, as long as they are within the designated timeframe.

The length of study in the academy will be two years, split into four semesters.

description_short:
School of Muhammad is a book written by Jihad Al-Turbani; it is a collection of texts that talk about some aspects of the biography of Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the lessons learned from his life, such as dealing with women and children, dealing with people of the book and polytheists, protecting the environment and being kind to animals.

The book takes you to another world to reflect on the Prophet’s biography, may Allah’s Blessings and Peace be upon him, and how he dealt with the various issues that went through in his life and the situations that he faced, whether between him and Muslims or between him and his people, and their torture and fight against him.

The book also tells us how the Messenger of Allah, may Allah’s Blessings and Peace be upon him, set an example for us in terms of persistence, defiance, perseverance and hope. His life, peace be upon him, was full of sad and difficult events from his birth until his death. He grew up an orphan after his father died, then his mother died, and his grandfather joined her. After his marriage, his two sons died, his people fought against him, he lost his wife and uncle in one year, and he was expelled by the leaders of Ta’if when he tried to seek their help. In Madinah the Muslims were betrayed by the Jews.

This book is one of our books for the general public, it contains general reminders, but it is not an academic book. Its modern literary style is suitable for reading by non-specialists and is more like a novel than a specialized technical book written by a scholar.

name: 101, The Secret of Arius - Jihad Al-Turbani
description_short:
The novel “101 Secret of Arius” is written by Jihad Al-Turbani.

We have reached the second part of the series 101, presented by the creative Palestinian writer Jihad Al-Turbani. We continue, here, with Abdulaziz and Nidal, who are constantly seeking to solve the secrets and mysteries. After succeeding in discovering the secret of Barbarossa, thinking that they came to the conclusion of their search, they were then surprised that Barbarossa’s journey was nothing but a prelude to entering into this new mystery. Indeed, they subsequently started a new search for another secret, which is the history of the Arians in relation to Arius, a Christians priest that refuse the new dogma of the strongly the deified nature of Jesus, which was subjected to unrivalled attempts for concealment and obliteration by the Church.

We will find ourselves talking about the “New Assassins” and “John’s pirates”, and go on a journey to learn about early Christianity, the history of Arius himself, detailing his doctrine that the Arians have followed. There is also reference to the most prominent figures affected by the Arius faith, the beginning of the conflict between Christianity of the Church and Christianity of Arius, the genocide attempts faced by the Arians, the involvement of the Roman emperors, and many other details. The author has also explained to us some symbols, such as the Enigma code, the puzzle of the letter X, Newton’s relationship with the Prophet’s (may Allah’s Prayers and Peace be upon him) message to Hercules, and other important historical topics.

We have reached the third part of the series 101 presented by the creative Palestinian writer Jihad Al-Turbani. We continue here in the company of Abdul aziz and Nidal, who are constantly seeking to decipher the secrets and mysteries.

After they succeeded in discovering the secret of Barbarossa and the secret of Arius, it was time to discover the secret of the Vandals, on an exciting journey in which we swing between the Eastern and Western worlds to find the Ten Rings of the Vandals.

name: Al-Kamil fi at-Tarikh - Imam ibn al-Athir (630H)
description_short:
This book is a monumental masterpiece of universal Islamic history, universally recognized as one of the most comprehensive and critical historical chronicles ever written. Composed by the famous historian Imam Izz al-Din Ibn al-Athir (d. 630 AH), it chronicles world history from the creation of the world up until the year 628 AH (1231 CE). The text serves as an indispensable reference for understanding the medieval Islamic world, offering a beautifully synthesized narrative that avoids the overwhelming textual chains found in earlier works like Al-Tabari.

Ibn al-Athir structures his work meticulously by year (Hawliyyat), recounting major political shifts, battles, and the biographies of prominent figures who died in each year. The text is particularly renowned for providing some of the most detailed, valuable, and emotionally raw contemporary accounts of both the Crusades in the Levant and the terrifying initial expansions of the Mongol Empire. By utilizing rare Levant-centric and Mesopotamian sources that are now lost to history, this multi-volume chronicle remains a cornerstone for researchers studying Islamic civilization.
searchable_keywords: Al-Kamil fi at-Tarikh - Imam ibn al-Athir (630H)

The text serves as an indispensable reference for understanding the medieval Islamic world, offering a beautifully synthesized narrative that avoids the overwhelming textual chains found in earlier works like Al-Tabari.

Ibn al-Athir structures his work meticulously by year (Hawliyyat), recounting major political shifts, battles, and the biographies of prominent figures who died in each year. The text is particularly renowned for providing some of the most detailed, valuable, and emotionally raw contemporary accounts of both the Crusades in the Levant and the terrifying initial expansions of the Mongol Empire. By utilizing rare Levant-centric and Mesopotamian sources that are now lost to history, this multi-volume chronicle remains a cornerstone for researchers studying Islamic civilization.

name: Ibn Taymiyyah's debates in matters of Aqidah
description_short:
Analyzing the historical and intellectual dynamics of the theological debates led by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728 AH) is the focus of this comprehensive contemporary study. The author, Dr. Haytham al-Hamri, provides a meticulous evaluation of how Ibn Taymiyyah defended the traditional Athari creed in open forums against prominent Ash'arite, Maturidite, and philosophical figures. This work serves as an exceptional academic guide for students looking to study the art of debate (Adab al-Bahth wal-Munadharah), showing how he balanced scriptural authority with rigorous logical arguments to dismantle complex philosophical innovations.

The book is structured into two main parts to give a complete view of these historical encounters. The first section details the specific dialectical methodologies, terminology, and debate principles that Ibn Taymiyyah utilized to expose inconsistencies in speculative theology (Kalam). The second section moves into a case-by-case documentation of his most famous debates, such as the major trials surrounding Al-Aqeedah al-Hamawiyyah and Al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah. By isolating his strategies and documenting the socio-political backgrounds of these trials, this volume provides researchers with a practical blueprint for defending orthodox theology.

name: Al-Mabsut by Imam Abi Bakr As-Sarkhasi Al-Hanafi
description_short:
Al-Mabsut is a valuable and useful book, and it is the most widely printed book on Hanafi jurisprudence and comparative jurisprudence. The Hanafi School relies on it in judiciary and issuing Fatwā, and in teaching and writing.

In this book, the issues discussed by Imam As-Sarkhasi cover many different subjects all based on Hanafi Fiqh. The author’s discussion comes in an easy style, clear statements, and full explanation for rules and evidences. The author establishes a comparison between the Hanafi Madhhab (a school of Islamic jurisprudence) and other Madhaahib, especially the Shafi’i Madhhab and the Maliki one. He may also mention the Madhhab of Imam Ahmad and adh-Dhahriyya.

The method adopted in Al-Mabsut is that the author mentions the jurisprudential issue, explains its ruling on the Hanafi Madhhab, infers it, then mentions the opinions of some of the different Schools of Thought, explains their evidence, then discusses the evidence and responds to it with what he deems right. The author may even combine the evidence of the Hanafi Madhhab with the evidence of other opposing Madhaahib in a good way, eliminating any contradiction.

Al-Mabsut is a commentary on the book “Al-Kāfi” of Muhammad Ibn Muhammad Al-Marwazi (d.334AH) the Imam of the Hanafis in his time, in which the latter compile books that rely on the outward (Dhahir) meaning of expressions in the branches of the Hanafi School of Thought written by Imam Muhammad bin Al-Hasan.

Complete edition in 9 volumes, with the majority of Harakats.

This is a contemporary summary of Sahih al-Bukhari, selected by Sheikh Sa'd al-Shathry, who has removed chains of narrations, repetitions, Athars of Tabi'ins and added annotations on some words and discussed some different versions of the Hadith.

Sheikh Sa’d Ibn Nasser Al-Shatri, may Allah have mercy upon him, has mentioned that he wanted to complement the efforts of the previous scholars in abbreviating “As-Sahih”, and his approach in doing so is as follows:

2- Collecting parts of the Hadiths in the first place where the Hadith is mentioned.

3- He referred to the conflicting narratives contained in the footnotes.

4- He mentioned all the tabulation of al-Bukhari on the Hadith in all its areas and put it in the margin.

5- He explained some unusual words.

A very nice book and an excellent introduction to the famous Sahih al-Bukhari.

name: Al-Muhaddith al-Fasil bayna ar-Rawi wa al-Wa'iy - Ar-Ramahurmuzi (360H)
description_short:
Al-Muhaddith al-Fasil is considered the first book written in the science of the fundamentals of Hadith. It was studied by the great past scholars who took interest in Hadith and its sciences and transmitted from it. Ibn Khallad ar-Ramahurmuzi (360H) wrote his book about half a century before Al Hakim Nisaburi’s book “’Ulum al-Hadith” and a century before Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi’s book “ al-Kifaya fi ‘Ilm ar-Riwaya”, from which he derived many of his quotations.

In this book, he collected the methods of narrating and hearing the Hadith, and issued tackled by the scholars of Hadith in this field. In the introduction of the book, he mentioned the virtue of the science of Hadith, its narrators and their high status. The first chapter of the book deals with the merit of the transmitter of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah - may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then the chapter on the merit of the student of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah - may Allah bless him and grant him peace - and those who adhere to it; then a chapter on the intention to learn the Hadith, and then a chapter on the descriptions and etiquette of the student. He concluded the book on a chapter about the compilers of Hadith narrators in the Muslim world.

name: Al-Muhaddith al-Fasil bayna ar-Rawi wa al-Wa'iy - Ar-Ramahurmuzi (360H)
description_short:
Al-Muhaddith al-Fasil is considered the first book written in the science of the fundamentals of Hadith. It was studied by the great past scholars who took interest in Hadith and its sciences and transmitted from it. Ibn Khallad ar-Ramahurmuzi (360H) wrote his book about half a century before Al Hakim Nisaburi’s book “’Ulum al-Hadith” and a century before Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi’s book “ al-Kifaya fi ‘Ilm ar-Riwaya”, from which he derived many of his quotations.

In this book, he collected the methods of narrating and hearing the Hadith, and issued tackled by the scholars of Hadith in this field. In the introduction of the book, he mentioned the virtue of the science of Hadith, its narrators and their high status. The first chapter of the book deals with the merit of the transmitter of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah - may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then the chapter on the merit of the student of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah - may Allah bless him and grant him peace - and those who adhere to it; then a chapter on the intention to learn the Hadith, and then a chapter on the descriptions and etiquette of the student. He concluded the book on a chapter about the compilers of Hadith narrators in the Muslim world.

description_short:
Al-Ashāʿirah School is one of the Islamic groups that has been surrounded by great confusion regarding the soundness of its approach and its compatibility with true Islamic Shari’ah. Whereas the scholars of Hadith have claimed that it is one of the innovated sects (Mubtadiah), some have disagreed and considered it one of the groups that proposed the middle course doctrine (Al-Madhab Al-wasat) that combines reason and the Shari’ah, and contributed to the development of Islamic thought. So what is the truth about this school? What are the origins of its doctrine? How compatible is its approach to the Qur’an and Sunnah?

This very detailed research (+ 800 pages) will unveil the story of the Asharis and its theological concepts.

description_short:

name: Al-Jumlah al-'Arabiyyah, Ta-lifuha wa Aqsamuha - Fadil As-Samara-i
description_short:
In this book there is a set of rules of (the Arabic sentence), its composition and its connection with the meaning. The Arabic sentence consists of two basic pillars: the Musnad (predicate) and the Musnad ilayh (subject), and they are the two cornerstones of the speech. The Arabic sentence has elements, the most important of which are: the singular, the morphological form, the partial composition, the complete composition, and the phonemic tone.

This book also seeks to tackle: deletion in the Arabic sentence; what is required and what is permissible; the standard deletion and the unwritten deletion; what is required for a specific assumption and what is not required; that the meaning of which is agreed upon and that which is not; the deletion required by the meaning which is required by the syntactic form; the deletion that denotes one meaning and that which denotes more than one meaning, according to the discretion.

It also discusses the purposes of deletion, which include concision (or brevity) and abbreviation when establishing evidence, and doublespeak , taking into account the Saj’ (سجع, a form of rhymed prose) and commas, widening and figurative, the augmentation and exaggeration, as well as other topics related to the nominal and verbal sentence, the major and minor sentences, the informative and the constructive, the spoken sentence, the one which is syntactically correct and the one which is syntactically incorrect, within many Qur’anic and poetic evidence to support it.

name: Fath al-'Alam fi Dirasat Ahadith Bulugh al-Maram (10 volumes)
description_short:
This expansive six-volume set is widely considered the most thorough contemporary commentary on the classic "Bulugh al-Maram," offering an unparalleled laboratory for Hadith criticism. The methodology is distinguished by its rigorous focus on "takhrij" (referencing), where the authenticity of each narration and its chains of transmission are discussed with academic precision. By applying the rigorous standards of early masters to this foundational text, the work provides students of knowledge (Tulab al-'Ilm) with a practical guide to identifying the strengths and weaknesses of Prophetic traditions.

Beyond mere technical analysis, the work serves as a comprehensive guide to legal rulings, synthesizing the opinions of the four schools of thought based strictly on the weight of evidence. Sheikh Muhammad ibn Hizam guides the reader through complex issues of worship and transactions with a sober, academic tone that avoids blind imitation. It effectively bridges the gap between Ibn Hajar’s classical text and modern scholarly research, making it a mandatory reference for those specializing in the jurisprudence of Hadith.

name: At-Tib al-Muluki - Abi Bakr ar-Razi (Rhazes)
description_short:
This book (The Royal medicine) was written by one of the most prominent Arab scholars of medicine, Abu Bakr Ar-Razi (Rhazes in latin), the Arab doctor, who was one of the most important and first of those who innovated, composed and classified Arab medicine, and taught this great science.

He was one of those who wrote in Arabic during the period of Islamic creativity in all sciences, throughout the glory days of the Abbasid Caliphate, in a particular period marked by transcription and translation from other civilizations, such as the Persian, the Greek, the Coptic, and others; and he is among those who remained loyal to authenticity and originality.

Ar-Razi wrote this book to treat all diseases with food, or to put indispensable medicines in food, to conceal its taste, and then he re-mentioned the diseases and what food can either be beneficial or harmful to them.

It is rare to see such exceptional compilation among the literature of our time. It is, in fact, suitable for every time and place, regardless of the development of the medical science it contains.

Very serious edition, verified and annotated by Dr. Yassir Zakour.

name: Al-Wasilah al-Adabiyah ila Ulum al-'Arabiyah - Husayn al-Marsafi
description_short:
The book “Al-Wasīlah al-Adabiyyah” (The Literary Way) by the distinguished scholar Ḥusayn al-Marṣafī, may Allah Almighty have mercy on him, is one of the sources of modern Arab criticism, and it is one of the most significant books that shaped modern Arab tendency, developed critical concepts, and paved the way for generations.

His author was one of the remarkable scientific and literary phenomena in the nineteenth century, and his book marked a turning point in the field of modern literary criticism.

The lectures, given by the author to his students at Dar Al Ulum, represented the foundation of his book, “Al-Wasīlah al-Adabiyyah”; he arranged the first volume as an introduction to the literary arts, which he tackled in the second volume. Indeed, he started his book with definitions and divisions of the word “Al-Adab” (literature), then the definition of “Al-Lughah” (language), and then he discussed philology, letters of meaning, synonyms and contrast. He also talked about morphology and its divisions and branches, and ended the first volume with a conclusion that reveals the abundant culture of Al-Marsafi, his talents and renewed views. He used to urge his students to develop their knowledge to reach sophistication and keep abreast of everything new. Then the author later moved to discuss the knowledge of rhetorical sciences to reach the level of mastery in composition.

Gorgeous new edition with nearly 60% of the Harakat.

It is a beautiful and interesting book in which the author has collected fragments of literature, without adhering to a specific era; rather, he came with a wonderful story from the Abbasid era, and after that with one from the diaspora Arab writers, and so on. He would then write his opinion at the end of the story. In this book, he has written masterpiece stories in the finest of speech.

This book varies in how historical events are narrated by the author, which has made Arabic literature a literary and scientific heritage that every Arab can be proud of. It will definitely benefit the reader and makes him look forward to learn about the history of literature, embodied by the Arabs many years ago, and the genius of poets and writers in their poetry and their writings, increasing his awareness of what he benefits from in various areas of his life.

This book has been enthusiastically received by many readers, many of whom consider it to be one of their best reads and one of the most interesting collections published. A treat for lovers of the Arabic language.

name: Al-Iqna' fi Masa-il al-Ijma' - Ibn Qattan al-Fassi
description_short:
The book “Al-Iqna’ fi Masa’il al-Ijma’”, written by the Muhaddith jurist, Abu al-Hasan Ali Ibn Muhammad Ibn Abd al-Malik al-Kutami al-Himyari al-Fassi, nicknamed Ibn al-Qattan (d.628 AH),” is a great book by which his compiler, may Allah have mercy on him, intended to avoid disagreement and seek agreement among scholars regarding certain issues. So he did a great job and spared no effort to provide a summary of what the scholars have agreed upon, or at least the majority among them.

 “Al-Iqna’ fi Masa’il al-Ijma’”is considered a supply book for the specialists, and, at the same time, an assistance for beginners and ordinary Muslims who are not qualified to consider differences or weight the evidence.

“Al-Iqna’ fi Masa’il al-Ijma’” is divided into Books: Kitab Al-Iman (Book of Faith), Kitab Salaat (Book of Prayer), Kitab Zakaat, etc., and through these Books, Ibn al-Qattan has presented the agreement and consensus of Muslim scholars on these topics.

Excellent edition with a serious Tahqiq and very important annotations in which the reader can find the references of the opinions quoted in the books of each school.

name: Maqasid ash-Shari'ah al-Islamiyyah - Sheikh Tahir ibn 'Ashour
description_short:
The author has divided his book into three parts: the first of which is devoted to the biography of Sheikh “Muhammad al-Tahir Ibn Ashur,” his reform movement, and a discussion of his writings. The second is in line with the objectives of Shari’ah (Maqaasid Ash-Shari’ah), adding to it a set of fundamental studies due to the relationship between them. He detailed his method in a set of scholarly writings. The third: is a chapter on the Objectives of Shari’ah, which is distinguished by its issues and research. Thus, this book was written, i.e. (Maqaasid Ash-Shari’ah), and published, with an introduction and commentary, in the hope that it would be easy and accessible to the students, reviewers and scholars.

In his book, Ibn Ashur intended to study the objectives of Islam concerning the laws and rules governing civil transactions, etiquettes and morals. These laws deserve to be exclusively called the Shari’ah, for they reflect Islam’s aim to specify and identify the various levels of benefit (Masa’lih) and harm (Mafa’sid), and the criteria for assessing them, and this is a manifestation of the greatness of Islamic Shari’ah law, in contrast to the rest of the laws and social policies, for preserving world order and reforming society.

Superb edition with serious Tahqiq by Dr Mohammed az-Zuhayli, annotations for references and harakat in part.
