name: Qasas min Hayat ar-Rasul wa Ashabuhu - Muhammad Ali Dawlah
description_short:
This work by Muhammad Ali Dawlah gathers a rich selection of stories drawn from the life of the Prophet ﷺ and his noble Companions. The author explains in his introduction that his aim was not to create a chronological biography, but rather to organize the material thematically — grouping stories of similar meaning and moral purpose under unified chapter titles.

Through these short narratives, the reader encounters vivid scenes from the Prophet’s life and that of his companions, illustrating lessons in faith, courage, mercy, and steadfastness. The author’s language is clear and engaging, blending authenticity with narrative warmth to make the events both educational and inspiring.

This new and refined edition stands out for its elegant layout, well-organized chapters, and beneficial scholarly notes that provide context and explanation throughout.

name: Misbah as-Sihah (Jam' bayna Sahih Bukhari wa Muslim) - Ibn Al-Barzi
description_short:
Ibn al-Barizi had a particular interest in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, so he wanted to present a book that allowed people to read both Sahihs, including the hadiths they agreed upon as well as those narrated individually by each. He based his work on the book Al-Jam' Bayn al-Sahihayn by Abu Abdullah al-Humaydi, using it as his primary source, but he focused solely on the sayings of the Prophet (hadith qawli) without including reports of his actions or approvals (taqrirat).

The author began his book with Qudsi hadiths, then organized its chapters based on the opening words of the hadiths. For example, he created chapters for hadiths that begin with "Inna" and "Man," etc. The book is methodically arranged, with each hadith assigned a specific number, its reference in Al-Humaydi's Al-Jam' Bayn al-Sahihayn, and a letter symbol indicating the companion who narrated it.

The editor, Hussein al-Darghami, contributed high-quality annotations that correct mistakes and omissions found in Al-Humaydi's book.

Beautiful, verified edition, 100% Harakat, never been published before.

name: Muqaddimah Ibn Khaldun
description_short:
Ibn Khaldun's Muqadimmah is among the greatest literary works in human history. Its famous author, historian and philosopher (although it would be reductive to limit him to that), wrote this work as an introduction to his famous book of history, Kitab al-'Ibar (known as Tarikh ibn Khaldun).

The book is often considered the first work on sociology, philosophy of history, demography and many other related fields. It also deals with Islamic theology, natural sciences, biology and chemistry.

According to the orientalist Georges Marçais, the Prolegomena (the translation given to the title of the Muqaddimah) is "one of the most substantial and interesting works that the human mind has produced".

name: Mu'jam an-Nafaes al-Kabir - 2 volumes, 2200 pages
description_short:
This is a modern dictionary of the Arabic language, which aims to be as complete and accurate as possible, and which complements and clarifies existing dictionaries in many aspects. Here are some of the features of "al-Nafais al-Kabir" dictionary:

Facing the needs and requirements of the modern age with appropriate words and forms;

adopting generative, Arabised, and extraneous words that are common among people, and admitting the active, the easy, and the familiar vocabulary and formulas;

disposing of vague explanations, and adopting clear, concise and accurate one;

adhering to accuracy, tight tabs, and accessibility; referencing the source of every strange meaning next to it, so that the one who knows the language can easily refer to it;

considering the common and usual language;

adopting what has been approved by the linguistic academies of modern civilized words, new scientific terms, and precise and clear definitions;

strengthening of words with Qur’anic Verses, prophetic Ahadiths, common proverbs, and transmitted eloquent structures, both poetry and prose;

putting pictures of animals, plants and machines on special drawings; ensuring that the text is precisely controlled, whether it is a lexical material, Qur’anic Verses, prophetic Ahadiths, slogans, proverbs, or otherwise;

ensuring that misconceptions, contained in some Arabic dictionaries, are corrected, either by modification, clarification, or deletion;

Thus, this book fills the intellectuals’ need for an easy-to-use dictionary, abundant in material, that combines the living inherited words and the correct contemporary ones.

description_short:
One should know that the issue of whether the dead hear or not is a matter of the unseen, among the matters of al-barzakh (the phase between Death and Resurrection) that only the Almighty Allah knows, so it is not permissible to delve into it with analogy and self-opinions; this is rather a matter settled with firmly established evidence to either prove or negate it.

This book by Shaykh Abu al-Barakat Nu'man al-Alusi (1317H) (son of Mahmud al-Alusi, the author of the Tafsir Ruh al-Ma'ani), is presented here with the Tahqiq and notes by Shaykh al-Albani.

name: Al-Isharah ila Wafayat (Muntaqa min Tarikh al-Islam) - Imam al-Dhahabi
description_short:
Imam adh-Dhahabi is the author of a wonderful book on the history of Muslims called: "Tarikh al-Islam" (printed in more than 30 volumes). He wrote this magnificent Muslim historical encyclopedia in the following way: he mentions the year as a title (e.g. the year 40 of the Hegira) and then he mentions everything that happened during that year, such as births, battles, conquests, problems, deaths, etc.

This book, "Al-Ishara" is written in exactly the same way: by mentioning the year as a title (e.g. year 128 AH) and then mentioning what happened in that year, but in this book he mentions only the deaths: all the people who died in that year, all the personalities related to the history of the Muslims, whether they are Muslims or disbelievers, pious or not.

The author begins his book with the year 1 of the Hegira until he reaches his time, the author died in the year 748 H.

A rare book, in a serious edition that has the majority of Harakats (about 60%) on proper names in particular, which is extremely useful.

name: 'Uyoon al-Akhbaar by Imam ibn Qutaybah (4 larges volumes)
description_short:
Uyun al-Akhbar is one of the most celebrated and foundational works of classical Arabic literature (Adab), authored by the polymath Imam Ibn Qutaybah (d. 276 AH). This monumental encyclopedia is a masterclass in the integration of knowledge, designed to refine the intellect and character of the reader through a vast collection of anecdotes, poetry, historical reports, and Prophetic traditions. Ibn Qutaybah meticulously organized the work into ten thematic "books," covering essential human and social spheres such as authority, war, nobility, character, eloquence, and even asceticism. It serves as a comprehensive record of the cultural and moral landscape of the early Islamic era, presented with the stylistic elegance for which the author is renowned.

The work is far more than a mere anthology; it is a pedagogical tool intended to cultivate the "Adib" (the refined individual). By blending religious insight with historical wisdom and linguistic beauty, Ibn Qutaybah provides a balanced framework for understanding leadership, social etiquette, and human nature. This book is an indispensable resource for students of Arabic literature and history, offering a window into the intellectual life of the 3rd century AH. Whether for scholarly research or personal enrichment, this masterpiece remains a primary source for anyone seeking to master the art of Arabic expression and the depth of classical Islamic thought.

This collection of quotations and sayings is published in 4 very large volumes (A4 size), with some of the Harakats.

Many people make mistakes in using letters with transitive verbs that are accompanied, for each verb has prepositions that are used with transitive verbs, which may not be used with others, and their incorrect use often changes their meanings.

Therefore, Dar al-Nafa’is has decided to publish a special dictionary for transitive verbs that are accompanied, dealing with their different uses, explaining their different meanings according to the different prepositions that come after them, which may help the contemporary reader who seeks to improve his pronunciation and writing, and, at the same time, tends to obtain information as quickly as possible.

The author was keen to come up with examples from the Noble Qur’an and ancient Arabic poetry, as well as to set the present tense verb according to the order mentioned in the introduction of the dictionary.

name: Taysir Al-Bayan li Ahkam Al-Qur’an - Ibn Nur ad-Din al-Muzi'i (825H)
description_short:
It is a book of great benefit and value, containing comparative jurisprudence, language, principles, interpretation of the Qur’an and the Hadith of the Prophet. It is this combination of subjects that distinguishes it from other similar books, and places it at the top of knowledge, moderation, fairness, and even Ijtihad (independent reasoning). This is apparent in the author’s preferences, discussions and inclination for an opinion that may contradict his Shafi’i doctrine, because of his ability as a jurist and his knowledge of jurisprudence, language and eloquence.

It is aptly named. It is easy and clear, due to the smoothness of its style, and the splendour of its approach, as it takes the reader directly to the content of the Verse, with an explanation of the rulings deduced from it, presenting the different kinds of deduction, explaining the doctrines of the jurists in each issue, in a logical order, with clear words, indicating the clarity of the idea and its meaning.

The author, a great Yemeni scholar from the 9th century, Ibn Nur ad-Din an-Muzi'i, does not stop at presenting opinions and sayings, and mentioning the doctrines and differences; but rather, he made some successful judgements and opinions of his own, discussing and inferring, correcting and choosing, which enriches the book’s scientific material, and helps the reader to feel the truth in the event of disagreement.

He then corroborates goodwill and good manners, enhances the ambition of the aspiring and highly determined people, and promotes honesty, piety and forbearance in a person’s way of life.

It exalts reason and wisdom, and protects the adults from overindulgence and falling into the world of recklessness and whims. It addresses the intellect with its sublime thoughts, just as it addresses the heart with its eloquent and moderate language, in a composed style free of pretension or frills. Complexities of its style do not prevent you understand its meanings.

For this reason, the book is great in its value, especially if we add that it sheds a lot of light on the literature of an important stage of our Arabic literature within the framework of prose and transmission, covering many ethics that start with the protocols of entering upon the kings and rulers and ends with the simplest things in life.

name: Kitab al-Ma'ani al-kabir fi Abyat al-Ma'ani - Ibn Qutaybah
description_short:
This book is one of the most outstanding works of Abu Muhammad ibn Qutaybah ad-Dīnawarī, an Arab author, jurist, Muhaddith (interpreter of Hadith) and historian. He has written many books, the most famous of which is ‘Uyun al-Akhbar.

In this book, the expression abyāt al-ma'ānī refers to the poetic verses that have ambiguous meaning, and they are called so because hearing them requires asking about their meanings, which prompted many scholars to be interested in this discipline (to interpret these verses).

Among the most prominent of these analytical books and most classified is Kitāb al-Ma'ānī al-kabīr of ad-Dīnawarī, which he divided into several Sections: First: Horses, Second: Beasts, Third: Food and Hospitality, Fourth: Flies... He divided each Section into several chapters, and the book is a reference for the literary connoisseur; it is characterized by its sublime language style, the beauty of its meanings and entertainment, enriched with scientific footnotes.

Lebanese edition Dar as-Sader, very serious, 100% Harakats.

name: Taj al-'Arus min Sharh Jawahir al-Qamus - Az-Zubaidi
description_short:
This book is one of the greatest books of the Arab heritage and the most important with regard to the Arabic language. Its author Fairūzābādī was one of the great lexicographers to whom people referred in disputes. His book "Al-Qāmus al-Muḥīṭ", which means The Surrounding Ocean, was so famous to the extent that every lexicon was called Qamus.

Of those who compiled its interpretation was Al-Murtada Az-Zubaidi in his book Taj al-Arus; he arranged it according to the last letter of the Subject alphabetically, naming it “Chapter of…” and then according to the first letter of the Subject as Subchapters within this book. For example, the word “zayt” is found in the Chapter “T” Subchapter “Z” and so on.

description_short:
This work examines the phenomenon of religious storytellers (Qussas) and preachers (Mudhakkirin) in early Islamic society and their impact on Hadith transmission. Ibn al-Jawzi traces the history of preaching from the era of the Companions—such as Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ibn Mas'ud—to distinguish between legitimate, sincere admonition and the problematic practices of entertainers. He identifies the dangers of those who prioritize emotional manipulation, greed, and the spread of weak or fabricated narrations over authentic scholarly truth.

To preserve the integrity of the faith, Ibn al-Jawzi establishes rigorous criteria for proper Islamic preaching. He emphasizes that a preacher must possess deep scholarly qualifications, maintain personal integrity, and avoid the hypocrisy of seeking public fame. Furthermore, he argues for the necessity of administrative oversight and authorization, ensuring that those who address the public are grounded in the Quran and the authentic Sunnah rather than personal whims or fabricated tales.

Excellent Tahqiq for this rare edition (1988), with verification of the text and authentication of Hadiths.

name: At-Tabsirah by Ibn al-Jawzi
description_short:
At-Tabsirah is a book on preaching, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Al-Jawzi (508-597). It is considered one of the most comprehensive books of Ibn al-Jawzi in the science of preaching; he was indeed the famous author of many books on preaching, guidance and softening of the hearts.

Ibn al-Jawzi has divided this book into nine Sections that include many Chapters, discussing aspects of Faith, legislation, morals and ethics, stories and biographies.

It is the most complete book on the science of preaching, written by Imam al-Hafiz Abd al-Rahman Ibn al-Jawzi in response to some fanatics who were spreading fear and calling to renounce worldly life.

In this book, Ibn al-Jawzi has touched on the doctrine of Monotheism, the pillars of Islam, its morals, etiquette, and its organization of relationships, and most importantly, he extracted the evidence from the Qur’an and the authentic Sunnah.

Very good print, checked from 7 manuscripts, with some notes on places and persons cited in the book.

name: Al-Mukhtasar fi Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim
description_short:
Features of this book, the Mukhtasar fi Tafsir:

- Clarity and simplicity of phrase, away from any verbiage and verbal complexity.

- Interpreting the verses and clarifying their meanings only, without going through issues of readings, syntax, jurisprudence, and so on.

- Explaining the Qur’anic vocabulary during interpretation and colouring the explanation in a different colour to make it easier for those who want it.

- Adopting the approach of the Salaf, may Allah be pleased with them, by following the evidence in the Qur’an and Sunnah.

- Considering the most likely meaning when there is opposition regarding the evidence, taking into account the rules of interpretation and the rules of preponderance (At-Tarjih).

- Citing a number of Verses and their benefits in order to help the reader reflect on them and make full use of them, under a separate title: Among the benefits of the Verses.

- Writing an introduction at the beginning of each Surah with a statement of its purpose and its general meaning.

- Collecting all of the above and writing it on the footnote of the Noble Qur’an, to be of assistance to the reader of the Qur’an in understanding the Words of Allah Almighty in the easiest way, without the need to refer to another book.

name: Kitab al-Ihkam (Mukhtasar Ibn al-Lahham) - Usul Fiqh Hanbali
description_short:
Al-Mukhtasar fi Usul Al-Fiqh is an abridged book on the principles of the jurisprudence of Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Al-Lahham (752-803).

He wrote this book, explaining its symbols and ambiguities, but without delving into the reasons and evidence, with reference to the difference or consensus in some issues. Al-Hafiz Ibn Al-Lahham arranged the book according to the books of Islamic Jurisprudence (Ilm Al-Usul), and answered some of the questions that were brought to him about this science (i.e. Usul Al-Fiqh).

Al-Hafiz Ibn al-Lahham said in the introduction of the book:

"This is an abridged version on the principles of jurisprudence according to the doctrine of Imam Abi Abdullah Ahmed Ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him.

I have endeavoured to abridge it, edit it, clarify its symbols, but without delving into the reasons and evidence, pointing to disagreement and concord in most issues, arranging it in the order of the books of Islamic Jurisprudence, and answering the repeated questions of our scholar brothers. We ask Allah, glory be to Him, to make this book sincerely for His Sake, beneficial and right; to protect us and make us righteous, and grant us His Grace and Generosity."

Beautifully checked and annotated edition.

name: Kitab al-Ihkam (Mukhtasar Ibn al-Lahham) - Usul Fiqh Hanbali
description_short:
Al-Mukhtasar fi Usul Al-Fiqh is an abridged book on the principles of the jurisprudence of Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Al-Lahham (752-803).

He wrote this book, explaining its symbols and ambiguities, but without delving into the reasons and evidence, with reference to the difference or consensus in some issues. Al-Hafiz Ibn Al-Lahham arranged the book according to the books of Islamic Jurisprudence (Ilm Al-Usul), and answered some of the questions that were brought to him about this science (i.e. Usul Al-Fiqh).

Al-Hafiz Ibn al-Lahham said in the introduction of the book:

"This is an abridged version on the principles of jurisprudence according to the doctrine of Imam Abi Abdullah Ahmed Ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him.

I have endeavoured to abridge it, edit it, clarify its symbols, but without delving into the reasons and evidence, pointing to disagreement and concord in most issues, arranging it in the order of the books of Islamic Jurisprudence, and answering the repeated questions of our scholar brothers. We ask Allah, glory be to Him, to make this book sincerely for His Sake, beneficial and right; to protect us and make us righteous, and grant us His Grace and Generosity."

Beautifully checked and annotated edition.

name: The contextual study of the verses in the Aqida as per Ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
The title of this research is, “The efforts of Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah in regard to clarifying the effect of the Qur’anic connotation on the issues of creed (Aqidah): Collecting and studying the Qur’anic Verses which Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, referred to as an evidence of the contextual expression (as of what comes before the text and what comes after the text), and that is in all the chapters of the creed.

Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, excelled in eliciting the inherent connotations in the context, by highlighting the connotation of the contextual meaning in many of his inferences, especially when he responds to the critics, his extensive knowledge of the writings of those who preceded him, his compatibility of the preceding scholars in his decisions of issues of creed, and the meanings of the Qura’nic Verses, and his comprehensive knowledge of the Arabic language, in regard to the semantics of its vocabulary, its constructions and stylistics.

Nice Saudi edition, with all sources mentioned at the bottom of the page.

name: The efforts of the Companions in teaching the Qur'an and its practice
description_short:
The Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon him, and their efforts in teaching and caring for the Noble Qur’an, written by Anas Ahmed Karazon. 

Allah Almighty has appointed for this Qur’an men who put it in their hearts and deeds, and at their head were the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, who exerted great efforts in teaching and caring for it, seeking only Allah’s Pleasure. So they set out to roam the deserts and wilderness, crossing the seas, spreading the Qur’an all over the world.

This book seeks to highlight their efforts and the authentic Prophetic method they followed in this way, in order to realise the great responsibility placed on our shoulders to follow in their blessed footsteps (Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so from their guidance take an example).

The Muslim Ummah is still enjoying the effects of their knowledge, justice and Jihad until the Day of Resurrection. Those are the followers of the Prophet and his party, and without them there would be no Muslim on earth.

name: As-Siraj fi Bayan Gharib Al-Qur’an
description_short:
This is one of the best books that explain the meanings of words in detail, without verbosity or repetition; written in easy, simple and accessible terms that everyone can understand.

The author has stated: "I have compiled this book to be a reminder for those who want to know the meanings of the strange terms of the Noble Qur’an. I have collected it from the books of interpretation (Tafsir) and the ancient and contemporary books dealing with the strange terms of the Qur’an; I made the phrase easier and tried to formulate the different sayings in one comprehensive phrase whenever possible."

The book begins with Surat Al-Fatihah, then Al-Baqarah, and continues downward until Surat An-Nas. The number of the Surah, the number of its Verses, and the place of its revelation are clarified in the introduction of each Surah, whether it is revealed in Makkah or Madinah. The word is coloured in red, then comes the interpretation or meaning of the word. The book contains the meanings of thousands of words.

name: Ulum al-Hadith (Muqaddimah Ibn Salah) - with annotations of al-Iraqi
description_short:
This is the most prominent book in the Science of Hadith terminology in which Ibn As-Salah has mentioned 65 types of Hadith Sciences.  It has received considerable attention from subsequent authors who explained, abridged and set it to poetry and it became an example for latter books of its genre. 

Ibn Hajar said that because Ibn As-Salah "Gathered in it what had been previously dispersed throughout other books, people focused upon it, following his methodology. The works are innumerable in which this book has been set to verse, abridged, added to and subtracted from, disagreed with and supported".

This immense work is published with the annotations of Hafidh al-’Iraqi (806H), as well as the annotations of the Muhaqqiq, Sheikh Muhammad Raghib at-Tabbakh, Egyptian scholar of the last century.

Serious edition, 100% Harakat.

name: Sulwatu at-Tullab (Solace for Students) - Dr 'Ali al-'Imran
description_short:
Solace for Students: excerpts from the concerns of students of science, culture, literature, and self-esteem and perfection.

The book came in the form of small chapters; each chapter tackles one topic, but they are all important and necessary for all students. Sometimes it treats distraction, and sometimes teaches you that you should be certain before being delusional, and sometimes it motivates you by mentioning some of those whose determination was so great that you belittle yourself and sometimes even despise yourself. Then afterwards, it tells you that they are just men; if you work hard, you could achieve what they have achieved, so that your admiration for them will not deter you from reaching your destiny or discourage you. In fact, you must take them as a role model and follow their guidance.

An inspiring book that will revive the heart of all Tullab al-'Ilm.

name: Kitab Taqyid al-'Ilm - Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi
description_short:
A precious work chronicling the question of recording knowledge in Islam: when and how it began, and its ruling in the Shari'ah. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi (d. 463 AH) surveys the narrations from the Prophet ﷺ, the Companions, and the Tabi'in prohibiting the writing of hadith, then sets against them those permitting it, demonstrating that the prohibition was a precaution lest anything be equated with the Quran. The book contains 316 narrations with full chains of transmission.

Beyond its historical value, the book is a source of inspiration for today's student: the accounts it carries of the early scholars' devotion to preserving knowledge, their attachment to books, and their tireless pursuit of learning kindle in the reader the desire to belong to that same blessed chain. An essential reference and a motivating read in equal measure.

description_short:
We are happy to offer you a real school program for learning the Arabic language, and moreover a program from one of the great countries where Arabic is the official language and where literary Arabic holds a great place: Egypt.

We chose this program because it is comprehensive, very colourful, well-structured and modern. And above all a great asset for homeschooler parents who homeschool their children, the program is full of advice, examples for the practical application of the subject, recommendations, there are even sometimes QR Code links to certain videos such as for the poems or the Nasheeds for example, to be able to repeat them with their child.

name: Sharh Ma'ani Al-Athar by Imam Tahawi
description_short:
Sharh Ma’āni Al-Āthār is a book about the Hadiths of rulings and the evidence of controversial jurisprudence issues. It is arranged on jurisprudence chapters, in which its author, Imam Abu Jaafar al-Tahawi, mentioned the traditions reported from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding the rulings which may be misinterpreted that some of them invalidate each other. He therefore explained an-Nasikh (the abrogating) and al-mansukh (the abrogated) and distinguished between al-Muqayyad (the restricted) and al-Mutlaq (the absolute), and what ruling should be put into effect, and what should not.

The book Sharh Ma’āni Al-Āthār is one of the reliable sources of the noble prophetic Hadith; it was considered by Al-Hafiz bin Hajar in his book “Itḥāf al-Mahara” as one of the Hadith books that follow the six books in terms of their collection of the most authentic Hadiths. This is due to the benefits related to these Hadiths in their chain of narrators and their narrations, to the clarification of its deductions, to the revelation of seemingly opposing traditions, to its distinction between the abrogating and the abrogated ones, and sayings in Jarh wa Ta’deel that help in accepting and refuting the reports; all set up in good arrangement and classification.

The value of this book was manifested by the interest of scholars, past and present, in their explanation, abridgement and verification, enlightening its methodology and providing a biography of its narrators with an extraction of the appendices of its Hadiths over the six books.

Very good edition, verified from 13 written manuscripts and from the book Nukha al-Afkar of Imam al-'Ayni.

name: Mukhtasar at-Tahrir fi Usul al-Fiqh - Ibn an-Najar
description_short:
Mukhtasar al-Tahrir—formally titled Al-Kawkab al-Munir—is a foundational and highly concentrated text in the field of Hanbali Usul al-Fiqh (Principles of Jurisprudence). Authored by the venerable scholar Ibn al-Najjar al-Futūḥī (d. 972 AH), this work is an abridgment of his own larger treatise, Al-Tahrir. It serves as a comprehensive synthesis of the Hanbali legal methodology, drawing heavily from the authoritative insights of Imam al-Mardaawi. Despite its concise nature, it covers the entirety of legal theory—from the definitions of ruling (Hukm) and the sources of evidence (Adillah) to the intricacies of linguistic derivation and the conditions of Ijtihad.

The text is prized for its surgical precision and its ability to organize complex jurisprudential debates into a structured, pedagogical format. For students of law and researchers of the Hanbali school, this book remains a primary gateway to understanding how legal rulings are derived from scriptural sources. It embodies the school's commitment to tradition, logic, and linguistic rigor, making it a masterpiece of legal academic discipline.

name: Irshad as-Sari li Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari - Al-Qastalani ash-Shafi'i
description_short:
“Irshād as-Sarī lī Sharḥ Sahih al-Bukhāri” is a book of Hadith verification books written by Imam al-Qastalāni (851-923). The book is considered a reference in the jurisprudence of Hadith; it is an explanation of the most authentic books after the Noble Qur’an, namely Sahih al-Bukhāri. In it, the author relied on the interpretation of the chain of narrators and the narrative text, explaining the vocabulary and showing what is also deduced from the Hadith, based on the statements and opinions of the scholars and jurists.

His greatest advantage is that al-Qastalāni contained the text of al-Bukhari, letter by letter and word by word, as mentioned by Abu al-Ashbal Ahmad Muhammad Shakir in the introduction to his book, the Greek version of Sahih al-Bukhāri. 

Abdul Karim Al-Khudair said: "Imam Al-Qastalāni relied, in many of his researches, on previous interpretations, such as those of Al-Karmāni, Al-‘Ayni and Ibn Hajar; it is in fact an abridged version of these books, especially the two great interpretations, by Al-Ayni and Ibn Hajar.

Sharh al-Qastalāni is a brief and refined explanation, which is indispensable for any student of knowledge, especially those looking for an accurate interpretation of al-Bukhāri; because Al-Bukhāri is narrated with multiple narrations, and this book Irshād as-Sarī is characterized by its explanation of these narrations. Indeed, its author has analyzed all those narrations to make it more useful, despite its abridgement."

Gorgeous edition, very large volumes (A4 size), excellent Tahqiq for this exceptionnal work.

name: Siraj as-Salik Sharh As-hal al-Masalik - Uthman al-Ju'ali al-Maliki
description_short:
The book “Sirāj as-Sālik Sharḥ As’hal al-Masālik li-Naẓm Targhīb al-Murīd al-Sālik” was written by the jurist ‘Uthmān ibn Ḥasanayn Birrī al-Ja’li al-Māliki; it is an interpretation of the poetic composition “Ashal al-Masālik li-Naẓm Targhīb al-Murīd as-Sālik” that followed the School of Thought of Imām Mālik ibn Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, and was written by Muḥammad al-Bashshār.

The author combined accuracy and simplicity, which indicates superior ability and extra proficiency. His interpretation was neither boring in length nor short of meeting its objective, turning the book into a source that cannot be dispensed with.

The explanation focused briefly on the analysis of the words and the clarification of their meaning, as long as there was no necessity for lengthening otherwise required by a particular situation; because in such case, it would be necessary for the commentator to elaborate longer to complete the benefit with his definition of the parts and chapters, and what needs to be defined in terms of words.

Good edition in 2 volumes with the authentication of the Hadiths.

The book is a summary of Shāfi’i Fiqh and ‘ilm al-Khilāf (the science of controversial subjects). It includes the opinions of al-Shāfi’i along with those of Abu Hanifa, Malik and al-Muzni.

The book “al-Wajeez” is part of a series of Al-Ghazāli books on Shāfi’i jurisprudence, named al-Baseet, al-Waseet and al-Wajeez. The basis of all these books is the book Nihāyat al-maṭlab fī dirāyat al-madhhab by Imam of al-Haramayn, al-Juwayni (d. 478.H), teacher of al-Ghazāli. This was clarified by Ibn Hajar al-Haytami (d. 973.H) when he said:

Al-Ghazāli has abridged the book “Nihāyat” (i.e. Al-Juwayni’s book) in a lengthy and rich summary and named it “al-Baseet”; then he abridged further and named it “al-Waseet” which in its turn was subject to additional abridgment and named it “al-Wajeez.” Then came Imam Al-Rāfi’i, who concluded a brief explanation of “Al-Wajeez”, then a detailed one, which turned out to be an unmatched compilation in the Shāfi’i School of Thought.”

Good edition with useful annotations and 100 Harakat.

name: As-Salsabil fi Sharh ad-Dalil by Shaykh Sa'd al-Khathlan
description_short:
In his writing, he - may Allah protect him - adopted the following approach:

- To explain the author’s statement.

- To explain the evidence or the commentary upon which the author based his statement.

- If there is a common disagreement on an issue, or that the outweighing opinion is different from what the author has mentioned, then one should mention the opinions of the jurists on the issue, the evidence of each statement, and analyze them, before emphasizing the preferred opinion among them.

- To carefully consider the evidence from the Qur’an, the Sunnah and the narrations from the Companions and the Successors, and that the outweighing of one opinion over others should be based on the requirements of the evidence, while also referring to the choices of the most prominent scholars.

- To thoroughly explain the category of Hadiths following the method of al-Muhaddithin (Transmitters and Interpreters of Hadith), and the reasons they have mentioned, and also clarify their rulings on the Hadiths, whether authentic or weak.

- To list the major contemporary crises and issues, depicting them, and explaining the Islamic ruling on them, with reference to the opinions of the most prominent jurisprudential academies and scientific bodies.

- To carefully link the interpretation with three sciences, which are essential for anyone seeking Islamic knowledge, namely: Al-Fiqh, the principles of Al-Fiqh and the Science of Hadith. In this method, a jurisprudence issue is mentioned along with the scholars’ opinions about them, including the rules of the fundamentalist issues associated with them, and traditions reported on the matter.

description_short:
The issue of Divine existence is the most visible evidence of man’s infringement and stubbornness towards his Lord. Although the existence of Allah Almighty is something rooted in the Fitrah (innate nature), by which the heart of man grows and his conscience is revived by it; however, the extravagance of the mind drives man away to misguidance and misery.

It may be cognitive ingratitude for the issue of the Divine existence to be placed on the platform of research and consideration, since knowledge, by its nature, is an issue that derives its validity and proof from Allah Almighty, so how can Allah, Glory be to Him, be the subject of research and consideration?

But any reader of the religious controversies, especially in this era, can find a wide hostility between believers and atheists to the extent that innate knowledge has shifted from being a starting point for establishing facts to be, itself, a subject of proof, and, hence, Fitrah has become subject of proof after it was proof itself.

In the book, the author has explained the Principles of Hadith Narration and writing a hadith through listening.

The author says: “The first chapters are knowledge of the ethics of seeking, attaining and listening to Hadith, then knowing the knowledge of that, its aspects and from whom to acquire it, then mastery and writing, then memorization and awareness, then discernment and criticism by knowing which Hadith is Sahih (authentic), Dai’f (weak), Maqbul (accepted), Matruk (abandoned), Mawdu’ (fabricated), and so on.”

Excellent Tahqiq from 4 manuscripts, with additional annotations. 100% Harakat.

name: Al-Isti'ab fi Ma'rifah al-AsHab - Hafidh ibn Abdil-Barr
description_short:
Al-Isti'āb Fi Ma'rifat Al-Ashāb is a book on the biography of the Companions, written by al-Hafiz Abu Omar Yusuf bin Abdullah al-Nimri, known as Ibn Abdul-Barr (368–463); it is considered one of the first books, discussing the life of the Companions. The author’s approach in his book was that he mentioned the Companion and those who narrated from him, and some information about those who narrated from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah’s prayers and peace be upon him, and some matters related to their lives, death and age.

Ibn Abd al-Barr has collected in this book whatever he was able to collect on the life of the Prophet’s Companions.

Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi has praised the entirety of his Sheikh Ibn Abdul-Barr’s books, saying: Al-Isti'āb Fi Ma'rifat Al-Ashāb, is a book about the Companions, in which he listed the names of those mentioned in the narrations, biographies and compilations, introducing them, summarizing alphabetically their conditions, status and main news, in twelve parts that were unparalleled by early scholars, despite the large number of what they had classified in this subject.

Edition in 3 volumes also containing the work "Al-Inbah 'ala Qabail ar-Ruwat" by Ibn Abd al-Barr also and "Al-Istidrak 'ala al-Isti'ab" by Ibn al-Ameen (529H) (the biographies of Companions that Imam Ibn Abd al-Barr did not mention).

name: Mafhum Ahl Sunnah Wal Jama’ah by Adil Al-Shamiri
description_short:
This book is entitled “Mafhum Ahl Sunnah Wal Jama’ah bayna Sheikh Al-Islam ibn Taymiyyah wa Ahl Al-Ifrat wa Tafreet” by Author Adel bin Muhammad al-Shamiri. In this book, the author discusses issues where concepts vary between exaggeration and negligence; indeed much has been said about it, and disputes have been intensified between many of those affiliated with Ahlu  Sunnah wal-Jama`ah.

The book includes many important chapters and sub-chapters. One of the chapters tackles the issue of: Do Ahlu Sunnah believe that Takfir and Tafsiq is Allah’s Right only? Ahlu Sunnah do not bind people to the opinions they adopt from the sources of Ijtihād. This book is distinguished by its extensive presentation of the issues of the principles of I’tiqād, through explanation, thoroughness and Ta’sil (reference to the basic principles of Islamic Shari’ah).

Ibn Taymiyyah is one of the Scholars who embraced the doctrine of the Salaf and the successors of this Ummah. Ahlu Sunnah follow a middle course among the sects related to Islam; they believe in pure Islam, the religion of moderation.

This is a beneficial study for students of knowledge so that they do not fall into excessiveness (Ifrāt) and do not fall into negligence (Tafrit). Rather, they follow the truth that was explained by one of the trusted well-versed scholars, who is an authority in the doctrines of the predecessors and successors.

name: Dham al-Kalam wa Ahlihi - Imam Abu Isma'il al-Harawi (481H)
description_short:
Dhamm Al-Kalām wa Ahlihi by Al-Harawi. or "Condemning Kalām (speculative theology) and Mutakallimeen (practitioners of Kalām)" is a book written by Abu Ismail Abdullah Ibn Muhammad Al-Harawi Al-Ansari, known as Abu Ismail Al-Harawi (396H - 481H) in which he warns against speculative theology and responds to the Mutakallimeen. He is great scholar who established the Sunnah and rejected innovations.

He cited the Hadiths of the Prophet, the sayings of the Companions and Followers, and then the sayings of the Scholars of his time.

The book is considered one of the references in responding to the theologians, and its author have been nicknamed Sheikh al-Islam because of his immense mastery of religious sciences.

Ibn Taymiyyah said: “But many people did not take note of many of the sayings of the Salaf (righteous predecessors) and scholars on this issue and its meanings (speculative theology). People have collected from the sayings of the Salaf and scholars in this regard books, such as what the one was compiled by Sheikh Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, and like the great book compiled by Abu Ismail Abdullah Ibn Muhammad Ibn Ali Ibn Muhammad Ibn Ahmed Ibn Ali Ibn Jaafar Ibn Mansour Al-Harawi Al-Ansari, nicknamed Sheikh al-Islam, which he called “Dhamm Al-Kalaam wa Ahlihi”.

This series is titled: “Amrahu wa Astafeedu ma’a Tasāli at-Tajweedi” (I Have fun and benefit with Tajweed entertainment); it is a program in the science of Tajweed that studies its central principles and rulings with intelligent cumulative information. It is distinguished by its exercises, puzzles and games that enhance the scientific idea of ​​the lessons in an unprecedented, modern and interactive way, while clarifying the educational objectives of each lesson. It was designed to be the first assistant for children to master the science of Tajweed in a fun and interesting way, hence its name “I have fun and benefit with Tajweed entertainment”. Indeed, its fun and benefits make the child enjoy and learn Tajweed at the same time.

The series focuses on explaining the method of how the Qur’an controls perfectly the rules of Tajweed, through interactive lessons and exercises that help the student know the Tajweed ruling and introduce him to some of the characteristics of the letters that are frequently discussed about in the recitation. There is also explanation of the types of Madds (elongations) with the addition of lessons that compare between their different styles, which help the student distinguish between various forms of elongation letters. This series, by Allah’s Will, will be one of the most wonderful works to guide children in their homes, and in Qur’anic institutes and centres, so that they may learn Tajweed through the best ways and methods.

name: Series: Riyad as-Salihin for the Muslim child (7 levels, 350 Hadiths)
description_short:
This is a new series illustrated in the Hadith of the Prophet for school students, Quranic institutes, non-Arabic speakers and those wishing to memorize the noble Hadith of the Prophet.

This series consists of seven books, with each book containing fifty Hadiths. These Hadiths are arranged by their word count according to the age group.

The series Levels starts with the Kindergarten level: It includes the shortest Hadiths of the Prophet, from two to three words.

The first level: It includes prophetic Hadiths of four words. In this way, the number of Hadith words increases by one word in each level up to the sixth level.

The series is characterized by graduation, ease, clarity, suspense, entertainment, and the development of educational values. It is also characterized by titles that explain the content, by its beautiful output, and by attractive images. We have been keen to select most of the Hadiths in the series from the two authentic books of Al-Bukhari and Muslim.

It is also characterized by its easy style to endear the memorizing the Prophetic Hadiths to children; indeed, this experience enables the student to memorize three hundred and fifty Hadiths by the time he finishes studying at the primary level. Therefore, this series is considered the first educational curriculum for children, which takes them firm on the course to memorize the Noble Prophetic Hadith, in a way that is equivalent to the method of their memorization of the Holy Qur’an.

name: Al-Wafi fi al-Fiqh ala Madhhab al-Imam Abi Hanifah - An-Nasafi
description_short:
This is a beautiful book of Hanafi Fiqh written by the very famous Hafidh ad-Din an-Nafasi. Published for the first time from 2 ancient manuscripts, with an airy layout and 100% Harakat text. The book also benefits from useful explanations and commentaries in footnotes for a more complete and contextualized understanding of the book.

The first scholar to compile in Hanafi jurisprudence was Imam Muhammad Ibn al-Hassan, and his books were an authority in the Hanafi School of thought and a source for those who wrote after him. They are the six books, which were called: “Zahir Ar-Riwāya,” which are “Al-Mabsut, Az-Ziyādat, Al-Jāmi’ As-Saghir, Al-Jāmi’ Al-Kabir, As-Siyar As-Saghir, and As-Siyar Al-Kabir.

Abu al-Fadl al-Marwazi, known as al-Hakim ash-Shāhid, compiled the six books of Imam Muhammad Ibn Al-Hassan in the book “Al-Kāfi’”.

As for Imam Al-Nasāfi, may Allah have mercy on him, he compiled “Al-Wāfi’” from three books: Az-Ziyādat, Al-Jāmi’ As-Saghir, Al-Jāmi’ Al-Kabir, in addition to: “Mukhtasar Al-Qaduri” and “Manzumat Al-Khilafiyāt.”

Beautiful edition verified from the two oldest manuscripts available, with passages from an-Nasafi's explanation of his own Matn "al-Kafi Sharh al-Wafi" in 3 volumes.

description_short:

name: Reasons for the Genius of the Salaf - Abdul-Fattah Abu Ghuddah
description_short:
If we study the biographies of the Salaf (righteous ancestors), we will find wonders and strange stories, yet they are true. We will also find facts that are compared in our realities and modern era to myths, and, yet, they are not myths, they are real.

Our realities reflect this dimension upon us, because a person judges from his own perspective or knowledge. If his perspective is narrow or his information is limited, he will judge consequently, which results in his judgment being severed, incomplete and paralysed. This is the case for many of the issues tackled by the Salaf who did not miss any opportunity to work wonders, as they raced towards good deeds.

name: Al-Muqaddimah Al-Qurtubiyyah bi Sharh Sheikh Zarrouk El Bernoussi
description_short:
The poeem on the jurisprudence system in the Maliki school “Al-Muqaddimah Al-Qurtubiyyah” or “Arjouzat Al-Wildan fil Fard wal Masnoun” by Sheikh and jurist “Abu Bakr Yahya Ibn Saadoun Al-Qurtubi (d. 567 AH)”, which consists of 117 verses.

Today, we propose you the poeme enriched with its explanation by the Imam and jurist, the author of many famous books, Sheikh Ahmed Ibn Ahmed Ibn Muhammad Ibn Issa El Bernoussi Al-Fassi known as Zarrouk (846 AH - 899 AH). In his interpretation of the poem, Sheikh Zarrouk listed his explanation of the verses according to the usual arrangement in the books of jurisprudence. In it, he took care of linguistic and idiomatic definitions, branching, benefits, jurisprudential warnings, etc.

One of his approaches is to include evidence from the Noble Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet, and he may also cite poetry, as well as adopting some fundamentalist and jurisprudential rules.

With regard to the Hadith of the Prophet, he often took care of explaining the degree of the Hadith authenticity and mentioned those who produced it from among the owners of Hadith compilations; and it is out of his honesty that if he could not find the Hadith or its original text, he would make it clear and asked the reader to search for it.

As for the sources that Zarrouk relied on in his interpretation, it can be said that he referred to most of important and well-known books of fiqh.

This is an abridged and comprehensive explanation of the five pillars of Islam.

A very serious Tahqiq by a professor of Fiqh from the University of Wahran in Algeria, the poem is verified from 7 manuscripts and the explanation is verified from 3 manuscripts.

name: The Mushaf of the 10 Recitations from the Shātibiyah and Durrah Ways
description_short:
The book “The Mushaf of the Ten Recitations from the Shātibiyah and Durrah Ways” is one of the most important sciences of the Qur’anic recitations.

In our time, many wonderful and distinctive Qur’anic recitations of the Qur’an have appeared, but each of them has been distinguished in one or several aspects, but others were missing.

This Qur’an is distinguished by many scientific and exegetical features, among them are the following:

- Collecting the words in which the reciters differed in their way of reciting them and identifying their reciters.

- Mentioning the evidence of al-Shātibiyah and ad-Durrah by indicating only the position of their evidence.

- Investigating the sources mentioned on each page of the narration of Warsh in: (Al-Badal, Al Naql, Al-Lamat, Al-Ra’a’, and Al-Leen), and of Hamzah in: “Al-Sakin Al-Mawsoul and Al-Mafsoul”, and “Ha’at” of Al-Makki”, and “IKhfā’āt” of Abi Jaafar” and “Ibdāl Al-Hamz”.

As for the extrinsic features, they are:

- Writing the words on the margins in the Ottoman script.

- Using the opposite colour in letters, diacritics and control when there is a disagreement between the reciters, as well as when referring to the edited verses.

Comments on the book:

- This work is complete and helpful to everyone, among the students, who wants to memorize the ten recitations.

- This work is extremely accurate and perfect, as it adds to the library of recitations a great work in the service of the Book of Almighty Allah.

This book was prepared and coordinated by the professor: Hadiya Mustafa Kamal Al-Raqbi.

name: Badhl Al-Majhud Fi Hall Sunan Abi Dawud by Muhaddith As-Saharanfuri
description_short:
A modern explanation of the Sunnah of Abi Dawud by an eminent Indian Muhaddith of the last century, Sheikh as-Saharanfuri (1346H).

The author took great care of the sayings and statements of Abu Dawud about the narrators and of correcting the various versions of the circulating Sunan, as well as extracting the comments and linking them from other sources. In his book, he mentions the appropriateness of the Hadith to the biography of the narrator, and the benefit of repeating the Hadith if it is repeated; he also goes on to deduce and mention the schools of thought, as well as explaining the words of the Ahadith through mixing and showing their origins and derivations.

In explaining the Hadith, the author has often relied on the great references among the famous explanations of Hadith books, as well as the works of Ibn Hajar in 'Ilm al-Rijal and also the reference dictionaries (Qamus al-Muhit & Lisan al-'Arab).

The book is well-explained and contains many benefits. No one who takes interest in the Sunnah of Abu Dawud can dispense with it, due to its length and its several fields of research.

A magnificent edition correcting the errors of previous editions and based on the manuscripts, with referencing of Hadiths and Athars and finally complete search summaries (verse, Hadith, Athar, places, personalities).

description_short:
The curtain has been revealed about a pearl to which the souls of the students yearn to reach, and whose light the hearts of researchers aspire to, with a precious, unique and advanced Iraqi copy, copied in the scene of Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, in the year 480 AH, with difficulty in it.

The author of this book, Sheikh Al-Qudūri, may Allah have mercy on him (d. 428 AH), compiled the issues of disagreement between the early scholars, and mentioned the principles on which their differences were based on Chapters and Branches, and, thus, concurred with the Sheikh’s knowledge of the causes of disagreement, and the principles of the school of thought, enabling it to be a reference for jurisprudence study.

Sheikh Al-Qudūri is a great figure and an eminent scholar, and his book “At-Taqrib” is of the highest level and quality that any reader of Islamic jurisprudence should acquire and read.

This work of this great Hanafi Imam is published for the first time, with a very serious verification as well as notes pointing to other reference works for those who want to deepen the subjects treated.

name: Mu'in al-Hukkam - At-Tarabulusi ('Ilm al-Qadha)
description_short:
Mu‘īn al-Hukkām fīmā Yataraddadu bayna al-Khaṣmayn min al-Aḥkām by 'Alā' ad-Dīn at-Ṭarābulusī (1032H).

This book is a guide in the procedures of Islamic law. The book was written by Ali Ibn Khalil at-Ṭarābulusī, who was also known as “'Alā' ad-Dīn Ibn al-Hasan Ali Ibn Khalil at-Ṭarābulusī,” and he was a Hanafi jurist in Jerusalem. In the introduction to his book, at-Ṭarābulusī has referred to the exceptional importance of Shari’ah in the Qur’an and among the Messengers, and then went on to say that he wrote this book to explain the basic principles of his profession.

At-Ṭarābulusī has stated that most law books are generally simple summaries of cases and rulings, and in contrast, he tries to explain the mysteries of his art. In his book, he touches on aspects of his noble mission, in addition to some daily issues, such as the authority of judges, their status and compensation for their various services. He also cites many court rulings, although they often come without a theoretical explanation. 

Excellent edition, verified from 14 manuscripts, with most of the Harakats and some useful annotations on some terms and on the Hadith mentioned.

name: Al-Jawab al-Fasih lima lafaqqahu 'abd al-Masih - Nu'man al-Alusi
description_short:
This book is a response and critique of the Christian faith, as its foundations were deceitfully demonstrated in a fabricated letter between an alleged Muslim named al-Hashemi and a Christian who called himself al-Kindi. The writer of the book is in fact the impersonator of the two characters; his Christian name is Yahya Ibn Uday. This letter was part of the Colonial Translation Project of the Origins of Islamic Heritage, which was supervised by Peter the Venerable, also known as Peter of Montboissier. It has accordingly played a major role in the Islamic image drawn in the West since its writing, and its effects still extend to this day. 

The book is important for the specialists, who took interest in responding to the People of the Book, as well as for history students and analysts of the “modernism era” that followed the Middle Ages; it reflects the reality of the Western faith with its profound desire to slander Islam and spread falsehood against it.

Published in full for the first time in 5 large volumes, with the careful and beneficial Tahqiq of several scholars.

description_short:
It is truly an explanation that fulfils the need of literary people, and massively referenced by the linguists, due to its scientific and literary collection, compiled by its illustrious author, who has written several books in various disciplines.

Ibn Abi Tayy says: “As for what follows: I ask Almighty Allah, the Revealer of the Most Exalted (Divine Revelation) and the Bestower of the Universal Good to help me in my effort to facilitate the interpretation of the poem of Al-Shanfari “Laamiyat Al-Arab wa Minhaaj Al-Adab”, the poem with the rare rhyme... to show what I included of the witty jokes of literature.”

In his verification, Dr. Ibrahim Al-Batshan, gave it a high substantiated touch that adorned the book’s footnotes; he referred to several sources in various disciplines to verify the original, which turned the book into a unique work that a student of knowledge cannot do without, and All Praise is due to Allah. 100% Harakat.

name: Al-Bulghah fi Funun al-Balaghah - Sheikh Anwar al-Fadhfari
description_short:
A book presenting the science of Arabic rhetoric in an accessible yet sophisticated style, authored by Abu Suhayl Anwar Abdullah al-Fadfari as a streamlined introduction to the three arts of balaghah: 'ilm al-ma'ani (meanings), 'ilm al-bayan (exposition), and 'ilm al-badi' (embellishment). It delivers the material in clear, concise language suited for the beginning student without compromising scholarly substance, supported by examples and textual evidence that ground the rules and make them stick.

The title "al-Bulghah" — meaning what suffices and conveys the purpose — reflects its method: giving the student exactly what is needed without the excess and branching that distracts the beginner. An ideal book for anyone seeking a solid foundation in Arabic rhetoric in a concise format (254 pages).

name: Al-Kashshaf ‘an Haqaa’iq at-Tanzeel by Al-Zamakhshari
description_short:
This is an interpretation of the Qur’an book which reveals the miraculous quality of the Qur’an in its rhetorical, stylistic and linguistic aspects. 

It is the most famous interpretation of the Mu'tazilites, in which the author demonstrated the aspects of the rhetorical miracle in the Noble Qur'an due to his familiarity with the Arabic language, his knowledge of their poetry, and his knowledge of the sciences of rhetoric, eloquence, grammar, and literature.

The book became popular among people of knowledge everywhere and everyone recognized its merit, abundance of knowledge and ingenuity.

“Al-Kashshaf” was the first interpretation to reveal the secret of the eloquence of the Qur’an, its miraculous aspects, and the accuracy of its meanings in its words, which had a great impact on the Arabs’ inability to oppose it or come up with anything similar.

Al-Zamakhshari listed a thousand verses on the Arabic language evidence, and focused on syntax and grammar, with a very brief reference to the jurisprudential issues in the verses of rulings.

Nonetheless, Al-Zamakhshari used his interpretation to spread the principles of the Mu'tazilah and support his doctrine. He tried his best to pretend discussing the linguistic meanings while in fact he was strongly supporting the Mu'tazilite beliefs with the power of argument and evidence.

The best edition to date, verified from 6 manuscripts, with many useful annotations and most of the Harakat.

name: Collection of poems (Qasidah) on the biography of the Prophet ﷺ
description_short:
This is a collection of Rajaz poetry (prosody) and other short poems on the biography of the beloved Prophet Muhammad - may Allah’s Prayers and Peace be upon him-, composed by a group of jurists, who took into account in their praise of the Prophet not to exaggerate in describing his major character traits and merits. It includes:

• The Poem of Dar Al-Habib” by Abdullah Al-Biskri (d. 713 AH). 

• “The 100 Verse Rajaz Poem” by Abu Al-Walid Al-Halabi (d. 815 AH).

• “A Poem on the Migration of the Prophet” Ibn Nasir ad-Din ad-Dimashqi (d. 842 AH). 

• “A Poem on the Names of Al-Mustafa (the Prophet)”by Al-Balqini (d. 713 AH). 

• “A Poem on the Mission of the Prophet” by Ibn Al-Diba’i (d. 944 AH). 

• «A Rajaz Poem on the Names of the Prophet” by Al-Ghazi (d. 984 AH). 

• “A Rajaz Poem on the Important Aspects in the Prophet’s Biography” by Al-Fassi (d. 1100 AH). 

• “A Rajaz Poem from Halab on the Biography of the Prophet” by Al-Qustantini (d. 1190 AH). 

• “A Rajaz Poem on the Sublime Qualities of the Prophet” by Abdullah As-Salem Al-Hasani (died 1353 A.H). 

• “A Brief Rajaz Poem on the Incidents of the Migration Period” by Abdullah bin Sa’eed Al-Lahji Al-Hadhrami and then Al-Makki (d. 1410 AH).

The Tahqiq is serious and for each poem there are photos of the manuscripts, useful annotations and finally an Ijaza to fill in for those who wish to memorise the poems.

100% Harakat on the Qasidah.

name: Tafsir Ibn Ashur : At-Tahrir wa at-Tanwir
description_short:
Tafsir at-Tahrir wa at-Tanwir (Interpretation of verification and enlightenment) is a work of Quranic exegesis (Tafsir) by sheikh Muhammad at-Tahir Ibn ‘Ashur, Sheikh of Az-Zaytouna University in Tunis.

It is one of the most important interpretations referred to by specialists. Through this book, the author was able to place himself among the most prominent scholars of the interpretation of the Qur’an, and this Tafsir is one of the most prominent interpretations of the modern era that was written in respect to the theory of systems according to Al-Jurjani.

This book is a culmination of his fifty years of work, where Ibn ‘Ashur has poured in all of his innovative and reformist approaches. His approach is most notably characterized by his emphasis on the rhetorical aspect of the Qur'an, instead of relying entirely on the scientific heritage of interpretation. 

“At-Tahrir wa at-Tanwir”, which is the title shortened by Sheikh Ibn ‘Ashur in the preface to his book, was published in Tunisia by the Tunisian House of Publishing in 1984 in 30 parts under the title "Tafsir at-Tahrir wa at-Tanwir". 

This is the brand new revised edition in 12 volumes resulting from the collaboration between Dar ibn Hazm and Dar Sahnoun (Tunisia).

description_short:
The book of prayer by Imam Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya is a valuable book that deals with the topic of prayer in a comprehensive and profound manner. The book is also known by other names such as "The Secrets of Prayer" and "The Ruling on the One who Abandons Prayer".

Topics covered in the book:

  • The ruling on the one who abandons prayer: The book discusses in detail the ruling on the one who abandons prayer in Islam and the opinions of scholars on this issue, citing evidence from the Quran, Sunnah, and sayings of the Companions.
  • The virtues of prayer: It highlights the importance of prayer in Islam, its great virtue, and its status in the life of a Muslim.
  • The secrets of prayer: The book delves into explaining the secrets of prayer, its spiritual meanings, and its positive effects on the individual and society.
  • How to perform prayer: It provides a detailed explanation of how to perform prayer with all its pillars, conditions, and Sunnahs, based on the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

name: Al-Qu'ran, Taddabur wa 'Amal - (2 sizes)
description_short:
Here the methodology and structure of each page of this great Tafsir:


1- Deliberative interpretations:

There have been extracted from sixteen books from the leading books of Tafsir (interpretation), approved by the Sunni mainstream Muslims. We have kept the wording used by the interpreter, unless there is an error. The reference is mentioned for each interpretation, by naming the interpreter

There are some 4228 cases of interpretations, selected from about 15,000 entries.

There are no more than three interpretation instances in a single verse or part of it.

2- Table of the words’ meanings:

It contains the meanings of some uncommon words in the outset of the Qur’an, taken from the book “As-Siraj fi Ghareeb Al-Quran” by Sheikh Dr. Muhammad Ibn Abdulaziz Al-Khudairi.

3- Putting into practice the Verses of the Qur’an:

In order to train the reader to the level of putting what he learns in the Noble Qur’an into practice, they have proposed three measured applied practical actions deduced from the Verses in the beginning, and they have placed in front of each action the Verse from which it was derived.

4- Directions:

Are mentioned three general directives - educational, doctrinal and jurisprudential - drawn from the verses of the outset, and listed in front of each directive the Verse from which the guidance was derived.

description_short:
This book is the most important commentary on the book “Ghayat al-Muntaha fi Jam’ al-Iqna’ wal-Muntaha” and it is the third pillar of the Hanbali school of thought. The doctrine of the later Hanbalis has settled on what is in “Al-Muntaha” which is called “Muntaha al-iradat fi jam' al-muqni' ma'a al-tanqih wa-ziyadat,” by the scholar Taqi Ad-Din Abi Al-Baqa’ Muhammad Ibn Ahmed Ibn Abdul Aziz Al-Fatuhi, known as Ibn An-Najjar who died in 972 AH.

name: Nataaij Al-Fikr fi Nahwi - Abu al-Qasim as-Suhayli
description_short:
Al-Suhaili mentioned in the introduction to this “Nataa’ij Al-Fikr” (the results of thought), and said, “Our intention is to arrange them as chapters as in the book “Al-Jumal,” to incline people’s hearts to it. It may be understood from this phrase that the book “Nataa’ij al-Fikr” is an explanation of the book “Al-Jumal”, but it is not in the idiomatic sense of the word. The most that can be said about the relationship of the book “Nataa’ij Al-Fikr” with “Al-Jumal” is that it contains a commentary on some issues referred to by the author of “Al-Jumal”, but it was made according to the arrangement of the chapters of “Al-Jumal” as mentioned, not in the sense that he listed all of them and commented on them, but rather in the sense that he adhered to the order of the sentences in what was attached to them.

Al-Suhaili had a special view of what he mentioned of grammatical issues away from differences and other opinions; he had his own opinion in which he has recorded his grammatical doctrine. The book tells you about his issues and informs you about the view of Al-Suhaili the narrator/theologian, and you can notice that in the discussion about the “name” and the “specified”, and how Al-Suhaili, with his knowledge, unveiled that issue.

name: Tahqeeq Mawaaqif as-Sahaabah fi al-Fitnah
description_short:
This book is a doctoral thesis with which Dr. Amahzoune obtained his Phd. It is a wonderful dissertation on the approach of the Muslims towards reading history in general, and the chance to study the events of the fitnah (trials) among the Companions and its substantiation through the narrations of Imam al-Tabari and Hadith scholars. The book of history by Imam at-Tabari was specially selected, due to its collection of all the narrations with their chains of transmission (Note: He who reports the narrations with their chains of transmission has freed himself from disconcertment); indeed, other scholars will then come forward to examine and review these narrations to distinguish the bad from the good (the fabricated from the authentic). But the book has been exploited by the prejudiced throughout the ages to slander the Companions and engage in them unjustly; so Dr. Amahzoune writes this book to put the records straight, by analyzing history according to the approach of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah and with precepts that are consistent with the belief of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah with regards to the Companions.

The book is ideal and I recommend it to everyone who wants to read about the fitnah in order to reassure his heart with sound knowledge. I was fortunate with guidance by Allah to come across this book, after a series of different readings on this controversial subject.

name: Al-Hidayah Sharh Bidayat Al-Mubtadi - Al-Marghinani
description_short:
This is one of the most important Hanafi jurisprudence books, written by the Hanafi jurist Burhan ad-Din Al-Marghinani. It is an explanation of his other book “Bidayat Al-Mubtadi’”, which is considered an essential text in Hanafi School of Fiqh.

Haji Khalifa said in his book “Kashf ad-Dhunun”: “It is an explanation of a matn (text) he called “Bidayat al-Mubtadi’” but it is in fact like the explanation of Mukhtasar al-Qudduri and Al-Jami’ as-Saghir of Muhammad, and it is his custom to edit the two imams’ speeches from the claimant and the evidence, then liberate the claimant of the great imam (Abu Haneefa) and simplify his evidence so that the answer comes out from their evidence. However, if his editing was contrary to this custom, then it is perceived as a tendency to what the two imams claimed and the task of explaining the issues of “Al-Jami’ As-Saghir” and “Mukhtasar al-Qaduri”.

name: I’anat at-Talibin ‘ala Hall Alfadh Fath al-Mu’in - Sayid al Bakri
description_short:
I'anat al-Talibin 'ala Hall Alfaz Fath al-Mu'in by Sayyid al-Bakri Muhammad Shata al-Dimyati (d. 1310 AH) is a foundational supercommentary (hashiyah) in late Shafi'i jurisprudence, dedicated to unpacking and contextualizing Zayn al-Din al-Malibari’s renowned commentary Fath al-Mu'in. Serving as an extensive reference across the Shafi'i legal corpus, the work systematically traverses every legal sphere: from ritual purification and prayer (ibadat), to commercial transactions (mu'amalat), familial obligations, estate division, criminal torts, and judicial procedure. Its comprehensive nature transforms al-Malibari’s dense, abridged base text into a detailed exposition accessible to advanced students and practitioners alike.

Methodologically, al-Dimyati conducts a clause-by-clause textual and lexical analysis (hall alfaz), resolving grammatical ellipses and elucidating complex syntax. More critically, the work functions as a definitive arbiter of the relied-upon position (al-mu'tamad) within the school, meticulously compiling and evaluating the legal verdicts of the paramount late Shafi'i authorities—most notably Ibn Hajar al-Haytami (Tuhfat al-Muhtaj), Shams al-Din al-Ramli (Nihayat al-Muhtaj), al-Khatib al-Shirbini, and Shaykh al-Islam Zakariyya al-Ansari. Enriched with practical ancillary legal cases (furu'), documented fatwas, and responses to real-world inquiries, the work remains an indispensable teaching curriculum and fatwa manual across traditional Islamic institutions worldwide.
searchable_keywords: I’anat at-Talibin ‘ala Hall Alfadh Fath al-Mu’in - Sayid al Bakri

name: Tafsir al-Baydawi (Anwar at-Tanzil wa Asrar at-Ta-wil)
description_short:
It is a complete interpretation of the Noble Qur’an, medium in size; it combines explanation and interpretation as required by the rules of the Arabic language, and establishes the evidence based on the principles of Ahlu as-Sunnis and the Mu’tazilah. Al-Baydawi’s excellent and concise work was extensively based on the earlier work of az-Zamakhshari’s book “Al-kashshaaf” (The unveiling), which displays great learning, has Mu'tazilite views, some of which al-Baydawi has amended, and some omitted. It is followed by mentioning a Hadith about the virtue of each Surah, but most of them are Fabricated Hadiths.

Tafsir al-Baydawi is also based on “At-Tafsir al-Kabir” by Fakhr ad-Din ar-Razi as well as Ar-Raghib al-Isfahani’s “Mufradaat Alfaaz al-Qur’an and his tafsir.”

Al-Baydawi added to his Tafsir some narrations from the Companions and the Followers, and some inferences and deductions in a wonderful style and accurate expression. Sometimes he is concerned with mentioning the different Readings of the Qur’an and presents the grammar without expansion. He briefly discusses some jurisprudential issues in the Verses of rulings, and tends to support his Shafi’i school. He also delves into the issues of the universe and nature when presenting the cosmic Verses, influenced by Ar-Razi.

Tafsir al-Baydawi is well-known and circulated in ancient and modern times, and was approved for teaching in many universities and religious institutes.
searchable_keywords: Tafsir al-Baydawi (Anwar at-Tanzil wa Asrar at-Ta-wil)

This is an objective Qur’anic study of love in the Noble Qur’an, which came to clarify the reality of love. It is the influential drive and motivator for the actions and words that the individual performs in his life; it is the source and the real stimulus that reflects the individual’s behaviour towards his Creator, Glory be to Him, and towards others around him.

When a person decides to choose, he does not accompany or sit or walk except with whom he loves, he does not eat except what he loves, he does not wear except what he loves, and he does not read except what he loves. When a person loves something, his soul will feel relaxed and pleased with it, but if he does not love it, his soul will obviously reject it. Accordingly, this book has addressed the wrong concept of love, studied its origins and explained its details in the Noble Qur’an.

name: The Gift to the Intelligent for Refuting the Arguments of the Christians
description_short:
The Gift to the Intelligent for Refuting the Arguments of the Christians - Abdullah At-Tarjuman, the Majorcan.

This book is written by a former priest called “Anselm Turmeda” and after his conversion to Islam he changed his name to “Abdullah At-Turjuman,” may Allah have mercy on him and accept it in his good deeds.

This book is considered one of the most important books in the field of comparative religion, and a significant reference for preachers and those seeking knowledge of the Christian religion.

Its presentation is easy; its words are simple and uncomplicated. It contains 148 pages. Sheikh Abdullah At-Turjuman started his book by talking about his upbringing and learning of Christian sciences, then the stated the reason for his conversion to Islam, his departure to Tunisia, and his service to the Commander of the Faithful, Abu Al-Abbas Ahmed Ibn Faaris, then his son, Abu Faaris Abdul Aziz, and the good graces that were bestowed upon him. He then proceeded to refute the religion of Christianity and to prove the virtue and superiority of the religion of Prophet of Islam, Muhammad, may Allah’s peace and blessing be upon him.

The book was published in 823 AH. Ironically, his manuscript remained in limbo. The first time it was published was by non-Muslims in 1885 AD in the magazine (History of Religions) in Paris, may Allah hasten to conquer it, and it continued to be published in the West, while Muslims were in oblivion and disorientation until it was brought to light by Dr. Mahmoud Ali Himayah in 1983. Unfortunately, it did not last long and soon it was banned from publication, so there is currently no copy until this new reprint, elhamdulillah.

name: Juhud Shaykh al-Islam ibn Taymiyyah fi Naqd Istidlalat Ahl al-Ahwae
description_short:
The efforts of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah in refuting the arguments of heretics by Lotfi Abu Khasheem.

The author of this book has obtained a doctorate degree from the Department of ‘Aqeedah at the Islamic University of the Prophet in Madinah, earning an excellent grade with first honours. Several sheikhs have praised the book, including: Dr. Saleh Al-‘Aqeel, Dr. Saud Al-Khalaf and Dr. Muhammad Al-Khamis, and they explained that it is a valuable research, in which its author made a praiseworthy effort.

The book is distinguished by:

- Its explanation of the innocence of the legal texts from the falsehood attached to them and the contradictions of the innovators’ dubious arguments, and that they have no authentic connexion to the divine texts.

- Its collection of the general arguments of the people of heresy, all refused the author, and which no reader may find them exclusively collected in a similar book; they were also thoroughly disproved by Sheikh of Islam.

- The author was not contented with mentioning Sheikh al-Islam’s refutation of the innovators’ argument, he also presented a report on the methodology of the rightly guided ancestors on the issue, quoting the words of Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him.

The book contains 720 pages of medium volume, and it was reviewed by a number of eminent Shafii scholars from Yemen.

There are also numerous footnotes that complete the explanation, notably on sources, proper names, and some additional Fawaid.

name: Al-Mukhtasar fi as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah - Musa al-'Azimi
description_short:
Al-Mukhtasar fi al-Sirat al-Nabawiyyah is a condensed and highly accessible version of the author’s multi-volume masterpiece, Al-Lu'lu' al-Maknun. In this volume, Musa bin Rashid al-'Azmi provides a streamlined chronological narrative of the Prophet's ﷺ life, focusing on the most authentic reports while maintaining a fast-paced and engaging writing style. It is designed for those who seek a reliable overview of the Seerah without the extensive academic footnotes found in larger encyclopedias.

The work places a heavy emphasis on the Prophetic character, highlighting traits of honor, integrity, and the virtuous methodology that guided the first generation of Muslims. By stripping away weaker narrations and focusing on the core milestones—from the early days in Makkah to the final moments in Madinah—al-'Azmi provides a clear roadmap of the events that shaped Islamic history. This Book includes seventy-one chapters on issues related to the Noble Qur’an, and these issues can be divided into five sections:

First Section deals with issues related to the virtue of the Qur’an, following its directives, acting upon it, venerating its people, and so on.

This is a book written by Professor Muhammad Zahid Al-Kawthari, one of the greatest specialists of Hanafi Fiqh of our time, which counters the claims of those who abuse the topic of divorce, and their despicable inclusion of Sharia rulings.

He emphasizes the fact that Shariah is not a typical manmade system of laws that can be changed from time to time.He unveils the evil claim that mentioning the divorce three statements is a complex and impracticable matter. He disproves the claim that Raj’i divorce does not permit the husband to take back his wife as long as the waiting period is in place. He examined the consensus of the jurists in this matter, and also concluded that divorce and Rij’ah (return of the divorced wife to her husband) are valid without testimonies.

name: Aqidah al-Asha'irah (rebuttal of Jawahir at-Tawhid) - Hassan ar-Ruday'an
description_short:
The Ash'ari Doctrine: A Critical Study of the Poem Jawharat at-Tawheed - Hassan ibn Ibrahim Al-Radayan

This book aims at clarifying the Ash'ari creed through a book approved by their late scholars, then submit it to the creed of the righteous predecessors to check all the points of agreement and disagreement therein.

The author chose the poem Jawharat at-Tawheed of Burhan Ad-Din Al-Laqani, for its popularity and importance among the later Ash’aris, as it is the pillar of their doctrine, and because of the many explanations and footnotes on it.

This book has several advantages, the most important of which are:

- The author relied in his criticism on a reliable source for the opponents, which is an important matter in critical studies, so that the author is not accused of attributing any statements to them.

- He relied on a late source, which is useful in ensuring the stability of the School of Thought, since the composition of the Jawharat at-Tawheed was at the beginning of the eleventh century AH.

- It carefully covers most chapters of faith, due to its comprehensive analysis of the entire poem and not being limited to some topics over others.

- The reader can feel the objectivity of the author, as he did not expose only the places of error, but rather deals with the places of error and the places of correctness, and where their belief was in agreement with the belief of the Sunnis, he would declare it.

- The author’s method of inference is easy and brief, and his evidence are based on the indication of the Qur’an and Sunnah, without any lengthy analysis.

name: Ma'alim as-Suwar - Fayez Sayyaf al-Suraih ( Landmarks of the Suras of the Qur'an)
description_short:
The author has followed a certain methodology, which is:

The first axis: The names of the Surahs, whether they are based on Shari’ah texts or independent reasoning, with an explanation of the meaning.

The second axis: describing each Surah, whether it was revealed in Makkah or Madinah, the number of Verses, the order of their revelation and their arrangement in the Qur’an.

The third axis: which is the general purpose of each Surah.

The fourth axis: the themes of each Surah with clarification of the numbers of the Verses.

The fifth axis: the purposes included in the Surah.

The sixth axis: the uncommon words in the Qur’an.

The seventh axis: the occasions in which the Surah was revealed, the one before and after it.

The eighth and final axis: The inspiration behind the Verses; it contains guidance, and many subtleties and kindness.

Each of the above axes and landmarks provides you with information, knowledge and understanding of the greatest and most honourable books (the Noble Qur’an).

The topics of this book were compiled from a collection of books mentioned in it. It is a comprehensive, general and very simple book; both its design and presentation are distinctive and wonderful, enabling the readers to get ample benefits.
