name: Muhtawayaat Suwar Al-Qur’an - Ahmed Al-Taweel
description_short:
A unique reference guide offering a comprehensive introduction to each surah of the Quran from al-Fatihah to al-Nas, authored by Sheikh Ahmad ibn Ahmad al-Tawil, Inspector of Mushafs and Recitations at the Quran Radio, and drawn from his complete 15-volume tafsir "Wahat al-Tafsir." For each surah he presents its names, virtues, classification (Makki or Madani), verse count, occasions of revelation, and main themes — covering its doctrinal, devotional, legal, narrative, and ethical content, with connections between its verses and purposes.

This book fills a real need: many Muslims read the Quran without grasping the overall subject and themes of each surah. This work gives the reader that comprehensive overview in a clear, concise style, serving as a permanent companion to the mushaf and a quick reference for anyone wanting to grasp the content of any surah before reciting or teaching it.

name: Al-Ghaayah fi Sharh Al-Hidaayah - Al-Saruji Al-Hanafi
description_short:
This book was written by Abu Al-Abbas Ahmed ibn Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Ghani Al-Saruji Al-Hanafi (d. 710), the Chief Justice in Egypt. His interpretation is one of the rare explanations in the Hanafi School. He had an interest in discussing the Hadiths and their chains of transmission and their causes, unlike the work of the other Hanafi scholars in their commentaries, who were less interested in this field.

He was also interested in mentioning the opinions on many issues of scholars from other Schools of Thought - including the Zahiriyyah – emulating the method of Ibn Qudamah in his book "Al-Mughni", which I consider an important scientific wealth.

This was likely due to the fact that its owner was a Hanbali when he first studied Fiqh, then he turned to the School of Abu Hanifa and memorised “Al-Hidaayah” and took interest in it.

Many scholars of the School of Thought have benefited from this explanation, such as Al-Zayla’i in his book “At-Tabyeen”, Ibn Al-Hammam, Al-Mulla Khusraw, Ibn Abideen, and others.

name: Sharh Mukhtasar Al-Karkhi - Imam Al-Quduri (Fiqh Hanafi)
description_short:
Al-Qudduri compiled this commentary and mentioned in it the opinions of the imams of the Schools of Thought, with giving evidence and preponderance sometimes, and he would mention the disagreement of other jurists such as Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Sufyan Al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Laila and others.

Al-Quduri mentioned in the introduction to the book that the reason for his writing was the answer of one of his students or others, who reminded him of the need to explain Al-Mukhtasar, due to its importance.

The importance of the book is reflected in:

- That the book explained the most important Hanafi abridgment of his time, and it is Mukhtasar Al-Karkhi.

- The high scientific status of both the author of Al-Mukhtasar Al-Karkhi and the author of Al-Sharh Al-Quduri.

- This book is one of the works that deals with jurisprudence between the Hanafi School and others on the one hand, and between the scholars of the Hanafi school itself on the other hand, with attention to explanation, evidence, and preponderance.

This book was thoroughly accepted by the jurists of the Hanafi School, so they increased their transmission and reliance on it in giving preference and clarifying the opinions of the School on many issues.
searchable_keywords: Sharh Mukhtasar Al-Karkhi - Imam Al-Quduri (Fiqh Hanafi)

name: "He is ALLAH" | Innahu Allah - Sherif Fawzi Sultan
description_short:
He is Allah - Sherif Fawzi Sultan

In such current circumstances and turbulent trials and strife, where the people summon one another to attack this Muslim Ummah as people when eating invite others to share their dish, and disasters and sufferings have multiplied incessantly, not to mention the spread of forbidden acts in the open, such as usury, fornication, bribery, ill-gotten earnings, neglecting prayers, following desires, and drowning in temptation. Here the voices of honest Muslims rise, calling for the necessity of sincere education, and building a generation that can resist temptation with a satisfied soul and a thinking mind.

However, one of those primary and vital solutions is: Knowing Allah Almighty through His Most Beautiful Names and Exalted Attributes, and worshipping Him accordingly.

The first step is the knowledge of Allah; a pure heart and strong faith can only be attainable through Knowledge of Allah by His Names and Attributes. Building a strong effective society can only be attainable by hearts with strong faith; will Allah help us unless we know Him, worship Him, and thank Him?

name: Waahat at-Tafsir (Oasis of Interpretation) - Ahmed At-Taweel
description_short:
In this book, the author has followed the path of scholars of interpretation and covered many aspects of its disciplines, such as presenting the virtues before each Surah and its position with regard to what preceded it, summarising its topics, and explaining its words from the aspects of the readings attributed to its narrators from the famous reciters, with its guidance in Language and grammar.

The author has followed the pattern of interpreters; he begins by explaining the Verse by mentioning the reasons for its revelation, then by referring to other Verses of the Qur’an, then from the Sunnah, then from the interpreters among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and then from the interpreters among the followers, may Allah have mercy on them.

Hadiths and Athars are referenced and authenticated.

Then when he finishes this stage (Tafsir bil-Mathur), he proceeds to Tafsir the words and phrases that need clarification and explanation, using eloquent words and an easy and accessible style so that the reader understands their meaning.

He follows up the Tafsir of the verses with remarks in which he relates the meaning of the verses to the actual life we live every day, without abuse or exaggeration, while deducing beneficial points in education and the line of conduct to be had in society and explaining some of the judgments found in the Qur'anic sentences. 

This work is prefaced by Sheikh AbdALLAH ibn Abdel-Muhsin at-Turki and Sheikh Ghanim ibn Salih as-Sadlan, as well as a group of scholars of Tafsir.

name: Al-Jami’ as-Sahih Li Athar as-Sahabah : 8 volumes, 9052 Athars
description_short:
Al-Jaami’ as-Saheeh Li Athaar as-Sahaabah (The Authentic collection of the Companions’ Traditions) - Mohammed Al-Inani

This is a book in which the authentic and actual statements and traditions of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were collected according to the rulings of the earlier and later hadith scholars. We disregard whatever Hadith deemed weak by them and report every Hadith they ruled as authentic. As for Hadiths on which there is disagreement, I mention in the footnotes that the chain of transmission of a particular Hadith is considered as authentic by so and so, but ruled as weak by another, along with mentioning the source.

I have tried to make this book as wide-ranging as possible; it is comprehensive on the topics of belief, trials, interpretation, acts of worship, transactions, civil status, permissible acts, legal politics, justice, piety, morals, ethics, asceticism, history, virtues, and others.

There are 9052 traditions in this book, listed in 8 volumes of medium size.

The book has collected from 85 sources from the Sunnah books, between original sources and compilations.

It was taken into account to avoid any repetition of texts, providing an appropriate Hadith referencing and documentation with attribution to the original sources by number or page.

We ask Allah Almighty to benefit Muslims in the East and West with this book and accept our good deeds and guide us to the right path.

The origin of this book is an introduction to one of his books, titled “Mughni Dhawil-Afhaam ‘Anil-Kutub al-Katheera fil Ahkaam ‘ala Madhhab Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal.” It is his fundamentalist introduction that he extracted in this book and named it “Qawaa’id Usul al-Fiqh allati Ya’lamu minha Haaluhu.” 

The book establishes and briefly explains the four main foundations of Fiqh: The Book and Sunnah, Consensus (Ijma'), Analogy (Qiyas) and Interpretative Effort (Ijthad).

Beautiful edition, verified from 4 manuscripts.

name: Encyclopaedia of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (Pack of 6 books)
description_short:
This first edition of the “Encyclopaedia of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ” came as a compilation of six sciences of the biography of the Prophet in six volumes, through the abridgement of eight books, which are as follows:

The first volume: On the Science of Evidence: "The Book of Evidence of the Prophethood" by Abu Naim (430H).

The second Volume: On the Science of the Prophet’s Biography: The Book of “The Prophet’s Biography” by Ibn Hisham (218H).

The third volume: On the Science of Characteristics: The book “Ghayat al-Saul fi Khasaa’is ar-Rasoul” by Ibn al-Mulaqqin (804H).

The fourth volume: On the sciences of the Perfect Qualities, and it contains three books, which are:

• The book “the Perfect Qualities of the Prophet ﷺ” by At-Tirmidhi (279H).

• The book “Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the Rights, Values, Morals and the Cure of Contemporary World Problems” by Prof. Dr. Ahmed ibn ‘Uthman Al-Mazeed.

• The book “Zad al-Ma’ad fi Hudye Khayr al-‘Ibad” by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya (751H).

The fifth volume: On the science of the rights of the Prophet ﷺ : The book “Al-Shifa: Defining the Rights of the Chosen One” by Al-Qadi ‘Iyadh (544H).

Volume Six: On the Science of the Noble Prophetic Hadith: The book “Riyad As-Saalihin” by Al-Nawawi (676H).

The author said: My objective in this approach was to bring the reader closer to the life of the Prophet ﷺ so that we all learn the vast knowledge in the Prophet’s biography from the authentic books of the scholars among our righteous predecessors, and follow his example in his belief, worship, transactions and morals to achieve happiness in this world and gain the rewards in the hereafter.

name: Ikhtilaf al-Ulama / Ikhtilaf al-Fuqaha by Imam at-Tabari
description_short:
A rare work, a book of comparative Fiqh from the pen of one of the greatest Imams, the Mufassir Ibn Jarir at-Tabari (310H).

In this book, Abu Jaafar at-Tabari has mentioned the controversial issues between the Mujtahideen (Pl. of Mujtahid, an expert scholar of fiqh (Islamic Jurisprudence), such as the three Imams: Abu Hanifah, Malik and ash-Shafi’i, and he also mentioned the sayings of al-Awza’i and al-Layth and the like. However, he has omitted to mention Imam Ahmed, because he stated that he was a Muhaddith, not a jurist.

He then mentioned the evidence of each opinion in detail. At the end of each issue he favours the most predominant one in his opinion by saying: And what is correct for us is such and such or Abu Jaafar said so and so.

Published for the first time by bringing together all the existing parts at our disposal, this book sets out the different opinions known at the time on certain Fiqh issues.

The Muhaqqiq has taken care to quote additional sources when available, and has also given some linguistic explanations when necessary.

name: Kitab as-Sama' by Ibn Tahir al-Qaysarani (507H)
description_short:
Book by Ibn al-Qaisarani, historian and scholar of Hadith, on the subject of as-Sama', listening. While this may refer to listening to the Qur'an or other permissible things, its meaning has shifted over time to Sufi chanting with or without instruments, and other types of innovative or forbidden acts.

Ibn al-Qaysarani was a Dhahirite in Fiqh, and as such his position on Sama' is not necessarily that shared by his fellow Muhaddiths, including the opinion of the absolute permission of the Duff.

Hadifh ibn Mandah, one of his contemporaries, said of him, "He was one of the Huffadh, endowed with good Aqidah..."

name: The Etiquette of Companionship and Good Behaviour - Al-Sulami (412H)
description_short:
The Etiquette of Companionship and Good Behaviour - Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Salami (412H).

The author discussed in this book a great issue related to the etiquette that both companions and brothers should be endowed with, the etiquette related to a brother’s right over his brother and a friend over his friend in Islam.

The author has perfectly drafted the subject matter in this book and gave it an orderly context. He would mention a particular character and say: Among its etiquette is such and such, then he would provide its evidence from the Qur’an, the transmitted Hadiths, and the traditions of the Companions and the Followers and the successors after them, while also referring to the use of poetry and inspirational anecdotes of wisdom. He would sometimes quote the Hadiths and traditions with their chains of transmission, and then he would move on to discuss the next character. It should be noted that the book was not classified, and all its subtitles are the work of the book’s examiner, and the Hadiths of this book amounted to two hundred and ten.

It is a precious book by a noble-minded author Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Salami, and it has satisfactory traditions on the etiquette of companionship.

Verified and authenticated edition, 100% Harakat.

description_short:
Al-I'lam bi Qawati' al-Islam is a critical jurisprudential treatise by the renowned Shafi'i polymath, Imam Ibn Hajar al-Haytami. In this work, the author meticulously compiles the specific words, actions, and beliefs that legally constitute Kufr (disbelief) and Riddah (apostasy) according to Islamic law. Writing with the precision of a master jurist, al-Haytami seeks to define the boundaries of faith clearly, providing a scholarly warning against the pitfalls that can lead a person out of the fold of Islam.

This beautiful edition is based on three verified manuscripts, ensuring a highly accurate and reliable text. To facilitate ease of study, the book features 100% Harakat (vocalization) on the entire text, making it accessible for students and scholars alike. It serves as an essential reference for those studying Fiqh (Jurisprudence) and Aqidah (Creed), offering a rigorous academic framework for understanding the gravity of various statements and deeds within the classical legal tradition.

name: Ar-Rad 'ala al-Jahmiyyah - Imam ibn Mandah (395H)
description_short:
This book is a classical text focused on defending the early Sunni creed against the theological views of the Jahmite movement. The author, Imam Ibn Mandah (d. 395 AH), was a well-known Hadith scholar from Isfahan who traveled extensively to collect chains of transmission. His primary goal in this work is to clarify traditional Islamic beliefs using textual evidence, making it a direct reference for students studying how early scholars verified the attributes of Allah through reported narrations rather than speculative theology.

The text is organized by topic, with each chapter addressing specific claims made by early rationalist groups. Ibn Mandah compiles direct narrations from the Companions and the following generation to support core beliefs, such as the reality of the divine attributes, the uncreated nature of the Quran, and the belief that believers will see their Lord in the afterlife. By presenting these early reports plainly, the book provides a clear, text-based framework that avoids complex philosophical arguments.

name: Muqaddimah al-Jarh wa at-Ta'dil - Imam Ibn Abi Hatim ar-Razi (327H)
description_short:
The foundational introduction to the monumental encyclopedia of hadith narrator criticism composed by Imam Ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi (d. 327 AH), one of the most eminent scholars of his era, heir to the learning of his father Abu Hatim and of Imam Abu Zur'ah al-Razi. It is in reality a standalone work that lays the methodological foundations of the science of al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil: beginning with the place of the prophetic Sunnah and its relationship to the Quran, then presenting the successive generations of transmitters from the Companions through the Tabi'in and their followers, with concise biographical entries for the most prominent in each generation.

The author details the technical terminology for classifying narrators, defining the criteria of reliability (thiqah) and weakness (da'if), and devotes sections to the earliest great critics of the Sunnah — Malik ibn Anas, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ahmad ibn Hanbal — illustrating their rigor and precision. Beyond its foundational scholarship, the accounts it contains of the early scholars' devotion to travel, study, and memorization make it a reading that stirs ambition and motivates the student to persevere on his path.

This edition has been established and annotated by Abu Hammam Muhammad bin Ali al-Sawma'i al-Baydani based on two original manuscripts, incorporating the historical marginal notes of scholar Al-Mu'allimi al-Yamani.

name: Al-Jami' li Masa-il al-Mudawwanah - Ibn Yunus As-Siqilli (451H)
description_short:
This book, written by Imam and jurist Abu Bakr Muhammad Ibn Abdullah at-Tamimi as-Siqilli (died 451 AH), is considered one of the best books dealing with Al-Mudawwana (Al-Mudawwana is a compendium of the legal opinions of the school of Madinah as stated by Imam Malik). He has abridged it in a wonderful way, without interrupting with its issues, explained it in a full and comprehensive manner, collecting its scattered topics, citing the evidence, clarifying and facilitating the ambiguous words, interpreting its issues, and separating the similar ones so that they do not confuse each other.

The Imam relied on the most important sources of Maliki jurisprudence, such as Ibn al-Qasim, Ibn al-Mawaz, Ibn al-Atabi, Ibn Wahb, Ibn Habib, al-Abhari, Ibn al-Qassar, Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad, Abu Ishaq Ibn Sha’ban and Abu Bakr Ibn al-Labbad. Sometimes he used statements such as: more than one of Baghdad scholars have said, some of our companions have stated, and statements from most of the prominent Maliki jurists from those who were before him.

The importance of this book is great; it was the main authoritative book of the Malikis in the old days. Rather, it was called the Mushaf of the Madhhab, and that is to compare it to the Noble Qur’an in which everything is clarified, and that whoever had this book is in no need of others.

People have studied the book from east and west, and transmitted from it. You can hardly find a Maliki book of jurisprudence, hadith or interpretation without it being quoted from Ibn Yunus, and this alone is sufficient to prove the value of the book, in addition to the fact that some used to memorise it by heart, and answer the issues from it.

name: Lawami' al-Durar fi Hatk Astar al-Mukhtasar - al-Majlisi ash-Shinqiti
description_short:
Lawāmiʻ al-durar fī hatk astār al-Mukhtaṣar - Muḥammad al-Majlisi ash-Shinqiṭi

This book, written by the great scholar Muhammad Ibn Muhammad Salem Al-Majlisi Ash-Shinqiti Al-Maliki (1206-1302 AH), is considered the largest and most comprehensive explanation of Mukhtasar of Sheikh Khalil in terms of its size and on issues of jurisprudence and its branches, and it is one of the most extensive books written in the doctrine of Imam Malik.

The book is also distinguished by its length, scrutinising, abundance of quotations, and a multiplicity of references, so that its author wanted it to be: “one that dispenses with all books and no one else can dispense with it.”

Therefore, the author makes mention of every little detail, and refers to the various branches and different sayings from everything related to the topic, then unleashes his imagination, comparing, weighing, and criticising with insight. He always discusses issues raised by the scholars who preceded him and expresses his opinion in many places, deducing, modifying and redressing. Despite his piety and proven character, his scientific personality was always present in what he wrote, which is a rare thing in the scholars of his time.

In short, this book is one of the most comprehensive explanations of Mukhtasar of Sheikh Khalil, and the most complete on issues of jurisprudence. In it the author has tackled all the issues that Khalil referred to in Mukhtasar, explicitly or implicitly, with elaborate editing of its texts, so the style appears easy and smooth. The book is so detailed, authentic, and clear that it dispenses with all other books of jurisprudence of its time, and no one else can do without it.

name: Ijabah ad-Du'a (Answering prayers) - Dr 'Ali al-'Imran
description_short:
Answering prayers - Ali al-Imran

This is a brief treatise in which the author has collected the places, times, and conditions in which supplications are answered, from what is mentioned in the honourable Sunnah of the Prophet, peace and blessing of Allah be upon him.

Any statement that a particular supplication is answered in certain place or time should be based on the Shari’ah texts (Qur’an and Sunnah), so it is not right to invent places and conditions that are not mentioned in the texts of the Shari’ah, let alone for those places and conditions where it is forbidden to supplicate, such as graves and shrines, and innovated supplications and Awraad (saying certain prayers daily) and innovated acts of worship.

In his choices, the author has opted only for the authentic Mutawatir (mass transmitted) narrations, keeping away from any weak ones.

100% Harakat, beautiful layout.

name: 'Asr at-Taabi'in by Abdul-Mun’im Al-Hashimi
description_short:
A narrative history of the Tabi'in generation — those who received the tradition directly from the Companions and carried it forward — covering a period that saw the founding of Islamic sciences and the crystallization of the major jurisprudential schools. Al-Hashimi presents the events, figures, and religious, intellectual, and political life of this pivotal era in a clear, engaging style that combines historical substance with readable prose. The book forms the second part of a two-volume series alongside his 'Asr al-Sahaba, together covering the first two Islamic centuries.

It introduces the major Tabi'in figures and their role in transmitting hadith, fiqh, and tafsir, highlighting the living connection between this generation and the foundations laid by the Companions. This is narrative history rather than specialized academic research — well suited for the beginning student or general reader seeking a coherent and accessible account of this golden era.

name: 'Asr as-Sahabah by Abdul-Mun’im Al-Hashimi
description_short:
This volume provides a narrative history of the Sahaba generation, tracing the foundational decades of the Islamic state from the passing of the Prophet until the end of the Righteous Caliphate. Al-Hashimi reconstructs the pivotal political events and internal trials of this era through a collection of documented biographies of many honorable Companions. The text specifically highlights the lives of the four Caliphs, the appointed leaders of the Prophet, and distinct groups within the first generation, including Al-Abadilah Al-Arba'ah (the four Abdullahs), Al-Bakka'un (those who wept when they lacked the means to join the Prophetic expeditions), the early Muslim slaves, and the seven martyrs.

Written in a fluid, non-technical prose style, each biography portrays their great historic situations and pivotal life events, glorified by their merits and traditional virtues. The work serves as an introductory survey of their collective role in preserving the Quran and transmitting the nascent sciences of Islam, focusing on historical storytelling rather than dense academic debate. It functions as the essential first part of the author’s historical series, pairing directly with his subsequent volume, Asr al-Tabi'in, to provide a highly readable and coherent sequential timeline of the first two Hijri centuries.

name: A'lam as-Salafiyyin (1000 biographies, 3 volumes) - Merkez as-Salaf
description_short:
Encyclopaedia of eminent Salafi scholars in Eleven Centuries from 300 to 1400 AH

An encyclopaedia that includes biographies of those attributed to the methodology of the ancestor or contributed to its defence

The idea of ​​the encyclopaedia came to highlight these masters, preserve their right and value, and testify about Allah’s Mercy of His Prophet’s nation that He did not deprive it from those who uphold the Sunnah of His Prophet and the preserve the traditions of this nation’s ancestors.

The encyclopaedia did not address the biographies of the first three centuries, due to the predominance of the Salafi approach, the supremacy of its scholars and their disciples in the Islamic world. The choice of the fourth century coincided with the spread of heretic doctrines and their large number of followers.

There is reference to the important compilations of the scholars’ biographies from the fourth century until the fourteenth century, and a deep study of these works in order to extract all evidence on the integrity of the scholar’s approach in line with established methodological regulations.

The encyclopaedia contains biographies of a thousand of eminent scholars, compiled in three volumes.

In the appendix, there are biographies of the emirs who supported the doctrine of the rightly guided ancestors, as for those of them who were distinguished as knowledgeable, they were included in the principal content of the encyclopaedia.

The work took five years. Salaf Center and its management people had the leading role in producing this book in terms of its idea and methodology, review and rectification, adjudication and financing.

name: Al-Matalib al-Mufidah fi Masa-il al-'Aqidah - Tariq ibn Said al-Qahtani
description_short:
Designed specifically for the Student of Knowledge (Talib al-Ilm), this work functions as a comprehensive roadmap for navigating the foundational pillars of Islamic belief. It breaks down complex theological concepts into a structured, pedagogical format that simplifies the understanding of Tawhid (Monotheism), its categories, and its practical implications in the life of a believer. The methodology is rooted in the "Question and Answer" style, a time-honored teaching tool that ensures the reader can quickly grasp specific points of creed while seeing how they are supported by direct evidence from the Quran and the Prophetic Sunnah.

The significance of this primer lies in its strict adherence to the methodology of the Pious Predecessors (Salaf al-Salih), providing a clear defense against common misconceptions and deviant ideologies. By focusing on clarity and conciseness, the author ensures that the first paragraph of each section serves as a complete mental summary, making it an ideal companion for introductory circles and classroom settings. It effectively serves as a bridge for the beginner, transitioning them from a general understanding of faith to a grounded, evidence-based conviction that is necessary for any serious study of Islamic sciences.

Al-Ijaz fi Qiraa’at Al-A’immah as-Sab’ah bil-Iraq wa-Sham wal-Hijaz, by Imam Sabt Al-Khayyat.

This book was written by the Sheikh of Iraq, who mastered the Quranic readings in his time, Imam Sibt Al-Khayyat (d. 541 AH).

Sibt Al-Khayyat has several books on Qur’an recitations, which Imam Ibn Al-Jazari (d. 833 AH) relied on as a documented basis in authoring his book “an-Nashr fil Qira’at Al-‘Ashr”, including this book “Al-Ijaz”. This book was deemed lost, as there was no known written copy of it, until Allah Almighty, by His Grace, has helped me find a valuable copy, dating back to the year 530 AH, which means that it was written in the life of the author.

The Muhaqqiq, Shaykh Ayman Suwayd said: "It is a complete copy, All Praise to Allah. I have thoroughly analysed it and studied it in the manner followed in university postgraduate studies. I have made it accessible to the students of the Holy Qur’an and its sciences. May Allah benefit everyone who received it with a sound heart."

name: At-Tafwid fi as-Sifat al-Ilahiyyah - Muhammad ar-Rabah
description_short:
This detailed research deals with Tafwidh in names and attributes. Indeed, for the Asharis, the Hanbalis / Atharis are part of Ahl as-Sunnah because they practice Tafwidh, i.e. they accept the attribute, without giving a meaning to it, a meaning they leave to Allah. For Ibn Taymiyya to say this of the Salafs is an injustice, for they affirmed the known meaning of the attributes without evading, except for the Kayf - the how.

Some statements of the Salafs or some Hanbalis refer to a Tafwidh of the meaning, others to a Tafwidh of the how. This research tends to verify, with evidence, whether or not the Salafs did Tawfidh, and if so how. And what about the Tafwidh of the meaning of the attributes which authenticates the word, but leaves out its explanation, even linguistically?

name: Tadwin as-Sunnah an-Nabawiyyah - Sayyid Abd al-Majid al-Ghuri
description_short:
The early Muslims paid great attention to recording everything that was reported from the Prophet, peace and blessing be upon him, whether verbal, practical or tacit approval, because it is the second source of Islamic legislation. The process of that recording passed through several stages of codification, then writing, classification, and authorship, after it was limited only to word of mouth and narration. Then, with the passage of time, the types of Hadith and Sunnah books branched out between Sahih, Sunan, Muwattas, compilations, chains of narrators, Mustadraks and extracts, which contain thousands of prophetic Ahadiths and honorable narrations on various topics of religion and its law.

This book deals with a brief inductive study of the history of writing the Sunnah and its codification in the first centuries, and then of the development of classification and writing it through the Hijri centuries, with a brief definition of the famous scholars of this scientific movement, as well as the most important books they wrote in those centuries.

The book is written in a simplified and easy manner, without delving into controversial issues that are useless.

A real encyclopaedia of books and scholars of Hadith through the centuries, with the Harakats as part of it.

name: Al-Madkhal ila Dirasah 'Ilm as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah
description_short:
Al-Madkhal is a specialized methodological manual that serves as a gateway for students and researchers into the "Science of Seerah." Rather than simply narrating events, Ahmed bin Ghanim al-Asadi focuses on the epistemology and historiography of the Prophet's ﷺ life. The book provides a rigorous framework for how the Seerah was recorded, the various schools of thought (such as the schools of Madinah and Makkah), and the criteria used by classical scholars to verify historical reports.

The author categorizes the sources of Seerah into primary tiers—the Qur'an, authentic Hadith, and early poetry—and explains the nuance between the methodology of the Muhaddithin (Hadith scholars) and the Akhbariyyin (Historians). It is an essential read for those who value academic depth and wish to understand the structural integrity of the Prophetic heritage. This work helps the reader distinguish between authentic historical milestones and later interpolations, ensuring that the study of the Prophet's ﷺ life remains rooted in the highest standards of intellectual honor and precision.

name: Qawa'id fi A'mal al-Qulub - Rules concerning acts of the heart
description_short:
While many Islamic texts focus strictly on the physical actions of worship, this brilliant contemporary book shifts the focus inward, mapping out the systematic laws that govern the human heart. It presents a series of foundational rules (Qawa'id) to help the reader understand, cultivate, and rectify internal acts of devotion - such as sincerity (Ikhlas), absolute trust (Tawakkul), fear (Khawf), hope (Raja), and divine love (Mahabbah). It treats the spiritual heart not as an unpredictable emotional center, but as an engine of faith that operates on clear, textually proven guidelines.

What makes this work uniquely valuable is how it bridges the gap between high-level theology and practical everyday discipline. Dr. Aqeel al-Shammari takes the complex spiritual insights of classical giants like Ibn al-Qayyim and Ibn Taymiyyah and distills them into clear, actionable axioms. Written with analytical precision yet deeply moving, each rule is backed by Quranic evidence and Prophetic guidance, showing you how to diagnose spiritual ailments, protect your worship from hidden insincerity, and maintain a sound heart (Qalb Salim) in a world full of ideological and material distractions.

name: Majmu’ al-Amir (Mukhtasar al-Amir) - Fiqh Maliki
description_short:
Majmou’ Al-Ameer wa Sharhih, by Muhammad Al-Ameer Al-Maliki

This book “Majmoo’ al-Amir” and it is also called “Mukhtasar al-Amir” by Sheikh Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmed ibn Abdul Qadir al-Sibnawi al-Maliki al-Azhari, known as the Amir (1154 AH - 1742 AD / 1232 AH - 1817 AD) may Allah Almighty have mercy on him. He adopted the approach of Sheikh Khalil in his “Mukhtasar”, but he relied on the most preferred opinions in the School of Thought, in contrast to those mentioned by Sheikh Khalil. He added jurisprudential branches that were not mentioned in Khalil’s “Mukhtasar”, and called his: “Al Majmoo’” because it covers the content of several books in a fluent and stylish interpretation.

He was so famous among his contemporaries to the extent that his sheikh, Sheikh Ali Al-Adawi Al-Sa’idi, used to refer to him.

100% Harakat, with lots of useful annotations, prefaced by Shaykh Ahmad Taha Rayan.

name: Fath ar-Rahman bi kashf ma yaltabisu fil Qur’an - Zakariya Al-Ansari
description_short:
Fath al-Rahman is a specialized masterpiece in the genre of Mutashabih al-Lafz—the science of explaining verses in the Qur'an that appear nearly identical in wording but contain subtle variations. Authored by the legendary Sheikh al-Islam Zakariya al-Ansari (d. 926 AH), this work is an exercise in linguistic and theological precision. It addresses the "why" behind a change in word order, the addition of a letter, or the substitution of a synonym across different Surahs, revealing the underlying wisdom and miraculous nature (I'jaz) of the Divine speech.

The text is characterized by its conciseness and its reliance on the insights of earlier masters like al-Kirmani and al-Sakhawi, yet it bears the distinct analytical mark of al-Ansari’s jurisprudential and linguistic mastery. It is an indispensable tool for students of Tafsir and those who have memorized the Qur'an, as it aids in resolving common points of confusion during recitation while deepening the reader's appreciation for the rhythmic and semantic perfection of the text.

Very nice, verified and annotated Saudi edition.

name: Al-'Ilal by Imam Daraqutni
description_short:
Al-'Ilal al-warida fi al-ahadith an-nabawiyyah: by Imam Ad-Daraqutni

Ad-Daraqutni’s book “Al-Ilal” is considered to be one of the most comprehensive and best books on Al-Ilal (hidden defects of Ahadith).

Imam Ad-Dhahabi says: “If you want to know the ingenuity of this distinguished imam, then read his book Al-Ilal to your amazement and high admiration.”

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir says: “Ad-Daraqutni’s book “Al-Ilal” comprises all of what we have mentioned, and it is one of the best and finest books that have been written on this field. It is unprecedented as many have failed to produce a book like it; so may Allah have mercy on him and honour his resting place.”

Imam As-Sakhawi said: “It is a comprehensive book.”

The book “Al-Ilal” includes the defective Ahadith, classified as Marfu’ (Attributed to the Messenger of Allah and narrated by a Companion), Mursal (A Tabiyee narrating directly from the Messenger of Allah leaving a Sahabi from the chain)), Mawquf (stopped: a narration from a companion only), Maqtu’ (Severed: cannot be traced back to the Prophet peace be upon him, but to one of his companions, who explained it in their own words) and others; and it also covers the opinions of Imam ad-Daraqutni on some Hadith narrators.

The book editor has allocated a special index to it at the end of each volume.

Excellent edition verified from 8 manuscripts and annotated.

name: Jami' as-Sahihayn - Dr Walid Abderrahman al-Hamdan (harakat)
description_short:
The book “Jaami’ as-Saheehayn” was distinguished by its combination of the two authentic Hadith books of Al-Bukhari and Muslim in one abridged volume, containing a total of 2,970 hadiths in 984 pages. It included most of their attributed Hadiths, with the deletion of the repeated ones. The Hadith testimonies were summarised, with the deletion of their chains of transmission, keeping only the comprehensive words, unless there is more benefit in others.

The author has arranged the Hadiths in terms of the abrogating and abrogated, the absolute and the restricted, the general over the specific, the one with the order denoting the obligation, and the one that denotes the prohibition, and additions in the narrations, so as nothing in them can be missed as much as possible.

He has adopted the opinion of the majority in this compilation. Any agreed upon opinion was highlighted with the sign (خ م).

This book is a bestseller among students because of its format and methodology.

Beautiful Saudi edition 100% Harakat.

name: Al-Muqtafi li Tarikh Abi Shama - 'Alam ad-Din al-Barzali (739H)
description_short:
Al-Muqtafi’ li Tarikh Abi Shaamah, by Àlam-ad-Din al-Qàssim Ibn Muhàmmad Ibn Yússuf al-Birzalí 

This book was written by Alam Ad-Din Al-Birzali (665-739 AH). His full name is Alam Ad-Din Al-Qassim Ibn Muhammad Iin Yusuf Ibn Zaki Ad-Din Muhammad Ibn Yusuf Ibn Abi Yaddas Al-Birzali Al-Ishbili Ash-Shafi’i. He is the Imam, ash-Sheikh, Al-Hafiz, and the historian. It is a chronicle of events during the life of its author, between 665 and 721 AH, in which he reports births, deaths and significant events, year by year, month by month, according to the chronology. A dive into the 7th and 8th Hegira centuries and a real treasure for historians and biographers.

This valuable historical book has been edited and commented upon by the following renowned Muhaqqiqs: Dr. Bashar Awad Maarouf and Dr. Abdul Rahman Al-Othaimeen and Dr. Turki Ibn Fahd Al Saud.

Beautiful edition in 6 volumes, with an introduction about the author and the theme of the book, precise and useful annotations on the personalities and places quoted and an alphabetical research index. The text is published with most of the Harakats.

name: 'Urubah al-'Ulama al-Mansubin ila Buldan al-A'jamiyah - Naji Ma'ruf
description_short:
Among the generalities often admitted and spread in the community, is the fact that a large part of the scholars of Islam were of non-Arab origin (Khurasan in particular). It is a frequently conveyed image that among the greatest Imams of Hadith or Fiqh of the Ummah, their greatest defenders were sometimes "foreigners", i.e. non-Arab.

Although their origin does not change their merit or deed, the historian and biographer Dr Naji Ma'ruf, with his knowledge, has written this book to set the record straight on many of the Ulema who, although from non-Arabic lands, were in fact of Arab origin.

The Arabness of Scholars from Foreign (non-Arab) Countries is a unique work, which aims to be accurate about the geographical expansion of the Ummah and the biographies of the Ulema, explaining the reasons for the error in attributing nationality to some of them and the reasons for the presence of Arab families in those countries. This book is also an interesting collection of biographies.

Beautiful edition in 2 volumes, prepared and annotated by the great Muhaqqiq and historian Bashar Ma'ruf.

name: Operation 101 - Jihad Al-Turbani
description_short:
The novel "Operation 101" written by Jihad Al-Turbani marks the 5th and final book in the series.

A new adventure with our hero Nidal, the young historical researcher, and various historical stories in a beautiful and simple style, and interesting events about Operation 101 that Nidal and his companions will carry out against the new Hashashin.

Who are the new junkies, what is their relationship to the Vandal treasure, and what are the details of Operation 101? This is what we will know in the novel.

The historical stories in the novel are diverse, some of them are about the Hashshashin organization and their history, some are about Nazism, the Persians and the Romans, and some are from the biography, including stories I have not heard of before.

Some of these stories are also about the history of beloved Iraq, its ancient civilization and its role in building human civilization.

Also during our trip, the writer accompanies us with the story of Al-Muthanna bin Al-Harithah Al-Shaibani, one of the greatest Muslim leaders, and tells us the story of his conversion to Islam and his eternal battles with the Persians, which were a wonderful example of courage and strength.

Along with the story of Al-Muthanna bin Al-Harithah, the writer also tells us some of the biography of Saifullah Al-Masloul, Khaled bin Al-Walid, may God be pleased with him, and tells us about his battles with the Persians and Romans and the genius plans he used in his battles against them...

name: Talkhis al-Habir (at-Tamayyiz) by Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani - 7 volumes
description_short:
Al-Talkhis al-Habir fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Rafi'i al-Kabir (popularly known as Talkhis al-Habir, and classically titled Al-Talkhis al-Habir fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Sharh al-Kabir) by the supreme Hadith master of the late classical period, Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (d. 852 AH), is the definitive reference manual in the science of legal Hadith extraction (takhrij ahadith al-ahkam). Composed to critically examine, source, and verify all prophetic narrations and traditions cited by Imam al-Rafi'i (d. 623 AH) in Al-Sharh al-Kabir, the work serves as an indispensable bridge between Hadith authentication and comparative Islamic jurisprudence.

Ibn Hajar formulated this monumental work by condensing and thoroughly refining Al-Badr al-Munir, the massive multi-volume compendium by his master Ibn al-Mulaqqin. He integrated critical observations and additions from leading traditionists—including Ibn Kathir, al-Zarkashi, and Imam al-Nawawi—while enriching the text with his own unrivaled mastery of narrator criticism (al-jarh wa al-ta'dil), tracing hidden paths of transmission (turuq), uncovering subtle chain defects ('ilal), and delivering decisive verdicts on hadith authenticity.

Although organized according to a foundational Shafi'i legal text, Al-Talkhis al-Habir serves as an exhaustive, universally relied-upon encyclopedia of legal proofs across all schools of Islamic law. It remains a standard desk reference for Hadith scholars, muftis, professors of comparative law, and advanced researchers.

The Dar Adwae As-Salaf edition of Talkhis al-Habir is considered the definitive standard due to its rigorous reconstruction from three primary manuscripts and cross-referencing with Al-Badr al-Munir, which corrected errors found in previous Indian, Cairo, and Cordoba prints. This edition is characterized by superior manuscript fidelity, in-depth analytical footnotes addressing 'Ilal, and a comprehensive seventh volume of indices, making it the most precise and functional resource for Hadith verification.

name: Kashf al-Asrar wa Hatak al-Astar - Abu Bakr al-Baqlani (403H)
description_short:
Kashf al-Asrar wa Hatk al-Astar is a pivotal polemical work authored by the master theologian and jurist Al-Qadi Abu Bakr al-Baqillani (d. 403 AH). Written during a period of intense theological and political friction, this book is a rigorous refutation of the Batiniyyah and various esoteric sects of his time. Al-Baqillani, acting as a premier defender of Sunni orthodoxy, employs his formidable dialectic skills to expose the hidden doctrines and internal inconsistencies he perceived within these groups.

The work is not merely a historical critique but a masterclass in classical Kalam (speculative theology). It provides a granular analysis of the intellectual challenges facing the Ummah in the early 5th century AH, focusing on the preservation of the clear, outward meaning of the Sharia against esoteric interpretations. For researchers of Islamic history, theology, and the evolution of sectarian thought, this volume remains an essential primary source that demonstrates the intellectual rigor and defensive maneuvers of the early Ash'ari and Maliki traditions.

Verified from an original manuscript, this edition opens with an extensive scholarly introduction detailing the history and doctrines of the Batiniyyah sect alongside a comprehensive biography of Qadi al-Baqillani. It is a finely produced volume featuring partial vowelization (harakat) and insightful annotations that provide essential context for modern readers.

name: Muqarrarat Barnamij Muhimmat al-'Ilm - Salih al-'Usaymi
description_short:
Structured by one of the most respected scholars of our time, Sheikh Salih al-'Usaymi, this program consists of a rigorous selection of fundamental manuals covering fifteen different Islamic sciences, such as Creed, Hadith, Fiqh, and Arabic Grammar. This monumental two-volume set gathers all 27 essential Matn (foundational texts) of the complete curriculum into a single reference spanning over 1,800 pages.

The edition is specifically designed for active study and annotation. The unique layout features the primary text on the left-hand page, while the right-hand page consists of a blank lined sheet. This allows the Student of Knowledge (Talib al-Ilm) to transcribe personal notes and benefits directly alongside the source material while following the Sheikh's lectures.

While some of the Matn include Harakats (vowelization) to ensure accurate recitation, others are presented without them to encourage linguistic independence and mastery of the Arabic language. This setup transforms the work into a personalized educational archive, making it the premier choice for those committed to a disciplined path of learning.

name: Fath al-Mawla an-Nasir bi Sharh al-Jami' as-Saghir li Suyuti (6 vol.)
description_short:
Fath al-Mawla al-Nasir is a preeminent and expansive commentary on Imam al-Suyuti’s famous collection, al-Jami' al-Saghir. Authored by the scholar Al-Qalqashandi, who passed away in 922 H, this work transforms the original alphabetical collection of Hadith into a rich theological and legal landscape. It provides a disciplined and comprehensive investigation into the Prophetic traditions, supporting every explanation with a wealth of evidence from the Quran, the Sunnah, and the authoritative sayings of the early generations and the great masters of jurisprudence.

The work is celebrated for its structural clarity and its honorable commitment to preserving the integrity of the Shafi'i tradition while providing a panoramic view of the broader Islamic sciences. By expanding on the concise reports found in the Jami', Al-Qalqashandi creates a bridge between the brevity of the source text and the depth of classical scholarship. It is an essential reference for any researcher seeking a rigorous and verified understanding of the Sunnah, offering a clear and transparent path to the logical and spiritual roots of the Prophetic mission.

This high-quality edition is established from a complete and unique manuscript, representing the most exhaustive treatment of this collection published for the first time. It features precise annotations concerning text authenticity and legal nuances, expertly verified to ensure absolute academic integrity for the modern researcher.

name: Naqd Uthman ad-Darimi ala al-Marisi al-Jahmi + Ar-Rad ala al-Jahmiyyah
description_short:
This two-volume set contains Imam Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi's two separate yet complementary works against the theological deviations of the Jahmiyyah sect. The first work, "Naqd 'ala al-Miriisi al-Jahmi," specifically targets Bishr al-Miriisi's rationalist interpretations, while the second, "al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyyah," provides a broader refutation of Jahmi theology. Together, these texts represent one of the most comprehensive early defenses of orthodox Sunni positions on divine attributes and the nature of the Quran against speculative theology.

This superb edition, verified and annotated by Adil ibn Abdullah Aal Hamdan, ensures textual authenticity while providing hadith authentication and source references, making these foundational texts accessible to contemporary students of Islamic creed.

name: Sharh Nuzhatu-Nadhar by Imam ibn Hajar (harakat) - Tariq 'Awd Allah
description_short:
This foundational work on hadith terminology is Ibn Hajar's detailed commentary on his own concise manual "Nukhbat al-Fikr fi Mustalah Ahl al-Athar". The original manual was an innovative summary of Ibn al-Salah's introduction to hadith science, created at the request of colleagues who wanted the essential points condensed.

Ibn Hajar explains that after producing the concise version, he was asked to provide a detailed commentary that would "unlock its secrets, open its treasures, and clarify what might be unclear to beginners." He responded by creating this comprehensive explanation, noting that "the author of a house knows best what is in it."

The work represents Ibn Hajar's unique methodological approach to hadith science, combining systematic organization with practical application. He deliberately chose an expanded format, integrating explanations directly within the text for maximum clarity and accessibility.

This edition features detailed verification and commentary by Sheikh Abu Mu'adh Tariq 'Awd Allah, with complete harakat and full authentication.

name: Al-Muqni' fi al-Fiqh - Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdissi (Hanbali Fiqh)
description_short:
Al-Muqniʿ is one of the cornerstone intermediate-level manuals in Ḥanbalī fiqh, authored by al-Muwaffaq Ibn Qudāmah (d. 620H), one of the most authoritative scholars of the school. It presents the relied-upon positions of the Ḥanbalī madhhab without evidences, making it suitable for memorization and structured study. The book was designed as part of a progression in Ibn Qudāmah’s pedagogical method, sitting between his ʿUmdah and al-Mughni.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Qudamah said in the introduction to his book “Al-Muqni’”: "This is a book on jurisprudence on the doctrine of Imam Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal Al-Shaybani, may Allah be pleased with him. I worked hard to compile it and arrange it, to make it brief and approximate, in moderation between the short and the long style. I have collected most of the rulings without mentioning their evidence and justification, in order to increase its knowledge, reduce its size, and facilitate its memorization and understanding; it will be conclusive for those who memorise it and useful for its analyser. We turn to Almighty Allah to help us achieve our hope, correct our words and deeds, and make our striving close to Him, and beneficial in His Mercy."

This work is widely used in traditional Ḥanbalī curricula and has been the subject of countless commentaries and super-commentaries. Its clarity, balance, and structure make it ideal for students aiming to master the madhhab's core positions before moving to more advanced usul-based discussions.

name: Muntaha ar-Raghbah fi Halli Alfadh an-Nukhbah - Imam al-Kharashi
description_short:
A valuable book in the Sciences of Hadith, of great benefit, meaningful, in which Al-Kharashi, may Allah mercy on him, has followed the method of objective explanation, which depends on tackling some issues in the annotated book that the author sees as needing an explanation, comment, advice, etc.

It is one of the most comprehensive explanations of the book “Nuzhat an-Nadhar” by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him, because Al-Kharashi has included in his explanation useful footnotes on “Nuzhat an-Nadhar”.

These footnotes are by Ibn Qutlubugha al-Hanafi, al-Biqa’i, Ali al-Ajhuri, and Ibrahim al-Laqqani. He has also included useful information from annotations of al-Kamal Ibn Abi Sharif, al-Yawaaqit and “Ad-Durar” by al-Minawi, and others.

Al-Kharashi’s explanation has combined the most significant explanations of the book “Nuzhat an-Nadhar” discussing it, supporting and opposing some of it, and explaining what was hidden from it, with a summary, and at the same time, offering advice about certain issues and benefits, so the students can find it in one book.

This explanation was like a completion to what al-Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar neglected in explaining “Nukhbat al-Fikr” and a clarification to what he summarised in “Nuzhat an-Nadhar.”

name: Baghdad - Shaykh Ali al-Tantawi
description_short:
Ali At-Tantawi, a master among writers and jurists, provides us with inventive glimpses into depicting Baghdad, its history and civilization, and tells us about some of his visits and observations there in this book. It shows the geography of Iraq, Baghdad, its neighbourhoods, and its history, King Ghazi, the generosity of the Iraqi people, their manners, arts, and food, the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers, and the cities of Samarra, Kufa, and Basra.

The book combines an interesting narrative style with a wonderful and attractive description, and a lamentation on the condition of Baghdad, mentioning its current political situation. He told us about his love for King Ghazi, an Arab nationalist who tried to support the people against the British mandate, only to end up killed in a planned assassination.

Ali At-Tantawi, a writer and jurist from the Sham, gives us an account, imbued with the spirit and shadows of this worthy city: Baghdad.

name: Qisas min al-Hayah - Shaykh Ali al-Tantawi
description_short:
This book “Stories from Life” was written by Sheikh Ali At-Tantawi and published in 1959. It is a collection of twenty-seven short stories, the majority of which were written in the period between the mid-thirties and mid-forties.

These are stories from life, so named by their author because they were written by life. Does life make up stories?

The majority of the stories in this collection are brief. Except for one that exceeds thirty pages, they barely exceed ten pages in length, and many of them are within the limits of five or six pages. This is true in terms of form, but in terms of content, the majority of them deal with social or ethical issues.

They are true-life stories. The writer is the nation’s mirror and its expression tool, revealing what is hidden in its people’s hearts, and every nation has advantages and disadvantages.

name: As-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah: Knowledge and Duty - Muhammad Al-Tuwaijri
description_short:
A comprehensive study of the Prophetic Biography (al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah), systematically divided by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tuwaijri into two complementary halves: "Knowledge" (al-Ma'rifah) and "Duty" (al-Wajib). The first part covers the thorough knowledge of the Prophet ﷺ: his lineage, birth, character, physical attributes (Shama'il), proofs of prophethood, and the chronological phases of his mission from the Makkan da'wah through the Madinan state to his death. The second part delineates the binding obligations of the believer toward him: sincere belief, submission to his command, supreme love, reverence, strict adherence to his Sunnah (Ittiba'), and propagating his message.

Drawing directly upon explicit Quranic verses and verified authentic hadiths, the work deliberately bypasses unverified historical lore to bind every biographical milestone to its direct spiritual and practical duty. Structured with clear thematic divisions and accessible prose, it serves as a functional, evidence-based manual of the Sirah—designed for structured family reading, classroom halaqat, and students of knowledge seeking both knowledge of the Messenger ﷺ and adherence to his way.

name: Mawsu'ah al-Asmaa al-Husnaa - Muhammad Al-Tuwaijri (≈ 5000 pages)
description_short:
An expansive four-volume encyclopedia spanning nearly four thousand pages—averaging approximately 1,000 pages per volume—dedicated to the Beautiful Names of Allah established in the Quran and authentic Sunnah. Shaykh Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tuwaijri examines each divine Name through four structured angles: its linguistic and legal meaning, its observable manifestations throughout creation and the universe, how to supplicate and praise Allah through it, and the specific devotions of the heart and limbs it demands from the believer. The work represents the structured culmination of 424 lectures delivered by the author before being systematically compiled.

The enduring value of this work lies in transforming doctrinal knowledge into living worship—guiding the reader from understanding the Name to actively realizing true servitude ('Ubudiyyah) through it. Contemplating divine majesty inspires reverent awe and humility, meditating on divine mercy awakens hope and gratitude, and living with the conscious realization of divine vigilance directs daily conduct toward uprightness. An authoritative reference for Tullab al-'Ilm and an essential guide for the Muslim household, uniting sound creed with immediate devotional practice.

description_short:
Bawsalat Al-Muslih (The Reformer's Compass), by Ahmed Al-Sayed

Each period of time has its major questions that clarify its most important problems, reveal its most prominent challenges, and point to the priorities to which energies are directed, times are spent, efforts are expended, and lives are exhausted.

If we want to express one question that summarises the major problems that reformers should be preoccupied with at this stage, we will find it very difficult to do so. Because this exceptional, transitional stage came after a sharp decline in the gains of many Islamic projects, which led to the ranks losing their cohesion, and the emergence of a state of frustration and despair. It generated crucial questions related to the feasibility of working for Islam, and even went beyond that to the question about the credibility of Islam itself for some of those who were overwhelmed by despair and frustration.

There are also questions related to the validity of the approach and the parameters of the correct path among the many different Islamic trends, in addition to questions of the present fundamental duty and the work priorities, the best methods of reform, the most important projects and fronts, and other types of questions.

The book comes with a large schema attached, that resume all the process of the Reformer's Compass.

The book presents the suspicions as they are usually reported by its people with their assertiveness and reliability in the validity of historical claims or understandings of Quranic texts, before responding to them by refuting the credibility of the historical claim or the discredited or preferred understanding of the Quranic verses. The author has opted for a brief and varied response to the suspicions, while documenting every piece of information from its considered scientific perspectives, without elaborating, making the book as simple as possible to the seeker of knowledge.

I hope that this book will contribute to clarifying the importance of taking care of the scripture studies and biblical archaeology for those interested in the sciences of the Qur’an, especially the science of Tafsir (Qur’an Interpretation), as well as for those interested in the study of Oriental Studies. Indeed, most of the orientalist suspicions are based on deducing oppositions after studying the Jewish and Christian heritage, and discrediting the Qur’an in that aspect, either by approving of that heritage’s content by simply disavowing the Qur’an and those who follow it.

name: Women, between Islam, atheism and Christianity - Dr. Sami 'Amiri
description_short:
Today, a wide debate is taking place in the world on the topic of “women, their position and their rights”; it has indeed developed into a massive conflict between the upholders of the great worldly visions, in presenting the fair doctrinal and legal value system for the female.

This topic is of particular importance in the Arab world, due to the doctrinal conflict prevailing in the region between the Islamic perception and non-Islamic ones that reject the reference to the Qur’anic creed; be it the vision that rejects the Divine Revelation altogether, which is the atheistic vision, or the vision that offers a religious alternative that its people attribute to revelation as well, i.e. Christianity.

In order to clarify the truth in detail, and to respond fairly to the objections, the author in this book presented the position of Islam, atheism, and Christianity towards women and their rights, based on the fundamentals of these textual or universal visions, while responding to both the scientific and popular objections that are repeated in the atheistic and Christian discourses. The purpose of the book is to reveal the messages of Islam, atheism and Christianity to women, away from any free compliment or biassed distortion.

The book also seeks to provide the female callers to Islam with a comprehensive and detailed statement to help them respond to widespread suspicions.

name: At-Tajrid by Imam al-Quduri : Comparative Jurisprudence Encyclopaedia
description_short:
Al-Qoudouri’s book “at-Tajrid” is the largest Islamic encyclopaedia in comparative jurisprudence. It is the first jurisprudential book that gives us a true and integrated picture of the Science of Comparative Jurisprudence (the Science of Disagreement) among Muslims. He collected the evidence of the Hanafis and defended them by all means, and also collected the evidence of the Shafi’is. The book includes jurisprudential texts of the Hanafis and Shafi’is that do not exist now in the books of the two Schools of Thought, despite their abundance.

Al-Quduri exerted all efforts to explain the doctrine of each School in the most important matters in which the difference occurred between them in the branches of jurisprudence, while examining the evidence, and the responses to the evidence of the other. He honestly expresses the spirit of tolerance and peaceful scientific discussion among all the Schools of Jurisprudence that characterize Muslim jurists, and that is evident when Al-Quduri prays for Ash-Shafi’i and his companions, not using violent words in response to them, or sarcastic words while listing their evidence.

An excellent edition verified from 4 manuscripts, and annotated in detail to provide readers with the available sources and references of the evidence and statements quoted by the Imam.

In this book, Ibn Hajar has explained the major sins and what is related to them in terms of judgment, rebuke, promise and warning. He arranged it in the form of an introduction and two Chapters. In the conclusion, Ibn Hajar mentioned the virtues of repentance. As for its conditions and what is related to it, he mentioned it in the section on testimonies; then he mentioned the hellfire, its characteristics, and the types of deterrents and painful punishment that it contained. At the end he mentioned Paradise, its attributes, and the types of rewards, prosperity, and bliss that it contains.

name: Maqalat al-Islamiyin wa Ikhtilaf al-Musallin - Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari
description_short:
This book is a historical survey and record of all the intellectual sects and trends witnessed in the Islamic world from the death of the Prophet of Islam, Muhammad, may Allah's Peace and Blessing be upon him, until the beginning of the Third Century AH. It is a collection of articles about Islamic sects' ideologies. It originally consisted of three books: “Al-Maqaalaat”, “Daqeeq al-Kalaam”, and “Al-Asma’ was-Sifaat”. Al-Ashari combined these three books in one book, which included all their different opinions.

In the First Section, he tackled Jaleel al-Kalaam (concerning Divinity and the Divine attributes, etc.) and the doctrines of the different sects with regard to it: the Shiites, the Kharijites, the Murjiah, the Mu’tazila, the scholars of Hadith and Ahlu as-Sunnah. Each sect includes many groups, although he had started the book by dividing Muslims into ten categories: Shiites, Kharijites, Murji’ites, Mu’tazila, Jahmiyyah, Al-Diraria, Husayniyyah, al-Bakriyyah, the masses, Ashaab al-Hadith, al-Kullabiyyah the followers of Abdullah Ibn Kullab al-Qattan. He cited their different opinions in “Jaleel al-Kalam”.

Two-thirds of the Second Section deals with issues related to Daqiq al-Kalaam (Accurate speech: which is related to the science of nature and issues related to the occurrence of the world and its antiquity and the meaning of causation) and the opinions of the various sects about them, especially the Mutazilah. In the last third, he tackled some of what he had discussed in the first section of Jaleel al-Kalaam.

name: The Theory of Time and Place according to Belief of Ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
The Theory of Time and Place according to Belief of Ibn Taymiyyah by Ahmad ‘Issam an-Najjar.

The author said: We collect and present Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah's comprehensive vision regarding the terms “Time” and “Place”, and then we discuss the effects of that vision in his successful defence of the Sunni creed.

We present his legal evidence as well as the philosophical principles upon which Sheikh Al-Islam based his theory, such as his vision of the two types of existence: the conceptual and the external, his vision of the sequence of universal occurrences and the causes, al-qidam an-naw’i (the Major Eternity), and so on.

We also list some of the theories and suspicions of some contemporary opponents such as the Mu’tazilites and the Ash’aris, and respond to them; then we quote the consequences of their theories on doctrinal research. Indeed, the opponents have gone astray in numerous studies, based on their visions that contradicts the concepts of time and place, such as their deviation in the belief in Allah’s Attributes of Al-Uluw (Elevation) and Istiwa’ (Transcendance above the Throne), the Attributes related to Allah’s Will (as-Sifaat al-Ikhtiyaariyah), the Creation of the Universe, and so on.

name: Tuhfat al-Yaqin fi Sifat 'Uluw Allah ala Al-'Aalamin - Ammar Khanfar
description_short:
The issue of the Attribute of Allah’s Transcendence over His Throne (Al-'Ulu) is one of the greatest and most controversial issues of Faith throughout Islamic history. This book is a unique and comprehensive study on all aspects of the legal, linguistic and philosophical Attribute of Allah’s Transcendence.

The author starts by mentioning the evidence from the Quran, the Sunnah and the sayings of the righteous predecessors among the Companions, the Followers, and the early scholars (with Tahqiq and referencing of each quotes).

He then explained the description of Al-Istiwa’ (Elevation and Rise of Allah over His Throne) and its meaning from a linguistic viewpoint.

Then he discussed the opinions and arguments of interpreters of the two Attributes of Al-'Ulu and Al-Istiwa.

Then he explained the doctrine of Tafweedh, the history of its inception and its flaw and corruption.

Then he discussed the interpretation that defines Al-Istiwa as al-Istilaa (to take over) and tackled the issue from a historical perspective and determined the date of the emergence of such interpretation.

He concluded the book with a valuable chapter on the theological arguments that the theologians (Al-Mutakallimah) adhered to in denying the Attribute of Allah’s Transcendence, by discussing and invalidating them.

The book is over 900 pages and is a collection of the arguments, suspicions and points of dispute that revolve around this issue. It is also a rich and huge reference for students and researchers in matters of Aqidah. It is a valuable and interesting book that contains many unique legal foundations and good responses, in addition to many linguistic, literary and historical benefits.

name: Takwin al-Madhhab al-Hanafi, by Dr. Said Bakdash
description_short:
The Hanafi School of Thought with Reflections on the Regulations of its Fatwas:

Saed Bakdash

It is common among many honourable Hanafi jurists and scholars and others that the Hanafi school of thought is composed of the sayings of Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, and the sayings of his senior companions: Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, Zafar, and Al-Hasan Ibn Ziyad, may Allah have mercy on them; this is despite their disagreement with Imam Abu Hanifa in several minor and fundamental issues.

In view of the overlapping of the sayings of Abu Hanifa with the statements of his companions, the author raises the most prominent question in this book: How did the three or more sayings, or we may call them the three or more schools of thought, become all “the Abu Hanifa School of Thought”? When were all these sayings merged? Did this merging take place in the early, middle or late books of the doctrine? Or is it in some of them, without the other? Is this only in lengthy books and explanations or in texts as well? And when was the merger established and spread? And what was the reason for that?

This book will provide answers to the aforementioned questions, along with many other benefits for the jurists, through what the author comprehends from the sayings of the scholars and Imams of the Hanafi School who had tackled this issue, as well as through his study of some books of the Hanafi School.

This systematic approach allows the student to transition from theoretical knowledge to a rigorous, evidence-based mastery of Aqidah. By linking every rule to tangible instances, Al-Sa'idan provides a protective barrier against intellectual inconsistency and ensures that the reader’s understanding remains grounded in the authentic methodology of the early generations.

name: Tas-hifat al-Muhaddithin by Abu Ahmad al-'Askari (382H) - 1400 pages
description_short:
A book that examines names and problematic expressions that are similar in calligraphy, in which a misspelling or mistake takes place in setting the word or its image, such as substituting a letter for another letter.

Originally, it was a book that the author shortened from a major book that he did in misspelling or metaplasm (At-Tas’heef). Then he was asked in the city of Ar-Rayy and Isfahan to single out what the hadith narrators and transmitters need, so he removed everything that has nothing to do with the hadith and limited it to what the hadith narrators and transmitters need to explain that which is misspelt from the words of the Messenger, may Allah’s prayers and peace be upon him, as well as the names of the Companions, the Followers, and those who follow them among the narrators whose names can be misspelt, such as: Habbab, Hattat, Hayyan, Habban, and so on.

A rare work of great value to the researcher and student. The edition we have chosen is the most reliable insha Allah, with the Tahqiq of Dr. Mahmud Ahmad Mayrah. He has scrupulously verified the text from 4 manuscripts and has made many necessary annotations for the reader.

The 3 original volumes are published here in one volume of 1400 pages!

name: At-Takhrij al-Fiqhi fi Madhhab al-Imam ash-Shafi’i
description_short:
At-Takhrij al-Fiqhi fi Madhhab al-Imam ash-Shafi’i: (At-Takhrij al-Fiqhi is the derivation of practical Shari’ah rulings and what leads thereto by examining the opinions and principles of a given Madhhab’s leading thinkers (Imams).

 

At-Takhrij al-Fiqhi is one of the most important characteristics of doctrinal jurisprudence. The jurisprudential rulings in each of the schools of the four Imams, may Allah be pleased with them, are divided into two parts: the texts of the Imam of the Madhhab, and the study of methodological principles in the interpretation of these texts of the imams of the Madhhab.

At-Takhrij al-Fiqhi has the credit for the growth of doctrinal jurisprudence since the era of the four founding Imams till now, and if it were not for it, the practice of Islamic jurisprudence would have stopped, and the jurists would not have been able to keep pace with different eras and answer the rulings of newly emerging issues, because there is no absolute, independent Mujtahid, so the effective way for doctrinal jurisprudence was At-Takhrij al-Fiqhi according to what was stipulated and enacted by the founding Imams of the schools, may Allah be pleased with them.

This book is an original and applied study that deals extensively with At-Takhrij al-Fiqhi in the doctrine of Imam Ash-Shafi’i in particular, and shows the role of the Mujtahids of the Madhhab and scholars in dealing with emerging issues that are not stipulated for the imam, explaining the nature of the work of the Imams and scholars and how they derive the rulings on the sayings, according to the texts and principles of Imam Ash-Shafi’i, and their impact on the Madhhab.

name: Masaa-il al-Khilaaf fi Usool al-Fiqh by Al-Qadi as-Saymari (439H)
description_short:
Masa'il al-Khilaaf fi Usul al-fiqh (Issues of Disagreement in the Principles of Jurisprudence) by Al-Qadi as-Saymari

This book is one of the most important rare books on the principles of jurisprudence, and the author was one of the earliest jurists on this field. He is Abu Abdullah As-Saymari, the sheikh of the Hanafi School in his time, as he lived in the second half of the fourth century AH until the first half of the fifth century AH. This is one of the best and oldest works on Hanafi principles, and he has included many disputed problems in it so that his readers can become acquainted with the most essential subjects in jurisprudence with the least amount of effort and the quickest path.

This book deserves the attention of researchers in the study of jurisprudential principles in general, whether for Hanafis, Hanbalis, or Shafi'is.

The book’s author is the jurist judge Al-Hussein bin Ali bin Muhammad bin Jaafar, Abu Abdullah As-Saymari (351 - 436 AH), a Baghdad Hanafi master. He was born in Saimar (Khuzestan) and served as the judge of Al-Mada’in and the province of Al-Karkh until his death in Baghdad.

Abu Bakr al-Khatib said about him: “He was well-spoken and well-insighted.” He said, “He was truthful, sharp in mind, good-natured, respectful of scholars.” Ibn al-Athir described him as “the master of Abu Hanifa’s companions in his time.”

According to Ibn al-Imad al-Hanbali, “He was a trustworthy and a scholar of Hadith.” In his Biography, Imam adh-Dhahabi described him as “The master of al-Hanafiyyah, the scholar of Hadith.”

This is a book printed for the first time from the legacy of the great scholar, Dr. Muhammad Ibrahim al-Banna, may Allah have mercy on him. It is a book that is easy to read and understand, gentle in reference, and accessible to the readers. Its origins are a series of radio episodes prepared and presented by Sheikh Al-Banna in a radio program in Makkah Al-Mukarramah entitled “Min Balaaghat al-Qur’an”, between the years 1986 and 1987 AD, when he was delegated to teach at Umm Al-Qura University. The author used a different approach to semantic differences than all other writers, dealing with the disparities between Qur'anic words with common meanings by referring to the context and its requirements; the context ensures that the veils of concealed meanings be revealed.

The two honourable researchers took care of the material of this book, correcting, reviewing and publishing it, without any interference from them in the text, so it came, as we hope, as its venerable author intended.

This fascinating book has a lovely preface by the scholar and master of rhetoricians, Dr. Muhammed Muhammed Abu Musa, may Allah grant him a long life of goodness and wellbeing.

description_short:
Al-Birkawi (or al-Birkali) holds a prominent position in the Arabic language arts, and he is one of those rare individuals who appear over time and are marked by a special spirit that appears to be represented in the traces they leave. One of his most valuable works is “Imtihaan Al-Adhkiyaa”, an explanation of the text of “Al-Lub” by Al-Baydawi, and “Al-Lub” is an acronym for “Kaafiya” by Ibn Al-Hajib, in grammar.

Anyone who reads “Imtihaan Al-Adhkiyaa” will appreciate the author's work because of his wealth of information, accuracy, freshness in viewpoints, and skill to debate. With the inclusion of Sheikh Mustafa Ibn Hamzah Ataha li’s “Hashiya” on the “Imtihaan Al-Adhkiyaa,” the editor has completed the task of three great minds, leaving beneficial knowledge.

Gorgeous edition, with some of the Harakats.

name: Al-Minha as-Saniyyah fi Sharh al-Lamhah al-Badriyyah fi Ilm al-Arabiyyah
description_short:
Imam Abu Hayyan Al-Andalusi’s (d. 745 AH) writings achieved a great reputation in the study of language. A small treatise titled “Al-Lamha Al-Badriyyah fi Ilm Al-Arabiyyah” was one of his most notable works. It is one of the grammatical texts that is considered a foundation for all educational levels, in which Abu Hayyan limited himself to the fundamental chapters in grammar without going into points of contention.

More than one grammarian has explained it, and foremost among them was his student, the Imam and author of “Umdat as-Salik,” Shihab al-Din Ahmed Ibn Lu’lu’ Ibn an-Naqib ash-Shafi’i (d. 769 AH). His explanation is being printed for the first time; in it Ibn an-Naqib sought to solve the ambiguous terms in “Al-Lamha”. He starts his book by citing the text of “Al-Lamha”, and then proceeds to explain its terminologies and phrases, correcting what he missed, so that he has completed the whole texts of “Al-Lamha”.  Ibn Al-Naqib drew his scientific material from grammatical literature in general and the books of two Imams in particular: Abi Hayyan and Ibn Malik.

The honourable editor took great care in explaining this, so she wrote an introduction to Abu Hayyan’s life and book, Ibn al-Naqib’s life and his book, and concluded it with a number of indexes that disclose its hidden content for students.

name: The Poetry of pre and post Islamic era and the effects of Islam in it
description_short:
The Poetry of pre and post Islamic era and the effects of Islam in it: Yahya Juburi

The book discusses the phase of collision between two cultures, an inherited pre-Islamic culture that extends towards the unknowns of history, and a new culture that carries a project to change not only the social and moral systems, but the structure of spirit and intellect, or rather the individual himself.

In the midst of this collision, each of the two cultures had to mix and interact at the same stage, especially since the past had its historical justification and the hadith had its religious and human justification. And since it was difficult or even impossible for a person to steer away from his past, a new culture had to be born in which these two cultures drew each other. It is this culture of the poets who had lived in both pre and post Islamic era that is the subject of this book.

This is a reprint of this unique and important work in the field of Arabic poetry.
