name: Pre-Islamic Poetry, specificity and disciplines - Dr. Yahya al-Juburi
description_short:
The book is useful as an introduction to pre-Islamic poetry.

It begins with a summary of the geography of the Arabian Peninsula and each of the political, social, mental and religious life of its pre-Islamic population. Jahiliyyah is seen by the author, not as promoted by many writers and authors as being opposite to knowledge, but rather opposite to tolerance.

The first chapter was devoted to issues of pre-Islamic poetry such as poetry narrators, the issue of plagiarism, the response to Taha Hussein, and a word on Al-Mu’allaqaat (The Suspended Odes).

In the second chapter, the author discusses the characteristics of pre-Islamic poetry; he explains the then nomadic aspect of the poetry, its clarity and realism, then he talks about the structure of the poem and highlights the thematic unit of the poem.

The third chapter discusses the arts of pre-Islamic poetry, which are: Al-Ghazal (love poetry), enthusiasm, pride, lamentation, satire, description, and finally wisdom.

description_short:
The book compiled by 'Adil l-Hamdan gathers 5 books on the ethics of teachers and learners, on education and learning:

“Adab al-Mu'allimin”, by Muhammad Ibn Sahnun (256 AH), who is considered one of the earliest to single out chapters on education and schooling. He discussed many issues related to teachers and their approach in teaching children.

“Masa-il fi Abwab al-Tarbiyah wa al-Ta'lim”, by Ibn Abi Zaid Al-Qayrawani (386 AH)“Malik Al-Saghir”. These are issues collected from the book Fatwas of Ibn Abi Zaid Al-Qayrawani and arranged according to chapters.

“Al-Risalah al-Mufassalah fi Ahwal al-Muta'allimin wa Ahkam al-Mu'allimin wa al-Muta'allimin”, by Ali bin Muhammad Al-Qabisi (403 AH). It explains and arranges many of its chapters and issues, with important benefits and additions that many teachers and students cannot do without.

“Al-Muntaqa min Abwab al-Mu'allimin wa al-Muta'allimin” by Ibn al-Hajj al-Maliki, (737 AH). He carefully discussed the issues of education, teaching methods, and the condition of teachers with the children. He eloquently expounded this subject, treating many issues which were not discussed by his predecessors.

“Jami' Jawami' al-Ikhtisar wa al-Tabyan, Fima Ya'rudh Bayna al-Mu'allimin wa Aba'a al-Subyan” by al-Maghrawi al-Maliki (898 AH). It explains many of their issues, with important additions and many quotes from the imams of the Maliki School.

“Wasaya al-Abaa li Mu'allimi al-Abna”. The compiler of these books says: To add more benefits, I thought of appending these five books by mentioning the commandments fathers to the educators and teachers of their children; these are important and useful commandments in the field of education.

description_short:
As-sirah An-Nabawiyyah (Biography of the Prophet) by al-Hafidh Jamal ad-Din Al-Mizzi.

The eminent hafiz Jamal al-Din al-Mizzi (d. 742 AH) composed this work on the Prophet’s life. It is a biography extracted from the introduction to his book “Tahdhib al-Kamaal,” which is one of the most comprehensive books on narrators’ biographies, making it difficult to extract the chapter on the Prophet’s biography from it, so it is good that it is singled out with independent care so that it is a subject studied in mosques, universities, and scientific centres. This book includes, with its brevity, the biography of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his birth, his names, his upbringing, his children, his pilgrimage, his conquests, his writers, his messengers, his uncles, his aunts, his wives, his servants, his maidservants, his horses, his camels, his weapons, his attributes, his morals, and his miracles.

This book is concluded with a nice section by the scholar Ibn al-Adim al-Halabi (d. 660 AH) on the circumcision of the Prophet, may Allah's blessing and peace be upon him, in which he explains the weakness of the reports that the Prophet was circumcised at birth, or by his grandfather, or by the honourable Angel Jibreel.

name: The Scholar and the Ruler - Hmida Ennaifer
description_short:
A new book, written by Prof. Dr. Hmida Annaifer, has been published with an introduction by Professor of History, Muhammad Daifallah.

The book sheds light on an aspect of the state's relationship with the Zaitouna institution, as well as Bourguiba’s ties with the Zaitouna elites via Sheikh Muhammad al-Bashir Annaifer. The significance of these selected texts stems from numerous factors, the first of which is that they are drawn from documents that constitute the most essential portion of his memoirs. These selections are particularly significant because they include correspondences between the Sheikh and political officials in contemporary Tunisia, and their revelations in terms of an intellectual background and a conceptual vision, and what they call for in terms of the correspondents' expressions and political positions. On the other hand, the selections concentrated on documents concerning the Sheikh’s relationship with the leader “Habib Bourguiba” (1903-2000 AD), with whom he had ties that were not adequately and accurately addressed.

All of these texts, particularly those pertaining to the period preceding the proclamation of the republic on July 25, 1957, reveal a watershed moment in Tunisia’s contemporary history in terms of two distinct areas of public affairs: the new state and its policies on the one hand, and the status of the olive branch and the fate of religious affairs on the other.

It heralds the end of the period of religious legitimacy as a point of reference for the state and the emergence of a new articulation between the religious and the political, based on the principle of submitting the religion to the state rule.
searchable_keywords: The Scholar and the Ruler - Hmida Ennaifer

description_short:
Because the Arabic language is the primary and essential passage for the speech of revelation addressed to the Mukallaf (i.e. a legally competent and responsible person), and because the quality of receiving through it an understanding and awareness of the connotations and intent is the first step to improving the practical applications of the true Shari’ah discourse.

And because the Arabic language was established in the Arabs' environment in a natural disposition and well-trained manner, and its rules were rooted through the extrapolation of the Arabs’ historical tongue, as well as the discourse of legal and idiomatic revelation, and because the lived reality with its problems and setbacks produced a gap, vagueness and invisibility in writing, and lack of eloquence in speech for the Arabs, with their language, and the state of civilizational dependence on the West has uprooted the most specific characteristics of the Ummah and its most fortified fortress; that is the Arabic language.

The NAMA Center provides, as part of the "Takween" series, this study in which the author aimed to frame a practical plan to restore the role of the Arabic language in our society and civilized process. In the folds of the research, he monitored the points of failure that afflicted the incubators of teaching the Arabic language, and he also charted a practical and scientific path for the development of individual linguistic faculties, through the levels and branches of grammatical, morphological, rhetorical, and literary linguistic sciences, with an indication of aspects of application and training.

name: Quranic sciences - scientific criticism and new construction
description_short:
This book is a critical project for Qur’anic sciences, as well as a suggestion for a new foundation, in light of fundamental methodological misconceptions of the contemporary reality of Qur’anic sciences. The project is divided into two studies.

The first is a detailed systematic review of the science of the Qur'anic sciences, as well as an explanation of the features of methodological imbalance that arise in it and how to deal with it.

The second is concerned with assessing the progress made in the methodical creation of the Qur’anic sciences as a whole, and providing a new vision for constructing these sciences.

This project carries a systematic discussion of the idea of science in terms of its nature and definition: what is complex and rooted in it; what is the methodological condition for what can or cannot be described as scientific in terms of research frameworks, as well as the methods of classifying sciences. It also proposes the vision concluded for rebuilding the sciences of the Qur’an as being methodologically valid to clarify and explore the methodological defect in building all heritage sciences and rebuilding these and any others sciences, whatever their nature.

name: Dispute between Abul-Hasan Ashari & the Muhaddithin - Sharif Al-Awni
description_short:
One of the most common, diverged and lengthy discussions of legal thought over the Islamic centuries is the issue of reasoning with traditions as referential evidence, because it is related to the second source of legislation, which is the honourable Sunnah of the Prophet. Despite the abundance of what has been written in the Sunnah sciences of single compilations, chapters and researches, it is an independent science among the sublime Islamic sciences; however, the field of research for its secrets is still ongoing.

The issues of definite and speculative narratives in the Prophet’s Sunnah, and the method of distinguishing one narration from the other, are among the subjects related to narration, which concerned the hadith methodology, the fundamentalist thinking and the scholastic research. Furthermore, this issue has been the subject of scientific debates, which have affected (and continue to affect) the Sharia sciences with the greatest and deepest impact.

The author wanted to contribute to the study of one aspect of this subject, by shedding light on the positions of agreement and divergence between the approach of Imam “Abul Hassan Al-Ash’ari” and the approach of the hadith scholars in differentiating between the certain and the presumptive in the narrations and their approach in using them to support their argumentation. Are there any agreement or divergence in their methodologies, regarding the issue of certainty or presumption in the narrative’s information?

name: Al-Jami' fi Tafsir Ayat al-Ahkam (Mawsu'ah 'Ilmiyyah) - 7 volumes
description_short:
An enormous work of research, a scientific encyclopedia that brings together verses dealing with legal rulings and the clarification of Fiqh subjects arising from them.

This research is the result of a group of Egyptian researchers under the general supervision of Sheikh Majdi ibn Atiyah Hamoudah, and here is the methodology they used for this 7-volume compendium:

Enumerations of verses concerning a legal rule.

General exegesis of the verse according to the great recognized Tafsir.

Causes of revelation.

Establishment of the legal rules derived from the verse(s).

Comparison, where applicable, of different readings and the impact this may have on judgments.

For each legal question, evidence from the Qur'an, then from the Sunnah, then from the sayings of the Sahabas is listed. 

Finally, the opinions of the 4 schools are cited, as well as books dealing with Ijma', and the opinions of Ibn Taymiyyah, as-San'ani, ash-Shawkani...

A scientific resource full of riches that will save students a lot of research by finding everything concerning Ayat al-Ahkam in a single place.

In this book, I have done everything in my power to restore the right to its people in a variety of subjects, including literature, jurisprudence and its foundations, Quranic science, Hadith science, history, biographies, and creeds.

I do not claim to be aware of everything attributed to unclassified literature, as this is both implausible and true, but I do claim to have come across a wide spectrum of those works.

I pray to Allah that our endeavour would benefit researchers and seekers of knowledge...

Ameen.

The Aristotelian logic depicted in religious scientific circles contains both what is true and what is corrupt, and yet theologians have defined it as a legal instrument that shields the mind from error, which is a solemn claim; however, that instrument that they claimed was a shield for the mind: When the Ash'aris used it, they came to the conclusion that Allah Almighty is neither inside nor outside the world!

name: I am still a Salafi: dialogue with the neo-Hanbalis and the modernists
description_short:
The occurrence of mistakes in individuals and groups is unavoidable; no one denies this; this is human nature, and Salafists are not immune to it. Pointing out these errors, correcting them, and denying them to those who commit them does not invalidate the methodology in any way, but rather is one of the acts of enjoining good and forbidding evil.

And a call with such attributes would never bring fruitful fruit, just as grapes are not reaped from thorns!  The danger of such new calls is that they represent the true beginning of the materialistic modernist call, by claiming the sophistical view: the relativity of truth, as the postmodernists do, or the overthrow of scholars committed to the apparent Shari'ah, as the new Hanbalis do, so that the natural alternative for these people is either a final relapse and the modernist view, or that the spiritual alternative is the tendency to dervishism."

name: Tafsir Ikhtilaf Lafdh Ayat Al-Mutashabih - Muhammad AbdelHalim Awaydah
description_short:
The idea for the book came to me while I was reading Allah’s Words (the Qur’an) and trying to think about them. I discovered some passages that were somehow similar but not identical... and the distinction may be a letter, a word, a precedence, a delay, a mention, an omission, an expansion, an abbreviation, and so on.

This begs the question: Is there a reason for the disparity between these passages that necessitates this?

So I began searching through the works of scholars, both past and contemporary, who had written on this topic, and by Allah’s permission, I found the answer, and all discrepancies and imaginary disagreements were eradicated, after a long hard searching for the verse I was wondering about. I would read dozens of pages, until I discovered the verse I needed, and occasionally I would read an entire book and still not locate the requisite verse. This is because there is no book that contains these verses in an organized and easy-to-reference format. So Allah made me wonder why we do not collecting what scholars wrote about such verses and arranging them in the order of the chapters in the Holy Qur'an, similar to Qur’an interpretation books, so that the reader can easily follow the verses, ponder them, and know the ruling from this difference and similarity in an easy and simple way.

I began the journey of the book after performing Istikharah and consulting some of the scholars and sheikhs who wrote on this topic and who strongly encouraged me to start this work. The journey took more than two years in research, collection, arrangement, and coordination. I beseech Allah to accept it and turn it into a huge reward and benefit.

name: Tahafat al-Mutakallimin - Ammar Khanfar
description_short:
It is a new study on Islamic theology and the Ahlu as-Sunnah's attitude toward Islamic theology and its followers. In approximately 500 pages, the author discussed the emergence of Islamic theology, as well as the most fundamental grounds on which theologians built their doctrine, issues, and their doctrinal and methodological evidences, as well as the invalidity of those issues.

We find that the topic of Allah's Attributes and the challenges that arise from them is one of the most difficult topics in Islamic religion and history. Schools and sects arose as a result of issues in which faith intersected with philosophy and theology, resulting in deep and profound intellectual confrontations between the Islamic theological school and the philosophical schools.

Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have pity on him, challenged and explained theological and philosophical schools’ fallacies. His publications served as the foundations and pillars of the current school, as Ahlu as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah academics followed his method and defended correct belief in the face of theological school.

This book represents a continuation of the modern school's approach, but it was distinguished from other works by the strength and originality of the proposition, as well as its independence from the cloak of imitation, which was aided by the author's mastery of logic and philosophy, which contributed to revealing the secrets of the theological approach and demonstrating its falsity.

name: Rihlat Ibn Battuta (The Journey of Ibn Battuta)
description_short:
Rihlat Ibn Battuta (The Journey of Ibn Battuta: A Masterpiece of the Spectators In the Strangeness of the Lands and the Wonders)

The Cambridge Society dubbed Ibn Battuta the Prince of Muslim Travelers because of his most popular trip book and his great reputation in Europe.

Ibn Battuta began his journey from Tangier. He left it in the year 725 AH. He traveled through Morocco, Egypt, the Levant, the Hijaz, Iraq, Persia, Yemen, and Bahrain, and returned to perform the Hajj again during the Hajj of Al-Nasser Ibn Qalawun, and returned to Egypt, and from there to the Levant, then to Anatolia, Turkestan, Transoxiana, some parts of India, China, and Java, and the country of the Tatars, as well as Central Africa.

Ibn Battuta spent more than thirty years of his life traveling and documenting his experiences. In a narrative pattern and an appealing style comparable to the language and style of the public, Ibn Battuta detailed every country he travelled through, mentioning its inhabitants, kings, scholars, and judges.

name: Al-Khitat Al-Maqriziyyah - Al-Maqrizi (The History of Egypt)
description_short:
Kitab al-Mawa'iz wa-al-I'tibar bi-Dhikr al-Khitat wa-al-Athar, or "Khitat al-Maqriziyyah" is a book written by Taqi Al-Din Ahmed bin Ali bin Abdul Qadir Al-Maqrizi (845 AH).

This book has another name known by it, which is “Al-Khitat Al-Maqriziyyah.” In this book, the author chronicles Umm al-Dunya, Egypt, during the period extending from the year twenty of the honorable Prophet’s migration to the year nine hundred and six, speaking about its great Nile and its impact on the life of Egypt, its weather and climate, and the construction of Egypt and Cairo, its streets, its alleys, its hotels, its bays, its bridges, its kings, its sultans, its mosques, its beliefs, its religions, its schools, endowments, and other things related to Egypt until the beginning of the tenth century AH.

The subject of this book falls within the art of writing plans, topography—a type of regional historical geography. This art was known in many Islamic countries, where the introductions to books that chronicled Islamic cities, such as “The History of Baghdad” by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi, “The History of Damascus” by Ibn Asakir, and “Al-Alaq Al-Khathirah” by Ibn Shaddad, included topographical descriptions of these cities. Nevertheless, we can say that this art is one of the arts that Islamic Egypt was specialized in and that it grew and developed throughout its long history, and it had a glorious history in it that paved the way for the completion that this art reached in Al-Maqrizi’s huge book “Al-Khitat Al-Maqriziyyah”, which is undoubtedly the largest representative of the art of topography.

The book is a seminal work in urban history and one of the first to concentrate in city history.

name: Encyclopedia of Fiqh of the Hearts - Muhammad al-Tuwaijri
description_short:
Mawsu'at Fiqh al-Qulub addresses the essential inner dimension of Islamic worship, returning the focus to the spiritual foundation that governs all outward deeds. While conventional legal manuals concentrate primarily on the jurisprudence of the limbs (Fiqh al-Jawarih), Shaykh Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tuwaijri dedicates this comprehensive work to the sovereign reality of the heart. The author methodically explores the realization of Tawhid, the deepening of Ma'rifatullah through His Sublime Names and Attributes, and the central devotions of the soul—such as Ikhlas, reliant trust (Tawakkul), reverent fear (Khawf), hope (Raja'), love (Mahabbah), and steadfast patience. Every chapter is anchored directly in the text of the Quran and verified prophetic Hadith, deliberately bypassing speculative scholastic disputes in favor of pure scriptural guidance.

Drawing heavily on the Athari tradition and spiritual depth championed by Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim, the work frames spiritual rectification not as an abstract luxury, but as an urgent obligation inseparable from sound belief. The Shaykh offers an insightful diagnosis of inner spiritual maladies—including arrogance, ostentation, malice, and heedlessness—pairing each affliction with tangible prophetic remedies centered on Dhikr and watchful contemplation. Structured with pedagogical clarity and accessible language, this encyclopedia serves as an indispensable reference for Tullab al-'Ilm studying Tazkiyat an-Nafs, as well as a practical manual for anyone striving to cultivate a sound and upright heart (Qalb Salim).

name: Acts of Worship of the Heart - Muhammad al-Tuwaijri
description_short:
A comprehensive work on the inner acts of the heart that constitute the true foundation, essence, and living spirit of all Islamic worship—sincerity (Ikhlas), reliance upon Allah (Tawakkul), divine love (Mahabbah), reverent fear (Khawf), hope (Raja'), gratitude, patience, awe, repentance, and certainty. Authored by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tuwaijri in two volumes, the book approaches these stations not as mere optional spiritual virtues or transient emotional moods, but as binding, primary obligations. Each devotion is treated with its own defined conditions, direct spiritual fruits, and destructive nullifiers—standing on equal, if not superior, footing to the outward acts of worship performed by the limbs.

The work fills an essential void in contemporary Islamic literature: it moves beyond the purely exhortative storytelling common to standard books of Raqa'iq, while steering clear of dry, detached theological theory. Drawing directly from the explicit texts of the Quran and verified prophetic hadiths, it provides a structured, evidence-based roadmap for the inner life—illustrating how each worship takes root, how to shield it from spiritual corruption, and how inner faith directly translates into outward righteousness and tranquility. A book that fills the heart with Tawhid, brings true peace to the soul, and steers the limbs toward righteous deeds.

name: Al-Ihtifal bi Ahkam wa Adab al-Atfal (40 Hadith) by 'Adil al-Hamdan
description_short:
Childhood jurisprudence, newborn sunnahs, and prophetic parenting form the core of this specialized work, which revives the classical tradition of thematic forty-hadith collections (al-Arba'iniyyat). Moving past abstract theoretical advice, the text compiles forty sourced prophetic narrations tracing early human development from the first moments of life. It systematically covers post-natal rites—including the initial call to prayer, the softening of dates (tahneek), selecting wholesome names, the birth sacrifice ('aqiqah), and circumcision—before detailing the Prophet's ﷺ personal interactions with young children through tangible expressions of affection, mercy, and patience.

Grounding each narration in an authentic hadith apparatus, the author provides source referencing (takhrij), definitions of rare vocabulary, and deduced legal and moral directives (al-fawa'id wal-ahkam). The commentary addresses key developmental stages from a juristic perspective, including the transition to the age of discernment (tamyiz), gradual training in ritual prayer, and the cultivation of Islamic ethics without harshness or alienation. The resulting manual offers a scripture-based practical guide tailored for parents, primary educators, and students of hadith.

name: Misbah al-Muhtaj ila ma fi al-Minhaj - Ibn Qasim al-Ghazzi
description_short:
This wonderful work stands as one of the finest explanations of Minhaj al-Talibin by Imam al-Nawawi, which is regarded as the ultimate reference in Shafi'i jurisprudence. The author, Ibn Qasim al-Ghazzi (d. 918 AH), was a towering authority in the school whose extensive body of work has guided generations of jurists. This particular commentary is characterized by its intermediate length, making it a highly practical tool for those who find shorter summaries too brief and exhaustive encyclopedias too dense.

The methodology focuses on illuminating the complex legal terminology and internal logic of the Shafi'i madhhab with precision and clarity. By breaking down the concise phrasing of Imam al-Nawawi, it provides the Student of Knowledge (Talib al-Ilm) with a reliable bridge to mastering advanced legal rulings. Its utility in traditional circles cannot be overstated, as it maintains a sober, academic tone that prioritizes the strength of evidence and the established positions of the school’s later masters.

Superb 5-volume edition, verified from 2 manuscripts, with Harakats approximately 50% complete. This Sharh is published for the first time, and the quality of editing and layout are exemplary.

name: Custom and its impact on legal application in the Hanafi School
description_short:
The secret of Islamic jurisprudence’s width and comprehensiveness is owing to the magnificence of its sources, their sanctity, and the diversity of original and dependent sources, to encompass all areas of life and to suit the differences of time and place. Among these sources that contributed in this regard is the source of custom and tradition, which scholars defined as “what is settled in the souls in terms of intellect, and is received by sound natures with acceptance”; it is supported with Allah’s Words: “Show forgiveness, enjoin al-‘Urf (what is good), and turn away from the ignorant.” (Q.S7:199), and also with the Hadith mawquf, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: “Whatever Muslims view as good is good to Allah, and whatever the Muslims view as evil is evil to Allah.”

Custom has great and strong power over individuals, societies and nations; it meets with minds and souls, and plays a great role in all aspects of dealings in life. Judgments result from it, judges and rulers resort to it, and arbitrators and reformers make use of it. Custom and tradition are constantly renewed, so they occupy a wide space in life, and therefore jurists developed the jurisprudential rule “There is no denial that rulings change with the change of times.”

We find the convergence of textual transmission in the Qur’an and Sunnah with the renewed and open human mind. The jurists, scholars, mujtahids, and judges grabbed hold of its rulings that are accepted by Shari’a in meeting the interests of the people, to add them to the stock available to them, resulting in extensive and rich jurisprudence.
searchable_keywords: Custom and its impact on legal application in the Hanafi School

name: Al-Mahsoul fi 'Ilm Usul al-Fiqh - Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (2 volumes)
description_short:
It is a very important book that examines the science of the Principles of Islamic Jurisprudence, and it is a reference to anyone who wants to write on this field. In this book, the author has presented the fundamental premises, languages, commands and prohibitions, actions, the abrogating and abrogated, consensus, analogy, equivalence, weighting, Ijtihad, and he has detailed that in great detail.

The book deals with a number of issues that exhausted the efforts of fundamentalists and jurists despite their differing sectarian affiliations and intellectual visions over a period of time, spanning six centuries.

Al-Razi’s contribution to writings on jurisprudence principles is considered relatively late in time, as it came after this field had established itself as an independent science since the end of the fourth century (A.H), despite the fact that its issues began to gel in the minds of jurists as early as the second century (A.H). Because of that lateness, Al-Razi was able to learn about the diverse viewpoints and positions on the fundamentals.

Al-Razi has added the benefits of his thought, in addition to the eloquence of expression, the good arrangement and refinement, the accuracy of the expression, and the smoothness of the style, which drew the interests of the students of knowledge.

The book has received great attention from scholars; some have written commentaries about it and others have abridged it.

Great 2-volumes edition, verified and annotated, under the supervision of Shu'ayb al-Arna'ut. 50% Harakat.

name: Kitab al-Fitan - Hafidh Nu'aym ibn Hamad al-Maruzi (228H)
description_short:
Kitab al-Fitan is one of the earliest and most famous specialized collections dedicated to the narrations concerning tribulations, civil strides, and the signs of the Hour. Authored by the early Hadith scholar Nu'aym ibn Hammad (d. 228 AH), this work serves as a massive historical repository for reports regarding the end of times, the appearance of the Dajjal, the descent of Isa (Jesus) عليه السلام, and the various political upheavals predicted to occur within the Ummah. Given its compilation in the early 3rd century AH, it provides a unique window into the apocalyptic discourses and historical anxieties that were documented during the formative period of Hadith codification.

This 2-volume edition features Harakats on Hadith and authentication of chains of narration. 100% Harakat on Hadith and authentication of chains of narration.

name: The Mohammedan Horsemanship (Al-Furusiyyah) - Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
description_short:
Imam Ibn al-Qayyim - may Allah Almighty have mercy on him - singled out most of the book to explain the meaning of ar-Ramiy (Archery) and its status and virtue in Islam, the virtue of competition, wrestling and fighting. Nevertheless, he expanded the jurisprudential researches related to the organisation of competitions between contestants and wrestlers, the betting contract between them and the permissibility of introducing the permitted between them, the evidence of those who claim permissibility and those who claim prohibition, the types of matches and contests, what is permissible in them and what is not permissible. Then he mentions the different jurisprudential branching of the different schools of thought on these issues.

The author demonstrates in the book the various sorts of horsemanship, its ranks and tools, as well as the sayings and acts of many virtuous ancestors in horsemanship, and demonstrates information about horsemanship that only those active in horsemanship are aware of. He accurately describes the character of the archer, the method of archery and its limits, the quality of the bow, the arrow and the spear, quoting from the early jurists, and how their archery, their machines, and their skill in this field, which indicates the chivalry of our righteous predecessors, their courage, and their willingness to jihad for the sake of Allah.

name: Hidayat al-Tullab fil-Fiqh al-Maliki - Sheikh Sidi Al-Mukhtar Al-Kunti
description_short:
Hidayat At-Tulaab fi al-Fiqhi al-Malki: (Guidance of students in Maliki jurisprudence) is a summary that explains to the students the branching of the issues of Imam Malik’s school of thought. The author “Has followed Khalil's method in abbreviation and brevity, by using the easiest style, the most beautiful phrase, and the clearest statement.”

The book has tackled most of the chapters and sections of jurisprudence that the earlier scholars had used to deal with, even those that are no longer urgently needed in this era, such as manumission, correspondence, the maintenance of the kings, and rules regarding Umm al-Walad (slave-girl who has borne her master's baby boy). But the book has also tackled other chapters and sections of jurisprudence that matter a lot to us today, whether in dealings or in acts of worship, such as selling with its chapters (a corrupt contract, Islamic banking, dealing with building and trees, loan, mortgage, fines and bankruptcy....), as well as some chapters related to etiquette, piety, and repentance that the author has chosen as a conclusion to his valuable book, which he began with acts of worship as usual.

What distinguishes ‘Hidayat At-Tulaab’ from ‘Khalil’s Mukhtasar’ (Khalil’s Abbreviation), despite its replication in the same way, is that he has corrected some of the mistakes of the Mukhtasar in many of its issues, added others which Khalil did not examine, and linked the branches to their origins, all of this in an easy style, beautiful phrases, and a clear statement.

name: Fath al-Fattah ala Mukhtasar Sheikh Khalil - Ibn Rahal al-Ma’dani
description_short:
This huge book has reached a total of 71 volumes. It is an encyclopaedic commentary on Sheikh Khalil’s Abbreviation of Maliki jurisprudence. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, has collected all the texts of the Malikite school of Islamic jurisprudence and the texts of the Maliki Imams in the eras that existed between him and Imam Malik, until scholars said: “He almost did not miss a text from the texts of the Malikite school of Islamic jurisprudence.”

This significant achievement is regarded as the result of collective effort overseen by the scholar Ibn Rahaal al-Ma’daani al-Tadlawi, who died in 1140 AH. It is a scientific tradition carried out by the best scholars and has a counterpart in the history of Islamic sciences.

Dr. Ahmed Abadi has explained that this book/encyclopaedia “is considered a symbol of the great Alawite state, as Sultan Ismail had commissioned scholars, led by the great scholar al-Ma’dani, to collect fatwa and Islamic rulings according to the rules and principles of the Maliki school of thought.”

The value of this remarkable explanation of Sheikh Khalil's Mukhtasar stems from the fact that it is a scientific treasury in itself, with a multitude of literature, footnotes, revisions, appendices, and jurisprudential edits that are uncommon in others. This constitutes a text that highlights the extent of the richness of the Maliki school of thought in dealing with current controversial issues.

name: The Kuwaiti Encyclopaedia of Islamic Jurisprudence - 45 volumes
description_short:
The Encyclopaedia of Jurisprudence is the most comprehensive jurisprudence encyclopaedia in the modern era. Its volume count has so far reached 45 large-format volumes, and it has been classified in the form of terms, grouped in lexical (alphabetical) order and it contains 200,000 references.

The Kuwaiti Encyclopaedia of Islamic Jurisprudence contains 3,000 jurisprudential terms in terminology and primary titles, as well as 27,000 sub-titles organized in a unique objective classification known as "Thesaurus."

Its features include comprehensiveness, ease of arrangement, and a streamlined style.

The State of Kuwait's tireless efforts over more than forty years (between 1965 and 2005 AD) resulted in the publication of the Encyclopaedia of Jurisprudence in its final form in forty-five large-sized volumes to include general jurisprudence research that was formulated in the style of jurisprudential terminology arranged in alphabetical order, facilitating access to jurisprudence for all who wish from a medium culture, knowing that the Encyclopaedia of Jurisprudence mostly covered the Four Schools of Jurisprudence and adopted the approach of unifying the agreed-upon jurisprudential opinions, giving them priority over the opinions that are unique to each School of Jurisprudence, and at the same time providing more evidences of the jurists, without weighting or digression, nor comparing between them, or addressing either emerging issues or fundamentalist issues.

Hundreds of eminent Islamic jurisprudence academics contributed to the creation of this Encyclopaedia of Jurisprudence.

name: The 14 Different Readings with regard to Faith and Jurisprudence
description_short:
The Fourteen Different Readings with regard to Faith and Jurisprudence by Waleed Al-Meneese

To be a building block in the structure of Qur'anic studies, contributing to its upliftment, and it is based on study for which its author received an exceptional master's degree in jurisprudence and its principles.

The subject of the research: The effect of different readings on issues of faith in terms of increasing the evidence on the validity of the doctrine of the righteous predecessors in the matters of belief, and the impact of the diversity of readings as well in responding to the suspicions of the people of innovation, and then the impact of different readings on issues of jurisprudence in terms of their indication of a jurisprudential ruling or Its impact on weighting a statement over a statement in controversial issues.

The fourteen recitations are the ten frequent readings, along with the reading of Ibn Muhaisin, Yahya Al-Yazidi, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Al-Amash. These four recitations are still narrated with authentic chains of narrators, although they are not frequent, and therefore I decided to study their impact in the fields of creed and jurisprudence with the recurring recitations.

name: Al-Bukhala - The Misers - Al-Jahiz
description_short:
The book deals with the disease of miserliness and stinginess in a way of ridicule and mockery. It describes the funny arguments of misers, and their gentle tricks. Their weird anecdotes are not lacking in the book.

Al-Jāḥiẓ’s work “Al-Bukhala’” depicts the misers he met and became acquainted with in his private milieu, particularly in Merv, the capital of Khorasan. He portrays the misers in a realistic, sensual, psychological, and humorous manner; he shows us their movements, anxious or reassuring looks, and psychological whims, exposes their secrets and the secrets of their homes, informs us of their various conversations, and shows us all their attitude and conditions, but he does not make us hate them or leave us with a negative impression.

The stories in the book are short instructional comedy scenarios. The work was presented in a realistic way, using vernacular phrases and frequent dialogue. The book is a sociological, educational, psychological, and economic study of the misers.

name: Ayna Nahnu min Akhlaaq as-Salaf ?
description_short:
Just as it is not acceptable for anyone to abide by the morals of the predecessors while abandoning their belief, it is also not justified to understand their belief without adhering to their behaviour and morals.

As we all know, various books have been written addressing the topic of the predecessors' beliefs, praise be to Allah, but this book is an attempt to provide the groundwork for the Salaf's approach to behaviour and morals. It is drawn from two books: al-Dhahabi's “Siyar A'lam al-Nubala” and Ibn al-Jawzi’s “Sifat al-Safwa”. The predecessors’ points of view have been taken into account in an objective order, and the book is a decent size and easy to read. The book is divided into twenty-six chapters, which include, for example, the following:

Sincerity and honesty / fear of admiration / asceticism in the world / jurisprudence in religion / obedience to the truth / patience when calamities befall/ predecessors and the trial of Sultans / predecessors and women’s trial / righteousness to mothers/ rights of creation / dealing with mistakes / etiquette with scholars / etiquette of speech and tongue / keeping time… etc.

We beseech Allah Almighty to grant us success in adhering to the morals of the forefathers and to aid in the propagation of honourable morals among believers, and may Allah's Blessings and Peace be upon Muhammad, his family, and his companions.

name: Al-Munsif: Explaining Al-Mazini’s book At-Tasrif - Abul-Fath Ibn Jinni
description_short:
The book (Al-Munsif) is the result of the combined efforts of two great scholars who sought to serve the Arabic language in their endeavor to serve the Book of Allah. The reviewer of the book will determine its the high status among the author’s other works of art, a status that seduced Ibn Jinni’s heart so much that he dedicated himself and his time to it, which ended with this unique explanation of Abu Uthman Al-Mazini’s book of “Tasreef” (morphology).

The researcher has classified the study of the book into six chapters, and this study was an account about Al-Mazini and Ibn Jinni, about Ibn Jinni’s approach in (Al-Munsif) and his sources, about the listening, which is the first principle of the argumentation in language and grammar, and about analogy, which is the second principle of the argumentation in language, and then he concluded his study by discussing conjugational causes.

As for the verification, the researcher has followed the approach adopted by the masters of this art, according to what they deemed endorsable. Then he described the written transcripts (five in number) upon which he relied to show the verified text, before delving into the investigation. Eventually, the book came in three parts except the study: The first and second parts were to explain the book “at-Tasreef” of Abi Uthman Al-Mazini, which included a narrative about the origins of the Arabic morphology; the third part was to explain the unfamiliar words present in the context of the book, as well as for the complex and puzzling issues.

Beautiful edition, checked and annotated, with about 50% of the Harakats.

name: at-Tatawu' fi al-'Ibadat - Volunteering in Acts of Worship (harakat)
description_short:
It is Allah's Wisdom and Mercy toward His servants that He has prescribed acts of worship for them, which He has divided into two categories: obligatory acts that He has commanded them to perform and voluntary acts (supererogatories) that He has recommended and urged them to perform in order to increase their reward and complete what is missing from the obligatory acts. In addition, He made for every obligatory act a volunteer act of its sort. Purity has a volunteer of its kind, as does prayer, fasting, charity, Hajj, and Umrah, all of which have volunteers of their own kind.

 This book explains the rulings on voluntary acts of worship (purification, prayer, fasting, seclusion, charity, Hajj, Umrah, and circumambulation), which are taken from the book “Fiqh al-Ibaadaat” (the jurisprudence of worship), from the Encyclopedia of Jurisprudence, with some issues and additions revised.

The book is built like a modern Fiqh manual, listing each time the obligations, recommendations, annulments etc... In a simple and understandable style, all with the majority of the Harakats.

name: Al-'Awasim wal-Qawasim: Defending the Sunnah - Ibn Al-Wazir Al-Yamani
description_short:
The book “Al-‘Awasim wal-Qawasim” of Ibn Wazir al-Yamani includes many significant topics, including:

- The conditions of ijtihad (independent reasoning), and what is sufficient for the mujtahid to know regarding the Prophet’s traditions, the methods of correcting, the methodology of Jurh and Ta’deel (criticizing and praising people of knowledge), and the cases where ijtihad is deemed impossible.

- The opinion as to when the scholars of Ta’weel (allegorical interpretation) accept the narration from the types of innovators providing their sincerity and memorization is approved.

- In defence of the honourable Companions.

- Deeming the imam of the Sunnah, Abi Abdullah Ahmad ibn Hanbal, free from any statement of Tashbeeh and Tajseem (Anthropomorphism), and the scholars of Hadith altogether.

- Reply against those who attributed Imam Malik - may Allah have mercy on him - and his fellow jurists and scholars of Hadith to idiocy and stagnation.

- Critical study on the issue of vision in defence of Imam Shafi'i.

- Reply against the Mu’tazilah is a variety of issues.

- A narrative about divine decree and destiny, and the revelation that prohibits delving into it.

A wondeful print in 5 volumes, checked and annotated by Shu'ayb al-Arnaoot, with referencing of Hadith, margin notes regarding the topic, and useful footnotes.

name: Aqida of Ahl as-Sunnah in the Sifat mentioned in analogies
description_short:
This specialized scholarly work addresses a precise theological issue: understanding Allah's attributes when mentioned alongside human qualities in Islamic texts. The author examines hadiths like "Whoever conceals a Muslim's faults in this world, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the hereafter," where divine and human actions appear comparable.

The book systematically analyzes seven categories of such attributes, providing detailed explanations of scholarly positions and resolving apparent contradictions. Rather than applying uniform interpretations, the author demonstrates how different textual contexts require nuanced approaches while maintaining core theological principles.

Each case study includes comprehensive analysis of classical and contemporary scholarly opinions, with the author presenting conclusive explanations based on sound methodology. The work addresses critical questions about anthropomorphism, divine transcendence, and proper understanding of comparative religious language.

Essential reading for students of Islamic theology seeking rigorous treatment of this complex subject.

description_short:
Introduction to the Science of Quranic Recitations/Readings - Dr. Abdulqayyum As-Sindi

This book defines the science of readings and its terminology: such as the choice, the novel, the manner, the path, the origins, and the specific rules for some Quranic words. It demonstrates the source of the recitations, the relevance of the science of recitations, its virtues and its benefits. It differentiates between the Qur’an and al-Qiraa’aat, shows the relationship of recitations to the seven letters, chronicles the origins of the science of recitations and the stages it went through, and shows the conditions for the validity of the recitation, and the types of recitations in terms of validity.

The book covers what was said about the reasons for the different recitations, the issue of preference between them, the suspicions raised around them, and shows ways to receive and approve the recitations, and the sciences related to the science of recitations and its impact on them. It also provides biographies of the ten imams of the recitation, their narrators, their paths, and the most prominent Quran readers who authored books in this field. It explains the origins of the ten recitations, mentions their chains of transmission, and the most important recitation books.

name: Al-Muyassar fi 'Ilm at-Tajweed - Dr. Ghanem Qaddouri Al-Hamad
description_short:
“Al-Muyassar fi ‘Ilm at-Tajweed” is an educational book that meets the needs of those enrolled in courses to improve the recitation of the Holy Quran. The objective of this book is to facilitate the teaching and learning of the rules of Tajweed, based on the first sources of the science of Tajweed, and to benefit from the findings of linguistic phonology in terms of facts related to the nature of the linguistic sound, how it is produced and its diversity.

The author defines the science of Tajweed and mentions its principles, and shows how to pronounce linguistic sounds and their characteristics, the work of the articulators in the oral cavity, and the exits of letters and their characteristics. Then he shows the provisions of improving the phonetic letters: tarqiq (vocal thining), Tafkhim (emphatic articulation), al-Idgham (merging a non-vowel with a vowel) and its types, and the rulings of extension and shortening.

It concludes with a statement of the complements of quality recitation, which are the provisions of stopping and starting, and related issues of Quranic manuscripts.

name: At-Taqrib wal-Taysir - Al-Nawawi (Ulum al-Hadith)
description_short:
A book that examines the Noble Hadith terminology, presenting all forms of this science, such as Sahih (Sound), Hasan (Good), Daeef (Weak), Munkar (denounced), Mufassal (detailed), and the Mudallas (Deceitful). It also addresses the numerous hadiths and their rulings, the abrogating and abrogated, the chains of narrators and those whose narration was accepted, as well as the remaining subjects relevant to this science.

In his introduction, the author mentioned that at-Taqrîb is the abridgement of another of his works, the Irshâd al-Hadîth, itself abridged from Ibn al-Salah’s “Introduction to the Sciences of Hadith:

“The science of hadith is one of the best means of drawing closer to the Lord of the worlds, and how could it not be? It is a clarification of the path of the best of creation and the most honourable of the first and the last. This is a book that I have abridged from the book “Irshâd”, itself abridged from the sciences of hadith by the sheikh, the Imam, the meticulous hafiz, Abu Amr Uthman Ibn Abdul-Rahman, known as Ibn as-Salah, may Allah be pleased with him. I will try to abridge it, Allah willing, without prejudice to what is intended, seeking to clarify the phrase, and upon Allah the Most Generous is the dependence and the reliance.”

A superb, high-quality edition, verified from 6 manuscripts, with a beautiful layout and some of the Harakats.

name: Diwan ad-Du’afa’ wal-Matrukin - Imam Al-Dhahabi
description_short:
The writer of this book is Imam Al-Hafiz Shams Al-Din Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ahmed ibn ‘Uthman ibn Qaymaz Al-Dhahabi Al-Damashqi Al-Hanbali, the Hadith scholar and historian of the Levant. He was born in the year 673 A.H in Kafr Batna, Ghouta, Damascus, and he sought the Hadith knowledge at the age of eighteen. He rose to prominence in the arts of Hadith, especially in the sciences of Hadith narrators. He presided over the sheikhdom of Al-Dhahiriya in the past, and devoted himself to authoring and compiling. Therefore, he wrote a lot of knowledge and compiled useful books, the longest of which is Tarikh al-Islam, and one of the best is Mizan al-I’tidal. Ibn Taghri Bardi has listed sixty-five books for him in Al-Manhal Al-Safi.

Ibn Shakir al-Kibti said about Imam al-Dhahabi: “He mastered the Hadith and its narrators, examined its causes and conditions, knew the narrators’ biographies, and removed any ambiguity or injustice therein. He made numerous collections and resorted to abridging to avoid extensive compilations. Among his exploits is this book, “Diwan ad-Du’afa’ wal-Matrukin”, in addition to his published books on Al-Jarh and Ta’deel (Science of Criticism and Praise). Because of this book’s importance, it was taken care of in terms of control, scrutiny, investigation and commentary, and then it came out in this edition in a contemporary scientific form.

Serious edition verified from 4 manuscripts.

name: Al-Kashif fi Ma'rifat man Lahu Riwayat fi Kutub Al-Sittah - Al-Dhahabi
description_short:
Al-Kashif fi Ma'rifat man Lahu Riwayat fi Kutub Al-Sittat (Discovering cognition in those for whom there is narration in the Six Books) - Adh-Dhahabi

A book written by Imam Al-Hafiz Adh-Dhahabi, may Allah Almighty have mercy on him, and “Al-Kashif” suffices to be one of his works. Al-Kashif is the fourth in a series of books on this discipline, and it is more of a training and teaching manual than a reference book. The first book is the book of Al-Hafiz Al-Maqdisi, who died in the year (600 AH), who wrote “Al-Kamal fi Asma’ Al-Rijal”, then followed by Al-Hafiz Al-Mazzi, who died in the year (742 AH), and wrote “Tahdheeb Al-Kamaal”, then Al-Hafiz Adh-Dhahabi wrote the third book in the series and called it: “Tadhheeb Tahdheeb al-Kamal,” then he added the fourth, which is “Al-Kashif,” which is the fourth of the golden series.

The Imam took great care of his book, and the researcher, scholar Muhammad Awama - may Allah Almighty protect him - was not satisfied with this precious book, but rather added another masterpiece, and an invaluable gem, namely, "Haashiyat al-Imam Burhan ad-Din Sibt Ibn al-Aajmi al al-Kashif " (The footnote of al-Imam Burhan ad-Din, the grandson of Ibn al-Ajami on al-Kashif," and in his handwriting as well, so the two books became flaunting in a new look.

Therefore, it is a thrill and pleasure to give such books of these men who have bequeathed upon us a summary of their knowledge, which a student of knowledge, let alone others, cannot do without. So here is this masterpiece, which we ask Allah to reward them greatly for their good deeds.

name: Kitab al-Wara' by Imam Ahmad reported by Abu Bakr Al-Marouzi (275H)
description_short:
This classical masterpiece serves as a foundational guide to the spiritual and ethical rigor of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, specifically through the transmission of his close companion, Abu Bakr al-Marwazi. The work explores the concept of Wara' (scrupulousness)—the practice of avoiding not only the forbidden but also the doubtful—as a means of purifying the heart and perfecting one's faith. This particular edition is a landmark in Hanbali studies, as it includes marginalia, commentaries, and additions that are being published for the first time, offering unprecedented depth into the practical application of piety in the early generations.

The methodology of the book relies on a series of anecdotes, rulings, and responses provided by Imam Ahmad, reflecting his legendary caution in matters of worship and daily transactions. Appended to the main text is a specialized collection of Quranic exegesis (Tafsir) narrated by al-Marwazi from Imam Ahmad, providing a rare glimpse into the Imam's approach to interpreting specific verses.

name: Manasik al-Hajj (Pilgrimage rituals) by Imam Khalil
description_short:
The book “Mansik Khalil” or “Manasik al-Hajj” by the famous jurist and scholar, Sheikh “Abu al-Mawaddah Khalil ibn Ishaq ibn Musa al-Jundi al-Masri, famously known as Sheikh Khalil, the author of the famous al-Mukhtasar (d. 776 AH)”, is considered one of the most important books of Maliki jurisprudence, exclusively on the Hajj rituals, which is one of the five pillars of Islam; but the importance of this book lies in the status of its author: Sheikh Khalil is one of the prominent imams of the madhhab who were famous for their well edited compilations.

The contents of the book “Manaasik Sheikh Khalil” are divided into seven chapters. The first: the virtue of Hajj, its obligation, the etiquette of travel, the times of Hajj, and the ruling on the actions that occur during the pilgrimage. The second: Ihram, its rituals, aspects, and prohibitions. The third: Entering Makkah, the actions of Hajj from beginning to end, and explaining its pillars, highly recommended and voluntary acts, and the pilgrimage of the boy and the slave. The fourth: The subsequent and eventual acts of Hajj; the prohibited acts, hiring someone to perform it on one’s behalf, the provisions of Umrah, and the farewell circumambulation. The fifth: Residing in Makkah and the rules related to it, the Haram (sanctity of the City), the Haram Mosque, the Kaaba (House of Allah) and what is related to that. The sixth: visiting the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in Madinah. The seventh: visiting Al-Quds and Al-Khalil, peace be upon him, in Palestine. It should be noted that the book contains important warnings on many prohibited matters that pilgrims fall into.

description_short:
Ila Mata al-Khisam? is a touching and practical social guide by Sheikh Abd al-Latif bin Hajis al-Ghamdi, centered on the Islamic ethics of reconciliation and the dangers of prolonged disputes. Written with a deep sense of pastoral care, the book addresses the common causes of conflict between relatives, friends, and neighbors, urging believers to revive the Prophetic virtue of pardoning others. The author combines Quranic verses, Prophetic traditions, and moving anecdotes to illustrate how holding onto grudges harms one's spiritual health and community cohesion, ultimately asking the reader: "Until when will this estrangement continue?"

The book serves as both a spiritual reminder and a practical manual for repairing broken relationships. Sheikh al-Ghamdi provides a step-by-step approach to overcoming pride and initiating peace, emphasizing the immense rewards promised to those who reconcile people. It is an ideal read for anyone seeking to purify their heart from resentment or looking for a way to bridge the gap with loved ones. Its accessible style makes it a valuable resource for general readers, educators, and social counselors focused on building a harmonious and forgiving society.

name: 'Ilm Tabaqat al-Mufassirin - Generations of Exegetes of the Qur'an
description_short:
Charting the historical evolution of Quranic exegesis through the science of tabaqat al-mufassirin — the discipline of classifying exegetes across their historical and methodological generations. Rather than merely compiling a list of biographies, the study structurally analyzes the very discipline of tabaqat literature — its origins, its rules, its sources, and the methodologies of its practitioners — providing the student with an analytical map for navigating the vast body of tafsir literature.

Books of tabaqat are plentiful, but a dedicated study of the science of tabaqat itself at this level is rare. A work that equips the talib al-‘ilm with the critical tools to evaluate the methodologies, historical context, and scholarly weight of exegetes throughout Islamic history. Authored by the researcher Zahra bint ‘Ubaydillah al-Ghamidi as a university thesis, endorsed by four senior specialists in Quranic studies led by Prof. Dr. Fahd al-Rumi.

Al-Thamarat al-Raiqah fi Ilm al-Arabiyyah is a concise and highly beneficial treatise on Arabic grammar authored by the prolific Hanbali polymath, Imam Ibn al-Mubarrad (d. 909H). This work serves as an introductory primer designed to simplify the complexities of Nahw (syntax) for beginning students. Ibn al-Mubarrad, known for his vast contributions across many Islamic sciences, employs a pedagogical style that focuses on the core rules of the Arabic language, presenting them in a structured manner that facilitates quick comprehension and retention of foundational grammatical concepts.

The treatise is valued for its clarity and its focus on the essential aspects of Arabic grammar without delving into the exhaustive longitudinal disputes between different grammatical schools. By providing clear definitions and illustrative examples, the author offers a "splendid fruit" for learners who wish to rectify their speech and understand the structural beauty of the language. This work is an excellent choice for students of the Islamic sciences who require a solid, traditional grounding in Arabic as a prerequisite for deeper study in Tafsir, Hadith, and Fiqh.

name: Ahkam al-Qur'an - Ahmad ibn Ali Al-Razi Al-Jassas (Hanafi)
description_short:
Ahkam Al-Qur’an is a book of jurisprudential interpretation of the Holy Qur’an according to the Hanafi School of Thought, written by Abu Bakr Al-Jassas. Its author deduces the verses of rulings, while mentioning the difference among scholars, then he expands on mentioning the evidence extensively from the Book, the Sunnah, the Arabic language, and mental process of contemplation.

The book collects issues with evidence of the Hanafis on them, and discusses the evidence of the opponents and refutes them; he shows their weaknesses while confirming some of them. The book highlighted the Hanafi jurisprudence through his book, and filled a loophole for the Hanafis in this section.

The book was distinguished by several advantages: its comprehension of the verses of rulings; it clarifies the disagreement of the predecessors regarding these verses, and shows the disagreement of scholars regarding the rulings of the verses, mentioning the evidence of each party. It often mentions the Hadiths and traditions with their chains of transmission and discusses some of them.

The author of this book was a leading Hanafi imam in his era. He singled out the verses of rulings in the Holy Qur’an, and extracted from them what can be learned from jurisprudential rulings, based on other verses, on the Hadiths of the Prophet and the reasons for their Revelation, in addition to the opinions of jurists and the leaders of the Schools of Thought. This science falls under the jurisprudential interpretation of the Holy Quran.

Beautiful Lebanese edition, a very large volume of over 1600 pages.

name: Irshad al-'Aql as-Salim - Tafsir Abi al-Su'ud (Hanafi) - 9 volumes
description_short:
In the introduction to his Interpretation, Abu As-Saud states that after reading "Al-Kashshaf" by Az-Zamakhshari and "Anwar At-Tanzil" by Al-Baydawi, he decided to write an interpretation that would combine the benefits of these two interpretations and add the benefits obtained from other interpretations. So he wrote this interpretation in which the eloquence and miraculousness of the Qur'an were manifested; he also mentioned the subtle benefits and wonderful wisdom indicated by each Verse and the rare rhetorical anecdotes, and he also refers to the readings and aspects of syntax and explains the meaning of the Verse accordingly, without much detail.

He also presents the jurisprudential issues learned from the Verse, and without digression alludes to the opinions of the scholars of the four religious schools of Islamic jurisprudence, but he emphasizes and favors the sayings of the Hanafi scholar.

The Interpretation comprised various points, the most notable of which were:

  • His interest in revealing the eloquence of the Qur’an and the secret of its miraculousness;
  • His interest in events and his familiarity with some readings;
  • Lack of mentioning Isrā'īliyyāt (The word Isrā'īliyyāt refers to the stories and narratives from Jewish sources);
  • His narration on some of the famous lies;
  • Lack of mentioning jurisprudence issues;
  • Mentioning what the Verses imply from the faces of the syntax.

Published for the first time from the author's manuscript, with a meticulous Tahqiq.

name: 'Uyun Al-Adillah fi Masa-il al-Khilaf bayna Fuqahaa, Ibn Qassar (397H)
description_short:
The book “‘Uyun Al-Adillah” by Ibn al-Qassar is regarded as an original reference in the high dispute among the early jurists; and the book has a place among the works of istidlal (inference) and tarjih (giving preponderance). Many of those who came after him were influenced by his approach, whether from the Maliki scholars or others who dealt with the science of khilaf (different opinions), or those who were concerned with the rulings upon the arguments and evidence from the people of the fifth and sixth centuries. It is also considered as one of the oldest books that have reached us of jurisprudence written on the high dispute, in addition to being one of the books that gave jurisprudential care to the inference with textual and rational evidence.

In it, Ibn al-Qassar al-Maliki collected a large number of controversial issues, reaching one thousand four hundred and forty issues (1440). The author’s lengthy analysis appears in mentioning extensive discussions and responding to objections, and this may be repeated several times in the same evidence.

Many scholars’ have praised this work, which was vastly approved. Al-Shirazi said in the author’s biography: “He has a great book on issues of disagreement. I do not know of a better book on disagreement.” Abu Hamid Al-Isfaraini said about him: Your friend - meaning Ibn al-Qassar – has not left anything for someone to say.” Judge Abdul Wahhab ibn Ali ibn Nasr.

An excellent, verified and annotated edition.

name: Nusrat ul-Qawlayn (Ibn al-Qass) & Haqiqat ul-Qawlayn (Al-Ghazali)
description_short:
The book is of great and useful scientific importance. It is a well-known fundamental issue of Ash-Shafi’i school of thought (Madhhab). Ash-Shafi’i, as well as other imams, may have expressed two opinions regarding some issues without clarifying the correct one. Some of the Hanafi and Mu’tazilites scholars became increasingly critical of ash-Shafi’i in this matter, so it became one of the issues of disagreement between the Hanafi and ash-Shafi’i schools first, and then it became one of the issues of the principles of jurisprudence recorded in his books. Some of ash-Shafi’i’s scholars have assigned books to it, such as Ibn al-Qass and al-Ghazali.

Explaining a single issue to different opinions; he explained the issue of the two opinions with ten explanations, which is the goal of the entire manuscript. The author has mentioned several chapters that serve as an introduction at the beginning of the book, out of his desire to achieve his goal. After understanding these ten explanations of the issues of the two opinions and the author’s purpose in explaining them, it is possible to read ash-Shafi’i’s Madhhab accordingly and understand the differences reported from Imam Ash-Shafi’i, may Allah be pleased with him.

The book includes "The Reality of the Two Opinions" by Abu Hamid al-Ghazali, may Allah have mercy on him.

An excellent, verified and annotated edition.

name: Categories and characteristics of Halal and Haram to Imam Shafi'i
description_short:
The book is authored by the esteemed jurist and usuli scholar Abu Bakr Ahmad Al-Khaffaf Al-Shafi'i (345H). It addresses the subject of categories and characteristics as a science, explaining the methods of divisions and types. When a scholar discusses a topic, he may say, for example, that it falls into three categories or that a particular attribute has ten characteristics, and so on. This approach was commonly employed by early scholars.

Al-Khaffaf, may Allah have mercy on him, structured his jurisprudential book following the method of the Shafi'i scholars of Iraq. Additionally, he provided an unprecedented introduction in Usul to the book.

Dr. Adnan bin Zaid bin Muhammad Al-Fahmi, in his introduction, states that there is no known text of an introduction in Usul that encompasses almost all Usul issues after Al-Shafi'i's Risala except for the introduction to the book "Categories and Characteristics." Al-Khaffaf concluded this introduction with a discussion on the art of debating, making him among the first to write on this subject.

The book is introduced by Sheikh Dr. Salih ibn Abdallah al-Humayd, who speaks about the emergence of jurisprudential schools, their merits, and characteristics.

Excellent Saudi edition with most of the Harakat.

This book is a scientific treatise that provides an explanation of a well-known foundational abridgment (Mukhtasar), namely Ibn Al-Hajib's abridgment derived from his book "Muntaha al-Su'al wa al-Amal." Ibn Al-Hajib's Mukhtasar is among the go-to books in the science of Usul, and it has many commentaries, several of which the researcher has mentioned in this book.

The book currently in our hands is one of the early commentaries, printed for the first time under the title: "Explanation of Ibn Al-Hajib's Abridgment on Usul," authored by the distinguished scholar, Osman bin Ali, known as Ibn Khateeb Jabreen Al-Halabi Al-Shafi'I (739 A.H.), may Allah have mercy on him.

The researcher, Dr. Amal bint Abdul Rahman bin Saleh Al-Ghufays, has meticulously researched and annotated the book, relying on a unique manuscript from the author's era. The book's methodology involves presenting Ibn Al-Hajib's words from his abridgment, followed by the commentary of Ibn Khateeb along with side headings explaining the origin of the mentioned issue. Subsequently, the researcher provides her own comments. The book is filled with comparisons between the abridgment and the original book from which it was derived ("Muntaha al-Su'al wa al-Amal"), Ibn Al-Hajib's statements in his other books, and comparisons with the commentaries of other scholars who wrote their own books about the abridgment.

The book is printed in two large volumes by Dar Taybah Al-Khadra in Mecca.

name: Salah Ad-Din (Saladin) - Shakir Mustafa
description_short:
When Salah Ad-din lived 800 years ago, in the late sixth century AH, the twelfth centuries AD, his name sounded like a big storm. Like a great eagle, this name swept across the entirety of Islam and the West. No Muslim heart remains on earth that did not cheer for him, and no heart remains in the West that does not shudder in dread of him. Even those whose views and teachings he had demolished waited for him to pass away in order to try to discredit him in some way.

One may ponder what it means to attack and attempt to destroy a noble symbol that came before us. Or do you strive to destroy it without considering the time, the situation, the conditions that have passed, or the reality of the contemporary Zionism conflict? As though we had completed fixing everything and this monument was the last thing left to be demolished!

This book is neither a reaction nor a starting point for a debate on a topic where the rule ended 900 years ago. Its sole purpose is to examine Salah ad-Din, the man, the politician, the strategic leader, and the Islamic hero, in the context of his time and within the parameters of that time - its conditions and notions. So, if this book can refute slander, expose misguidance, or reveal the truth, that is sufficient. The area of history is the rulings of existence, and there are a thousand and one judges for the rulings of values; or do we want our heroes or some humans to be superhuman?

name: Nahu al-Basriyyin - The Grammar of Basrah
description_short:
The Grammar of the Basrans between the metalingual function and the linguistic reality by Ibrahim Muhammad Ibrahim Dawood

The purpose of this study is to explain the grammar foundations of the Basra school, as opposed to the Kufi school, those two pioneering schools that dominated the science of Arabic grammar for many centuries, and whose debates were one of the tributaries and sources of the development of Arabic grammar, as well as the large number of works in it.

The author writes "...The breadth of schools of Arabic grammar and the diversity of their differences is nothing more than a reflection of the language’s flexibility and the breadth of its paths, and reveals the nature of the text that is not characterised by stagnation, and the different approaches of the Arab mind.”

The Basran method is focused on rule consistency and not surrendering to the aberrant and unusual, but the Kufan approach is based on taking into consideration all that comes from the Arabs. We are faced with two ways, the first of which is a logical approach and the second of which is a transmission approach, with a hundred years, separating the two.

There is little question that these two techniques represent the Arab’s zeal for his language, which cooled the debate among Baghdadis, who absorbed the two ideas and saw no alternative but to accept them. The Baghdadis did not stop at adoption, but instead added their idea and attitude, which is rational. It is a continuation of the development year, and it considers the reasons of mental growth; we will discuss all of these ways in depth in the introduction that we have written for this research, God willing.

name: Fasih al-Kalam - Muhammad ibn Ali al-Ghaznawi (442H)
description_short:
This book is a classical Arabic linguistic text written as a lexicographical supplement (dhayl) to the famous Kitab al-Fasih by Abu al-Abbas Tha'lab (d. 291 AH). The author, Abu al-Fawa'id Muhammad bin Ali al-Ghaznawi (d. after 442 AH), was an early grammarian who compiled this work to preserve and explain eloquent vocabulary that was omitted in the original master text. He titled it Faseeh al-Kalam to provide speakers with an expanded vocabulary, making it an essential reference for students tracking the historical expansion of early Arabic dictionaries and classical prose.

The text is structured alphabetically according to the Arabic alphabet, featuring over one thousand correct words and phrases that complement Tha'lab's dictionary. Al-Ghaznawi defines each entry with precise semantic distinctions, supporting his explanations with textual evidence from the Quran, prophetic traditions, and classical pre-Islamic Arabic poetry. This edition, critically edited from rare manuscripts and published by Maktabat al-Rushd, provides researchers with a clean, fully vocalized text that highlights early linguistic derivation without later scholastic additions.

name: Ma'ani al-Qur'an wa Tafsir I'rabihi - Qutrub the Grammarian (214H)
description_short:
One of the earliest works ever composed on Quranic linguistics and syntax, written by Imam Qutrub (d. 206 AH), who was historically known as a premier student of Sibawayh and the first to compile linguistic triplets (Muthallathat), it serves as a foundational source for understanding the lexical meanings and grammatical challenges of the Quranic text. The text provides an early Basran perspective on classical grammar by analyzing obscure vocabulary, phonetic shifts, and problematic parsing (i'rab) found in individual verses.

The book is distinguished by its preservation of early Arab dialects and its detailed chapter structure that addresses difficult vocalizations, marshalling evidences from pre-Islamic poetry and transmitted oral traditions. The work is structured chronologically according to the chapters of the Quran, utilizing classical linguistic analysis to validate each grammatical point, making it an indispensable reference for students in the field of Arabic lexicography and a living witness to the early evolution of grammatical thought in the 3rd century of the Hijrah.

name: Tasmiyat man Rawa Al-Muwatta ‘an Malik ibn Anas + 2 Risalah
description_short:
This book originated from a precious manuscript by one of the scholars of Andalusia, Abu al-Abbas al-Siqilli, who wrote it in the year 542 Hijri. It contains a collection of works which are very useful in the Maliki school of thought. Adel bin Ali O-Aasim extracted these separate works from the manuscript, verified them, and provided commentary in this elegant volume. This edition includes three original works:

1. “Tasmiyat man Rawa Al-Muwatta ‘an Malik bin Anas”, written by Hibat Allah bin Ahmad bin al-Akfani (d. 524 A.H.). In this book, Al-Akfani mentions 48 Imams who narrated Al-Muwatta from Malik. The editor provides their biographies and discusses their narrations of Al-Muwatta, whether printed or transmitted, along with other scholarly details.

2. “Names of the scholars from whom Malik narrated in Al-Muwatta,” written by Ibn al-Qassaar al-Siqilli, in whose handwriting the whole manuscript collection was written.

3. “The testament of Imam Malik to students of knowledge,” heard from Imam Yahya bin Yahya al-Andalusi, a well-known narrator of Al-Muwatta (d. 234 A. H.). Despite its brevity, the testament contains extremely valuable guidance for students of knowledge.

description_short:

The author of the annotations explains his method:

I wrote this commentary to further explain the treasures contained in "Riyad as-Salihin," and to highlight the most important lessons derived from its hadiths.

My Methodology in the book:

1. I used the edition by Maher Al-Fahl as the primary source. I also benefited from the editions by Dar Al-Minhaj and Dar Ibn Al-Jawzi.

2. I provided a brief explanation of unfamiliar words in the hadiths, if any, below each hadith.

3. I highlighted the most important lessons to be drawn from each hadith, distinguishing them from the book's text. I referred to the explanations of scholars in the books of Sunnah and books of commentary on "Riyad as-Salihin." I made sure to mention the benefits of all the hadiths, including those whose deemed unauthentic by Sheikh Al-Albani, with appropriate references.

4. When paraphrasing other scholars about the benefits of the hadiths, I made sure to use simple language that reaches the targeted audience of the book without deviating from the intended meaning of the authors.

5. I attributed the hadiths to the sources mentioned by the an-Nawawi. If a hadith is not narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, I specified its rank in terms of authenticity or weakness according to the scholars of hadith, especially Sheikh Al-Albani.

The inclusion of the Mukhtasar (abridgment) within the same volume makes it a versatile tool, catering to both the dedicated researcher and the student looking for a concise, high-level reference.

The author focuses on the practical fruits of knowing Allah, linking each attribute to the refinement of human character and the pursuit of an honorable, virtuous life. The commentary is structured to be academically rigorous yet accessible, prioritizing the most sublime meanings derived directly from the Quran and authentic Prophetic tradition. By providing both the expansive explanation and a distilled summary, al-Musai'id ensures that the core message—that the knowledge of the Creator is the foundation of all true wisdom—is easily retained and applied in daily worship and conduct.

Included with the hardcover edition is a small paperback suitable for memorization or as a travel companion, which includes the Beautiful Names of Allah and their meanings.

name: Aqwal at-Tabi'in fi Masa-il at-Tawhid wa al-Iman - AbdulAziz al-Mudbal
description_short:
This book is a contemporary academic study that compiles, examines, and verifies the theological statements made by the Successors (Tabi'in) regarding monotheism and faith. Written by Dr. Abdulaziz bin Abdullah al-Mubaddal as a doctoral thesis at Umm Al-Qura University, the work features introductory forewords by the prominent scholars Sheikh Abdullah al-Ghunayman and Professor Sheikh Ali bin Nafi’ al-‘Alyani. The main objective of the research is to demonstrate that the generation following the Companions maintained the exact same scriptural methodology in theology, showing no deviation or innovation in foundational creed.

The text compiles over 1,500 distinct narrations (athar) organized systematically into standard categories of Islamic theology, including Tawhid al-Uloohiyyah, Tawhid al-Rububiyyah, Allah's names and attributes, and the technical definitions of faith (Iman). Al-Mubaddal isolates every report from early source texts, provides its full chain of transmission, and delivers a rigorous critical grading (tahqiq) to establish the historical authenticity of each narration. This methodical, text-based structure makes the two-volume set a primary source for studying the preservation of early Athari creed.

name: Hadiths on the Virtues of the Surahs of the Holy Qur’an
description_short:
An extremely useful and interesting work that brings together all the prophetic narrations concerning the merits of the suras of the Qur'an. 

Scholars throughout history have paid great attention to the purified Sunnah and made every effort to safeguard it, whether by collecting editing it, criticizing it, studying its chains of transmission, or deriving rulings from it. This research, which was initially a PhD dissertation, examined all of the Ahadiths and narrations found in the virtues of the Surahs of the Holy Qur'an.

The book is divided into two sections: the accepted segment, which includes authentic and good Ahadiths and narrations, as well as weak ones that are reliable, as well as evaluating each hadith or narration and describing its status of authenticity, good, or reliability. The second section is the rejected section of hadiths and narrations, which are extremely weak, fabricated, and well-known Ahadiths and narrations, with a study of the reasons for their fabrication, an explanation of those accused of fabricating them, and an explanation of their current status.

For all the Hadiths cited, there are detailed annotations concerning their degree of authenticity.
