name: Kitab at-Tawhid - Muhammad at-Tuwaijri
description_short:
Built entirely on the evidences of the Quran and the authentic Sunnah, this comprehensive work addresses the oneness and absolute perfection of Allah. Sheikh Muhammad ibn Ibrahim at-Tuwayjiri outlines the three categories of Tawhid—ar-Rububiyyah, al-Uluhiyyah, and al-Asma wa as-Sifat—before dedicating the vast majority of the volume to an extensive study of the Divine Names and Attributes. Drawing directly upon Quranic verses and prophetic narrations, the text examines each Name and Attribute in detail, demonstrating how the sound knowledge of Allah forms the very foundation of faith and worship.

True to the author's emphasis on connecting creed with devotion and the actions of the heart, the book presents Tawhid as an active reality that cultivates love, reverent fear, hope, and reliance upon Allah. By grounding theological instruction in practical servitude ('ubudiyyah), this work serves as an expansive reference on the Names and Attributes of Allah, well suited for students of knowledge, teachers, and study circles seeking a scripture-centered manual on Islamic monotheism.

name: Bada-i' as-Sana-i' fi Tartib ash-Shara-i' - al-Kasani Al-Hanafi
description_short:
It is one of the books dealing with the branches of Hanafi jurisprudence; a comprehensive book covering the Chapters of Islamic jurisprudence according to the Four Schools of Thought. It was composed by Imam 'Ala' al-Din al-Kasani Al-Hanafi, who died in 587 AH. It is a commentary on Sheikh Alaa al-Din al-Samarqandi's Hanafi work, “Tuhfat al-Fuqaha,” which is a commentary on Mukhtasar al-Qadduri. The author has organized the issues in this commentary around the evidence. He discusses the difference between Hanafi jurists and other jurists of different Schools of Thought, providing brief evidence for each; then he prefers one of them when he says “our” and explains it in depth.

He primarily cites the opinions of Abu Hanifa and his two companions, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad Ibn Al-Hasan Al-Shaybani, as well as Zufar Ibn Al-Hudhayl and Ash-Shafi'i, and analyzes the evidence for each of their claims. The book is noteworthy by its simple language and use of Hadith evidence to support the jurisprudential rulings it includes.

name: Al-Awsat min as-Sunan wa al-Ijma' wa al-Ikhtilaf - Imam Ibn Al-Mundhir
description_short:
The Book of Al-Awsat is one of the greatest and most important jurisprudence books ever written. It is considered to be an encyclopaedia of the jurisprudence of the Companions, the Followers, and those below them (including the four Imams). This book is distinguished from other jurisprudence texts by its advantages, such as its classification as a jurisprudence encyclopaedia, particularly in terms of the doctrines of the scholars and their areas of agreement and disagreement.

The book is divided into jurisprudence chapters, which are listed below. The translation is based on the issues on which there is agreement and the disputed issues falling under the chapter.

Each chapter mentions the doctrines of Companions, Followers, Companions, and the four Imams, citing the hadiths or narrations of each group as proof.

The book of al-Awsat is distinguished by the fact that it records what it receives from the scholars, whether it comes from them to report it, or it comes from their books or from their students, etc. Ibn al-Mundhir is notable in his book because he does not prefer one School of Thought to another, nor does he prefer one School to another. He prefers what he believes to be correct, so he narrates it and follows it. He is also different in the scope of his narration because he produces narrations that you might not find anywhere else. He also discusses the authenticity of the Hadith and chains of its narrations, whether they are true or not, and about the narrators, if they are good or bad. He has quoted in his book other works that have not yet reached us.

name: Mafhum al-Bid'ah by Dr Abd al-Ilah al-'Arfaj
description_short:
This book is a one of the very interesting, yet controverted books that researchers have written on innovations, both past and present. It classifies heresy as five categories: the mandatory, recommended, reasonable, disdained and prohibited, thereby aiming to dispel the myth that all types of bid’ah are misleading. Even though this classification has already been highlighted by others, this book is distinguished by the examples and evidence that the author has assembled and worked hard to collect.

In the opening pages of his book, Dr. Al-Arfaj clarified that his intention was not to promote religious innovation, but rather to define what constitutes repugnant innovation and make clear the distinctions between it and the other 36 issues on which scholars have disagreed from the Companions and Successors and, later, from the great imams in the Salaf eras. “Some opinions described the issue - under dispute - as an innovation, and some described it as permissible, desirable, or legitimate,” he said, elucidating the good Sunnah in Islam. Allah knows, what I intended to convey to all Muslims through the listing of these issues was not to force them to accept every new invention under the guise of “the scholars differed in their opinions about heresy,” but firstly to rather liberate the precise definition of heresy from difficult situations, and secondly, to highlight the fact that the distinction between what constitutes heresy and legitimate religious innovations, particularly those related to science, can fall within the bounds of permissible disagreements and centre around the idea that “between right and wrong, it needs not be all between truth and falsehood.”

description_short:
The book "My Journey with Imam Al-Shafi'i and His Book Al-Risalah," written by Dr. Fahd bin Saad Al-Johani, provides an enriching journey into the life of Imam Al-Shafi'i and his seminal work, "Al-Risalah." 

The book is divided into two sections: a biography of Imam Al-Shafi'i and a study of "Al-Risalah," focusing on its origin, content, methodology, importance, and impact on Islamic jurisprudence. Key points in the book include a comprehensive overview of Imam Al-Shafi'i's life, his contributions to Islamic jurisprudence, the history and significance of "Al-Risalah," and the author's personal connection to Imam Al-Shafi'i and his book.

The author's deep understanding and analysis of "Al-Risalah" provide valuable insights into the work and its enduring relevance. The book is praised by scholars for its successful efforts in presenting Imam Al-Shafi'i's efforts in establishing the principles of jurisprudence. 

Overall, the book is a valuable resource for anyone interested in Islamic jurisprudence, Islamic history, or the life and thought of Imam Al-Shafi'i.

name: Annotations of Najdi Scholars on ar-Rawd al-Murbi
description_short:
This scholarly work, compiled and edited by Sheikh Ahmad Al-Jammaz, is a valuable contribution that reveals the efforts of Najdi scholars in advancing Hanbali Fiqh. The author meticulously studied eighteen manuscript copies of Ar-Rawd al-Murbi', extracting the diverse annotations and marginalia of Najdi scholars, which include evidential reasoning, justifications, preferred opinions, and critical notes. Through this work, the author highlights the significant role played by scholars of the reform movement (followers of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab) in the field of jurisprudence, demonstrating that they were accomplished jurists whose interests extended beyond matters of Aqidah, contrary to common perception.

This book stands out for its precise scholarly methodology in collecting and organizing annotations and commentaries. The author created special symbols for each manuscript and scholar to facilitate reference, provided excellent biographical sketches of the scholars who wrote the annotations, and explained the distinctive features of each manuscript. This work represents a valuable addition to the Hanbali library and serves as an important reference for researchers interested in the intellectual history of the Najd region since the emergence of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab's reform movement.

name: Al-Isabah fi Tamayiz Al-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar : 12,000 biographies
description_short:
Al-Isaabah fi Tamyeez Al-Sahaabah is a comprehensive work by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani that focuses on detailing the biographies of the companions of the Prophet Muhammad. The book is respected for its depth and scope, covering over 12,000 biographies of companions and setting criteria for distinguishing between sound companions and others. Ibn Hajar spent forty years completing this monumental work, which spans from the pre-Islamic era to the death of the last recognized companion.

Ibn Hajar arranged the names of the companions alphabetically and divided them into four categories based on their association with the Prophet. He also referred to lost books and clarified misconceptions in previous works.

The book includes biographies of varying lengths, ranging from a few lines to several pages. It is considered a reference for scholars and researchers in Islamic history and hadith studies.

name: Afat Ashab al-Hadith wa-l-Radd 'ala 'Abd al-Mughith by Ibn al-Jawzi
description_short:
The book "Afat Ashab al-Hadith wa-l-Radd 'ala 'Abd al-Mughith" by Ibn al-Jawzi is a response by the renowned Hanbali scholar to the work of "Abd al-Mughith" which discussed some issues related to the science of Hadith. Ibn al-Jawzi describes the book as "few have heard of it, let alone seen it." The focus of the book is on highlighting some of the afflictions that may affect the narrators of Hadith, such as a lack of understanding and improper comprehension of the Hadiths.

The book also includes Ibn al-Jawzi's criticism of some Hadith scholars who are knowledgeable about the authenticity of Hadiths but are lacking in their understanding of jurisprudence. Additionally, the book discusses Ibn al-Jawzi's response to Abd al-Mughith and some of the issues raised in his work. ​The book is considered an important work in the field of Hadith sciences, offering a critical and corrective perspective on some of the problematic practices that may occur in this discipline. The report recommends further study of this work by students of knowledge and researchers in the field of Hadith and jurisprudence.

Great edition verified by Shaykh Sa'd ibn al-Humaid.

name: Al-Ilma' ila Ma'rifat Usul ar-Riwaya by Al-Qadi 'Iyadh (544H)
description_short:
The book "Al-Ilma' ila Ma'rifat Usul ar-Riwaya wa-Taqyid as-Sama'" is a book on the sciences of Hadith written by the Qadi ‘Iyad ibn Musa al-Yahsubi as-Sabti (d. 544 AH). In this book, Qadi Iyad explained the principles of hadith narration and the recording of hadith transmission. He addressed several fundamental topics, such as the etiquette of seeking knowledge and listening, the knowledge of that and its aspects and from whom it is taken, precision and recording, memorization and comprehension, and distinguishing and criticism to know the authentic, weak, good, accepted, abandoned, and fabricated hadith.

​This book is considered an important reference in the sciences of narration and hadith, as Qadi Iyad explained in it the principles of hadith narration and the recording of hadith transmission. Qadi Iyad's methodology in narration was based on verification, scrutiny, and authentication of the text, as he considered transmission and narration as the basis for establishing the authenticity of a hadith. He also emphasized the importance of scrutinizing the hadith text, which reflects the significance of this aspect in his approach. This book is considered an important reference in this field due to the precise rules and principles it contains in the sciences of narration and hadith.

Great edition verified by several searcher, supervised by Shaykh Sa'd ibn al-Humaid.

name: Al-Furooq al-Lughawiyyah fi Tafsir al-Kalimat al-Qur’aniyyah
description_short:
This book studies and analyzes the nuances between Quranic words that are close in meaning, such as "الجسم" (al-jism) and "الجسد" (al-jasad), "الأب" (al-ab) and "الوالد" (al-walid), "الألم" (al-alam) and "العذاب" (al-'adhab), etc. The author relates the opinions of Arabic scholars, Quran interpreters, and scholars who wrote on this subject, resulting in a rich and engaging content.

The book consists of two parts. The first part addresses the main topic: the nuances between Quranic words that are similar in meaning, arranged alphabetically. The second part is titled "Reflections on Words," aiming to focus on some of the Quranic insights that arise from understanding linguistic nuances between words. The author relies on "Lisan al-Arab" by Ibn Mandhoor for this part.

This is a wonderful book, beneficial in Tafsir and in Arabic sciences.

name: Alfiyyat Lisan al-Arab fi 'Ulum al-Adab - Zayn al-Din al-Athari (868H)
description_short:
The distinguished scholar and poet Zain al-Din al-Athari was known for his prolific composition. He composed numerous poems in the field of Arabic language, including the "Alfiyyat Mujmal al-Arab fi 'Ulum al-Adab," which he completed in the year 808 Hijri. A year later, he revisited it, preserving two-thirds of the original and adding and removing content. He named this revised work "Alfiyyat Lisan al-Arab fi 'Ulum al-Adab." In this work, he covered ten sciences of the Arabic language, such as morphology, calligraphy, rhyme, rhetoric, and more. He allocated around one hundred verses for each Arabic science, with a title for each, and he compiled these ten poems into a numbered "Alfiyya," creating a refined and revised masterpiece.

This work was edited by Muhammad bin Mahmood Aal-Rihab. One of the fruits of his labour was a very interesting comparison between the two versions of the "Alfiyyah."

Quality Saudi edition, with a neat and pleasant layout, 100% Harakat on the poem.

name: Scientism, the atheistic ideology of science by Dr Sami 'Amiri
description_short:
Scientism: A Critical Analysis

Scientism, a term derived from the word "science," is an ideology that seeks to interpret everything through the lens of laboratories, observatories, and microscopes. Within the new atheist movement, scientism has been elevated above the truths of reason and the tenets of religion. It stands unchallenged in its claims and uncontested in its authority.

Scientism goes beyond simply proclaiming the honor of scientific knowledge. It is, in essence, a declaration of the imperialism of experimentation. Scientism advocates for science to monopolize the balance of judgment, shaping the contours of all existence with a pen that knows only the dimensions of length, width, and depth, and the measurement of motion.

The book sheds light on the ideological exploitation of natural science and its achievements by scientism, and how all this is harnessed to serve atheism. Scientism claims that science is the companion of irreligion or secularism.

In this regard, the book stands as a pioneering work in Arabic literature. It examines scientism as an ideology, rather than limiting the debate to the traditional discourse in the East and West, which revolves around the relationship between science and religion, often focusing on the conflict between sacred texts and certain scientific discoveries.

name: Why Did the Muslims Decline and Why Did Others Progress?
description_short:
Shakib Arslan, also known as "The Eloquent Prince," was a prominent Lebanese thinker, historian, and diplomat. He lived during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, witnessing the collapse of the Ottoman Empire and the beginnings of the Arab Renaissance. He gained fame for his writings and lectures on Islamic issues, with his most notable work being the book "Why Did the Muslims Decline and Why Did Others Progress?"

In this book, Arslan attributes the decline of Muslims to a combination of factors, primarily the deviation from the core principles of Islam, leading to widespread corruption. He also highlights the political weakness that plagued the Islamic world, along with intellectual stagnation and scientific regression. Additionally, Arslan sheds light on the detrimental impact of Western colonialism. In contrast, Arslan explains the progress of the West as a result of their adherence to Christian values, political unity, scientific superiority, and the role of colonialism, which enabled them to exploit and benefit from the world's riches.

This highly instructive book was prepared and annotated by Sheikh Mashhour Al Salman, and benefits from numerous praiseworthy prefaces by the following Shuyukhs: Muhammad Rashid Rida, Ali at-Tantawi, Muhammad Taqi eddin al-Hilali, Ibn Badis...

description_short:
A book of biographies aimed at illustrating the virtues of the early generations of Islam, highlighting their asceticism, piety, devotion, worship, reverence for the Sharia, patience, and adoption of the morals of the prophets, along with their narrations related to self-purification. It was authored by the esteemed scholar Ibn al-Athir, the great linguist and hadith scholar, known for his book "Jami' al-Usul" and "Al-Nihaya fi Gharib al-Hadith." He is the brother of the historian Ibn al-Athir, the author of "Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh."

The book primarily relies on "Hilyat al-Awliya" and also selects from "Sifat as-Safwa" and other books concerning asceticism and heart-softening narrations. It includes biographies of the Companions, the Tabi'un, and those who followed them. The book is arranged alphabetically by letters, and each letter is divided into three sections: one for the Companions, another for the Tabi'un, and a third for those who are unknown or known by their kunya. Each biography includes the individual's state of asceticism and worship, followed by their sayings in this field.

This new edition relies on three recently discovered manuscripts in addition to three older ones, allowing the editors to review errors, fill gaps, and provide a good update of the book. The edition consists of six volumes, the last of which is for the indexes.

name: A Guide to the Causes and Treatment of Deviation, Abdulwahab Al-Hadhai
description_short:
This book is a contemporary two-volume study focused on analyzing the root causes of religious and behavioral deviation and providing practical treatments based on Islamic principles. The author, Abd al-Wahhab al-Hada'i, provides a comprehensive manual to help Muslims understand why individuals experience backsliding (intikasah) or stray from religious practice, whether partially or entirely. The work serves as an analytical reference for parents, educators, and students investigating the preservation of Islamic identity and faith stability.

The book is organized into two volumes, covering both theoretical causes and practical methodologies for correction. Al-Hada'i categorizes the causes of deviation into distinct spiritual, social, and intellectual factors, such as doubts (shubuhat), desires (shahawat), family breakdown, and negative peer groups. He follows this analysis with dedicated sections outlining practical remedies drawn from the Quran and Sunnah, including strengthening core creed, encouraging righteous companionship, and establishing preventative parenting methods to protect youth against ideological challenges.

It contains over 1069 alphabetically arranged animal entries, covering a wide range of species. The book provides detailed information on animal anatomy, behavior, reproduction, and environments, combining scientific accuracy with storytelling. The book also links scientific information about animals with cultural and historical backgrounds related to them in the Arab and Islamic heritage.

Al-Damiri aimed to correct erroneous information and incorporated personal experiences and experimental methods, relying on over 560 references including Aristotle and Al-Jahiz. "Hayat al-Hayawan al-Kubra" remains a valuable resource in the field of zoology and showcases Al-Damiri's commitment to scientific integrity and accuracy.

name: Hashiyat al-Qalyubi 'ala Sharh Ibn Qasim al-Ghazi 'ala Matn Abi Shuja
description_short:
The book "Hashiyat al-Qalyubi 'ala Sharh Ibn Qasim al-Ghazzi 'ala Matn Abi Shuja'" is one of the important jurisprudential books in Shafi'i fiqh. The text "Abi Shuja'" is considered one of the fundamental texts in Shafi'i fiqh, and its explanations and commentaries complement each other to explain the jurisprudential rulings in an extensive manner.

Components of the book:

- Hashiyah (Marginal Notes): Hashiyah is an extensive commentary on another scholar's explanation. In this book, the Hashiyah is authored by Sheikh Ahmad al-Qalyubi.

- Sharh (Explanation): Sharh is the interpretation and explanation of the original text (Matn Abi Shuja'), which was done by Sheikh Ahmad ibn Qasim al-Ghazzi.

- Matn (Text): The original text is "Matn Abi Shuja'" or "Ghayat al-Taqrib," authored by Abu Shuja' al-Asfahani, which is considered a primary introduction and reference for students of Shafi'i fiqh.

The book is used as an educational reference for students in intermediate and higher levels. It provides an extensive explanation of the jurisprudential texts, which helps students and scholars gain a deeper understanding of the Sharia rulings. The Hashiyah provides simplified commentaries that help resolve issues and clarify the branches of fiqh.

Gorgeous verified and annotated edition, with Harakats in part.

This is the first book to deal with this particular subject, it has been checked by Abdulqadir al-Arnaout, who added several useful annotations.

name: Kitab al-Mawa'idh by Imam Al-Qasim ibn Sallam (224H)
description_short:
This is a more comprehensive edition of a previously printed book, which is the Kitab al-Mawaa’idh by the great Imam Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim ibn Salam, may Allah have mercy on him, one of the prominent early scholars who excelled in the fields of language, recitations, and jurisprudence. He was a companion of Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

The editor of the previous edition was not well-versed in Hadith, its chains of transmission, and the narrators, which led to many Hadith-related errors, in addition to relying on a poor-quality manuscript. The editor of this new print, Farid bin Muhammad Fuwaila, provided a good biography of the author, discussed the old edition and manuscripts of the book, then presented the Hadiths of Kitab al-Mawaa’idh, elaborating on them with corrections, comments, explanations of defects, supporting evidence, and corroborations. He then added a long appendix narrated by Al-Qasim ibn Salam's student from his Sheikh. Thus, the book in our hands consists of two books: the well-known Kitab al-Mawaa’idh, and an additional Hadith section.

The first part includes the sermons of the prophets, then the sermons of Muhammad, peace be upon him, followed by the sermons of the companions, and so on. The second part, which is being published for the first time, includes 33 Hadiths with extensive verification and commentary.

name: Al-Insaf fi Masail al-Khilaf Bayn al-Nahwiyyin - Ibn al-Anbari
description_short:
Kamal al-Din al-Anbari's book "Al-Insaf fi Masail al-Khilaf Bayn al-Nahwiyyin al-Basriyyin wa al-Kufiyyin" (Equity in Matters of Disagreement Between the Basran and Kufan Grammarians) is a unique reference in its treatment of the grammatical differences between the schools of Al-Basra and Al-Kufa. Al-Anbari did not merely present these differences; he systematically analyzed them, clarifying the points of disagreement and agreement between the two schools, and using evidence and proofs to favor the most likely opinions.

In his book, al-Anbari focused on one hundred and twenty controversial issues, covering a wide range of Arabic grammar topics, such as inflection and syntax, derivation, and morphology. His presentation style is characterized by presenting the views of both the Basrans and Kufans in a balanced manner, mentioning the evidence and examples of each group, then moving on to a detailed analysis of these views, choosing the most likely one based on the strength of the evidence.

"Al-Insaf fi Masail al-Khilaf" is considered a valuable source for anyone interested in the Arabic language and its sciences, as it provides a clear vision of the grammatical differences between the Basran and Kufan schools and contributes to understanding the principles of each school and its approach to dealing with the language. The book is also distinguished by its precise scientific method in research and discussion, as it relies on evidence and proofs and avoids bias and prejudice.

name: Bulghat al-Wusul ila 'Ilm al-Usul (Mukhtasar al-Bulbul) - Al-Kinani
description_short:
This is a simple and accessible book on the principles of Islamic jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh), essentially a summary of a summary. The original work is Al-Mustasfa by Al-Ghazali, which was abridged by Ibn Qudamah in Rawdhat al-Nadhir. Then Al-Tufi further summarized Rawdhat al-Nadhir in his book Al-Bulbul. The book in our hands is a summary of Al-Bulbul, titled Bulghat al-Wusul ila ‘Ilm al-Usul. It is the final link in a valuable scholarly chain, reflecting its importance despite its small size.

The author preserved much of Al-Tufi's wording, added certain points, and critiqued others. He also drew from Ibn al-Hajib's Mukhtasar. This book is one of the core texts in usul al-fiqh that is recommended for explanation and study. It includes an elaborate introduction, in which the author lists and arranges the major Hanbali usul summaries in chronological order.

This work is considered one of the most important books in the science of Usul al-Fiqh (principles of Islamic jurisprudence), and focuses particularly on the Shafi'i school of thought.

The book is characterized by a comprehensive methodology in presenting jurisprudential issues, where it presents the opinions of scholars arranged in groups and balances between them. The author mentions the evidence and critiques it, explains the reasons for disagreement, and weighs and evaluates the different opinions.

Al-Zarkashi did not limit himself to jurisprudential references, but rather expanded to include books of Tafsir (Quranic exegesis), Hadith (Prophetic traditions), language, and Aqidah (Islamic creed). This book is considered an important reference in Usul al-Fiqh for its deep analysis of jurisprudential issues, along with an explanation of their foundations and ramifications.

name: Al-Muqaddimah al-Izziyah by Al-Manufi (Fiqh Maliki)
description_short:
The book "Al-Muqaddimah al-Izziyah for the Azhar Community", by the scholar and jurist Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Manufi al-Masri al-Shadhili al-Maliki (857-939 AH / 1453-1532 AD), is a text on Maliki jurisprudence. It is an abridged version of his book "Umdat al-Salik ala Madhhab al-Imam Malik" (The Support of the Traveler on the School of Imam Malik). The book consists of eleven chapters on acts of worship: including purification, prayer, zakat, fasting, i'tikaf, Hajj, sacrifice, expiations, and slaughter. It also includes chapters on transactions such as the eighth chapter, which is devoted to the rulings of marriage and divorce, and the ninth chapter on sales. The tenth chapter deals with inheritance, and finally, the eleventh chapter explains some general rules of obligations, Sunnahs, and manners.

In addition to the book "Al-Muqaddimah al-Izziyah", Abu al-Hasan al-Manufi has other works on Maliki jurisprudence, perhaps the most prominent of which is his book in which he explained the "Risala of Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani" entitled: "Kifayat al-Talib al-Rabbani ala Risalat Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani" (Sufficiency of the Devout Student on the Epistle of Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani).

Since al-Manufi authored "Al-Muqaddimah al-Izziyah", scholars have been keen on explaining, commenting on, and even versifying it.

name: Al-Istidhkar (Sharh al-Muwatta) - Hafidh Ibn Abdil-Barr
description_short:
The book "Al-Istidhkar al-Jami' li Madhahib Fuqaha' al-Amsar wa 'Ulama' al-Aqtar" was authored by al-Hafiz Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (463H). This book is considered one of the most important commentaries on Hadith books, and it is a commentary on the book "Al-Muwatta" by Imam Malik. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr arranged the book according to the chapters of al-Muwatta, omitting the repetition of supporting evidence and chains of narration, and he relied on the narration of Yahya ibn Yahya in his commentary.

Al-Istidhkar is characterized by its comprehensiveness in explaining the hadiths of al-Muwatta, as it deals with both connected and disconnected chains of narration, and explains the sayings of the Companions and their followers (Tabi'un). The author also clarifies the opinion of Imam Malik and what was built upon it from the sayings of the people of Medina, in addition to mentioning the opinions of jurists from other regions. 

Al-Istidhkar is considered one of the most important books in explaining al-Muwatta, and scholars such as al-Dhahabi and Ibn Kathir have praised it. Although Ibn 'Abd al-Barr also authored the book "Al-Tamhid" in explaining al-Muwatta, al-Istidhkar differs from it in several aspects, including its comprehensiveness in explaining everything mentioned in al-Muwatta, including disconnected narrations and traditions, and its detailed explanation of jurisprudential issues in a more understandable manner.

name: 'Umdat al-Qari Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari - Badr ed-Dine al-'Ayni
description_short:
Imam Badr al-Din al-Ayni's book, "Umdat al-Qari Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari," is among the best commentaries on Sahih al-Bukhari. In fact, it is a comprehensive fiqh encyclopedia that makes it unnecessary for the student to refer to many other sources. The commentary is distinguished by its combination of accurate linguistic analysis, deep fiqh deduction, and extensive knowledge of the opinions of previous scholars, making it a fundamental reference for jurists and hadith scholars throughout the ages.

In his commentary, al-Ayni was keen on explaining the meanings of the prophetic hadiths, clarifying any uncommon words they contained, explaining their purposes, and extracting fiqh rulings from them. He also mentioned the differences of opinion among scholars on each issue, clarifying the point of contention and giving preference to the most likely opinion with evidence. He did not limit himself to the fiqh aspect but also addressed the linguistic, rhetorical, and historical aspects related to the hadiths, which enriches the reader's culture and increases their understanding of the religious texts.

Undoubtedly, "Umdat al-Qari" is one of the greatest services that scholars have provided to the noble prophetic hadith. It opens wide horizons for the reader to understand Sahih al-Bukhari and helps them utilize its scientific treasures and act upon its rulings.

name: Al-Jam' bayn as-Sahihayn - Abdul Haqq al-Ishbili (100% Harakat)
description_short:
The Huffadh al-Wahyayn Center wanted to select a book from those that combine Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. So they studied ten books in this field and concluded that the best book for combining the Sahihayn is the work of Abdul Haqq al-Ishbili, a famous book praised by many scholars.

Al-Ishbili's method in his book is as follows: he primarily relied on the wording of Muslim's narrations, removed the chains of transmission but kept the narrator and companion, and omitted repeated narrations. He maintained the order of Sahih Muslim, then compared it with Bukhari's narrations, adding comments and sometimes additional information.

As for the researchers at Huffadh al-Wahyayn Center, they took Al-Ishbili’s book and made the following modifications: they removed Al-Ishbili’s commentary, retained the wording of Sahih Muslim, and highlighted any additions from Sahih Bukhari in red. If Muslim had another version of the narration, they indicated it in green. They divided the book into three sections: the first section contains what the two Sahihayn agreed upon (in three volumes), the fourth volume covers what is unique to Bukhari, and the fifth volume covers what is unique to Muslim.

name: 'Ilal al-Waqf wal-Wasl wal-Ibtida' fil-Qur'an - Mustafa Salloum
description_short:
The signs for pausing (waqf), resuming (wasl), and starting (ibtida') in the Quran were established for grammatical or semantic purposes, such as completing the meaning or avoiding ambiguity. In this brilliant academic treatise, the author refers to a collection of books by nine renowned scholars in this field, mentioned in the introduction, as well as five Mushafs from which he derives the signs for waqf and ibtida'.

The author uses the thirteenth juz’ of the Quran to apply the issues discussed in the book. He approaches a Quranic verse marked with a waqf or ibtida' symbol, identifies the symbol across the five Mushafs, then cites the opinions of waqf scholars on the matter. He delves into the semantic and grammatical aspects of the issue, examining key points in detail. The book concludes with the author's proposal of new signs for waqf and ibtida', offering explanations and suggesting they be considered for future use.

This distinguished book is a comprehensive work and represents a commendable effort in its field.

name: Al-Jabarti's History: 'Aja'ib al-Athar fi al-Tarajim wa al-Akhbar
description_short:
The book "Aja'ib al-Athar fi al-Tarajim wa al-Akhbar", known as "Al-Jabarti's History", is a rich record of the events that Egypt witnessed in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. The book narrates, in a detailed narrative style, the events of the French campaign on Egypt, the Egyptian people's revolution against it, then the turbulent Ottoman rule period that followed, up to the beginnings of the era of Muhammad Ali Pasha.

This book is distinguished by its focus on the minute details of daily life in that period. It is not limited to major political and military events, but also deals with various social, economic, and cultural aspects. Al-Jabarti describes, for example, the conditions of markets and crops, details of fashion and social customs, and even the prices of various goods. The book also provides biographies of a large number of prominent figures in that period, from rulers, scholars, jurists, merchants, and artists, which makes it a rich source for understanding the nature of Egyptian society in that crucial historical era.

"Al-Jabarti's History" is considered one of the most important historical references for understanding that period of Egyptian history. It provides an eyewitness perspective, although it carries some personal biases, it remains of high value to researchers and historians. The book is distinguished by its smooth literary style and its ability to transport the reader to the heart of events, making it enjoyable to read even for those who are not specialized in history.

This book is distinguished by its focus on analogies from authentic and accepted hadiths, making it a reliable source for researchers and students of knowledge.

The book highlights the value of analogies in the Prophetic hadiths, as they embody the style of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in communication and conveying messages. They are characterized by their ease of understanding and memorization, and their ability to establish meanings in the minds. The book also reveals the eloquence of the Prophet in using analogies, as they carry deep meanings and valuable lessons, and vary in their topics to cover various aspects of life.

Abu al-Shaykh al-Asbahani was one of the prominent scholars of his time. Al-Dhahabi described him in "Al-Siyar" as the Imam, the Hadith memorizer, the truthful, and the Hadith scholar of Isfahan. description_short:
"Tahdhir al-Muslimin 'an al-Ibtida' wal-Bida' fi al-Din" is a book authored by Ahmad bin Hajar Al Butami Al-Bana'ali, addressing the topic of religious innovations in Islam and their impact on faith and religious practice. ​Through this book, the author aims to raise awareness among Muslims about the dangers of innovation, discussing how bid'ah (religious innovations) affects monotheism and the integrity of faith.​ The book includes historical examples and religious evidence to illustrate the harm that may result from these practices. 

The book consists of several chapters providing a detailed analysis of the concept of bid'ah, explaining its types and related misconceptions that may spread in Islamic societies. The author emphasizes the importance of adhering to the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and stresses the necessity of returning to the Quran and Sunnah as primary sources of religious guidance. The book presents a call to combat innovation and adhere to the correct approach in practicing religion, contributing to the enhancement of a proper understanding of Islam among Muslims.

Ahmad bin Hajar Al Butami was a prominent Islamic scholar and former Mufti of Qatar, born around 1915 and passed away in 2002. He served as a judge, educator, and author, contributing significantly to Islamic jurisprudence and education in Qatar and the Arabian Peninsula. Al Butami authored numerous works on Islamic theology, jurisprudence, and social issues, and was known for his dedication to Salafi beliefs and teachings.

name: Psychological Disorders and Their Impact on Responsibility in Fiqh
description_short:
Psychological Disorders and Their Impact on Responsibility in Islamic Jurisprudence and Secular Law by Dr Al-Husaini Arafat.

In the past, Islamic jurists were familiar with certain psychological disorders and would base legal rulings on them. However, as psychology has developed, psychological disorders have become more diverse, with varying degrees of impact on accountability and the capacity to bear responsibility.

The author sought to study these psychological disorders and their effects on legal responsibilities, eligibility, civil and criminal liability, and punishments from the perspective of Islamic jurisprudence and secular law. He categorizes these disorders into three types: those that completely negate legal capacity, those that partially reduce it, and those that have no effect on capacity.

This valuable book is an important study, much needed in our time, particularly in the judicial field.

name: 5 Rasa-il Muhimmah fi al-Qur'an wa as-Sunnah li Al-Imam al-Khattabi
description_short:
This valuable book presents five important epistles by Imam al-Khattabi, may God have mercy on him, on various Quranic and Sunnah topics. They are:

1. Bayan I'jaz al-Quran (Exposition of the Miraculous Nature of the Quran): In it, Imam al-Khattabi discusses the miraculous nature of the Holy Quran and details the aspects of this miracle in a sound scholarly style.

2. Shan al-Du'a wa Tafsir al-Ad'iyah al-Mathurah (The Importance of Supplication and Explanation of the Reported Supplications): It explains the importance of supplication in Islam and interprets the supplications narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, along with explaining their meanings.

3. Islah Ghalat al-Muhaddithin (Correcting the Errors of Hadith Scholars): In it, Imam al-Khattabi discusses some common errors made by some Hadith scholars in narrating or understanding Hadith.

4. Risalah al-Ghina 'an al-Kalam wa Ahlih (The Epistle of Contentment with Silence and its People): It clarifies the virtue of silence and the wisdom of speaking little, and warns against excessive and pointless talk.

5. Al-I'tisam bi al-'Uzlah (Adhering to Seclusion): It deals with the virtue of seclusion at certain times to devote oneself to worship and reflection.

This book is a great collection that demonstrates the vast knowledge of Imam al-Khattabi, may God have mercy on him, and sheds light on important aspects of the Quranic and Sunnah sciences. It is a beautiful, verified, and authenticated edition, with full vocalization (100% Harakat).

This book is considered an important reference in the field of Hadith sciences, especially with regard to the accuracy of the names of the narrators and distinguishing between them. It helps researchers and Hadith scholars avoid confusion between narrators whose names or surnames are similar, which contributes to preserving the accuracy of Hadith transmission and the validity of chains of narration.

name: Islah Khatae al-Muhaddithin fi al-Kutub as-Sittah - Sa'id Bashanfar
description_short:
The work focuses on corrections made by scholars to specific wordings in hadiths. The author does not critique the chains of narration or the authenticity of hadiths, but rather addresses specific words that were challenged by some narrators in the six hadith books. These corrections do not affect the authenticity of the hadiths but rather concern the issue of using specific wordings as evidence.

This is the book's methodology: For example, the first volume on Sahih al-Bukhari contains 89 instances where narrators made mistakes in wording. The author presents the hadith containing the word in question, then identifies the narrator(s) who made the mistake, followed by citing scholars who pointed out the error. He then presents the correct wording and its narrators, and also notes Bukhari's own comments on the error. This methodology is consistently followed across all six volumes, with each volume dedicated to one of the six major hadith books.

name: TasHifat al-Muhaddithin - Sa'id Abdul Qadir Bashanfar
description_short:
This is a unique research study on tas-hif (textual corruption) in hadith. Tashif refers to errors that occur in wording, such as misspelling or scribal errors. The author thoroughly examined books of Sunnah and filtered through their hadiths, extracting 287 words that scholars have identified as containing tashif.

The book begins with a section containing 10 chapters presenting a foundational study of the issue of tashif. The practical section that follows forms the core of the book: it lists all the hadiths in which scholars found tashif. For each hadith, the author presents its chain of narration starting from the narrator suspected of causing the tashif, highlighting the location of the error in red. He then presents the hadith and begins studying its tashif by citing scholars' opinions, who among them corrected it, and other related matters.

After this extensive research, the author reached valuable conclusions about the impact of tashif on hadith authenticity and disagreements between legal schools. He concluded his book with tables summarizing all types of tashif in hadith, making it easier for future researchers to build upon his work.

Known for her research quality, this work may be her finest contribution yet.

The book includes Ibn Qudama's original text, followed by Al-Wa'ili's interpretation, with Al-Kawari's additions in the footnotes. It spans 20 volumes, with the final volume dedicated to indexes.

This Sharh is considered an excellent reference for students and researchers in Hanbali Fiqh. It helps in understanding the text of "Al-Kafi" in a deeper and more accurate way. It contributes to the dissemination of fiqh knowledge and makes it easier for students.

description_short:
Irshad al-Udul li Hal Alfadh Nihayat As-Sul by Dr Kamila Al-Kawari.

Minhaj Al-Wusul by Al-Baydawi is a well-known text that has numerous commentaries, among which is Al-Asnawi's "Nihayat As-Sul," which is heavily relied upon in Islamic legal institutions and studies of Usul. In this book, Kamila Al-Kawari aimed to simplify Nihayat As-Sul for beginners.

The researcher examined the various commentaries on Al-Minhaj and the annotations of Nihayat Al-Sul, which she mentioned in the introduction. Tafsir al-Hakimi, i. e. Talkhis ad-Durar by al-'Allamah Abdul Hamid bin Abdul Majid Al-Hakimi

This is a medium-sized Tafsir being published for the first time, addressing only the most important interpretations of the verses, written by the scholar Abdul Hamid bin Abdul Majid Al-Hakimi, who lived in the sixth century AH. The book's title reflects its content. Al-Hakimi extracted the "pearls of interpretation" from sources he divided into two categories: The first category comprises 4 books he considered foundational Tafsirs which are no longer extant today - this being one of the book's distinctive features. The second category, which he called subsidiary Tafsirs, consists of the well-known commentaries available today.

Ahmad Ibn Faris Al-Fallum edited the book using a unique manuscript. He provided a biography of Al-Hakimi and explained his ideas, methodology, and sources. The commentary style is concise while addressing aspects of Qur'anic recitations, circumstances of revelation, abrogating and abrogated verses, meanings, and obscure vocabulary. The editor added numerous useful footnotes.

A scholarly edition based on a manuscript, including referencing and authentication of the Hadiths.

name: Qayd Al-Awabid - Al-'Isami (Tafsir, Fawa-id, 'Awa'id & Zawa-id)
description_short:
"Qayd al-Awabid" by Abd al-Malik ibn Husayn al-Isami al-Shafi'i al-Makki.

Al-'Allamah AbdelMalik ibn Husayn Al-Isami ash-Shafi'i (1049H) wrote this book as a Tafsir, but he focused only on addressing the concept of similarities in the Quran (both in words and meanings) and resolving interpretative difficulties, misconceptions, and seemingly contradictory meanings. Rather than interpreting every verse, he concentrated his efforts on passages that appear to contain contradictions, presenting the issues and resolving them.

He divided the interpretation of each surah into three sections: Benefits (Fawa'id), Returns (Awa'id), and Additions (Zawa'id). In the Benefits section, he addresses complexities and clarifies ambiguous verses. The Returns section contains what the author gathered from studying historical and literary works that benefited his tafsir, including the occasions of revelation and the virtues of each surat. The Additions section consists of poems that contain the meanings and words of the explained verses. One of the book's distinguishing features is that it's rich with citations from rare books, as Al-Isami possessed a vast library from which he both learned and taught.

This edition is based on two manuscripts in the author's hand.  A work of Tafsir Mushkil al-Qur'an (Interpretation of Difficult Qur'anic Passages), it offers insights into reconciling apparent contradictions, includes historical and anecdotal accounts, and additional material on rhetoric and literature.

description_short:
"The Emergence of Grammar and the History of the Most Famous Grammarians" by Muhammad al-Tantāwī is a literary work that explores the world of Arabic grammar from its roots. It takes us on a journey through the history of this science, which has been a cornerstone in the construction of Classical Arabic. The book not only narrates the evolution of grammar but also pays tribute to the iconic figures who contributed to its transformations, starting with the efforts of Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali, through the famous Sibawayh, and reaching various eras that witnessed pivotal contributions from scholars of Basra, Kufa, and other schools.

This text offers the reader a blend of historical accuracy and deep grammatical analysis, making it a vital addition to the library of any researcher or enthusiast interested in the history of the language. This book is more than just a historical account; it is an invitation to reflect on the precision of the Arabs and their keenness to document and protect their language across centuries. It highlights the contributions of prominent figures in grammar, such as Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali, al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi, and Sibawayh, whose works remain indispensable references for understanding linguistic contexts and positions that continue to challenge researchers to this day. The book of al-Tantāwī renews interest in our linguistic heritage, reinforcing our appreciation for the importance of grammar in preserving the identity and cultural richness of the language.

name: Jaami' as-Sunnah - Shaykh Abdulaziz Al-Muqhim
description_short:
The author aimed to compile all authentic prophetic hadiths in a single book that any Muslim could read regardless of their knowledge or education level. He studied 37 books from the collections of Sunnah and extracted authentic hadiths from them without repetition. His methodology relied on two books: Ibn Al-Athir's Jami' Al-Usul, which served as his starting point, and Al-Albani's Al-Sahih Al-Jami'.

The author excluded hadiths that were subject to debate even if some scholars authenticated them, and included only those that were unanimously agreed upon as authentic or had minimal disagreement. He collected approximately 4,000 hadiths, numbered them all, with complete harakat on the matn and explanations of obscure vocabulary and essential meanings that cannot be dispensed with (such as abrogated rulings and some Fiqh). Most of the commentary is taken from Ibn Hajar's explanation of Sahih al-Bukhari or Al-Nawawi's explanation of Sahih Muslim.

This book represents a valuable new addition to the field of compiling authentic Sunnah. What distinguishes it from others is its combination of contemporary and classical scholarship in the science of narrator criticism and validation: Al-Albani and Ibn al-Athir.

name: Consensus in Grammar (Al-Ijma' fi al-Nahw) - Dr Dakhil al-'Awwad
description_short:
This book examines how early scholars reached agreement (ijma') when establishing the foundations of Arabic grammar. It explores what made these agreements authoritative, what evidence supported them, and how legitimate these grammatical consensuses were. It investigates which grammarians' opinions were considered valid enough to count and what obstacles sometimes prevented scholars from reaching agreement. The book traces how these scholarly agreements in grammar emerged and evolved through different historical periods, along with related aspects of this principle.

The significance of this topic becomes clear when we see how much attention grammarians have given to scholarly consensus. While researchers throughout history have extensively studied disagreements in grammar – as evidenced in classical works like al-Anbari's "Al-Insaf fi Masail al-Khilaf," al-'Ukbari's "Al-Tibyan," and al-Zubaydi's "I'tilaf al-Nasra" about disputes between Kufan and Basran grammarians – modern studies on grammatical disagreements are also numerous. Yet, the rules that grammarians actually agreed upon deserve even more attention than their disagreements. When scholars study these disputes and their causes, they're really examining what prevented consensus from being reached, since consensus is simply what remains when disagreement is resolved.

This book is a valuable reference for anyone who wishes to delve deeper into understanding the rules of recitation and Tajweed, and the related jurisprudential rulings, particularly concerning the reader's errors in prayer.

name: Al-Fawakih al-'Adidah fil Masa-il al-Mufidah - Ibn Manqoor al-Hanbali
description_short:
Ibn Manqoor was a scholar from Najd who served as both judge and mufti. In these roles, he constantly fielded questions from the public about religious and legal matters, which inspired him to create a comprehensive reference guide. Drawing from his extensive personal library, he compiled relevant scholarly opinions and organized them following the traditional chapters found in Hanbali legal texts. Rather than trying to cover all Fiqh issues like most authors did, he took a practical approach - focusing on the real-world issues people actually came to him with. The result was a unique compilation of fatwas and judicial rulings.

Ibn Manqoor built each entry in the book in the following manner. He would present an issue and then weave together various expert opinions, starting with teachings from his own mentor, Abdullah bin Dahlan (who was the chief judge and mufti of Riyadh at the time). He also incorporated views from prominent Hanbali scholars like Al-Buhuti, as well as religious authorities from across the Levant and Egypt. Since the book grew directly out of his work with the community, it offers fascinating glimpses into the social, economic, and historical realities of his time.

The current edition was carefully pieced together by three scholars who worked from four original manuscripts, complete with biographical details, a full accounting of his 122 sources, and an analysis of his methodology.

Uncover the pioneering legal distinctions that shaped Islamic jurisprudence!

"Kitab al-Furuq" (The Book of Distinctions) by Abu al-Fadl Muhammad ibn Salih al-Karabisi stands as a groundbreaking 4th century Hijri masterpiece that established a fundamental methodology in Islamic legal thought. This seminal work meticulously documents subtle distinctions between seemingly similar legal cases that actually warrant different rulings in Hanafi fiqh. As one of the earliest known texts dedicated to legal distinctions, al-Karabisi's work represents a watershed moment in Islamic juridical analysis that influenced generations of subsequent scholars across all legal schools.

The author, a distinguished Samarqandi Hanafi jurist who passed away in 322 AH, masterfully demonstrates how minor variations in circumstances can lead to completely different legal judgments. This critical edition, expertly verified by Abdullah Hamid al-'Afri and published by Dar al-Fath, offers modern readers access to an invaluable window into the sophisticated analytical methods of early Islamic legal thought. The book's enduring significance lies not only in its historical importance as one of the earliest works in the genre of legal distinctions (furuq), but also in its continued relevance for understanding the nuanced reasoning processes that characterize Islamic jurisprudence at its finest.

This volume serves as an indispensable reference for specialists, Hanafi jurisprudence researchers, and those interested in hadith methodology and narrative jurisprudence.

description_short:

The author refutes this claim from its foundation, dedicating an entire chapter to disproving the attribution of creedal positions to jurisprudential schools with 12 points of refutation. 

He addresses the historical aspect of Tafwid's emergence since the time of al-Ja'd ibn Dirham and explains the general positions of the Hanbalis on divine names and attributes compared to those of the Kullabiyya, Ash'arites, and those who differed from the majority of Hanbalis. This book addresses an important contemporary theological debate and fills a crucial gap in scholarship. It helps clarify confusions that might otherwise mislead young Muslims and interfere with students' proper understanding of traditional Salafi Aqida.

name: Sharh al-Asalib al-Nahwiyyah - Muhammad Makkawi
description_short:
This is a substantial work of nearly 700 pages, noted for being one of the few comprehensive texts dedicated solely to the study of grammatical styles in Arabic. This book is particularly beneficial for students of Balaghah (rhetoric), serving as a valuable introduction to 'Ilm al-Ma'ani (the science of meanings), and is highly useful for anyone wishing to delve into the nuances of these distinct grammatical constructions. The author provides detailed explanations of fifteen grammatical styles, extensively supported by examples, many drawn from the Holy Quran.

The work is methodically structured with an introduction, two main chapters, and a conclusion. The first chapter focuses on grammatical styles found in declarative sentences, covering topics such as emphasis, exception, restriction, negation, and condition. The second chapter addresses styles associated with performative sentences, including various forms of request, exclamation, praise and dispraise, and warning and enticement. The author has endeavored to explain each style distinctively with numerous practical applications, enabling readers to thoroughly understand and apply these styles in any Arabic text.

name: Kitab Akhbar al-Nisaa - Emir Usama Ibn Munqidh (584H)
description_short:
The King Faisal Center for Research and Islamic Studies has published "Akhbar al-Nisa" (Accounts of Women) by Prince Majd al-Dawla Usama ibn Munqidh al-Shayzari al-Kinani, as part of its heritage preservation series. This book, published in 2024, is a unique manuscript that covers a wide range of topics related to women, from mothers and wives to descriptions of their beauty and stories of their lives. Ibn Munqidh is considered one of the most famous princes and literati of the Ayyubid era. He was a knight, politician, historian, and poet who witnessed and participated in the Crusades and left many important literary and historical works. The book, which had been missing for centuries, was discovered only recently among a set of manuscripts, and has now been edited for publication.

"Akhbar al-Nisa" is distinguished by its comprehensive approach, blending history, literature, and biographies of famous women. Although many books have been written about women, none possess the scope of ibn Munqidh's work. It includes poetry, prose, and legal insights, providing a rich tapestry of women's experiences. In the introduction, the editor clarifies the confusion surrounding the book's authorship, distinguishing it from other works with similar titles, including one by Ibn al-Jawzi. The rediscovery and publication of "Akhbar al-Nisa" is a significant contribution to the study of women's history and Arabic literature.

name: Talkhis al-Miftah by al-Khatib al-Qazwini (749H)
description_short:
This is a seminal work by the renowned master of Arabic rhetoric, Imam Jalal al-Din al-Qazwini (d. 739H). This text is a brilliant abridgment of the third part of Miftah al-'Ulum by Abu Ya'qub al-Sakkaki (d. 626H). Al-Qazwini refined al-Sakkaki's work, improving its organization, clarifying definitions, and removing complexities, making the advanced sciences of rhetoric more systematic and accessible.

Due to its clarity and pedagogical structure, Talkhis al-Miftah became the definitive textbook for studying Balaghah across the Islamic world for centuries. Its impact was so profound that it superseded its source text and became the central work around which nearly all subsequent rhetorical studies revolved. Its importance is evidenced by numerous major commentaries, notably al-Taftazani's Al-Mutawwal and al-Qazwini's own Al-Idah.

The single-volume Dar Al-Lubab edition, verified by Dr. Diya' al-Din al-Qalash, is based on seven manuscripts, five written during the author's lifetime, with some reviewed and annotated by al-Qazwini himself, making it uniquely authoritative.

name: Al-Idah li-Talkhis al-Miftah by al-Khatib al-Qazwini (749H)
description_short:
This book is a masterpiece of Arabic rhetoric by the celebrated Imam Jalal al-Din al-Qazwini (d. 739H). This book holds a unique status in the field, as it is the author's own detailed commentary on his own highly influential abridgment, Talkhis al-Miftah. Al-Qazwini had first summarized the rhetoric section of al-Sakkaki's (d. 626H) Miftah al-'Ulum, and his summary became so authoritative that he then wrote Al-Idah to explain and expand upon its finer points himself.

In this work, al-Qazwini provides an authoritative and clear explanation of the three sciences of Balaghah: 'Ilm al-Ma'ani, 'Ilm al-Bayan, and 'Ilm al-Badi'. Unlike other commentaries on his Talkhis, Al-Idah is valued for presenting the author's own intended meanings with precision and eloquence, making it a foundational text for understanding the nuances of the discipline. For centuries, Al-Idah has been studied as an indispensable resource for mastering Arabic rhetoric.

This edition is the result of over twenty years of work by Dr. Diya' al-Din al-Qalish. It is based on five manuscripts, the most important being a copy in the author's own handwriting, making it a uniquely authoritative text for researchers.

The original work is a comprehensive and systematic defense of the principle that sound, uncorrupted reason can never genuinely conflict with authentic, established revelation. Given the original's immense size and philosophical density, it has long been considered a challenging text accessible only to specialists, making this refined summary a highly valuable undertaking.

The researcher Nader ibn 'Umar Baltaji worked hard to make Ibn Taymiyyah's core arguments accessible to a broader audience of students and readers. The methodology of this abridgement involves distilling the essential principles, clarifying the primary lines of reasoning, and omitting many of the lengthy, intricate refutations of specific philosophical and theological sects that fill the original. This allows the reader to grasp the foundational thesis and evidence presented by Ibn Taymiyyah without being overwhelmed, thereby serving as a gateway to understanding this critical text of Islamic 'Aqidah.

name: At-Ta'liq al-'Ulaa fi Sharh Asmaa Allahi wa Sifatih - Maher Muqaddam
description_short:
This book is a true repository that compiles the statements of scholars regarding the meanings of the Names and Attributes and their proofs, and contains a comprehensive introduction covering the Sunni principles regarding the Names and Attributes.

The author divided his book into two major sections: one for the Names and one for the Attributes. He mentions each Name and provides its evidence from revelation. Then he explains its linguistic meaning and its technical meaning. He clarifies the majestic meanings contained in the Name, then mentions the fruits that a Muslim gains when he understands it, contemplates its meanings, and uses it in his supplications.

As for the second section, he began by mentioning the rules and principles of Sunni scholars regarding the Attributes. Then he addresses each attribute, providing its evidence from the Quran and Hadith, explaining its meaning and the Sunni methodology concerning it, and discussing related issues. In this section, the author answered many objections and provided detailed explanations for numerous issues.

This is a valuable book, rich in content at approximately 900 pages.

description_short:
Dr. Mas'ud al-Badri's work represents a valuable project scanning the biographical dictionaries of Hanbali scholars to uncover Imam Ahmad's authentic positions and opinions. Rather than relying solely on formal Fiqh books, al-Badri turns to the rich tradition of Hanbali biography literature, where later scholars preserved countless anecdotes, fatwas, and positions attributed to the Imam Ahmad.

This methodology is very clever because the books of biography often contain materials not found in standard Fiqh compilations. When Hanbali biographers wrote about their scholarly ancestors, they frequently included legal discussions, theological positions, and methodological insights that provide a more complete picture of Imam Ahmad's thinking. Al-Badri's systematic approach to this scattered material makes this book a treasure of information accessible to all Hanbali seekers of knowledge.

name: Ufool ad-Dawla ad-Diniya wa Dhuhur ad-Dawla al-Qawmiya al-Haditha
description_short:
Ufool al-Dawlah al-Diniyyah by Dr. Muhammad Amziyān, a scholar of Islamic political thought, critically examines the decline of the religious state and the rise of the modern nationalist state, drawing parallels to European history to inform Islamic political discourse. The book argues that the European transition from religious to nationalist states merely shifted the sacred from church to state authority, replacing religious zeal with ideological wars that mirror sectarian fanaticism in their intensity, such as the Crusades, mercenary wars, and imperial conflicts, which reinforced a war-driven evolution of the European state.  

Dr. Amziyān highlights the transformation of “sacred violence” and the culture of sacrifice (once tied to the cross in the era of religious states) into a devotion to national glory in the modern era, suggesting that this shift did not lead to peace but rather transitioned from theological violence to the violence of modernity. Applied to Islamic political thought, the book critiques theocratic models, arguing that they mirror the European trajectory by fostering authoritarianism, and advocates for a separation of religious and political authority to align with Islam’s ethical ideals in a pluralistic, modern context.

name: Atheism Defeats Itself - Dr Sami 'Amiri
description_short:
Dr. Sami Ameri's book, “Atheism Defeats Itself”, with the subtitle “A Critical Study of the Rationalization of Disbelief and Absurdity,” offers a contemporary philosophical critique of atheistic worldviews from an Islamic perspective. The central thesis of this work is that atheism, when subjected to rigorous logical and epistemological scrutiny, ultimately reveals internal contradictions or leads to conclusions that undermine its own purported rational foundations. Dr. Ameri sets out to demonstrate how, in his analysis, atheistic frameworks struggle to provide a coherent and sustainable basis for understanding existence, knowledge, objective morality, or human purpose.

The author examines various arguments and positions advanced by atheist thinkers, aiming to expose what he views as their logical inconsistencies or their inability to adequately account for fundamental aspects of reality and human experience. The book intends to provide a reasoned critique, suggesting that the attempt to build a comprehensive worldview devoid of God leads to philosophical impasses or a reliance on unacknowledged presuppositions. It is presented as an intellectual defense of theism, arguing that atheism, in its endeavor to rationalize disbelief, ultimately proves to be self-defeating.

name: Sharh Fath al-Majid bi Sharh Kitab at-Tawhid - Al-Fawzan (4 vol.)
description_short:
Sheikh Salih al-Fawzan's extensive four-volume commentary on "Fath al-Majeed" represents one of the most comprehensive contemporary explanations of Islamic monotheism (tawheed). This work builds upon a rich scholarly tradition: Fath al-Majeed is itself Abdurrahman ibn Hasan's commentary on his grandfather Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab's seminal "Kitab al-Tawheed." Thus, al-Fawzan offers a commentary upon a commentary, demonstrating the enduring relevance of these foundational texts in Islamic creed studies.

The scope of this four-volume work allows al-Fawzan to provide thorough analysis of every aspect of tawheed doctrine. This context is crucial, as it presents the Sirah through the lens of one of Islam's most preeminent historians and Hadith critics. It covers all aspects of the Prophet's life with historical precision and the author's signature conciseness. As a very well-verified edition, this work stands as a superior and trustworthy choice for students and researchers.

name: Those Who Stood by Ahmad in the Ordeal by Haytham al-Hamzi
description_short:
This is a historical study centered on the pivotal ordeal endured by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal (d. 241H) regarding the createdness of the Quran. The book uniquely shifts focus from the Imam alone to the individuals who surrounded him, dividing them into two key groups: "Those Who Supported/Strengthened Ahmad," detailing personalities who provided aid and encouragement to him, and "Those Who Stood Firm with Ahmad," recounting figures who shared in his steadfastness during the tribulation.

The first part of the book, "Al-Muthabbitun," explores the biographies and supportive actions of individuals who, though perhaps not all directly persecuted in the same manner, were crucial in providing Imam Ahmad with assistance, encouragement, or solidarity. The subsequent part, "Al-Thabitun," then focuses on those scholars and individuals who themselves faced the inquisition, resisted the prevailing pressure, and remained firm in their conviction alongside Imam Ahmad. This work thus aims to illuminate the broader communal and scholarly resilience during this critical era in Islamic history.

name: Al-Taysir fi al-Tafsir by Imam Abu Nasr al-Qushayri (514H)
description_short:
Al-Taysir fi al-Tafsir is a wonderful masterpiece of Tafsir by Imam Abu Nasr 'Abd al-Rahim al-Qushayri (d. 514H), son of the renowned Sufi Imam, Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri. Despite being scarcely known in modern times, this Tafsir was a major reference for later giants of Islamic scholarship; it was relied upon heavily by Imams al-Qurtubi (for whom it was a primary source), Abu Hayyan, and Ibn Kathir in their own celebrated works of Tafsir.

The book is distinguished by its exceptional clarity in both style and language, deliberately avoiding complexity, ambiguity, and doubtful reports (Israeliyyat). Imam Abu Nasr al-Qushayri demonstrates great concern for grounding his work in transmitted reports (Tafsir bi-al-Ma'thur), with a particular focus on matters of Arabic language, grammar, and the meanings of words. This balanced and clear methodology makes the work immensely beneficial and of great scholarly value.

The seven-volume Dar al-Lubab edition marks the first-ever printing of this masterpiece. Its verification is based on three manuscripts, including a remarkable copy from 542H read by the author's son-in-law, offering researchers a uniquely reliable text.

The ambition of this Tafsir is double. On one hand, it seeks above all to nourish the soul and elevate the reader's faith and piety; each page is imbued with wisdom, touching admonitions, and constant reminders of the divine presence, making it a deeply enriching spiritual read. On the other hand, the work aims to offer a complete mastery of the Quranic sciences. Imam al-Nasafi deploys an encyclopedic knowledge, gathering with remarkable ease the different arts of exegesis: he explores language, grammar, the subtleties of literal and allegorical interpretation, and mobilizes a vast corpus of traditions and sayings of the Salaf. It is a veritable mine of treasures, overflowing with benefits and citations that one does not find elsewhere.

The Dar al-Lubab edition represents a landmark achievement, presenting this masterpiece for the first time in a complete, fifteen-volume scholarly edition. Verified against three manuscripts, this publication provides researchers with a definitive and reliable text.

name: Athar al-Balaghah fi Tawjih Mushkil al-Quran by Dr Yasir al-Mutayri
description_short:
This academic study examines the role of rhetoric (balaghah) in clarifying problematic Quranic passages, demonstrating methods of reconciling seemingly contradictory verses and the role of rhetoric in removing ambiguity. Originally a doctoral dissertation at Imam Muhammad ibn Saud Islamic University, the research focuses on the most prominent works on Quranic difficulties, including Ibn Qutaybah's "Ta'wil Mushkil al-Quran," al-Izz ibn Abd al-Salam's "al-Fawa'id fi Mushkil al-Quran," and three other classical works.

The study employs a descriptive-analytical methodology, analyzing verse meanings, identifying sources of difficulty, and examining scholarly approaches to resolution in light of rhetorical principles. Structured in seven chapters covering individual words, sentences, multiple sentences, figurative speech, embellishment (badi'), the impact of belief in determining and directing problematic passages, and causes of difficulty with methods of resolution. Key findings include that rhetoric is not merely aesthetic but essential for textual understanding and problem resolution, the science of badi' serves functions beyond beautification in directing problematic passages, and exegetical works contain precise rhetorical discussions absent from rhetoricians' compositions. Published by Tafsir Center for Quranic Studies.

name: Asbab al-Nuzul wa-Atharuha fi al-Tafsir by Dr 'Isam al-Humaydan
description_short:
This comprehensive study examines the reasons for revelation (asbab al-nuzul) as a discipline within Quranic sciences, covering historical and classificatory aspects while reviewing in detail the two most important works in this field. The book discusses scholarly principles related to asbab al-nuzul, including conflicts between narrations, methods of preference, multiple revelations, and formulations of revelation causes. Originally a master's thesis at Imam Muhammad ibn Saud Islamic University, the work provides critical analysis and authentication of all asbab al-nuzul narrations found in the works of al-Wahidi and al-Suyuti.

The study is structured in four main sections covering the definition and types of asbab al-nuzul, scholarly principles including multiple narrations and the relationship between general text and specific cause, a historical survey of scholarly efforts and major works in the field, and a critical evaluation distinguishing authentic from weak narrations. Key findings include that authentic chained asbab al-nuzul narrations outnumber weak ones by approximately double, most asbab al-nuzul serve to clarify meaning rather than determine it entirely, and multiple revelation of verses occurred only once or twice authentically. Published by Tafsir Center for Quranic Studies.

description_short:
This comprehensive academic study focuses on collecting the names of the Companions who engaged in Quranic exegesis and their interpretative sayings, through systematic investigation and tracking from various sources. The study identifies 100 Companions who transmitted interpretative narrations, collecting the exegetical materials of 95 Companions whose interpretations had not been previously compiled. Drawing from 229 authenticated books across 787 volumes, the research provides numerical statistics of the Companions' sources in interpretation and presents the characteristics that distinguished their exegetical approach. The work demonstrates how the Companions relied on various sources including prophetic traditions (600+ sayings), personal reasoning and ijtihad (4,851 sayings), Arabic language (1,400 sayings), circumstances of revelation (1,208 sayings), Israelite reports (900 sayings), Quranic interpretation (268 sayings), and Sunnah (120 sayings).

name: Manhaj al-Imam Ibn Jarir al-Tabari fi al-Tarjih - Husayn al-Harbi
description_short:
This comprehensive academic study examines Ibn Jarir al-Tabari's methodology in weighing and selecting between interpretative opinions in Quranic exegesis. Originally a doctoral dissertation defended in 1422H at Imam Muhammad ibn Saud Islamic University with highest honors, this work systematically analyzes al-Tabari's formulas and methods of preference and selection among exegetical opinions.

The study extracts and analyzes 220 preference cases from al-Tabari's "Jami' al-Bayan 'an Ta'wil Ay al-Quran," covering interpretations from Surat al-Fatihah through the end of the third Hizb of the Quran. The research demonstrates how al-Tabari employed various approaches in his selections: explicit preference with evidence, preference through refuting alternatives, stating the preferred opinion with certainty while mentioning others tentatively, and other methodological approaches. The study reveals that al-Tabari's most frequent sources of evidence were scholarly consensus among authoritative interpreters, contextual indications of verses, and established usage in Arabic language. 

Published in two volumes by Tafsir Center for Quranic Studies, this work provides crucial insights into the methodological foundations of classical Quranic interpretation.

name: Al-Radd ‘ala al-Shadhili by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah
description_short:
This concise treatise by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah addresses theological concerns regarding the well-known Hizb al-Bahr (Litany of the Sea), composed by the Sufi figure Abu al-Hasan al-Shadhili. Ibn Taymiyyah examines select phrases from the litany that, in his view, contain ambiguities or problematic expressions in light of the Qur’an and sound ‘aqidah. These include wording that suggests excessive claims of spiritual protection, unclear invocations of divine names, or forms of tawassul that blur the line between reliance on Allah and mystical dependence on creation.

Ibn Taymiyyah’s refutation is rooted in his firm commitment to the principles of Tawhid and the Sunnah. He responds with clarity, referencing scriptural evidence and the understanding of the early generations, highlighting the necessity of precision in worship and supplication. The book reflects his broader approach: affirming sound Sufism while rejecting rhetorical or theological overreach found in some mystical writings.

This edition is verified by Shaykh Ali ibn Muhammad al-‘Imran based on two manuscript copies. It features clear typesetting, scholarly footnotes, and belongs to the ʿAtā’āt al-ʿIlm series. The print includes some tashkil (diacritical marks), which enhances readability and comprehension.

These episodic narratives combine eloquent prose, rhythmic rhymed speech (saj‘), linguistic artistry, and sharp wit, presenting lively tales revolving around trickery, social satire, and the complexities of human character. The author’s creativity in crafting rhetorical flourishes and playful language made the maqāma genre a hallmark of Arabic belles-lettres.

Beyond entertainment, the Maqāmāt serve as a rich linguistic resource, showcasing the heights of Arabic rhetoric and vocabulary. They influenced generations of writers, most notably al-Hariri, and remain foundational in the study of adab, eloquence, and classical prose style. Students of Arabic often return to these texts for their linguistic challenges and cultural insights into early Islamic society.

Manuscript variants are recorded with scholarly evaluation, and the text is fully vocalized, with modern punctuation and clear thematic divisions to support systematic study.

name: Al-Dhahabi's Al-Kaba'ir (Major Sins) & 3 Treatises - Mashhur Al Salman
description_short:
Kitab al-Kaba-ir is one of Imam al-Dhahabi’s best-known works, addressing the major sins through Qur’anic evidence, Prophetic hadith, and reports of the early generations.

This edition distinguishes itself by restoring the authentic text of al-Dhahabi. Shaykh Mashhur Hasan Al Salman carefully purified the work from weak reports and fabricated stories that had entered later copies, returning the book to the form approved by its author. The hadiths and reports are rigorously traced and graded, reflecting the editor’s expertise in hadith criticism.

This volume is further enriched by three appended treatises, which complete the topic from different angles:

• Manzumah al-Kaba ir by Musa al-Hajjawi, a didactic poem facilitating memorization of the major sins.

• A musnad section on major sins by Ahmad ibn Harun al-Bardiji.

• A compilation of major sins drawn from the writings of Ibn al-Qayyim.
