name: Umdat al-Huffadh fi Tafsir Ashraf al-Alfadh - al-Samin al-Halabi
description_short:
A comprehensive linguistic dictionary of Quranic vocabulary by Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Abd al-Da'im al-Samin al-Halabi (d. 756 AH), one of the leading scholars of Arabic language and Quranic sciences in the eighth Islamic century. The work organizes Quranic terms alphabetically by their root letters, providing detailed linguistic analysis of each word alongside its usage in the Quran. Al-Samin supports his explanations with evidence from hadith, Arabic poetry (nearly 2,000 poetic citations), and classical linguistic authorities, demonstrating the morphological and grammatical dimensions of Quranic vocabulary.

The work serves as a major reference for students of tafsir and Arabic language seeking to understand the precise meanings and linguistic nuances of Quranic terms. It surpasses other works in its genre in breadth and detail, incorporating elements of gharib al-hadith (uncommon prophetic terms) alongside Quranic vocabulary. The author's mastery of grammar and morphology enables him to refine and correct earlier scholarship, clarifying distinctions between related terms and identifying the etymological foundations of Quranic words. The work is used as a reference text rather than a teaching manual, valuable for those engaged in advanced Quranic studies.

Compiled by Sheikh Yasser Bayumi, this Mushaf employs a clear, color-coded system and marginal notes to highlight these similarities and clarify the subtle differences between them. By providing these visual cues and thematic links directly on the pages of the Divine Text, the work helps the reader navigate the potential points of confusion that often arise during memorization and recitation.

The methodology of this Mushaf is centered on strengthening the precision of one's Hifz through comparative analysis. Sheikh Bayumi includes concise explanations and mnemonic aids in the margins, explaining the context or linguistic reasons for variations in similar verses. This makes it an invaluable tool for students of the Quran and teachers alike, as it reduces the mental effort required to distinguish between recurring phrases. It is an essential resource for anyone striving for excellence in their relationship with the Quran, ensuring a firm and accurate retention of Allah's Words.

name: al-Dhayl 'ala al-Jami' li-Kutub al-Imam al-Ajurri by Adil Al Hamdan
description_short:
This volume represents a remarkable scholarly recovery project: fragments and scattered quotations from Imam Abu Bakr al-Ajurri's lost works, meticulously gathered by researcher Adil Al Hamdan from later scholars' writings. Al-Ajurri (d. 360 AH) was one of the major scholars of the early fourth Hijri century, renowned for his extensive writings on creed, ethics, and Islamic sciences. While many of his major works like "al-Shari'ah" and "Akhlaq al-'Ulama'" have survived, numerous other treatises were lost to time.

This compilation preserves what remains of those vanished works through a painstaking process: Al Hamdan traced citations, quotations, and references to al-Ajurri's lost books scattered throughout later Islamic literature, assembling them into this supplementary volume (dhayl) to complement his main collection "al-Jami' li-Kutub al-Imam Abi Bakr al-Ajurri." Each fragment offers a glimpse into the intellectual breadth of this fourth-century master, preserving insights that would otherwise be entirely lost.

Published by Dar al-Lu'lu'ah al-Misriyyah, this single-volume edition was compiled and edited by Abu Abdullah Adil ibn Abdullah Al Hamdan al-Ghamidi, who has dedicated significant scholarly effort to preserving and publishing al-Ajurri's heritage through critical editions.

name: The Martyrdom of Uthman and the Battle of the Camel - Dr. Khalid al-Ghaith
description_short:
This critical study examines the narrations of Sayf ibn Umar al-Tamimi concerning two pivotal events in early Islamic history: the martyrdom of Caliph Uthman ibn Affan and the Battle of the Camel, as preserved in al-Tabari's monumental historical work. Dr. Khalid al-Ghaith applies rigorous hadith criticism methodology to assess these accounts, analyzing them through chain of transmission and textual content while comparing them with other historical sources to separate authentic material from weak or fabricated reports that have contributed to distorting this critical period.

The study examines key topics including Kufa's role in the fitnah, Abdullah ibn Saba's involvement in igniting discord, Uthman's approaches to addressing the crisis, his martyrdom, the pledge of allegiance to Ali, and the Battle of the Camel. By applying hadith evaluation standards to historical narrations, it addresses the methodological gap in medieval historical sources that typically recorded accounts without critical assessment, offering readers scholarly tools to understand these formative yet contested events in the Rashidun Caliphate era.

It is an indispensable volume for those seeking to study the core of the Prophetic Sunnah in a streamlined, authoritative format.

Tarikh al-Tafsir (The History of Exegesis) is a major scholarly work by the former Mufti of Baghdad, Sheikh Qasim al-Qaisi (d. 1375 AH). Originally published by the Iraqi Scientific Academy decades ago, this book has long been considered one of the most comprehensive Iraqi contributions to the history of Quranic sciences. This modern edition, published by Maktabat al-Rushd, features a meticulous verification by Dr. Osama al-Hayyani, who corrected previous typographical errors and added a detailed biography of the author.

The book explores the developmental stages of Tafsir from the Prophetic era to the modern age. It details the requirements and tools needed by a commentator (Mufassir) and provides critical reviews of nearly 20 major classical works of exegesis. Sheikh al-Qaisi’s approach is celebrated for its breadth and depth, moving beyond mere historical listing to a profound analysis of methodologies. According to experts like Dr. Ghanim Qadduri al-Hamad, this work remains unparalleled in its field within the Iraqi scholarly tradition.

Premium quality print featuring most of the Harakat on the text.

name: Mukhtasar Tafsir al-Tabari (3 Vols) - Islam bin Mansour
description_short:
A well-executed abridgment of Imam Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī's tafsīr "Jāmiʿ al-Bayān ʿan Taʾwīl Āy al-Qurʾān," one of the most esteemed and comprehensive Quranic commentaries in conveying the statements of the early generations and weighing opinions with evidence. The abridger condensed this monumental work, which spans over twenty volumes in its critical editions, into three accessible volumes while preserving the essence and foundations of the commentary. The abridger faithfully transmitted the exegesis of verses as presented by Imam al-Ṭabarī while removing chains of transmission, repetitions, and material unnecessary for general readers, retaining al-Ṭabarī's preferences, justifications, and selections that distinguish his tafsīr.

This abridgment presents al-Ṭabarī's tafsīr to contemporary readers in a reasonable size without compromising content, maintaining al-Ṭabarī's methodology of interpreting the Quran with the Quran itself, then with the Sunnah, then with the statements of the Companions and their Successors. The work features complete vocalization facilitating reading and comprehension for students of knowledge and general readers. The esteemed hadith scholar Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Saʿd wrote the preface, praising the work and encouraging benefit from it, confirming that this abridgment brings this magnificent tafsīr within reach of the general Muslim community and its students after it had been beyond the grasp of most people due to its magnitude.

This edition spans 3 large volumes totaling over 2,800 pages, featuring most of the Harakat (majority tashkil) on the text.

name: Al-Nafs fi al-Qur’an al-Karim - Dr. Muhammad Amhazoun
description_short:
Al-Nafs fi al-Qur’an al-Karim (The Soul in the Noble Quran) is a masterful exploration of Quranic psychology and the spiritual anatomy of the human being. Dr. Muhammad Amhazoun, a prominent Moroccan scholar, delves into the Divine text to define the nature, states, and potential of the human "Nafs." The book provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the three primary states of the soul mentioned in the Quran: the soul that incites evil (al-Ammarah), the self-reproaching soul (al-Lawwamah), and the soul at rest (al-Mutma'innah).

Moving beyond theoretical definitions, Dr. Amhazoun outlines the Quranic methodology for Tazkiyat al-Nafs (Purification of the Soul). He analyzes the internal struggle between worldly desires and the innate longing for the Creator, providing practical insights on how to achieve emotional and spiritual equilibrium. This work is an essential resource for students of Islamic psychology, ethics, and spirituality, offering a roadmap for personal reform and the attainment of inner peace through the guidance of the Revelation.

Dr. Muhammad Amhazoun, a distinguished Moroccan scholar, argues that the "Science of the Hereafter" is the most honorable branch of knowledge after the study of Tawheed (Divine Oneness), as it directly outlines the path to eternal salvation. The book serves as a spiritual and intellectual roadmap, meticulously analyzing Quranic verses to contrast the transient nature of worldly life (Dunya) with the permanence of the eternal abode (Akhirah).

The work is organized into four thematic chapters that cover the necessity of asceticism (Zuhd), the balance between worldly means and spiritual ends, and a detailed breakdown of both the saving deeds (al-Munjiya) and the destructive traits (al-Muhlika) that determine an individual's fate. By grounding the discussion in a rigorous scientific methodology, Dr. Amhazoun moves beyond simple reminders to provide a comprehensive worldview that encourages the reader to reorganize their life priorities according to the eternal perspective of the Quran.

Al-Nuzul al-Mala'iki (Angelic Descent) is a specialized thematic study (Tafsir Mawdu’i) that investigates every instance where the Quran mentions the descent of angels to the earthly realm. Dr. Sultan al-Otaibi employs an inductive methodology, gathering all relevant verses to categorize the divine purposes behind these celestial interventions. The book explores the metaphysical relationship between the unseen world and human history, providing a structured look at how angels interact with creation by Allah's command.

The study is divided into chapters based on the objectives of the descent: support and tidings for the believers (such as in battles or during times of steadfastness), punishment and warnings for the disbelievers, and the critical moments of transition like death, the resurrection, and the Day of Judgment. This work is an excellent resource for those interested in Quranic sciences and creed (Aqidah), as it organizes a complex subject into a clear, evidence-based narrative.

name: Kitab al-Iman al-Awsat (Ibn Taymiyyah) : Talkhis wa Dirasah
description_short:
A scholarly summary of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah's (d. 728 AH) "al-Iman al-Awsat" — his renowned commentary on the hadith of Jibril explaining the reality of faith, Islam, and Ihsan. Isma'il al-'Adawi presents a focused distillation of Ibn Taymiyyah's discussions on the nature of faith, its pillars, and its levels, with particular attention to the question of the inseparability of faith and action — one of the most precise and contested issues in aqeedah between Ahl al-Sunnah and the Murji'ah: can there be faith without action? What is the relationship between the conviction of the heart and the deeds of the limbs?

Al-Adawi’s primary objective is to extract the core doctrinal rulings while removing extensive text chains, lengthy digressions, and dense philosophical polemics. The abridgment preserves Ibn Taymiyyah’s systematic refutations of deviant historical factions, such as the Murji'ah and the Khawarij, regarding the relationship between outward submission (Islam) and true faith (Iman). This layout yields a structured, highly scannable manual ideal for students seeking to master classical Athari creed without getting bogged down by medieval debating styles.

description_short:
Qa'idah fi Tawhid al-'Ibadah (A Rule on the Unity of Worship) is a concise yet profound theological treatise by Ahmad bin Marri al-Ba'labaki, one of the most loyal and earliest students of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. Known as "Ibn Marri al-Taymi" for his deep devotion to his teacher's legacy, the author wrote this work to clarify the core of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (Monotheism of Worship).

The book focuses on defining worship, distinguishing it from shirk (association), and explaining why direct devotion to Allah is the primary message of all prophets. It is especially significant because it reflects the intellectual atmosphere of Damascus in the 8th century AH, where the author famously suffered a trial (mihna) for defending these very principles. This edition is verified from a unique manuscript found in Turkey, making it a rare and vital addition for students of the Athari creed.

description_short:
This book is an exhaustive academic study dedicated to compiling, analyzing, and verifying all the instances of scholarly consensus (Ijma') cited by Imam Ibn Qudamah (d. 620 AH) in his monumental comparative jurisprudence encyclopedia, Al-Mughni. The author, Abd al-Latif bin Burayk al-Thubayti, systematically tracks every legal issue where Ibn Qudamah declared an absolute consensus or stated that "no disagreement is known" among Muslim jurists.

Organized according to the classical chapters of Islamic law—spanning both ritual worship (ibadat) and civil transactions (muamalat)—the text subjects each claim of consensus to a rigorous critical review. Al-Thubayti cross-references these issues with the primary source texts of the major Sunni schools of thought (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali) to determine whether the Ijma' holds true historically or if a valid, documented dissenting opinion existed. This work serves as an invaluable reference tool for advanced researchers in comparative fiqh and Islamic legal theory (Usul al-Fiqh).

He notes in his introduction that he had written an earlier mansak in his youth in which he included many unverified supplications and followed other scholars by taqlid, then reconsidered and wrote this one according to what became clear to him from the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ. It guides the pilgrim from ihram at the miqat through to the farewell tawaf, distinguishing between established sunnahs and innovations that have crept into the acts of hajj.

What sets this mansak apart is that it is not bound to any single madhhab but relies on evidence and proof, favouring what the texts support.

It then moves to explaining the five major qawa'id — matters are judged by intentions, certainty is not removed by doubt, hardship brings ease, no harm and no reciprocal harm, custom is authoritative — and the subsidiary rules under each, with applied examples.

This book serves as an ideal entry point into the science of qawa'id fiqhiyyah for anyone not ready to begin with the author's own encyclopedic work. He grew up in Damascus, then moved to Damietta where he led its people against the Crusaders for some ten years until he was martyred at the Battle of al-Tinah, advancing and never turning back. The book is arranged in thirty-three chapters covering the virtues of bravery and sacrifice, the specific rulings of military engagement and the distribution of spoils, and the descriptions of Paradise and the longing for the Divine — all woven through with moving accounts from the lives of the Salaf.

Scholars have agreed that it is the finest and most comprehensive book ever written on jihad. It is far more than a legal manual: it is a spiritual work that explores the psychological and devotional motivations behind self-sacrifice, written by a master of hadith and sealed with his blood.

What distinguishes this book is that its narrations are predominantly authentic despite belonging to the genre of fada'il, which is fitting for Ibn al-Mubarak, who was known for saying: "In authentic hadith there is enough to keep you busy from the weak ones." A book read for the heart before the mind, authored by an imam who combined scholarship, worship, jihad, and trade — a living embodiment of what he wrote.

This edition by Dr. Amir Hasan Sabri is the first complete critical publication of the book — also known as "Kitab al-Zuhd" — in the narration of Nu'aym ibn Hammad, after previous editions remained incomplete due to missing manuscript segments. A high-quality edition with most of its tashkil.

name: Sharh al-Hidayah: Nihayat al-Kifayah, Taj al-Shariah & Ibn Kamal Basha
description_short:
Nihayat al-Kifayah li-Dirayat al-Hidayah by the renowned Bukharian jurist Imam Taj al-Shari'ah Umar al-Mahbubi (d. 673 AH) is one of the earliest, most authoritative, and expansive classical commentaries on Imam al-Marghinani’s foundational masterpiece, Al-Hidayah. Spanning the entire breadth of Hanafi jurisprudence, the work meticulously untangles complex legal terminology, analyzes the underlying rationale of secondary rulings (furu'), and contextualizes internal debates among early Hanafi masters alongside comparative viewpoints across other schools of law. Revered for its exceptional precision, it served as an indispensable pillar for subsequent legal masters, being cited over 350 times by Badr al-Din al-Ayni in Al-Binayah and over 100 times by Ibn al-Humam in Fath al-Qadir.

Published for the first time in an exhaustive 13-volume edition by Maktabat al-Irshad in Istanbul, this set unites two major classical commentaries. Volumes 1 through 9 contain the complete text of Nihayat al-Kifayah by Taj al-Shari'ah, critically edited from three manuscripts. Volumes 10 through 13 feature the extensive, highly analytical Sharh al-Hidayah by the eminent Ottoman scholar Ibn Kamal Basha (d. 940 AH), verified against seven historical manuscripts (including the author's own handwritten holograph for the section on pilgrimage). The final volume is enriched by several supplementary legal treatises (rasa'il) authored by Ibn Kamal Basha, including specialized monographs on succession in prayer leadership, zakat, judicial etiquette (Adab al-Qadi), and the ranks of Hanafi jurists (Tabaqat al-Fuqaha).

This premium edition is carefully verified against ten manuscripts (three for Nihayat al-Kifayah and seven for Ibn Kamal Basha, including the author's autograph). The print quality is excellent, with partial tashkil on difficult words to facilitate reading.

name: Hashiyat al-Imam al-Fishi 'ala Mukhtasar Khalil - Al-Fishi al-Maliki
description_short:
Hashiyat al-Imam al-Fayshi 'ala Mukhtasar Khalil by the prominent 11th-century Egyptian Azhari jurist Imam Yusuf ibn Muhammad al-Fayshi (d. 1061 AH) is one of the most comprehensive and encyclopedic super-commentaries ever composed on Mukhtasar Khalil. Spanning twelve massive volumes, this monumental work occupies a prestigious place in late Maliki legal literature, serving as an exhaustive repository that deciphers the dense, telegraphic phrasing of Sheikh Khalil’s primary manual and provides authoritative determinations for fatwa and judicial rulings.

Drawing extensively from both early and late authorities within the school, Imam al-Fayshi methodically breaks down intricate legal scenarios, resolves grammatical and semantic ambiguities in the base text, and clarifies subtle distinctions across derived branches of jurisprudence (furu'). He critically examines and synthesizes the explanations of major earlier commentators—such as al-Hattab, al-Tata'i, and Nasir al-Din al-Laqqani—while consistently establishing the relied-upon (al-Mu'tamad) and widespread (al-Mashhur) positions of the Maliki school. This extensive twelve-volume collection stands as an indispensable primary reference for muftis, senior researchers, and specialized students of Maliki jurisprudence.

name: Collected Works (Athar) of Sheikh Muhammad al-Tahir ibn 'Ashur
description_short:
Athar Fadilat al-Shaykh Muhammad al-Tahir ibn 'Ashur represents the definitive encyclopedic collection of the scholarly, intellectual, and literary works of the Grand Imam of Ez-Zitouna and premier Maliki jurist of the 20th century, Allamah Muhammad al-Tahir ibn 'Ashur (d. 1393 AH). Renowned as the modern renewer of teleological Islamic jurisprudence (Maqasid al-Shari'ah), Ibn 'Ashur left a profound legacy characterized by independent legal reasoning (ijtihad), deep linguistic mastery, and a balanced vision for modern civilizational and educational renewal based on authentic Islamic roots.

Spanning seventeen comprehensive volumes, this monumental corpus brings together the author's groundbreaking contributions outside his thirty-volume exegesis Al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir. The collection encompasses his core foundational treatises on legal philosophy and sociology—such as Maqasid al-Shari'ah al-Islamiyyah and Usul al-Nizam al-Ijtima'i fi al-Islam—alongside his specialized Hadith and Fiqh commentaries including Kashf al-Mughatta 'ala al-Muwatta. It also features his educational reform manifestos like Alaysa al-Subhu bi-Qarib, his exhaustive literary commentaries, critical editions of classical Arabic poetry (such as the Diwan of Bashshar ibn Burd), and an extensive array of academic lectures, fatwas, and historical research papers.

This deluxe 17-volume edition, jointly published by Dar Ibn Hazm and Dar Ibn Sahnun (Tunis), gathers these historically dispersed masterpieces into a unified, systematically classified, and beautifully typeset reference, establishing itself as an essential cornerstone for research libraries, academic scholars, and serious students of Islamic thought and law.

name: Al-Durar fi Ikhtisar al-Maghazi wa al-Siyar - Ibn Abd al-Barr (463H)
description_short:
Al-Durar fi Ikhtisar al-Maghazi wa al-Siyar by the eminent Andalusian Hadith master and jurist Imam Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr (d. 463 AH) is a concise classical summary of the Prophetic biography and military campaigns. Regarded as one of the most reliable introductory works on the Sirah, this text synthesizes early historical chronicles—chiefly those of Ibn Ishaq and Musa ibn 'Uqbah—into an accessible chronological manual for students and scholars alike.

Applying his rigorous traditionist methodology, Ibn Abd al-Barr filters historical reports to retain sound narratives, detailing the major events of the Prophet’s ﷺ life, from his lineage and birth to the pivotal expeditions and his passing. Due to its clarity, brevity, and sound textual foundation, it serves as an ideal introductory textbook for memorization, foundational study, and structured teaching of the Prophetic biography.

name: Mu'jizat al-Nabi (Miracles of the Prophet) - Ibn Kathir
description_short:
Mu'jizat al-Nabi ﷺ (The Miracles of the Prophet) by the renowned Hadith master, historian, and exegete Imam Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH) is an authoritative classical compendium documenting the divine signs and extraordinary events granted to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The work methodically covers sensory miracles—such as the splitting of the moon, water springing from his noble fingers, the multiplication of scarce food, and the weeping of the palm trunk—alongside fulfilled prophecies regarding future events and the supreme, everlasting miracle of the Holy Quran.

Extracted from the extensive Dala'il al-Nubuwwah section of his monumental chronicle Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, this treatise reflects Ibn Kathir’s trademark critical Hadith methodology. The author brings together textual evidence from the Quran, authentic prophetic traditions, and historical reports, carefully evaluating chains of narration (asānīd) and distinguishing authentic reports from unverified historical legends to present a robust theological defense of the truth of Muhammad’s ﷺ prophethood.

Al-I'rab al-Mufassal li al-Qur'an al-Karim by Muhammad Makkawi is an exhaustive 5-volume grammatical reference offering a complete, practical, and highly accessible syntactic and morphological parsing of the entire Holy Quran from Surah al-Fatihah to Surah al-Nas.

Each page features a distinct framed block displaying the Quranic passage, followed immediately by an orderly, word-by-word and letter-by-letter grammatical breakdown. The text utilizes a functional two-color layout: every Quranic term, particle, and verse number is printed in crisp red, followed by its complete grammatical determination in black.

The analysis methodically covers word classes, attached and implied pronouns (al-damir al-mustatir), explicit vowel markings and inflectional signs (e.g., fathah, dammah, kasrah, hadhf harf al-'illah, thubut al-nun), as well as the overarching syntactic functions of complete clauses and semi-clauses (i'rab al-jumal wa shibh al-jumal). This crystal-clear structural presentation makes the set an essential desk reference for teachers, university students, and serious researchers in Arabic syntax and Quranic linguistics.

name: Tafsir al-Quran - al-Qadi Ishaq al-Busti (307H)
description_short:
A musnad-based tafsir from one of the earliest surviving exegetical works of the 3rd Islamic century, authored by al-Qadi Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Busti (d. 307 AH), a contemporary of Imam al-Tabari and Ibn Abi Hatim during the golden era of hadith compilation — among those who transmitted from him was his student Imam Abu Hatim ibn Hibban al-Busti, the author of the Sahih. Following the athari method of exegesis, it systematically records early interpretive reports with their complete chains back to the Companions — notably Ibn Abbas — and prominent Tabi'in such as Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and al-Hasan al-Basri. Only part of the book has reached us — from Surat al-Kahf through to beyond Surat al-Najm — yet what survives testifies to the elevation of its chains and its proximity to the age of transmission, making it a rare primary source in athari tafsir.

This three-volume edition features a critical tahqiq by Sabri ibn Abd al-Khaliq al-Shafi'i. Every narration is sequentially numbered with comparative takhrij cross-referencing each report against Tafsir al-Tabari, Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Durr al-Manthur. Printed in two colors (red for Quranic text, chapter titles, and narration numbers; black for commentary and footnotes) on chamois paper.

name: Al-Ifsah 'an Ma'ani al-Sihah - Ibn Hubayrah (560H)
description_short:
A comprehensive commentary on the Sahihayn of al-Bukhari and Muslim, considered the first complete work to combine hadith explanation with the extraction of comparative fiqh across the four schools. Authored by the scholar-vizier Abu al-Muzaffar Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Hubayrah al-Shaybani (499-560 AH), Vizier of the Abbasid Caliphate and a Hanbali jurist who united political authority with scholarly depth. He built it on al-Humaydi's "al-Jam' bayn al-Sahihayn," commenting on the hadiths, drawing out their jurisprudential content, and surveying the points of agreement and disagreement among the four Imams with the evidence of each.

The book's most celebrated section is its comparative fiqh, which grew from his commentary on the hadith "Whoever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding of the religion" — expanding into a comprehensive survey of agreed-upon and disputed fiqh questions that became so renowned it was extracted and published independently. This edition in six volumes (twelve parts) with tahqiq and takhrij by Prof. Dr. Fu'ad Abd al-Mun'im Ahmad.

name: Al-Tamyiz fi Takhrij Ahadith Sharh al-Wajiz - Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
description_short:
Al-Tamyiz fi Talkhis Takhrij Ahadith Sharh al-Wajiz is the original classical title given by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (d. 852 AH) to his monumental Hadith verification compendium, celebrated throughout Islamic history under its famous title Al-Talkhis al-Habir. Composed to critically examine, source, and authenticate all prophetic narrations, legal traditions, and historical reports cited by Imam al-Rafi'i (d. 623 AH) in Al-Sharh al-Kabir (his renowned commentary on al-Ghazali’s Al-Wajiz), this work stands as the crowning reference in the science of legal Hadith extraction (takhrij ahadith al-ahkam).

Ibn Hajar created this masterpiece by condensing and refining Al-Badr al-Munir, the expansive work of his teacher Siraj al-Din Ibn al-Mulaqqin, while integrating critical verifications and valuable additions from earlier traditionists such as Ibn Kathir, al-Zarkashi, and Imam al-Nawawi. He enriched the work with his own unrivaled mastery of narrator criticism (al-jarh wa al-ta'dil), tracing variant narration paths (turuq), uncovering hidden textual and chain defects ('ilal), and delivering decisive verdicts on hadith authenticity.

Whether consulted under its authentic original title Al-Tamyiz or its widely recognized name Al-Talkhis al-Habir, this indispensable universal encyclopedia of legal proofs remains a standard reference for Hadith scholars, muftis, professors of comparative law, and advanced researchers across all Islamic legal schools.

A high-quality print edition, revised and corrected, carefully verified against seven manuscripts and two early editions. It features most of the Harakat and complementary annotations for referencing and hadith authentication (takhrij).

name: Al-Talqin fi al-Fiqh al-Maliki - al-Qadi Abd al-Wahhab (422H)
description_short:
One of the most celebrated and finest abridgments in Maliki jurisprudence, and one of the books on which the school revolves. Authored by al-Qadi Abu Muhammad Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ali ibn Nasr al-Baghdadi (d. 422 AH), one of the great Maliki jurists who spread the school in Iraq. It covers the fundamental fiqh questions arranged on the standard chapters — from purification through the rest of fiqh — without going into detailed evidence, avoiding excessive branching and multiple opinions. Its style is concise and precise, lending itself to memorization and study.

Despite its small size, it is among the best and most beneficial books of the school, and scholars devoted themselves to commenting on it and explaining its meanings — the most famous being the commentary of Imam al-Maziri, who studied directly under the author, and which some leading Maliki scholars considered unmatched in the school. An essential text for every Maliki student seeking a concise and solid jurisprudential foundation.

This critical two-volume edition is based on seventeen selected manuscripts drawn from a survey of thirty-two codices, including copies transcribed from authorial reading sessions and early historical transmissions corrected by notable jurists. Edited, vocalized, and annotated by Muhammad Tawfiq ibn Ammar al-Bannani, the text provides complete variant apparatus notes, cross-references to early Maliki source literature, and full thematic indices.

The study investigates the classical phonetic heritage established by early grammarians and Quranic orthoepists—chiefly al-Khalil ibn Ahmad, Sibawayh, Abu Amr al-Dani, and Ibn al-Jazari—and evaluates their observations against the empirical framework of modern acoustic and articulatory phonetics.

The author conducts a detailed technical inquiry into points of articulation (makharij al-huruf) and sound attributes (sifat), addressing disputed areas such as the phonetic reality of the oral/pharyngeal cavity (al-jawf), the nature of long vowels (huruf al-madd), and vocal cord vibration dynamics. Makhluf analyzes the divergence between the classical sequencing of speech sounds (progressing from the deepest throat outward to the lips) and the reverse orientation favored by modern linguists, assessing whether these differences constitute substantive mechanical disagreements or merely terminological and pedagogical variations.

description_short:
Al-I'tiqad (also known as 'Aqidat Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi or Juz' fi al-I'tiqad 'ala Tariqat al-Salaf) is a foundational Athari theological treatise authored by the traditionist and jurist Taqi al-Din Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi (d. 600 AH). The work systematically articulates the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-al-Jama'ah, establishing the affirmations of the Divine Names and Attributes without distortion (tahrif) or anthropomorphism (tamthil), the uncreated reality of the Quran, the Beatific Vision in the Hereafter (al-ru'yah), and the principles of faith (iman) and divine decree (qadar). Drawing directly upon textual proofs from the Quran and authentic Sunnah, al-Maqdisi strictly adheres to the traditional transmission method of early traditionists, deliberately steering clear of speculative theological philosophy (kalam).

This critical edition, prepared by Prof. Dr. Tariq ibn 'Ayyadah al-Qahtani of the Islamic University of Madinah, marks the treatise's first publication based on nine authentic manuscript witnesses. Foremost among these primary sources is a unique manuscript that was auditioned multiple times before the author himself, featuring his handwritten validations and corrections. The editor prefaces the treatise with a comprehensive analytical monograph titled Fath Allah al-Wali fi al-Ta'rif bi-'Aqidat al-Maqdisi Abd al-Ghani, contextualizing the historical tribulations faced by the author, verifying the text's transmission line, and furnishing the core text with rigorous scholarly annotations and hadith cross-referencing.
